title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄序
萬曆己卯天下復當賓興士
御史顧鈐以
上命按廣西得監臨試事遵故事
聘禮繼及教諭陳志頤為考
試官教諭嚴思恭呂朝陽王
元弼訓導徐雲山吳道東為
===
同考試官以左布政使吳椿
右布政使盧仲佃司提調按
察使林澄源副使歐陽模司
監試暨百執事遴選咸稱入
鎖院御史進禮繼等而盟之
曰簾以內諸文學典之惟衡
乃平惟鑑乃明慎之哉又進
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄序
萬曆己卯，天下復當賓興士。御史顧鈐以
上命按廣西，得監臨試事。遵故事，聘禮繼及教諭陳志頤為考試官，教諭嚴思恭、呂朝陽、王元弼，訓導徐雲山、吳道東為同考試官。以左布政使吳椿、右布政使盧仲佃司提調，按察使林澄源、副使歐陽模司監試，暨百執事，遴選咸稱。入鎖院，御史進禮繼等而盟之曰：「簾以內，諸文學典之。惟衡乃平，惟鑑乃明，慎之哉！」又進
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the jimao year of the Wanli era [1579], the empire was once again due to ceremonialize the recommendation of scholars as honored guests. Investigating Censor Gu Qian 顧鈐, inspecting Guangxi by Imperial command, obtained the duty of Supervising Official for the examination affairs. Following precedent, he invited [me,] Li Ji 禮繼, together with Instructor Chen Zhiyi 陳志頤 to serve as Examiners; and Instructors Yan Sigong 嚴思恭, Lü Chaoyang 呂朝陽, and Wang Yuanbi 王元弼, along with Assistant Instructors Xu Yunshan 徐雲山 and Wu Daodong 吳道東, to serve as Associate Examiners. He appointed Left Administration Commissioner Wu Chun 吳椿 and Right Administration Commissioner Lu Zhongdian 盧仲佃 to take charge as Proctors; Surveillance Commissioner Lin Chengyuan 林澄源 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Ouyang Mo 歐陽模 to take charge as Censorial Monitors of the Examination; together with all the sundry functionaries, everyone selected was well suited to his post.

Upon entering the locked examination compound, the Censor summoned Li Ji and the others forward and administered a solemn oath to them, saying: "Within the screen, you literary scholars are in charge. Only the balance scale is level; only the mirror is clear. Be careful in this!" He also summoned…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諸司而盟之曰簾以外諸大
夫百執事典之科指具存矩
矱必飭亦自盟也曰予所不
虔毖以詒子大夫憂則有
昭昭之監在焉約已罔弗兢兢祗
厥事乃合提學副使鍾繼英
所程士一千四百有奇三試
===
之得士五十有五人梓其文
以
獻禮繼不佞以職事宜敘首簡
乃颺言於諸士曰爾諸士亦
知今日之奇遘乎夫桂林百
粤之地幅隕二千里夷獠之
族錯編氓而居者殆半其誦
punctuated:
諸司而盟之曰：「簾以外，諸大夫、百執事典之。科指具存，矩矱必飭。」亦自盟也，曰：「予所不虔毖以詒子大夫憂，則有昭昭之監在焉。」約已，罔弗兢兢祗厥事。乃合提學副使鍾繼英所程士一千四百有奇，三試之，得士五十有五人，梓其文以獻。
禮繼不佞，以職事宜敘首簡，乃颺言於諸士曰：爾諸士亦知今日之奇遘乎？夫桂林百粤之地，幅隕二千里，夷獠之族，錯編氓而居者殆半。其誦
translation_en:
… the various officials and made a covenant with them, saying: "Outside the curtain, you grandees and all the functionaries have charge of matters. The examination regulations are all in place, and the rules and standards must be strictly enforced." He also bound himself by covenant, saying: "Should I fail to be reverent and vigilant, thereby causing worry to you grandees, there is the bright and all-seeing supervision of the Emperor above." Once the covenant was concluded, there was no one who did not attend to his duties with the utmost caution and respect. Thereupon, bringing together the more than one thousand four hundred scholars tested and selected by Assistant Surveillance Commissioner for Education Zhong Jiying 鍾繼英, we examined them in three sessions and obtained fifty-five men, whose essays are now printed on woodblocks for presentation to the throne.

Unworthy as I, [Gu] Liji 禮繼, am, by virtue of my official duties it falls to me to write the preface on the opening pages, and so I proclaim to the scholars: Do you scholars realize what a rare and extraordinary opportunity you have met with today? Now Guilin 桂林, a land of the Hundred Yue 百粤, spans an expanse of two thousand li, and non-Chinese tribes live interspersed among the registered commoners as nearly half the population. That those who recite…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
法詩書羣黌校之間得號爲
士斯已難矣矧去
天萬里士白首牖下無繇望見
帝閽者何限而一旦舉之奧渫彈
冠出里待對
大廷抑又難焉至於
聖人御極山海廓清諸士處得脩
===
其故業出得覲其
耿光翱翔天衢若升虛邑則何
啻難之蓋千載一遘耳禮繼
故曰奇也然竊有過計焉夫
士者民所則也舉於千萬人
之中爲
明時用天下所環指而竊睨也是
punctuated: 法《詩》、《書》，羣黌校之間，得號爲士，斯已難矣。矧去天萬里，士白首牖下，無繇望見帝閽者何限！而一旦舉之奧渫，彈冠出里，待對大廷，抑又難焉。至於聖人御極，山海廓清，諸士處得脩其故業，出得覲其耿光，翱翔天衢，若升虛邑，則何啻難之，蓋千載一遘耳！禮繼故曰「奇」也。然竊有過計焉。夫士者，民所則也。舉於千萬人之中，爲明時用，天下所環指而竊睨也。是
translation_en: …and take as their models the Book of Odes (Shijing) and the Book of Documents (Shujing), gathering together in the local schools so as to be called scholars—this in itself is already difficult! How much more so when one is ten thousand li distant from the imperial court: how limitless is the number of scholars who grow white-haired beneath their windows with no means of ever gazing upon the gates of the Emperor's palace! Yet to be raised up one day from obscurity and lowliness, to dust off one's cap and leave one's native village, awaiting the opportunity to respond to the Emperor in the Great Court—this is harder still. And when it comes to a time when a Sage rules on the throne and the mountains and seas are swept clear of turmoil, so that in retirement you scholars are able to cultivate your accustomed studies, and in coming forth you are able to behold His radiant glory, soaring along the avenues of Heaven as easily as ascending into an unguarded town—how is this merely difficult? Indeed, it is an encounter that comes only once in a thousand years! That is why I, Liji, call it "extraordinary." Yet privately I harbor an anxious concern. Now, the scholar is one whom the common people take as their model. Selected from among tens of thousands of people to be employed in an enlightened age, you are those whom the whole world surrounds, points to, and watches closely. Therefore…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
故負超俗之望則標準難蒙
國士之遇則稱塞難際治平
之時則表見難一不當人將
求多而疵瑕之亡論諸士卽
主司者有餘責矣諸士其何
以自效乎夫鉅細異材淺深
異智方圓異器强弱異力稟
===
有固然弗可强也乃心之精
神則無不可自盡者要在本
之以慤耳故弓調而後求勁
馬服而後求良士必慤而後
智能著蓋慤則精專而神定
誠之所極金石爲糜卽智能
稍不及彼固足以辦之况其
punctuated: 故負超俗之望則標準難，蒙國士之遇則稱塞難，際治平之時則表見難。一不當，人將求多而疵瑕之，亡論諸士，卽主司者有餘責矣。諸士其何以自效乎？夫鉅細異材，淺深異智，方圓異器，强弱異力，稟有固然，弗可强也。乃心之精神，則無不可自盡者，要在本之以慤耳。故弓調而後求勁，馬服而後求良，士必慤而後智能著。蓋慤則精專而神定，誠之所極，金石爲糜，卽智能稍不及，彼固足以辦之，况其
translation_en:
…Therefore, when one bears a reputation that transcends the ordinary, it is difficult to serve as a standard; when one receives the treatment due a scholar of state caliber, it is difficult to live up to expectations; and when one encounters an era of peace and good order, it is difficult to distinguish oneself. Should there be a single misstep, people will demand much of them and point out their flaws; not to mention the scholars themselves, even the chief examiners will bear lingering blame. How, then, shall you scholars prove yourselves?

Now, great and small differ in talent, shallow and deep differ in wisdom, square and round differ in vessel, and strong and weak differ in strength. Natural endowments are inherently so and cannot be forced. Yet as for the vital spirit of the mind, there is nothing in which one cannot fully exert oneself; the key lies simply in grounding it in earnestness. Thus, only after a bow is well-adjusted does one seek strength in it; only after a horse is broken in does one seek excellence in it; and a scholar must first be earnest before his wisdom and ability can become manifest. For when one is earnest, one's essence is focused and one's spirit is settled. Where sincerity reaches its utmost, even metal and stone are pulverized. Even if one's wisdom and ability fall slightly short, that earnestness is certainly sufficient to accomplish the task—how much more so when one's…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
過人者耶今
廟堂作則垂範專尚本實思得忠
信樸茂之士布列有位而棄
浮脩實在中土稍難之何則
其所漸者深也乃廣右越在
西南僻徼士生其間類多恂
恂悃愊無一切靡麗之觀卽
===
所爲文大都發明理奧宗本
經訓斤斤守其尺寸雖光采
崛奇差遜中土〔禮繼〕等無寧
收之意所謂忠信樸茂之士
不出此耳語云社樹之峩峩
不如茗柯之細實侈言無當
固不若簡樸者之適用也且
punctuated: 過人者耶？今廟堂作則垂範，專尚本實，思得忠信樸茂之士布列有位，而棄浮脩實，在中土稍難之。何則？其所漸者深也。乃廣右越在西南僻徼，士生其間，類多恂恂悃愊，無一切靡麗之觀。卽所爲文，大都發明理奧，宗本經訓，斤斤守其尺寸。雖光采崛奇差遜中土，〔禮繼〕等無寧收之，意所謂忠信樸茂之士不出此耳。語云：「社樹之峩峩，不如茗柯之細實。」侈言無當，固不若簡樸者之適用也。且
translation_en: …surpass others? Nowadays the court establishes standards and sets down models, exclusively prizing what is fundamental and substantial, and hoping to obtain loyal, trustworthy, unadorned, and solid scholars to fill official positions. Yet casting aside superficiality and cultivating substance is somewhat difficult in the Central Plains. Why is that? Because what people there have been steeped in runs deep. Guangxi, however, lies far off on the remote southwestern frontier. The scholars born in this region are mostly modest, sincere, and earnest, devoid of all extravagant and ostentatious display. Even in the essays they compose, for the most part they elucidate the profound principles and base themselves on the teachings of the Classics, scrupulously adhering to the proper standards and measures. Although in brilliance and striking originality they are slightly inferior to those of the Central Plains, I, [Li Ji] 禮繼, and my colleagues preferred to select them, thinking that those who may be called loyal, trustworthy, unadorned, and solid scholars are surely to be found right here. As the saying goes: "The towering tree at the local altar is not as good as the fine fruit on the tea branch." Extravagant words that lack substance are certainly not as suited for practical use as what is simple and unadorned. Moreover,…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諸士不見桂嶺諸山終古巍
巍乎氣從昆侖自北徂南而
極于西粵則其基厚也又不
見湘灕諸水終古洋洋乎勢
從海陽支分為二而縈洄數
千里則其源深也士躡雲霄
之會將楨榦
===
王國恢弘
帝猷以建巍巍洋洋之業而使基
弗厚源弗深則胡以應之忠
信樸茂固士之基與源也操
玆往焉而益以閱天下之義
理習
國家之典刑精神所注何事弗
punctuated: 諸士不見桂嶺諸山終古巍巍乎？氣從昆侖，自北徂南而極于西粵，則其基厚也。又不見湘、灕諸水終古洋洋乎？勢從海陽，支分為二而縈洄數千里，則其源深也。士躡雲霄之會，將楨榦王國，恢弘帝猷，以建巍巍洋洋之業；而使基弗厚、源弗深，則胡以應之？忠信樸茂，固士之基與源也。操玆往焉，而益以閱天下之義理，習國家之典刑，精神所注，何事弗
translation_en: … Do you scholars not see how the mountains of Guiling stand towering through all eternity? Their vital force comes from Kunlun, extending from north to south until it reaches its limit here in Western Yue [Guangxi]—thus their foundation is thick. And do you not see how the waters of the Xiang and Li rivers flow vast and boundless through all eternity? Their momentum rises from Mount Haiyang, splitting into two branches and winding for several thousand li—thus their source is deep. When scholars ascend to the lofty heights of opportunity, they are about to become the pillars of the realm and expand the imperial plan, so as to establish towering and boundless achievements; yet if their foundation is not thick and their source not deep, how then can they answer this call? Loyalty, trustworthiness, and unadorned substance are indeed the foundation and source of a scholar. Holding fast to these as you go forth, and adding to them by examining the moral principles of the world and familiarizing yourselves with the statutes and institutions of the state, wherever you focus your spirit, what task could you not …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
任所以標準天下稱知己而
報
明時端在是矣脫或出見紛華弁
髦本質靡然改玉初終若兩
人則不惟負此舉負此時回
視閭里編氓且非故我安所
貴士矣諸士勉哉是舉也先
===
總督兩廣都察院右都御史
兼兵部左侍郎今晉南京兵
部尚書凌雲翼治教兼弘肅
清嶺海總督兩廣兵部右侍
郎兼都察院右僉都御史劉
堯誨威德並楙興起髦髦先
巡撫廣西都察院右副都御
punctuated:
任？所以標準天下、稱知己而報明時，端在是矣。脫或出見紛華，弁髦本質，靡然改玉，初終若兩人，則不惟負此舉、負此時，回視閭里編氓，且非故我，安所貴士矣！諸士勉哉！
是舉也，先總督兩廣都察院右都御史兼兵部左侍郎、今晉南京兵部尚書凌雲翼，治教兼弘，肅清嶺海；總督兩廣兵部右侍郎兼都察院右僉都御史劉堯誨，威德並楙，興起髦髦；先巡撫廣西都察院右副都御
translation_en:
… shoulder? The means to serve as a standard for the realm, live up to those who recognize your worth, and repay this enlightened era truly lie right here. Should you perhaps go out into the world, be dazzled by luxury and splendor, cast aside your innate substance like a useless cap, and yieldingly change your conduct as if switching jade pendants, so that at the end you are like a different person from who you were at the beginning—then not only will you fail this examination and fail this era, but when you look back upon the registered commoners of your home villages, you will not even be your former self. What, then, would be worthy of esteem in a scholar! Strive hard, gentlemen!

In this undertaking, the former Supreme Commander of Liangguang, Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate concurrently serving as Left Vice Minister of War, now promoted to Nanjing Minister of War, Ling Yunyi 凌雲翼, broadly advanced both governance and education, pacifying and cleansing the mountain ranges and seas; the Supreme Commander of Liangguang, Right Vice Minister of War concurrently serving as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, Liu Yaohui 劉堯誨, flourished in both majesty and virtue, rousing and inspiring talented scholars; the former Grand Coordinator of Guangxi and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
史今晉戸部右侍郎吳文華
握憲經文甄陶素洽巡撫廣
西都察院右副都御史張任
壯猷崇雅綱紀聿新鎮守廣
西總兵官署都督僉事王尚
文詰戎靖遠章縫樂業其襄
試事于外者左參政彭文質
===
右參政王原相右參政兼僉
事陳應春副使陳俊侯國治
右參議姜忻右參議兼僉事
李一迪參將于嵩倪中化李
應祥韓文啓張榜咸與有力
焉副使周舜岳左參議毛爲
光署都指揮僉事呂應暘則
punctuated: 史、今晉戸部右侍郎吳文華，握憲經文，甄陶素洽；巡撫廣西、都察院右副都御史張任，壯猷崇雅，綱紀聿新；鎮守廣西總兵官、署都督僉事王尚文，詰戎靖遠，章縫樂業。其襄試事于外者，左參政彭文質、右參政王原相、右參政兼僉事陳應春、副使陳俊、侯國治、右參議姜忻、右參議兼僉事李一迪、參將于嵩、倪中化、李應祥、韓文啓、張榜，咸與有力焉。副使周舜岳、左參議毛爲光、署都指揮僉事呂應暘，則
translation_en: … [Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate], now promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, Wu Wenhua 吳文華, held the censorial authority and promoted civil culture, his molding of talent having long been pervasive; the Grand Coordinator of Guangxi and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate Zhang Ren 張任, with grand plans and esteem for refinement, has renewed the laws and discipline; the Regional Commander of Guangxi and Acting Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief Wang Shangwen 王尚文, keeping the military in order and pacifying distant regions, has enabled scholars in their ceremonial dress to rejoice in their studies. As for those who assisted with the examination affairs from outside: Left Administration Vice Commissioner Peng Wenzhi 彭文質, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Yuanxiang 王原相, Right Administration Vice Commissioner concurrently Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Chen Yingchun 陳應春, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Chen Jun 陳俊 and Hou Guozhi 侯國治, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Jiang Xin 姜忻, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner concurrently Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Li Yidi 李一迪, and Assistant Regional Commanders Yu Song 于嵩, Ni Zhonghua 倪中化, Li Yingxiang 李應祥, Han Wenqi 韓文啓, and Zhang Bang 張榜 all contributed their efforts to it. Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhou Shunyue 周舜岳, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Mao Weiguang 毛爲光, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Lü Yingyang 呂應暘, who…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以入
賀行右叅政莊國禎則以遷秩
行亦與襄始事法得竝書
福建福州府福清縣儒學敎
諭尹禮繼謹序
punctuated:
以入賀行，右叅政莊國禎則以遷秩行，亦與襄始事，法得竝書。
福建福州府福清縣儒學敎諭尹禮繼謹序。
translation_en:
…had departed to present congratulations at Court, while Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right Zhuang Guozhen 莊國禎 had departed upon promotion to a new post; yet because they too assisted in initiating the affairs of the examination, by regulation their names may also be recorded together here.
Respectfully prefaced by Yin Liji 尹禮繼, Instructor of the Confucian School of Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian.

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萬曆七年廣西鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史顧鈐〔朝肅浙江仁和縣人辛酉貢士〕
提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司左布政使吳椿〔壽卿江西新建縣人己未進士〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司右布政使盧仲佃〔田叔浙江東陽縣人丙辰進士〕
監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使林澄源〔仲清福建莆田縣人己未進士〕
廣西等處提刑按察司副使歐陽模〔宏甫福建南安縣人己未進士〕
===
考試官

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
居敬而行簡以臨其民不亦可乎居簡而
行簡無乃大簡乎子曰雍之言然
唯天下至誠爲能經綸天下之大經
日月有明容光必照焉
易
君子進德脩業忠信所以進德也脩辭立
其誠所以居業也知至至之可與幾也
===
知終終之可與存義也
說而巽孚乃化邦也
然則聖人之意其不可見乎子曰聖人立
象以盡意設卦以盡情僞繫辭焉以盡
其言變而通之以盡利鼓之舞之以盡
神乾坤其易之縕耶乾坤成列而易立
乎其中矣
大有衆也同人親也
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

居敬而行簡，以臨其民，不亦可乎？居簡而行簡，無乃大簡乎？子曰：「雍之言然。」
唯天下至誠，爲能經綸天下之大經。
日月有明，容光必照焉。

易

君子進德脩業。忠信，所以進德也；脩辭立其誠，所以居業也。知至至之，可與幾也；知終終之，可與存義也。
說而巽，孚乃化邦也。
然則聖人之意，其不可見乎？子曰：「聖人立象以盡意，設卦以盡情僞，繫辭焉以盡其言，變而通之以盡利，鼓之舞之以盡神。」乾坤，其易之縕耶？乾坤成列，而易立乎其中矣。
大有，衆也。同人，親也。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"To abide in reverence and practice simplicity in governing one's people—is that not permissible? Yet to abide in simplicity and also practice simplicity—would that not be overly simple?" The Master said, "What Yong says is right."
Only he who possesses the utmost sincerity in the world can order and adjust the great invariable relations of the world.
The sun and moon have their brightness, so that wherever a ray of light can penetrate, they are sure to illuminate it.

Book of Changes (Yi)

The noble man advances in virtue and cultivates his work. Loyalty and trustworthiness are the means by which he advances in virtue; cultivating his words and establishing his sincerity are the means by which he abides in his work. Knowing the goal to be reached and reaching it, he can engage with the subtle incipient tendencies; knowing where things end and bringing them to an end, he can preserve righteousness.
Joyful and penetratingly compliant, his trustworthiness thus transforms the states.
"If this is so, then can the intentions of the sages not be seen?" The Master said, "The sages established the images to fully express their intentions, set up the hexagrams to fully expose what is genuine and what is false, appended the verbal judgments to fully convey their words, varied and carried them through to fully realize the benefit, and drummed and danced them to fully manifest the spirit." Are Qian and Kun not the storehouse of the Changes? When Qian and Kun are arrayed in order, the Changes are established in their midst.
Da You (Great Possession) signifies the multitude. Tong Ren (Fellowship with Men) signifies closeness.

Book of Documents (Shu)

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
臣哉鄰哉鄰哉臣哉禹曰俞帝曰臣作朕
股肱耳目
王忱不艱允協于先王成德
其汝克敬德明我俊民
澤潤生民四夷左衽罔不咸賴
詩
坎坎伐檀兮寘之河之干兮河水清且漣
猗
俾爾多益以莫不庶
===
思齊大任文王之母思媚周姜京室之婦
大姒嗣徽音則百斯男
王釐爾成來咨來茹嗟嗟保介維莫之春
亦又何求如何新畬於皇來牟將受厥
明明昭上帝迄用康年命我衆人庤乃
錢鎛奄觀銍艾
春秋
祭公來遂逆王后于紀〔桓公八年〕春紀季
姜歸于京師〔桓公九年〕
punctuated:
臣哉鄰哉！鄰哉臣哉！」禹曰：「俞。」帝曰：「臣作朕股肱耳目。
王忱不艱，允協于先王成德。
其汝克敬德，明我俊民。
澤潤生民，四夷左衽，罔不咸賴。

《詩》
坎坎伐檀兮，寘之河之干兮，河水清且漣猗。
俾爾多益，以莫不庶。
思齊大任，文王之母，思媚周姜，京室之婦。大姒嗣徽音，則百斯男。
王釐爾成，來咨來茹。嗟嗟保介，維莫之春，亦又何求？如何新畬？於皇來牟，將受厥明。明昭上帝，迄用康年。命我衆人，庤乃錢鎛，奄觀銍艾。

《春秋》
祭公來，遂逆王后于紀〔桓公八年〕。春，紀季姜歸于京師〔桓公九年〕。
translation_en:
“‘Ministers, my close associates! Close associates, my ministers!’ Yu said, ‘Yes.’ The Emperor said, ‘My ministers act as my legs and arms, my ears and eyes.’”

“The king’s sincerity is not difficult; it truly accords with the accomplished virtue of the former kings.”

“May you be able to revere virtue and bring to light our eminent men.”

“Beneficent moisture enriches the living people; the four barbarian tribes who fasten their garments on the left all without exception rely upon it.”

Book of Odes (Shi)

“Kan-kan go the blows on the sandalwood trees, and they are placed on the bank of the River; the waters of the River are clear and rippling.”

“Granting you much increase, so that there is nothing that is not abundant.”

“Reverent was Tai Ren, the mother of King Wen; loving was she toward Tai Jiang of Zhou, a wife in the capital house. Tai Si inherited her admirable reputation, and so bore a hundred sons.”

“The king has given you acharge of completion; come to consult, come to deliberate. Ah, assistant officers! It is now the end of spring, and what more do you seek? How is it with the newly cleared fields and those in their third year? Oh, splendid are the wheat and barley; we shall soon receive their bright bounty. Bright and glorious is the Lord on High, who will bring us a year of abundance. Order our multitudes to prepare their spades and hoes; soon we shall see the sickles reaping.”

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

“The Duke of Zhai came, and thereupon went to meet the queen in Ji [Eighth Year of Duke Huan]. In spring, Ji Jiang of Ji went as bride to the capital [Ninth Year of Duke Huan].”

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
冬楚子使椒來聘〔文公九年〕
楚人執鄭行人良霄〔襄公十有一年〕夏楚
子蔡侯陳侯鄭伯許男徐子滕子頓子
胡子沈子小邾子宋世子佐淮夷會于
申〔昭公四年〕
秋晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年〕
禮記
是故禮者君之大柄也
近者說服而遠者懷之此大學之道也
===
脩身及家平均天下此古樂之發也
子民如父母有憯怛之愛有忠利之教親
而尊安而敬威而愛富而有禮惠而能
散其君子尊仁畏義恥費輕實忠而不
犯義而順文而靜寬而有辨甫刑曰德
威惟威德明惟明非虞帝其孰能如此
乎
第貳場
論
punctuated:
冬，楚子使椒來聘〔文公九年〕。
楚人執鄭行人良霄〔襄公十有一年〕；夏，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申〔昭公四年〕。
秋，晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年〕。

禮記
是故禮者，君之大柄也。
近者說服而遠者懷之，此大學之道也。
脩身及家，平均天下，此古樂之發也。
子民如父母，有憯怛之愛，有忠利之教，親而尊，安而敬，威而愛，富而有禮，惠而能散；其君子尊仁畏義，恥費輕實，忠而不犯，義而順，文而靜，寬而有辨。《甫刑》曰：「德威惟威，德明惟明。」非虞帝其孰能如此乎？

第貳場
論
translation_en:
"In winter, the Viscount of Chu sent Jiao to come on a mission of friendly inquiry." [9th year of Duke Wen]
"The people of Chu seized Liang Xiao, the Messenger of Zheng" [11th year of Duke Xiang]; "In summer, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Viscount of Xu, the Viscount of Teng, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Shen, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, Heir Apparent Zuo of Song, and the Yi of the Huai met at Shen." [4th year of Duke Zhao]
"In autumn, Xun Wu of Jin led an army to attack Xianyu." [15th year of Duke Zhao]

Record of Rites (Liji)
"Therefore ritual is the great handle of the ruler."
"Those who are near submit with pleasure, and those who are distant cherish him: this is the Way of the Great Learning."
"Cultivating the person and extending it to the family, and bringing peace and equilibrium to all under Heaven: this is the manifestation of ancient music."
"Treating the common people as one's children, like a father and mother, having a deeply sympathetic love and a loyal,beneficial teaching: one is felt to be close and yet is honored, one inspires ease and yet is revered, one is awe-inspiring and yet is loved, one is wealthy and yet observes ritual propriety, one is beneficent and yet able to distribute generously. His noble men honor benevolence and stand in awe of righteousness, are ashamed of extravagance and think lightly of material wealth, are loyal without transgressing, righteous and yet compliant, accomplished and yet tranquil, magnanimous and yet discriminating. The Punishments of Fu (Fu xing) says: 'Through the awe of virtue they are awed; through the illumination of virtue they are enlightened.' If not for the Sovereign of Yu (Shun), who could be like this?"

Second Session
Discourse (Lun)

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄

===
錢糧互相覺察
致祭祀典神祇
縱放軍人歇役
修理橋梁道路
第叄場
策〔五道〕
問王業根本莫重農桑周自后稷開基文
武纘緒親耕親蠶爲天下先一時成法
具經籍中可備述歟攷詩書所稱先公
punctuated:
輔助德業而致太平。

詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕：
擬漢舉賢良文學詔〔元光元年〕；
擬唐以裴度爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔元〕〔和十年〕；
擬宋龍圖閣學士孫奭進《無逸圖》表〔天聖〕〔五年〕。

判語〔五條〕：
舉用有過官吏；
錢糧互相覺察；
致祭祀典神祇；
縱放軍人歇役；
修理橋梁道路。

第叄場

策〔五道〕

問：王業根本，莫重農桑。周自后稷開基，文、武纘緒，親耕親蠶，爲天下先。一時成法，具經籍中，可備述歟？攷《詩》、《書》所稱先公、
translation_en:
Assisting in Virtuous Enterprise and Bringing About Great Peace.

Imperial Edicts, Mandates, and Memorials [candidates select one]:
A simulated Han dynasty imperial edict recommending the Worthy and Upright and those of Literary Learning [first year of the Yuanguang era (134 BCE)].
A simulated Tang dynasty mandate appointing Pei Du 裴度 as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery [tenth year of the Yuanhe era (815)].
A simulated Song dynasty memorial by Sun Shi 孫奭, Academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, presenting the Illustrations of "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi tu) [fifth year of the Tiansheng era (1027)].

Legal Judgments [five items]:
Recommending and Employing Officials and Functionaries Who Have Committed Offenses;
Mutual Surveillance over Funds and Grain;
Offering Sacrifices to Deities in the Sacrificial Canon;
Releasing Soldiers without Authorization to Rest from Duty;
Repairing Bridges and Roads.

Third Session

Policy Questions [five items]

Question: At the root of kingly enterprise, nothing is more important than agriculture and sericulture. In the Zhou dynasty, from the time Hou Ji 后稷 laid the foundation and Kings Wen 文 and Wu 武 continued the line, the ruler personally plowed and the consort personally tended silkworms to set an example for all under heaven. The established institutions of that era are preserved in the canonical texts—can you recount them in full? When we examine what the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu) say of the former dukes and …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
先王未聞親耕親蠶之禮乃王業實肇
基是時其故何歟自漢而後亦有足稱
者歟我
太祖高皇帝再造區寰軫念民瘼伏讀元年之
詔與
廷諭諸臣孰非萬世當服膺者可得而恭述歟
列聖繼體崇實嗣徽務本有
訓織婦有
詞穀祇蠶壇有
===
賦悉心於民依之念說者謂軼周室而過之
亦可陳其槩歟我
皇上
冲年御宇卹災蠲賦加
惠黎元至渥也是歲仲春
俞廷臣之請脩籍禮有日矣未幾有
旨期於來年意必有待將二者並舉以重
盛典歟頃因春雨特廑
天語令農夫乘時力田無惰業聞者莫不舉手
punctuated: 先王，未聞親耕親蠶之禮，乃王業實肇基是時，其故何歟？自漢而後，亦有足稱者歟？我太祖高皇帝再造區寰，軫念民瘼，伏讀元年之詔與廷諭諸臣，孰非萬世當服膺者？可得而恭述歟？列聖繼體，崇實嗣徽，務本有《訓》，織婦有《詞》，穀祇、蠶壇有《賦》，悉心於民依之念，說者謂軼周室而過之，亦可陳其槩歟？我皇上冲年御宇，卹災蠲賦，加惠黎元至渥也。是歲仲春，俞廷臣之請，脩籍禮有日矣。未幾，有旨期於來年，意必有待，將二者並舉以重盛典歟？頃因春雨，特廑天語，令農夫乘時力田，無惰業，聞者莫不舉手
translation_en:
… the former kings, we do not hear of the rites of personally plowing and personally tending silkworms, yet the royal enterprise truly laid its foundations at that time—what is the reason for this? From the Han dynasty onward, were there also those worthy of praise?

Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), remade the realm and showed deep concern for the sufferings of the people. When we humbly read the edicts of his first year and his court instructions to the various officials, which of them is not something that ten thousand generations ought to take to heart? Can you reverently recount them? Successive sacred emperors inherited the throne, esteeming practical reality and continuing his fine example: there were the Instructions on Attending to the Fundamental, the Lyrics on the Weaving Women, and the Rhapsodies on the Spirit of Grain and the Silkworm Altar. In devoting their whole hearts to the concern for what the people depend upon, commentators say that they surpassed the House of Zhou and went beyond it; can you also set forth the general outline of this?

Our August Emperor ascended the throne in his youth; in relieving disasters and remitting taxes, the grace he has bestowed upon the common people is most generous. In the second month of spring this year, he approved the request of the court officials, and a date had already been set for performing the rite of the sacred field (jili). Before long, an imperial decree postponed it until next year. Surely there is something awaited—is it that both rites [plowing and sericulture] will be held together in order to give greater weight to the grand ceremony? Recently, on account of the spring rains, he specially lavished imperial words ordering farmers to seize the season to work the fields and not be lazy in their occupations. Among those who heard this, there was none who did not raise their hands…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
加額思見
仁政之成眞千載一時也多士躬逢
盛世沐浴太和願颺言之以附於豳風無逸之
歌
問天下之事未有不玩於習而作於明王
者授人以官而不考其成是權不懸而
欲輕重辨也堯命舜曰詢事考成乃言
底可績皐陶曰屢省乃成此在後世且
以爲督責之術而唐虞行之輒成無爲
===
之治何歟春秋所紀有自朝日至日入
無不自計乃職者周禮所紀有歲時月
日無不有考者此悉遵唐虞之遺以致
盛治而後之稱綜核稱總攬稱强明果
敢者又卒不免有遺議也抑又何歟我
祖宗
列聖以來法紀嚴明稽核整肅上下奉行至兢
兢也乃近者狃於治平日就蝓安卽所
上計簿入
punctuated:
加額，思見仁政之成，眞千載一時也。多士躬逢盛世，沐浴太和，願颺言之，以附於《豳風》、《無逸》之歌。

問：天下之事，未有不玩於習而作於明。王者授人以官而不考其成，是權不懸而欲輕重辨也。堯命舜曰：「詢事考成，乃言底可績。」皐陶曰：「屢省乃成。」此在後世，且以爲督責之術，而唐、虞行之，輒成無爲之治，何歟？《春秋》所紀，有自朝日至日入，無不自計乃職者；《周禮》所紀，有歲、時、月、日無不有考者。此悉遵唐、虞之遺以致盛治，而後之稱綜核、稱總攬、稱强明果敢者，又卒不免有遺議也，抑又何歟？我祖宗列聖以來，法紀嚴明，稽核整肅，上下奉行至兢兢也。乃近者狃於治平，日就蝓安，卽所上計簿入
translation_en:
…to their foreheads in gratitude, longing to see the perfection of benevolent governance—truly a moment that comes once in a thousand years. You gentlemen have personally encountered this flourishing age and bathed in its supreme harmony; pray set forth your views at length, so as to append them to the songs of the "Airs of Bin" (Binfeng) and "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi).

Question: In the affairs of the world, there are none that do not grow lax through habit and become invigorated through clarity. If a true king bestows office upon men without examining their achievements, it is like wishing to distinguish light from heavy without suspending the steelyard weight. When Yao gave his charge to Shun, he said: "Inquire into their affairs and examine their achievements, and their words have been brought to Accomplishment." Gao Yao said: "Frequently examine their achievements." In later ages, such practices would even be regarded as the techniques of harsh supervision and责 (accountability-enforcement), yet when Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] practiced them, they readily achieved governance by non-action (wuwei). Why is this? In the records of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), there were those who from morning until sunset never failed to take account of their own duties; in the records of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), there were examinations conducted by the year, the season, the month, and the day without exception. All of these followed the legacy of Tang and Yu to bring about flourishing governance; yet those in later times who were praised for comprehensive verification, for gathering all authority into their own hands, or for being forceful, clear-sighted, and resolute, ultimately could not avoid lingering criticism. Why is this so? Since the reigns of our Imperial Ancestors and the successive Sagely Emperors, laws and discipline have been strict and clear, and verification and auditing have been orderly and solemn; superiors and inferiors have carried them out with the utmost circumspection. Yet recently, grown accustomed to peace and order, officials daily slip into sluggish ease [reading 蝓 as 偷], and even the account registers submitted for entry into…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖覽者每廢時日我
皇上從輔臣請稽查積年章奏立限考成非唐
虞詢事考言意哉中外臣工罔不滌玩
愒改觀聽月有成歲有報矣欲自今行
之永永不替不知此外尚有當講可以
佐此者歟諸士行且服官聽任使者請
先言之以觀用世之具
問守令者民之師帥繫焉而建威銷萌則
在良將二者所需至亟矣粤西去
===
天萬里地瘠民貧且夷落盤錯其間時出爲患
所需二者不尤亟歟乃談達不羈之士
謂此也不足起名則何昔之垂聲西土
彬彬盛也試質所聞彼鬱林之廉石伏
波之銅柱爛然睹記有刺容管而綏定
八州有令布山而惠及嫏𡠉有順俗設
教禁而士人得師有睦鄰諭酋豪而蠻
夷歸命均稱良吏矣孰爲優歟有給士
焚營而卜陽破有誑諜逸囚而曹成遯
punctuated:
聖覽者，每廢時日。我皇上從輔臣請，稽查積年章奏，立限考成，非唐虞「詢事考言」意哉？中外臣工，罔不滌玩愒、改觀聽，月有成、歲有報矣。欲自今行之，永永不替，不知此外尚有當講、可以佐此者歟？諸士行且服官聽任使者，請先言之，以觀用世之具。

問：守令者，民之師帥繫焉；而建威銷萌，則在良將。二者所需至亟矣。粤西去天萬里，地瘠民貧，且夷落盤錯其間，時出爲患，所需二者不尤亟歟？乃談達不羈之士，謂此也不足起名，則何昔之垂聲西土、彬彬盛也？試質所聞：彼鬱林之廉石、伏波之銅柱，爛然睹記。有刺容管而綏定八州，有令布山而惠及嫏𡠉，有順俗設教禁而士人得師，有睦鄰諭酋豪而蠻夷歸命，均稱良吏矣，孰爲優歟？有給士焚營而卜陽破，有誑諜逸囚而曹成遯，
translation_en:
… for Imperial review frequently waste time and drag on for days. Our August Emperor, acting upon the request of the Grand Secretaries, has ordered an audit of memorials accumulated over the years and established deadlines to evaluate their completion—is this not the very spirit of the Tang and Yu eras in "inquiring into deeds and examining words"? Officials both in the capital and the provinces have without exception cleansed themselves of negligence and idleness, renewing what is seen and heard, so that every month brings achievements and every year brings reports. If we wish to carry this out from now on so that it never falters in perpetuity, I wonder whether beyond this there are still other matters that ought to be discussed which could assist in this endeavor? Gentlemen, as you are soon to take office and await assignment, please speak of this first, so that we may observe your wherewithal for serving the world.

Question: On prefects and magistrates depends the guidance and leadership of the people; while establishing awe and nipping rebellion in the bud rests with good generals. The need for both is utmost and urgent. Western Yue [Guangxi] is ten thousand li distant from the imperial court; its land is barren and its people poor, and moreover non-Chinese settlements are intertwined throughout the region, emerging from time to time to cause trouble—is not the need for both even more urgent here? Yet free-spirited scholars who talk of grand attainment say that this region is insufficient to make one's name; why then in former times were those who left behind a glorious reputation in this western land so richly abundant? Let us examine what we have heard: that "Stone of Integrity" in Yulin and the "Bronze Pillars" of the Wave-Subduing General [Ma Yuan 馬援] shine brightly in the historical records. There was one who served as Prefect of the Rong District Administration and pacified eight prefectures; one who served as Magistrate of Bushan and whose benevolence reached the local women and children [? 嫏𡠉]; one who established instruction and prohibitions in accordance with local customs so that the literati found a teacher; and one who promoted harmony among neighbors and instructed the chieftains so that the southern tribes submitted to authority—all of these are acclaimed as good civil officials, yet which of them was superior? There was one who provisioned his soldiers and burned the enemy camps so that Bu Yang 卜陽 was defeated; one who deceived spies and released prisoners so that Cao Cheng 曹成 fled; …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有斬袁用而儂智高敗走有趨懷遠而
羅世念請降均稱良將矣孰最奇歟今
主上神聖加意宇内大簡文武吏士計安元元
嚴且悉矣頃
徵郡國縣道治行最者增秩優異之介胄有乘
一障畫一策卽拔起戎行爲軍鋒冠士
生斯時有不自矜奮者非夫也果人人
各抒所抱卓有昔人風歟抑溺其職者
未盡無歟玆欲宣
===
德振威民安閭里夷戢疆場則何所施設哉諸
士其悉意陳之毋遜
問善理財者不加賦而國自足說者謂無
是理然至於賦必不可加而用必不可
不足也則謂之何今之稱瘠土者孰過
粤西乃其備征剿急歳用也又孰過粤
西吾於此得二策焉鹽筴者籌國長計
也自管子制鹽禁一切生于木産于池
煑于海者俱掌之官爲經國之助粤西
punctuated:
有斬袁用而儂智高敗走，有趨懷遠而羅世念請降，均稱良將矣，孰最奇歟？今主上神聖，加意宇内，大簡文武吏士，計安元元，嚴且悉矣。頃徵郡國縣道治行最者，增秩優異之；介胄有乘一障、畫一策，卽拔起戎行，爲軍鋒冠。士生斯時，有不自矜奮者，非夫也。果人人各抒所抱，卓有昔人風歟？抑溺其職者未盡無歟？玆欲宣德振威，民安閭里，夷戢疆場，則何所施設哉？諸士其悉意陳之，毋遜。

問：善理財者，不加賦而國自足，說者謂無是理。然至於賦必不可加，而用必不可不足也，則謂之何？今之稱瘠土者，孰過粤西？乃其備征剿、急歳用也，又孰過粤西？吾於此得二策焉。鹽筴者，籌國長計也。自管子制鹽禁，一切生于木、産于池、煑于海者，俱掌之官，爲經國之助。粤西
translation_en:
… there was one who beheaded Yuan Yong 袁用 and caused Nong Zhigao 儂智高 to be defeated and flee; and there was one who marched swiftly on Huaiyuan 懷遠 so that Luo Shinian 羅世念 begged to surrender. All of these are acclaimed as fine generals—which of them was the most extraordinary?

At present, the reigning Sovereign, divinely sage, pays keen attention to the realm within the seas. He conducts a grand selection of civil and military officials and officers, planning for the peace and security of the common people in a manner both strict and thorough. Recently, those from commanderies, principalities, counties, and marches who were summoned for having the best administrative records were granted increased ranks and special distinctions; and among armored soldiers, anyone who could defend a single frontier post or devise a single stratagem was immediately promoted out of the ranks to head the vanguard of the army. For a gentleman born in such times, not to take pride and rouse himself to action would mean he is no true man. Does everyone indeed give full expression to his aspirations, standing out with the style of the men of old? Or are those who fail in their duties not yet entirely absent? Now, if we wish to proclaim virtue andprojec awe, so that the people are at peace in their hamlets and the non-Chinese tribes are held in check along the frontiers, what policies and measures should be put in place? Let you gentlemen set forth your thoughts in full, without diffidence.

Question: Those skilled in managing finances make the state self-sufficient without increasing taxes, yet commentators say there is no such principle. When it comes to a situation where taxes absolutely cannot be increased, and yet expenditures absolutely cannot fall short, what is to be said of it? Today, among places called barren lands, which surpasses western Yue [Guangxi]? Yet in preparing for punitive expeditions and pressing for annual expenditures, which again surpasses western Yue? In this connection I have found two policies. The salt monopoly is a long-term plan for financing the state. Ever since Master Guan [Guanzi 管子] instituted salt prohibitions, all salt produced from trees, yielded by salt lakes, or boiled from the sea has been managed by the officials as an aid in governing the state. Western Yue …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
非産鹽之地近議出公帑轉鬻南海輸
之湖湘計歲入可當常賦一二矣比聞
湘湖之間稍稍稱苦鹽食國計既不可
廢而民困又不可不理也將何道以處
之而使公私兩利耶泉布自然之利自
周立圜府而八兩五銖鵞眼綖環制益
紛紛比歲海宇開局鑄錢乃粤西錢法
流行獨易即今稍有贏羨可備兵荒需
矣但地處極邊無所得銅以故開爐爲
===
獨少今且苦於銅之不繼銅不繼將至
廢局將何道以通之而使經久可行耶
此二者粤西以縮爲盈之術也子多士
留心世務日久况桑梓哉願有以相告
問兵者不得已而用也然亦有不可不用
粤西猺獞雜居山谷盤錯深箐陰木莫
知涯際固盜賊之所必穴也胡可無兵
勿論往事姑以近日言之無古田之舉
胡以成永寧無府江之舉胡以安平樂
punctuated:
非産鹽之地，近議出公帑轉鬻南海，輸之湖湘，計歲入可當常賦一二矣。比聞湘湖之間稍稍稱苦，鹽食國計既不可廢，而民困又不可不理也，將何道以處之，而使公私兩利耶？泉布，自然之利。自周立圜府，而八兩、五銖、鵞眼、綖環，制益紛紛。比歲海宇開局鑄錢，乃粤西錢法流行獨易，即今稍有贏羨，可備兵荒需矣。但地處極邊，無所得銅，以故開爐爲獨少；今且苦於銅之不繼，銅不繼將至廢局，將何道以通之，而使經久可行耶？此二者，粤西以縮爲盈之術也。子多士留心世務日久，况桑梓哉？願有以相告。

問：兵者，不得已而用也，然亦有不可不用。粤西猺、獞雜居，山谷盤錯，深箐陰木，莫知涯際，固盜賊之所必穴也，胡可無兵？勿論往事，姑以近日言之，無古田之舉，胡以成永寧？無府江之舉，胡以安平樂？
translation_en:
…is not a salt-producing region. Recently, it has been proposed to disburse public funds to purchase salt from the Southern Sea [Guangdong] for resale and transport it to the Hu-Xiang region [Huguang]; it is calculated that the annual revenue could match ten or twenty percent of the regular tax quota. Yet lately it has been heard that people in the Xiang and Hu region are gradually complaining of hardship. Since salt consumption and state finances cannot be abandoned, while the distress of the people also cannot be left unaddressed, by what way can this be managed so as to benefit both the public treasury and private citizens? Coinage is a natural source of profit. Ever since the Zhou dynasty established the Treasury of Round Money (Huanfu), through the banliang [half-tael, written 八兩 here], wuzhu [five-zhu], "goose-eye" (eyan), and "thread-ring" (tinghuan) coins, the systems have grown increasingly varied and complex. In recent years, minting bureaus have been opened throughout the empire to cast coins, and in Guangxi the circulation of currency has been uniquely smooth; at present there is already a modest surplus that can provide for the needs of warfare and famine. However, because the province is situated on the far frontier, there is nowhere to obtain copper, and for this reason the furnaces opened have been uniquely few. Now, moreover, we suffer from the failure of the copper supply to keep pace, and if copper supplies cannot be maintained, it will lead to the closing down of the minting bureaus. By what way can this be facilitated so as to make it sustainable over the long term? These two measures are the techniques by which Guangxi turns scarcity into abundance. You gentlemen have long paid close attention to the affairs of the world—how much more so when it concerns your own native land! I hope you have counsel to offer.

Question: Military force is something used only when unavoidable, yet there are also times when it cannot but be used. In Guangxi, the Yao and Zhuang peoples live intermingled; mountains and valleys wind and interlock, and deep bamboo groves and dark woods stretch without known bounds. It is naturally a place where bandits and rebels inevitably make their lairs—how could it do without troops? Leaving aside past events and speaking only of recent days: without the campaign in Gutian, how could Yongning have been established? Without the campaign along the Fu River (Fujiang), how could Pingle have been pacified?…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
信哉荆棘必剪而後嘉禾可生也比歲
粵東大征羅旁并議及粵西之六十三
山七山等巢時以兵糧弗繼暫從撫處
今西之諸巢未聞叛迹東之餘孽旋肆
跳梁撫與勦孰為長算耶說者謂東西
賊巢彼此藏匿非一時夾勦難語全功
而兵興糧從費且鉅萬粵西空乏何以
辦此耶狼兵一調騷擾村邑大眾一動
玉石俱焚何以戢悍卒保善類耶舉事
===
不難難於善後根株不拔勢必滋蔓功
旣告成何以挿羣黎成久安耶然諸巢
與粵東為鄰阻在一隅乃八寨稱腹心
患征勦之師果孰所當先孰所當後耶
多士生于其鄉籌之已熟其詳著于篇
此旦夕見之施行者毋虛談
punctuated: 信哉，荆棘必剪而後嘉禾可生也！比歲粵東大征羅旁，并議及粵西之六十三山、七山等巢。時以兵糧弗繼，暫從撫處。今西之諸巢未聞叛迹，東之餘孽旋肆跳梁。撫與勦，孰為長算耶？說者謂東西賊巢彼此藏匿，非一時夾勦，難語全功；而兵興糧從，費且鉅萬，粵西空乏，何以辦此耶？狼兵一調，騷擾村邑；大眾一動，玉石俱焚。何以戢悍卒、保善類耶？舉事不難，難於善後。根株不拔，勢必滋蔓；功旣告成，何以挿羣黎、成久安耶？然諸巢與粵東為鄰，阻在一隅；乃八寨稱腹心患。征勦之師，果孰所當先、孰所當後耶？多士生于其鄉，籌之已熟，其詳著于篇。此旦夕見之施行者，毋虛談。
translation_en:
Truly, the brambles and thorns must be cleared away before fine grain can grow! In recent years, when Eastern Yue [Guangdong] launched a major campaign against Luopang, deliberations also extended to the strongholds of the Sixty-Three Mountains and Seven Mountains in Western Yue [Guangxi]. At the time, because troops and provisions could not be sustained, a policy of pacification and accommodation was temporarily adopted. Now, while no signs of rebellion have been heard from the various strongholds in the west, the surviving rebels in the east have soon resumed their rampages. Between pacification and suppression, which is the better long-term strategy?

Some argue that the bandit strongholds in the east and west harbor one another, and unless a simultaneous pincer campaign is launched, it will be difficult to speak of complete success. Yet when troops are mobilized, provisions must follow, at a cost reaching into the tens of thousands; given the exhaustion and scarcity of Western Yue, how can this be managed? Once the native "wolf troops" (langbing) are requisitioned, they harass the villages and towns; once a large host is set in motion, jade and stone are burned alike. How can we restrain fierce soldiers and protect good, law-abiding people? Launching a campaign is not difficult; what is difficult is the post-campaign settlement. If the roots and stumps are not pulled up, they will inevitably spread again; once victory is declared, how can we resettle the common people and achieve lasting peace? Furthermore, those various strongholds bordering Eastern Yue are isolated in one corner, whereas the Eight Stockades (Bazhai) are known as a malady in our very heartland. For an army of suppression, which should truly come first, and which should come later?

You gentlemen were born in this region and have long deliberated over these matters; set forth your detailed views in your essays. These are measures to be put into practice at any moment—do not indulge in empty talk.

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
居敬而行簡以臨其民不亦可乎居簡而
行簡無乃大簡乎子曰雍之言然
王應泰
同考試官教諭王批君子執簡御煩惟在一敬
是作說理明透詞約意足殆可與論簡者宜錄以式
考試官教諭陳批簡當得體
考試官教諭尹批醇雅可誦
===
賢者以敬論簡而聖人與之也蓋簡主於敬而
一於簡焉不可也聖人所以然賢者之言與仲
弓見夫子可伯子之簡而言曰簡一也行之在
天下而居之在吾心論簡者顧所以居之何如
耳居之以敬吾心之自治嚴矣而行之以簡順
其所無事焉是我有執而民無擾也或者其可
乎居之以簡吾心之自治疎矣而所行又簡廢
其所有事焉是我無執而民斯玩也無乃太簡
乎是夫子之可伯子微詞也仲弓未之喻也而
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「居敬而行簡，以臨其民，不亦可乎？居簡而行簡，無乃大簡乎？」子曰：「雍之言然。」

王應泰

同考試官教諭王批：君子執簡御煩，惟在一敬。是作說理明透，詞約意足，殆可與論簡者。宜錄以式。
考試官教諭陳批：簡當得體。
考試官教諭尹批：醇雅可誦。

First Session

The Four Books

"To abide in reverence and practice simplicity in governing one's people, is this not permissible? To abide in simplicity and practice simplicity, is this not excessive simplicity?" The Master said, "What Yong says is right."

Wang Yingtai 王應泰

Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang 王 comments: The gentleman holds to simplicity in order to govern complexity, and this rests solely upon reverence. This essay explains the principle with clarity and penetration; its words are concise yet its meaning is complete. One might well discuss simplicity with its author. It ought to be recorded as a model.
Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳 comments: Concise, fitting, and proper in form.
Examiner and Instructor Yin 尹 comments: Pure, elegant, and worthy of recitation.

The worthy discusses simplicity by grounding it in reverence, and the Sage approves of him. Indeed, simplicity must be governed by reverence; to be devoted solely to simplicity will not do. Is this not why the Sage affirmed the worthy's words!

Seeing that the Master had approved of Bozi's 伯子 simplicity, Zhonggong 仲弓 spoke as follows: "Simplicity is one and the same in name, yet practicing it takes place in the world at large, while abiding in an inner state takes place within one's own mind. Those who discuss simplicity should only consider how one abides within oneself. If one abides in reverence, the self-governance of one's own mind is strict; when one then practices simplicity, following along smoothly without making needless trouble, one maintains a firm grasp within oneself while the people suffer no disturbance—perhaps that is permissible? If one abides in simplicity, the self-governance of one's own mind is lax; when what one practices is also simple, neglecting the affairs that ought to be attended to, one lacks any firm grasp within oneself and the people consequently grow negligent—is that not excessive simplicity?"

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
仲弓之論簡確論也聖人不能易也故曰雍之
言然蓋治以有本而立雍不尚夫簡而尚夫居
敬之簡論治斯有本也率斯言而帝王垂裳之
化不外是矣道以無弊而行雍不病夫簡而病
夫居簡之簡議道斯無弊也率斯言而帝王恭
己之道不越是矣信乎其可使南面也然此乃
仲弓受之夫子者非自為之言也其問仁也曰
見賓承祭敬也不欲勿施簡也孔門論學皆治
論治皆學非有二也南面之使亦知其請事斯
===
語者深乎故曰受之夫子也
唯天下至誠為能經綸天下之大經
劉延祚
同考試官教諭呂 批
講經綸處明析而統貫於
一誠甚得本旨非造理精到之士不能
考試官教諭陳 批 詞旨瑩徹
考試官教諭尹 批 體認精邃
中庸論至誠之盡倫所以明天道也夫大經未
易盡也非天下至誠其孰能經綸之哉中庸論
punctuated:
仲弓之論簡，確論也，聖人不能易也，故曰：「雍之言然。」蓋治以有本而立，雍不尚夫簡，而尚夫居敬之簡，論治斯有本也。率斯言，而帝王垂裳之化，不外是矣。道以無弊而行，雍不病夫簡，而病夫居簡之簡，議道斯無弊也。率斯言，而帝王恭己之道，不越是矣。信乎其可使南面也！然此乃仲弓受之夫子者，非自為之言也。其問仁也，曰「見賓承祭」，敬也；「不欲勿施」，簡也。孔門論學皆治，論治皆學，非有二也。南面之使，亦知其請事斯語者深乎！故曰受之夫子也。

唯天下至誠為能經綸天下之大經。
劉延祚

《中庸》論至誠之盡倫，所以明天道也。夫大經未易盡也，非天下至誠，其孰能經綸之哉？《中庸》論
translation_en:
… Zhonggong's (仲弓) discussion of simplicity is a definitive argument, one that even a sage could not alter; therefore the Master said, "Yong's (雍) words are right." For governance is established by having a root: Yong did not prize simplicity in itself, but rather prized the simplicity that abides in reverence, so his discussion of governance possessed a root. If one follows these words, the transforming influence of the emperors and kings who ruled simply by letting their robes hang down is nothing other than this. The Way operates by being free of defects: Yong did not find fault with simplicity in itself, but rather found fault with the simplicity that abides in simplicity, so his deliberation on the Way was free of defects. If one follows these words, the Way of the emperors and kings who simply held themselves in reverent composure does not go beyond this. Truly, he could be made to face south as a ruler! Yet this was actually what Zhonggong had received from the Master, not words of his own making. When he asked about humaneness (ren 仁), the Master's reply—to behave as though "receiving a great guest" and "officiating at a great sacrifice"—was about reverence; "not doing to others what you do not desire for yourself" was about simplicity. In the school of Confucius, every discussion of learning was governance, and every discussion of governance was learning; they were not two separate things. In saying that he could be made to face south, did the Master not also know how deeply he had taken to heart his request to put those words into practice? Therefore I say he received it from the Master.

By Liu Yanzuo 劉延祚.

It captures the original purport very well; no one but a scholar who has penetrated principles with precision could achieve this.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Chen 陳: The diction and meaning are crystalline and thorough.

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
至誠功用若曰大哉倫乎其理一誠而已誠有
未至者斯倫有未盡耳唯天下至誠實理完於
天賦一心有以涵秩叙之精眞機率於性成一
身有以會倫物之極大經有不得不分者唯至
誠爲能經之因天下自然之等爲天下而區別
焉若緒之有理而不亂也大經有不得不合者
唯至誠爲能綸之因天下自然之類爲天下而
聯屬焉若系之有統而無間也天合人合經雖
不一然皆本一誠以品節之則旣辨其異復統
===
其同天經地誼之懿固獨惇於此矣所以爲天
下立人極其在斯乎主恩主敬經雖不同然皆
本一誠以範圍之則旣分其羣復聚其類民彝
物則之常固獨全於此矣所以爲萬世正人紀
其在斯乎此脩道之敎也而盡性至命該之矣
噫斯其爲天道歟大抵至誠經綸非二也存之
聖心皆大經也發之大經皆聖心也外心以求
經綸非也中庸一書自造端夫婦及武周制作
三重九經莫非經綸地也莫非心也學者求諸
punctuated: 至誠功用，若曰：大哉倫乎！其理一誠而已。誠有未至者，斯倫有未盡耳。唯天下至誠，實理完於天賦，一心有以涵秩叙之精；眞機率於性成，一身有以會倫物之極。大經有不得不分者，唯至誠爲能經之，因天下自然之等，爲天下而區別焉，若緒之有理而不亂也。大經有不得不合者，唯至誠爲能綸之，因天下自然之類，爲天下而聯屬焉，若系之有統而無間也。天合人合，經雖不一，然皆本一誠以品節之，則旣辨其異，復統其同，天經地誼之懿，固獨惇於此矣。所以爲天下立人極，其在斯乎！主恩主敬，經雖不同，然皆本一誠以範圍之，則旣分其羣，復聚其類，民彝物則之常，固獨全於此矣。所以爲萬世正人紀，其在斯乎！此脩道之敎也，而盡性至命該之矣。噫！斯其爲天道歟！大抵至誠經綸，非二也。存之聖心，皆大經也；發之大經，皆聖心也。外心以求經綸，非也。《中庸》一書，自造端夫婦，及武、周制作，三重、九經，莫非經綸地也，莫非心也。學者求諸
translation_en: … the efficacy of utmost sincerity, as if to say: Great indeed are human moral relations! Their principle is nothing more than a single sincerity. Where sincerity has not reached the utmost, there human relations are not fully realized. Only he who possesses the utmost sincerity in the world has real principle complete in his heavenly endowment, so that his one mind is able to encompass the essence of order and rank; true vital springs follow the completion of his nature, so that his one person is able to unite the ultimate standards of human relationships and affairs. Where the great invariable relations must be differentiated, only utmost sincerity is able to arrange them as warp—following the natural gradations of the world, it distinguishes them for the world, just as silk threads have order and are not tangled. Where the great invariable relations must be joined together, only utmost sincerity is able to bind them as cord—following the natural categories of the world, it connects them for the world, just as a lineage has a unifying thread without any gap. Those joined by Heaven and those joined by man, though their invariable relations are not uniform, are all graded and regulated on the basis of a single sincerity; thus, having distinguished their differences, one again unites their commonalities, and the beauty of Heaven's invariable standard and Earth's righteousness is surely made richly substantial in this alone. Is it not right here that the ultimate standard of humanity is established for the world! Those governed by affection and those governed by reverence, though their invariable relations are not the same, are all encompassed and molded on the basis of a single sincerity; thus, having divided them into groups, one again gathers them by kind, and the constancy of the people's moral norms and the rules of things is surely made complete in this alone. Is it not right here that the human moral order is rectified for ten thousand generations! This is the instruction of cultivating the Way, and fully realizing one's nature and reaching destiny are encompassed within it. Ah! Is this not the Way of Heaven? In general, utmost sincerity and ordering the warp and binding the cord are not two separate things. Preserved in the sage's mind, all are the great invariable relations; manifested in the great invariable relations, all are the sage's mind. To seek the ordering and binding of the great relations outside the mind is wrong. Throughout the entire book of the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), from taking its beginning in husband and wife, down to the institutions created by King Wu and the Duke of Zhou, the three weighty matters, and the nine standard rules, there is nothing that is not the ground of ordering and binding, and nothing that is not the mind. title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
運其明者孰主宰是哉其在萬古光垂之矣卽
一間之微亦洞達焉何光昭之大若斯乎然則
明者見矣而所以貞其明者孰根柢是哉故觀
容光之必照而知日月之明之有本矣孔子之
道其大則日月之明中天者也而人皆仰之其
有本則日月之精得天者也而人孰窺之善學
者亦惟探其本而已矣本者何誠是已誠故大
語誠則孔子之一貫堯舜之執中天地之不貳
皆是道也何論日月哉噫非私淑有得者不能
===
推本言之故曰孟子之學獨識其大
易
君子進德脩業忠信所以進德也脩辭立
其誠所以居業也知至至之可與幾也
知終終之可與存義也
張孫念
同考試官敎諭嚴 批 講進脩處卓有定見是深
於易者允宜高薦
考試官敎諭陳 批 明簡可誦
punctuated:
運其明者，孰主宰是哉？其在萬古，光垂之矣，卽一間之微亦洞達焉，何光昭之大若斯乎？然則明者見矣，而所以貞其明者，孰根柢是哉？故觀容光之必照，而知日月之明之有本矣。孔子之道，其大則日月之明中天者也，而人皆仰之；其有本則日月之精得天者也，而人孰窺之？善學者，亦惟探其本而已矣。本者何？誠是已。誠故大。語誠，則孔子之一貫、堯舜之執中、天地之不貳，皆是道也，何論日月哉！噫！非私淑有得者，不能推本言之。故曰：孟子之學，獨識其大。

易
君子進德脩業，忠信，所以進德也；脩辭立其誠，所以居業也。知至至之，可與幾也；知終終之，可與存義也。
張孫念
同考試官敎諭嚴 批：講進脩處卓有定見，是深於《易》者，允宜高薦。
考試官敎諭陳 批：明簡可誦。
translation_en:
… moves their brightness, what presides over this? Throughout all antiquity, their light has shone down, and even the slightest crevice is thoroughly penetrated by it—how is it that the greatness of their shining brilliance is like this? Thus, their brightness is manifest, yet as for that which keeps their brightness constant, what serves as its root and foundation? Therefore, by observing how every crack that admits light is inevitably illuminated, one knows that the brightness of the sun and moon has a fundamental source. As for the Way of Confucius, in its greatness it is like the brightness of the sun and moon hanging in mid-heaven, and all people look up to it; in its having a fundamental source, it is like the essence of the sun and moon derived from Heaven, and who among men can fathom it? Those who are good at learning simply seek out its fundamental source and nothing more. What is this source? It is sincerity. Because it is sincere, it is great. Speaking of sincerity, Confucius's "one thread binding all," Yao and Shun's "holding fast the Mean," and Heaven and Earth's "ceaseless non-duality" are all this very Way—what need is there even to speak of the sun and moon! Alas! Were he not one who had privately cultivated himself after Confucius and gained true insight, he could not have traced it back to its fundamental source in speaking of it. Therefore it is said: the learning of Mencius alone recognized what was great in him.

Classic of Changes (Yi)
"The superior man advances in virtue and cultivates his sphere of duty. Loyalty and faithfulness are the means by which he advances in virtue; cultivating his words so as to establish his sincerity is the means by which he abides in his sphere of duty. Knowing the ultimate point to be reached and reaching it, he can deal with the subtle springs of things; knowing the end to be resting in and resting in it, he can preserve righteousness."

Zhang Sunnian
Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Yan, comments: In explaining the advancement of virtue and cultivation of duty, he possesses an outstanding and settled view. He is one who is profound in the Classic of Changes, and truly deserves a high recommendation.
Examiner, County Director of Studies Chen, comments: Clear, concise, and worthy of recitation.

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭尹批潔淨得旨
文言於君子而詳其進脩之實焉蓋君子以進
德脩業爲心者也然非忠信立誠亦何以造其
極哉文言論乾九三若謂君子者天下所由以
觀德業焉其責不易盡其心恒不自逸也九三
所以日乾而夕惕者果何心哉亦以德吾性也
業吾職也此理之合一者本無一息之或間德
欲其進也業欲其脩也此心之交儆者自無一
時之或違德何如而進耶忠信者實心也有實
===
心而實理可凝也非所以進德乎業何如而脩
耶脩詞立誠者實言也有實言而實行可履也
非所以居業乎忠信雖可以進德未可語德之
至也知其至而忠信以至之則一心有以窮其
神而幾微之理晰矣德之底於日新也不在是
歟立誠雖可以居業未可語業之終也知其終
而立誠以終之則一身有以體其化而時出之
義裕矣業之臻於富有也不在是歟噫君子進
脩之功必如是而後造其極也則其心之憂勤
punctuated:
考試官敎諭尹批：潔淨得旨。

《文言》於君子，而詳其進脩之實焉。蓋君子以進德脩業爲心者也，然非忠信立誠，亦何以造其極哉？《文言》論《乾》九三，若謂：君子者，天下所由以觀德業焉，其責不易盡，其心恒不自逸也。九三所以日乾而夕惕者，果何心哉？亦以德吾性也，業吾職也，此理之合一者，本無一息之或間；德欲其進也，業欲其脩也，此心之交儆者，自無一時之或違。德何如而進耶？忠信者，實心也；有實心，而實理可凝也，非所以進德乎？業何如而脩耶？脩詞立誠者，實言也；有實言，而實行可履也，非所以居業乎？忠信雖可以進德，未可語德之至也；知其至而忠信以至之，則一心有以窮其神，而幾微之理晰矣，德之底於日新也，不在是歟？立誠雖可以居業，未可語業之終也；知其終而立誠以終之，則一身有以體其化，而時出之義裕矣，業之臻於富有也，不在是歟？噫！君子進脩之功，必如是而後造其極也，則其心之憂勤
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Yin尹 comments: Pure, clear, and grasps the main purport.

The Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) speaks of the noble man and details the substance of his advancing in virtue and cultivating his task. Indeed, the noble man takes advancing in virtue and cultivating his task as his mind's aim; yet without loyalty, faithfulness, and establishing sincerity, how could he reach the ultimate? When the Commentary on the Words of the Text discusses the third yang line (jiusan) of the Qian hexagram, it is as if to say: The noble man is the one through whom all under heaven observe virtue and achievement; his responsibility is not easily fulfilled, and his mind never allows itself ease. Why, indeed, is the third yang line diligent all day and vigilantly apprehensive at night? It is simply because virtue is my nature and achievement is my duty—this unity of principle is originally without a single breath's interruption; virtue desires to be advanced and achievement desires to be cultivated—this mutual vigilance of the mind is naturally without a single moment's departure. How does virtue advance? Loyalty and faithfulness are a genuine mind; having a genuine mind, genuine principle can be consolidated—is this not the means to advance in virtue? How is achievement cultivated? Cultivating words to establish sincerity is genuine speech; having genuine speech, genuine action can be practiced—is this not the means to abide in one's task? Although loyalty and faithfulness can advance virtue, one cannot yet speak of the ultimate of virtue; if one knows its ultimate and uses loyalty and faithfulness to reach it, then with one mind one can exhaust its spiritual subtlety, and the principles of subtle incipient tendencies become clear—does not virtue's arriving at daily renewal lie in this? Although establishing sincerity can enable one to abide in one's task, one cannot yet speak of the completion of the task; if one knows its completion and uses establishing sincerity to bring it to completion, then with one's whole person one can embody its transformations, and the rightness of timely action becomes abundant—does not the task's attaining rich possession lie in this? Ah! The effort of the noble man in advancing and cultivating must be like this before it reaches its ultimate; thus the anxious diligence of his mind…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
哉大傳若曰甚矣哉聖人覺民之意無窮也然
意無窮而言有限聖人蓋有不能恝然者是豈
終無可見哉亦以聖人之意盡於象象之理盡
於乾坤故仰觀俯察而聖心之擬議者旣立夫
奇偶之畫斯類情體撰而聖意之包涵者自洩
於形象之表由是重之而爲卦而情僞盡焉發
之而爲辭而言盡焉莫非象也亦莫非意之所
由盡也由是通變于民而利盡焉鼓舞于民而
神盡焉莫非象也亦莫非意之所由盡也夫乾
===
坤未立意固以默而藏乾坤旣立意遂以象而
顯則乾坤也一易之蘊也何也乾列于左而凡
陽之易而爲陰者胥立本于其中坤列于右而
凡陰之易而爲陽者悉肇端乎其内所以設卦
繫辭者從此出也所以通變鼓舞者從此推也
易之蘊不歸於乾坤而何吁此乾坤之象所以
立也此聖人之意所以盡也善學易者因其象
之立求其意之存其於易也思過半矣雖然易
一陰陽也陰陽一太極也反之吾心而各足也
punctuated: 哉！《大傳》若曰：甚矣哉，聖人覺民之意無窮也！然意無窮而言有限，聖人蓋有不能恝然者。是豈終無可見哉？亦以聖人之意盡於象，象之理盡於乾坤。故仰觀俯察，而聖心之擬議者，旣立夫奇偶之畫；斯類情體撰，而聖意之包涵者，自洩於形象之表。由是重之而爲卦，而情僞盡焉；發之而爲辭，而言盡焉。莫非象也，亦莫非意之所由盡也。由是通變于民，而利盡焉；鼓舞于民，而神盡焉。莫非象也，亦莫非意之所由盡也。夫乾坤未立，意固以默而藏；乾坤旣立，意遂以象而顯。則乾坤也，一《易》之蘊也。何也？乾列于左，而凡陽之易而爲陰者，胥立本于其中；坤列于右，而凡陰之易而爲陽者，悉肇端乎其内。所以設卦繫辭者，從此出也；所以通變鼓舞者，從此推也。《易》之蘊不歸於乾坤而何？吁！此乾坤之象所以立也，此聖人之意所以盡也。善學《易》者，因其象之立，求其意之存，其於《易》也，思過半矣。雖然，《易》，一陰陽也；陰陽，一太極也；反之吾心而各足也。
translation_en: …! The Great Commentary (Dazhuan) is as if to say: How profound it is that the sages' intention to enlighten the people is inexhaustible! Yet while their intention is inexhaustible, words are finite, and the sages could not remain unconcerned about this. Could it be that this intention is ultimately impossible to make visible? It is simply that the intention of the sages is fully expressed in the images, and the principle of the images is fully expressed in Qian and Kun. Therefore, looking up to contemplate and looking down to examine, what was deliberated in the minds of the sages was established as the odd and even lines; thus classifying the dispositions of things and embodying the workings of the cosmos, what was encompassed within the intention of the sages naturally revealed itself beyond physical forms and appearances. From this, the lines were doubled to form the hexagrams, and the genuine and the false were fully expressed therein; they were articulated as the appended statements, and words were fully expressed therein. None of this is anything other than the images, and none of it is anything other than the means by which the sages' intention is fully expressed. From this, transformations were communicated to the people, and benefit was fully realized therein; the people were inspired to action, and the numinous was fully realized therein. None of this is anything other than the images, and none of it is anything other than the means by which the sages' intention is fully expressed. Now, before Qian and Kun were established, the intention was indeed silently concealed; once Qian and Kun were established, the intention was thereupon made manifest through the images. Thus Qian and Kun are the very storehouse of the Changes (Yi). Why is this? Qian is arrayed on the left, and all cases in which yang changes into yin establish their root within it; Kun is arrayed on the right, and all cases in which yin changes into yang originate within it. The means by which the hexagrams are set up and the statements are appended issue from this; the means by which transformations are communicated and the people are inspired are extended from this. If the storehouse of the Changes does not come down to Qian and Kun, then to what does it belong? Ah! This is why the images of Qian and Kun were established, and this is how the intention of the sages was fully expressed. For one who excels at studying the Changes, if by relying on the establishment of its images he seeks the preservation of its intention, then with respect to the Changes his understanding will already be more than halfway there. Even so, the Changes is simply yin and yang; yin and yang are simply the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji); and when one turns within to one's own mind, all of it is complete in each of us.

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
使天下皆能於心焉求之則何俟於象之立而
意之盡也奈之何百姓之愚不能得意而忘象
此易書所以不得不作也噫立象盡意豈聖人
得已哉
書
臣哉鄰哉鄰哉臣哉禹曰俞帝曰臣作朕
股肱耳目
戴九有
同考試官教諭呂批發明君臣一體意甚切而
詞復整肅不浮可以式矣
考試官教諭陳批精邃典雅
考試官教諭尹批婉切有味
聖君咏臣職之重因明其義之切也甚矣臣之
關於君者重也觀諸一體之相須而其義之切
不益見哉帝舜感禹弼直之語遂為之咏曰臣
哉鄰哉鄰哉臣哉夫臣而繫之鄰則凡服在大
僚而為保治之佐者孰無後先疏附之責乎信
乎弼之不容不直也鄰而屬之臣則凡左右厥
punctuated:
使天下皆能於心焉求之，則何俟於象之立而意之盡也？奈之何百姓之愚，不能得意而忘象，此《易》書所以不得不作也。噫！立象盡意，豈聖人得已哉？

《書》
「臣哉鄰哉！鄰哉臣哉！」禹曰：「俞。」帝曰：「臣作朕股肱耳目。」
戴九有
同考試官、教諭呂批：發明君臣一體，意甚切，而詞復整肅不浮，可以式矣。
考試官、教諭陳批：精邃典雅。
考試官、教諭尹批：婉切有味。

聖君咏臣職之重，因明其義之切也。甚矣！臣之關於君者重也。觀諸一體之相須，而其義之切不益見哉？帝舜感禹弼直之語，遂為之咏曰：「臣哉鄰哉！鄰哉臣哉！」夫臣而繫之鄰，則凡服在大僚而為保治之佐者，孰無後先疏附之責乎？信乎弼之不容不直也。鄰而屬之臣，則凡左右厥
translation_en:
If everyone in the world could seek it within their own minds, then what need would there be to establish the images and exhaust the meaning? Yet what can be done when the common people in their ignorance cannot grasp the meaning and forget the images? This is why the Book of Changes (Yi) had to be composed. Alas! Was establishing the images to exhaust the meaning something the sages did by choice?

Book of Documents (Shu)
"Ministers! Close associates! Close associates! Ministers!" Yu said, "Yes!" The Emperor said, "Ministers act as my legs and arms, ears and eyes."
Dai Jiuyou 戴九有
Associate Examiner and Instructor Lü comments: It elucidates how ruler and minister form a single body; the thought is very pertinent, and the diction is moreover orderly, solemn, and free of superficiality—it can serve as a model.
Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: Profound and refined.
Examiner and Instructor Yin comments: Gentle, pertinent, and flavorful.

The sage ruler chants of the weightiness of the ministerial office, and thereby clarifies the closeness of its significance. Great indeed is the importance of ministers to their ruler! When we look at their mutual dependence as a single body, is not the closeness of this significance all the more evident? Moved by Yu's words on assisting with uprightness, Emperor Shun thereupon chanted of it, saying: "Ministers! Close associates! Close associates! Ministers!" Now, when "ministers" are linked to "close associates," then among all those who serve in high office and act as aides in preserving good governance, who does not bear the responsibility of attending before and behind and drawing the distant near? Truly, their assistance cannot fail to be upright! And when "close associates" are attributed to "ministers," then among all those who attend the ruler on the left and right…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
辟以賛保治之業者不在宅揆亮工之選乎信
乎直之必藉於弼也夫弼直之語自禹陳之旣
啓帝之所未發而臣鄰之職自帝味之益契禹
之所欲言宜其感之深而遂俞之也帝復從而
申之曰汝知臣所以爲鄰之義乎彼人非股肱
無以運行朕不能自運行乎天下所資以爲馮
翼者臣也其作朕之股肱乎人非耳目無以視
聽朕不能自視聽乎天下所資以達聞見者臣
也其作朕之耳目乎四體效職而後元首尊良
===
臣交脩而後君治廣玆其相須爲至切而臣鄰
之義見矣有弼直之責者其尚無負斯託哉抑
論帝王通天下爲一身其視天下之大呼吸癢
疴靡不相關非獨股肱其臣而已故其精神日
加于四海而無壅閼何者一體故也舜甞明四
目矣達四聰矣而四方從欲應若指臂非一體
之明驗歟
澤潤生民四夷左衽罔不咸賴
譚汝講
punctuated:
辟以賛保治之業者，不在宅揆亮工之選乎？信乎直之必藉於弼也！夫弼直之語，自禹陳之，旣啓帝之所未發；而臣鄰之職，自帝味之，益契禹之所欲言。宜其感之深而遂俞之也。帝復從而申之曰：「汝知臣所以爲鄰之義乎？彼人非股肱無以運行，朕不能自運行乎天下，所資以爲馮翼者，臣也，其作朕之股肱乎！人非耳目無以視聽，朕不能自視聽乎天下，所資以達聞見者，臣也，其作朕之耳目乎！」四體效職而後元首尊，良臣交脩而後君治廣。玆其相須爲至切，而臣鄰之義見矣。有弼直之責者，其尚無負斯託哉！抑論帝王通天下爲一身，其視天下之大，呼吸癢疴靡不相關，非獨股肱其臣而已。故其精神日加于四海而無壅閼，何者？一體故也。舜甞明四目矣，達四聰矣，而四方從欲，應若指臂，非一體之明驗歟？
澤潤生民，四夷左衽，罔不咸賴。
譚汝講
translation_en:
… sovereign to assist in the enterprise of preserving good governance—are they not among those selected to occupy the prime ministership and brighten the royal works? Truly, uprightness must rely upon corrective assistance! Now, when the words about corrective assistance and uprightness were set forth by Yu, they opened up what the Sovereign [Shun] had not yet expressed; and when the duties of ministers as close associates were savored [or chanted, reading 味 for 咏] by the Sovereign, they accorded all the more with what Yu wished to say. Fitting it was that Yu was deeply moved and immediately assented to them. The Sovereign then went on to elaborate on this, saying: "Do you know the meaning of why ministers act as close associates? Just as a person cannot move and act without limbs, I cannot by myself move and act throughout the realm; those upon whom I rely as my support and wings are my ministers—they serve as my limbs! Just as a person cannot see and hear without ears and eyes, I cannot by myself see and hear throughout the realm; those upon whom I rely to extend my hearing and sight are my ministers—they serve as my ears and eyes!" Only when the four limbs perform their functions is the head exalted; only when good ministers cultivate their duties together is the ruler's governance broadened. Herein their mutual dependence is most intimate, and the meaning of ministers as close associates is revealed. May those who bear the responsibility of providing corrective assistance for uprightness not fail this trust! Furthermore, if we consider how emperors and kings unite the entire realm into a single body, in viewing the vastness of the world, every breath and every ache or itch is interconnected—it is not merely that they treat their ministers as limbs. Therefore, their vital spirit daily reaches throughout the Four Seas without obstruction. Why is this? Because they form a single body. Shun once illumined the eyes of the four quarters and opened the ears of the four quarters, and the four quarters followed his desires, responding as fingers to the arm—is this not clear proof of being a single body?

"His beneficence moistens the living people, and the four barbarian tribes who fasten their garments on the left all without exception rely upon him."
Tan Rujiang 譚汝講

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
夏廓如矣不獨列編氓者賴之也雖左衽之俗
亦皆霑餘潤以寧謐大順之休風自下都而通
之宇宙蕩如矣必至是而保釐之託副三后之
功成予小子殆永有慶也公其圖諸抑論成周
盛時九夷重譯中國聖人之化窮極天壤何有
于蕞爾之殷民哉乃成康之君周畢君陳之佐
相繼綏輯猶然廑安危之慮焉此見周家忠厚
之至而商先王之德澤結于人心而不可解者
亦足徴矣
===
詩
思齊大任文王之母思媚周姜京室之婦
大姒嗣徽音則百斯男
王應泰
同考試官教諭王批推本聖德處具見精蘊而
聖德不專藉于人尤知所本者可與言詩矣
考試官教諭陳批詞旨瑩徹
考試官教諭尹批莊雅之作
觀周家內德相承則聖德為有自矣甚矣內治
punctuated:
夏廓如矣。不獨列編氓者賴之也，雖左衽之俗，亦皆霑餘潤以寧謐，大順之休風自下都而通之宇宙，蕩如矣！必至是而保釐之託副，三后之功成，予小子殆永有慶也，公其圖諸！」抑論成周盛時，九夷重譯，中國聖人之化窮極天壤，何有于蕞爾之殷民哉？乃成、康之君，周、畢、君陳之佐，相繼綏輯，猶然廑安危之慮焉。此見周家忠厚之至，而商先王之德澤結于人心而不可解者，亦足徴矣。

詩
「思齊大任，文王之母，思媚周姜，京室之婦。大姒嗣徽音，則百斯男。」
王應泰
同考試官教諭王批：推本聖德處，具見精蘊；而聖德不專藉于人，尤知所本者，可與言《詩》矣。
考試官教諭陳批：詞旨瑩徹。
考試官教諭尹批：莊雅之作。

觀周家內德相承，則聖德為有自矣。甚矣，內治
translation_en:
…the central states [Hua-Xia] will be vast and open! Not only will those enrolled as registered commoners rely upon it, but even the peoples with left-fastened lapels [foreign tribes] will all be moistened by the overflowing grace and enjoy tranquility; the auspicious风 [influence] of great順 [compliance/harmony] will spread from the Lower Capital throughout the entire universe, vast and boundless! Only when this is reached will the commission to protect and regulate be fulfilled and the achievements of the Three Sovereigns be completed, so that I, the Little Child, may perhaps enjoy everlasting felicity. May you, Duke, plan for this!”

Moreover, if we consider the flourishing era of Chengzhou, when the Nine Yi tribes communicated through multiple interpreters and the transformative influence of China’s sages reached the utmost limits of heaven and earth, what difficulty could there be with the tiny remnant people of Yin? Yet sovereigns such as Kings Cheng and Kang, assisted by ministers such as the Dukes of Zhou and Bi and Jun Chen, successively pacified and harmonized them, still harboring anxious concern for security and peril. This shows the utmost loyalty and generosity of the House of Zhou, and it also suffices to prove how the virtuous beneficence of the former kings of Shang was bound so fast to people’s hearts that it could not be undone.

Book of Odes (Shijing)
“Reverent was Tai Ren, the mother of King Wen; loving was she toward Zhou Jiang, a wife in the capital house. Tai Si inherited her admirable reputation, and so bore a hundred sons.”
By Wang Yingtai.

Associate Examiner Instructor Wang’s comment: Where the essay traces the root of sage virtue, it fully reveals the refined essence; and in showing that sage virtue does not depend solely on others, it especially demonstrates knowledge of what is fundamental—one with whom we can discuss the Odes!
Examiner Instructor Chen’s comment: The diction and purport are crystal clear.
Examiner Instructor Yin’s comment: A dignified and elegant composition.

When we observe how domestic virtue was passed down within the House of Zhou, we see that the sage’s virtue had its source. Profound indeed is the way internal governance…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有關于君德也天啓文德而所賴于聖母賢妃
者豈其微哉此詩人詠歌文王之德而推本之
曰文王之德固天縱之而其所由盛尤有獨際
其隆者彼自古帝王君臨天下每難于母后之
聖維此大任乃文王之母焉齊莊本于性生而
祗服明于婦順執之以事周姜凡致愨而愨致
愛而愛允乎媚兹之忱而婦道其克稱矣蓋天
將啓一人明聖之資故先于篤生者而厚其眷
母以德聖則子以母聖淵源所漸夫豈偶然之
===
故哉自古人君正位於外每難于內助之賢維
此太姒乃文王之妃焉貞靜協于思齊而孝敬
嗣乎思媚由之以昌姬籙凡繼體而聖克肖而
賢莫非盛德之徵而多男以百計矣蓋天將翼
我周明聖之運故先于配德者而發其祥后以
德承則君以德顯贊助所及豈曰小補之哉吁
此文王之德之純有以夫雖然文王亦不專藉
乎此也成以聖母助以賢妃天之所以開聖人
也小心翼翼聖人之所以事天也事天至則天
punctuated: 有關于君德也。天啓文德，而所賴于聖母賢妃者，豈其微哉？此詩人詠歌文王之德，而推本之曰：文王之德，固天縱之，而其所由盛，尤有獨際其隆者。彼自古帝王君臨天下，每難于母后之聖。維此大任，乃文王之母焉。齊莊本于性生，而祗服明于婦順。執之以事周姜，凡致愨而愨，致愛而愛，允乎媚兹之忱，而婦道其克稱矣。蓋天將啓一人明聖之資，故先于篤生者而厚其眷。母以德聖，則子以母聖，淵源所漸，夫豈偶然之故哉！自古人君正位於外，每難于內助之賢。維此太姒，乃文王之妃焉。貞靜協于思齊，而孝敬嗣乎思媚。由之以昌姬籙，凡繼體而聖，克肖而賢，莫非盛德之徵，而多男以百計矣。蓋天將翼我周明聖之運，故先于配德者而發其祥。后以德承，則君以德顯，贊助所及，豈曰小補之哉！吁！此文王之德之純，有以夫！雖然，文王亦不專藉乎此也。成以聖母，助以賢妃，天之所以開聖人也；小心翼翼，聖人之所以事天也。事天至則天
translation_en:
… bears upon the virtue of the ruler! When Heaven initiates civil virtue, how could what it relies upon in a sage mother and a worthy consort be slight? Here the poet sings the praises of King Wen's virtue and traces it to its root, saying: The virtue of King Wen was assuredly endowed by Heaven, yet that whereby it flourished lay even more in his uniquely encountering such eminence. Since antiquity, when emperors and kings have ruled over All under Heaven, it has always been difficult to have a sage queen mother. Now this Tairen 太任 was the mother of King Wen. Reverence and dignity were rooted in her innate nature, and respectful compliance was manifest in her wifely obedience. Holding fast to these in serving Jiang of Zhou 周姜, whether in showing utmost sincerity and being sincere, or in showing utmost love and being loving, she was truly faithful in her affectionate devotion, and the way of a wife was thereby fulfilled. Indeed, because Heaven was about to open up the enlightened and sagely endowments of the One Man, it first lavished its favor upon her who gave birth to him. When the mother is sagely through her virtue, the son is sagely through his mother; imbued from this deep source, how could this be a matter of mere chance?

Since antiquity, when a ruler has occupied his rightful position in the outer court, it has always been difficult to have a worthy helper within. Now this Taisi 太姒 was the consort of King Wen. In chaste quietude she harmonized with the reverent Tairen, and in filial reverence she succeeded to her affectionate devotion. Through this she made the mandate of the Ji 姬 clan prosper: all those who succeeded to the line and were sagely, or who resembled their forebears and were worthy, were without exception emblems of flourishing virtue, and her many sons were reckoned by the hundred. Indeed, because Heaven was about to assist the enlightened and sagely destiny of our Zhou, it first manifested its auspicious signs in her who matched his virtue. When the queen succeeds in virtue, the ruler becomes illustrious in virtue; how could the reach of her assistance be called a mere minor supplement?

Ah! That the virtue of King Wen was so pure—there was truly a reason for it! Even so, King Wen did not rely solely upon this. To be brought to completion by a sage mother and assisted by a worthy consort was how Heaven opened the way for the sage; to be谨慎 and reverent (xiaoxin yiyi 小心翼翼) was how the sage served Heaven. When the service of Heaven reaches the utmost, then Heaven …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
純而天在我矣故繼之曰亦保亦臨事天也亦
式亦入純天也故聖人不恃其得天而脩其所
以純天者
王釐爾成來咨來茹嗟嗟保介維莫之春
亦又何求如何新畬於皇來牟將受厥
明明昭上帝迄用康年命我眾人庤乃
錢鎛奄觀銍艾
曹學程
同考試官教諭王批說出成王勤民重本之意
宛然在目蓋究心經義而有得者取之
考試官教諭陳批格調高古讀之灑然
考試官教諭尹批嚴整精密
周王詳戒農官惟欲求成法而已蓋乗時治田
成法具在也明農者可自緩于咨度哉周王戒
農官若曰我周以農事開國固立之官以董其
事又嘗釐之法以受其成矣世相授守允爲畫
一之規法當講求非直循行之具凡爾臣工欲
敬有位其尚來咨焉以詢其實來茹焉以度其
punctuated:
純而天在我矣。故繼之曰：「亦保亦臨」，事天也；「亦式亦入」，純天也。故聖人不恃其得天，而脩其所以純天者。
王釐爾成，來咨來茹。嗟嗟保介，維莫之春，亦又何求？如何新畬？於皇來牟，將受厥明。明昭上帝，迄用康年。命我眾人，庤乃錢鎛，奄觀銍艾。
曹學程
同考試官教諭王批：說出成王勤民重本之意，宛然在目，蓋究心經義而有得者。取之。
考試官教諭陳批：格調高古，讀之灑然。
考試官教諭尹批：嚴整精密。
周王詳戒農官，惟欲求成法而已。蓋乗時治田，成法具在也，明農者可自緩于咨度哉？周王戒農官若曰：我周以農事開國，固立之官以董其事，又嘗釐之法以受其成矣。世相授守，允爲畫一之規；法當講求，非直循行之具。凡爾臣工，欲敬有位，其尚來咨焉以詢其實，來茹焉以度其
translation_en:
… becomes pure, and Heaven is within oneself. Therefore, the ode continues: "Protected, and also overseen"—this is serving Heaven; "Following the model, and also entering into it"—this is being pure as Heaven. Thus, the sage does not rely merely on having obtained Heaven's favor, but cultivates that by which his virtue becomes as pure as Heaven's.

"The king has given you perfect rules; come and consult, come and deliberate. Ah, you attendants! It is now the end of spring; and what more have you to seek? How are the newly tilled fields and those in their third year? Oh, magnificent are the wheat and barley; we shall soon receive their bright bounty. The bright and glorious Lord on High will grant us a year of abundance. Order all our people to prepare their spades and hoes; anon we shall see the sickles reaping."

Cao Xuecheng 曹學程

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Wang 王: He brings out King Cheng's 成王 intent in caring diligently for the people and valuing the fundamental occupation, making it vividly apparent before one's eyes. This is someone who has deeply investigated the meaning of the Classics and gained true insight. Selected.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Chen 陳: The style is lofty and archaic; reading it is refreshing.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Yin 尹: Rigorous, well-ordered, and precise.

When the Zhou king admonished the agricultural officials in detail, he simply wished them to seek out the established rules. Indeed, for taking advantage of the season to cultivate the fields, the established rules are all complete; how could those who understand agriculture allow themselves to be remiss in consulting and deliberating? When the Zhou king admonished the agricultural officials, it was as if he said: Our Zhou dynasty founded the state upon agriculture; we not only established officials to supervise its affairs, but also bestowed rules by which to receive its completed results. Passed down and guarded from generation to generation, they truly constitute a uniform standard; these rules ought to be carefully studied and sought after, not treated merely as instruments for routine compliance.
