title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
詳誠莫有急於今日者咨茹維何嗟嗟保介職
副農官然皆以勸農爲責均當於成法是求也
一歲之計在乎春仰觀天時春則暮矣三農之
務乘乎春俯察新畬今何如哉毋但曰田之難
治而時可後也試觀來牟明昭之賜將受於上
帝而豐穰之利可必于新畬失今不治非法也
何以承天之休乎毋但曰效之難獲而力可懈
也率時農夫錢鎛之興方勤于俶載而銍艾之
舉奄觀於新畬失今不治非法也何以察地之
===
利乎此皆成法所在賜於王者爲甚重而繫於
民者爲不輕也汝農官尚其敬之哉吁周王亦
可謂善訓迪者歟抑務農重穀明王寶之故躬
先耕籍訓官飭務勤民重本之精意固有不專
在於成法者是以咨嗟勸勉洋洋乎盈廟堂徹
閭野宣之史館被之金石後世猶可想見其盛
徒法云乎哉昔人以農事爲帝王傳心之要詎
不信夫
春秋
punctuated:
詳，誠莫有急於今日者。咨茹維何？嗟嗟保介，職副農官，然皆以勸農爲責，均當於成法是求也。一歲之計在乎春，仰觀天時，春則暮矣；三農之務乘乎春，俯察新畬，今何如哉？毋但曰田之難治而時可後也。試觀來牟明昭之賜，將受於上帝，而豐穰之利，可必于新畬。失今不治，非法也，何以承天之休乎？毋但曰效之難獲而力可懈也。率時農夫，錢鎛之興，方勤于俶載，而銍艾之舉，奄觀於新畬。失今不治，非法也，何以察地之利乎？此皆成法所在，賜於王者爲甚重，而繫於民者爲不輕也。汝農官尚其敬之哉！吁，周王亦可謂善訓迪者歟！抑務農重穀，明王寶之，故躬先耕籍，訓官飭務，勤民重本之精意，固有不專在於成法者。是以咨嗟勸勉，洋洋乎盈廟堂、徹閭野，宣之史館，被之金石，後世猶可想見其盛，徒法云乎哉！昔人以農事爲帝王傳心之要，詎不信夫！
春秋
translation_en:
… details, for truly nothing is more urgent today. What are this consultation and deliberation about? Ah, you Assistant Agricultural Officers, your post is deputy to the chief agricultural officials, yet all of you bear the responsibility of encouraging farming and must alike seek out the established laws. The plan for the whole year lies in spring; looking up to observe the season of Heaven, spring is now drawing to a close. The tasks of the three classes of farmers take advantage of spring; looking down to examine the newly tilled and three-year fields, how are they now? Do not merely say that the fields are difficult to till and that the season may be delayed. Just look at the wheat and barley: this bright and manifest gift is about to be received from the Lord on High, and the benefit of an abundant harvest can be assured in the newly tilled and three-year fields. To miss the present moment and leave them untended is contrary to the law; how then could we receive the blessing of Heaven? Do not merely say that results are hard to achieve and that effort may be slackened. Lead these farmers: the wielding of spades and hoes is just now diligent in the spring commencement of work, and the act of reaping with sickles will soon be seen across the newly tilled and three-year fields. To miss the present moment and leave them untended is contrary to the law; how then could we realize the benefit of the earth? In all these things the established laws reside; what is bestowed upon the king is most weighty, and what is bound up with the people is of no light consequence. May you agricultural officials revere this!

Alas, the King of Zhou may truly be called skillful in instructing and guiding! Moreover, devoting effort to agriculture and valuing grain are what enlightened kings treasure. Therefore, personally leading the way in plowing the sacred field, instructing officials and ordering their duties—the essential intent of toiling for the people and valuing the root—surely did not lie solely in established laws. Thus his sighing and exhortations filled the court and reached the village fields in overflowing measure; proclaimed in the historiography institute and inscribed on bronze and stone, later generations can still envision that flourishing age. Could it be a matter of mere laws alone? People of the past regarded agriculture as the essential transmission of the mind of emperors and kings—how could that not be true!

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭陳批詞氣謹嚴格調高古
考試官敎諭尹批詞簡格整
春秋紀內外之屈服而伯主之績見矣此悼之
駕楚服鄭以謀勝以誠感也春秋所以與之歟
晉至中葉悼公復霸命昭糾逖之勳業紹館穀
之烈其功伐著於春秋何踔絕也彼外之強而
撓霸者莫如楚于汜振旅之後屢爭而不可制
其誰能威之東門三駕而北圖遽寢豈其以力
屈之哉蓋惟謀可以制勝楚非屈於晉也屈於
===
謀也息民聽於魏絳還師聽於知罃分軍逆來
楚且疲於奔命矣及至良霄之遣執一行人而
其憤已洩不然會伐之師方興告絕之使復至
馮二廣之力以臨之其不夷為縣鄙乎觀楚之
屈而知謀之能制敵也內之攜而背霸者莫如
鄭于戲要言之後屢盟而不可信其誰能懷之
蕭魚一會而南轅遽挽豈其以力服之哉蓋惟
誠可以動物鄭非服於晉也服於誠也入盟命
於趙武遣告命於叔肸赦囚禮歸鄭且懷其明
punctuated:
考試官敎諭陳批：「詞氣謹嚴，格調高古。」
考試官敎諭尹批：「詞簡格整。」
《春秋》紀內外之屈服，而伯主之績見矣。此悼之駕楚服鄭，以謀勝，以誠感也，《春秋》所以與之歟！晉至中葉，悼公復霸，命昭「糾逖」之勳，業紹「館穀」之烈，其功伐著於《春秋》，何踔絕也！彼外之強而撓霸者莫如楚，于汜振旅之後，屢爭而不可制，其誰能威之？東門三駕，而北圖遽寢，豈其以力屈之哉？蓋惟謀可以制勝，楚非屈於晉也，屈於謀也。息民聽於魏絳，還師聽於知罃，分軍逆來，楚且疲於奔命矣。及至良霄之遣，執一行人，而其憤已洩。不然，會伐之師方興，告絕之使復至，馮二廣之力以臨之，其不夷為縣鄙乎？觀楚之屈，而知謀之能制敵也。內之攜而背霸者莫如鄭，于戲要言之後，屢盟而不可信，其誰能懷之？蕭魚一會，而南轅遽挽，豈其以力服之哉？蓋惟誠可以動物，鄭非服於晉也，服於誠也。入盟命於趙武，遣告命於叔肸，赦囚禮歸，鄭且懷其明…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: "The tone and phrasing are rigorous and disciplined; the style and structure are lofty and ancient."
Examiner and Instructor Yin comments: "The wording is concise and the structure orderly."

The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records the subjugation and submission of external and internal powers, and thereby the achievements of the hegemon are made manifest. Such was Duke Dao [of Jin] overpowering Chu and winning the submission of Zheng—prevailing through strategy and moving others through sincerity! Is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals commends him?

When Jin reached its middle period, Duke Dao restored the hegemony. His royal mandate shone with the merit of "correcting the distant," and his enterprise continued the illustrious achievement of "lodging and feeding [the army at Chengpu]." How surpassingly peerless are his meritorious exploits as recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals!

Among those external powers that were strong and disrupted the hegemony, none matched Chu. After the withdrawal of troops at Fan, it repeatedly contended and could not be controlled; who then could overawe it? Yet with the three campaigns reaching the eastern gate [of Zheng], Chu's northern ambitions suddenly ceased. Was it subdued by mere force? Indeed, only strategy can secure victory. Chu did not yield to Jin; it yielded to strategy. In resting the people, Duke Dao heeded Wei Jiang; in withdrawing the army, he heeded Zhi Ying. By dividing the armies to meet Chu's advances, Chu was left exhausted from rushing about at Jin's command. When it came to the dispatch of Liang Xiao, Chu detained a single envoy and its resentment was already vented. Otherwise, just as the allied expeditionary forces were rising, an envoy announcing the severance of relations would have arrived again; had Chu relied on the strength of its "Two Broads" (Erguang) chariot divisions to bear down on Zheng, would Zheng not have been leveled into outlying counties and districts of Chu? Observing the yielding of Chu, one knows that strategy can subdue the enemy.

Among those internal states that were duplicitous and turned their backs on the hegemony, none matched Zheng. After the coerced covenant at Xi, it repeatedly made alliances that could not be trusted; who then could win its allegiance? Yet with a single assembly at Xiaoyu, its southward-pointing chariot shafts were suddenly turned back. Was it won over by mere force? Indeed, only sincerity can move others. Zheng did not submit to Jin; it submitted to sincerity. Entering the capital to covenant was entrusted to Zhao Wu, and dispatching the announcement [to the Zhou court] was entrusted to Shu Xi; prisoners were pardoned and sent home with ritual courtesy, so that Zheng cherished his bright…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
德矣及至申之會歷二十四年而其志始攜不
然紓民之謀孔多擇疆之歌猶在勤二境之使
以待之其不渝此載書乎觀鄭之服而知誠之
能感人也悼其覇之賢者乎然晉所以覇蓋有
繇也悼以君子之資而得賢人之輔君明臣睦
夫是以九合諸侯而繼三覲之績耳彼二國謀
臣曰晉不可敵曰晉不棄鄭其亦豫見於此乎
禮記
是故禮者君之大柄也
===
李時盛
同考試官訓導吳 批 治國莫急乎禮是作發揮
透徹而講大柄處語尤不俗宜錄以式
考試官教諭陳 批 詞理精到
考試官教諭尹 批 雅健
記者重禮而指其切於治也夫人君之治國必
有為之柄也然其大者孰有過於禮哉記禮運
者蓋曰甚哉人君之道不可無所執而在明其
所執之大吾嘗自禮之得失觀之而知禮之於
punctuated:
德矣。及至申之會，歷二十四年而其志始攜。不然，紓民之謀孔多，擇疆之歌猶在，勤二境之使以待之，其不渝此載書乎？觀鄭之服，而知誠之能感人也。悼其覇之賢者乎！然晉所以覇，蓋有繇也。悼以君子之資，而得賢人之輔，君明臣睦，夫是以九合諸侯，而繼三覲之績耳。彼二國謀臣，曰「晉不可敵」，曰「晉不棄鄭」，其亦豫見於此乎！

《禮記》
「是故禮者君之大柄也。」
李時盛
同考試官訓導吳批：治國莫急乎禮。是作發揮透徹，而講大柄處語尤不俗，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭陳批：詞理精到。
考試官教諭尹批：雅健。

記者重禮，而指其切於治也。夫人君之治國，必有為之柄也，然其大者孰有過於禮哉？記《禮運》者蓋曰：甚哉！人君之道不可無所執，而在明其所執之大。吾嘗自禮之得失觀之，而知禮之於
translation_en:
…virtue. Not until the covenant at Shen, after twenty-four years had passed, did its allegiance finally waver. Otherwise, with plans for relieving the people so numerous and the song of "choosing a strong neighbor" still echoing, while keeping envoys busy between the two borders to await their turn—would they not have violated the covenant text? Observing the submission of Zheng, one knows that sincerity can move people. Was not Duke Dao a worthy hegemon! Yet there was indeed a reason why Jin achieved hegemony. Endowed with the qualities of a gentleman, Duke Dao obtained the assistance of worthy men; the ruler was enlightened and his ministers were harmonious, and for this reason he was able to assemble the feudal lords repeatedly and continue the achievements of the three audiences before the Zhou king. When the advising ministers of those two states said, "Jin cannot be matched," and "Jin will not abandon Zheng," did they not also foresee this!

Record of Rites (Liji)
"Therefore ritual is the great handle of the ruler."
Li Shisheng
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Wu, comments: In governing a state, nothing is more urgent than ritual. This composition expounds the theme thoroughly, and in explaining "the great handle" its language is especially free of vulgarity; it should be recorded as a model.
Examiner, Instructor Chen, comments: The diction and reasoning are precise and thorough.
Examiner, Instructor Yin, comments: Refined and vigorous.

The chronicler attaches great weight to ritual and points out how vital it is to governance. When a ruler governs a state, there must be something that serves as his handle; yet among the greatest of such handles, what could surpass ritual? The author of the "Evolution of Rites" (Liyun) chapter is saying, in effect: Crucial indeed! The way of the ruler cannot be without something to hold fast to, and it lies in understanding the greatness of what he holds. I have observed the matter from the perspective of the success or failure of ritual, and thus know that in relation to…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
治爲最切矣蓋禮者先王以承天之道也而君
之凝承天命者必以是爲持循之要務禮者先
王以治人之情也而君之統理民物者必以是
爲運量之要樞經禮三百秩然示人序矣隆而
由之則所守者至約而可以定天下之民志曲
禮三千燦然示人文矣敬而守之則所持者至
簡而可以立斯世之大防刑政所以輔治而非
治之所關也惟禮爲義理之準得則治而失則
亂人君所以化導海內而消其僭亂之萌者賴
===
有此耳其所當執者果孰大於此哉法度所以
維治而非治之所急也惟禮爲中正之規用則
安而舍則危人君所以綱維天下而杜其陵替
之漸者特有此耳其所當務者孰能爲之大哉
噫禮爲君之大柄如此用器者不可一日而舍
乎柄治國者獨可一日而廢乎禮哉然禮亦難
言矣君子必脩己以敬而無體之禮立故能以
禮讓爲國乎何有否則綿蕞之儀野外之陋習
也果何補於治云是禮者君之大柄也敬者禮
punctuated: 治爲最切矣。蓋禮者，先王以承天之道也，而君之凝承天命者，必以是爲持循之要務；禮者，先王以治人之情也，而君之統理民物者，必以是爲運量之要樞。經禮三百，秩然示人序矣，隆而由之，則所守者至約，而可以定天下之民志；曲禮三千，燦然示人文矣，敬而守之，則所持者至簡，而可以立斯世之大防。刑政所以輔治，而非治之所關也。惟禮爲義理之準，得則治而失則亂，人君所以化導海內而消其僭亂之萌者，賴有此耳，其所當執者，果孰大於此哉？法度所以維治，而非治之所急也。惟禮爲中正之規，用則安而舍則危，人君所以綱維天下而杜其陵替之漸者，特有此耳，其所當務者，孰能爲之大哉？噫！禮爲君之大柄如此。用器者不可一日而舍乎柄，治國者獨可一日而廢乎禮哉？然禮亦難言矣。君子必脩己以敬而無體之禮立，故能以禮讓爲國乎何有；否則綿蕞之儀，野外之陋習也，果何補於治云？是禮者，君之大柄也；敬者，禮
translation_en:
…governance is most urgent. For ritual is that by which the former kings received the Way of Heaven, and a ruler who consolidates and receives the Mandate of Heaven must take this as the essential task to uphold and follow; ritual is that by which the former kings regulated human feelings, and a ruler who governs the people and things must take this as the essential pivot of his deliberation and management. The three hundred cardinal ceremonies systematically show people the proper order; if one exalts and follows them, what is maintained is most concise, yet it suffices to settle the minds of the people throughout the realm. The three thousand detailed rules of demeanor brilliantly show people cultural refinement; if one reverently upholds them, what is grasped is most simple, yet it suffices to establish the great bulwark of this world.

Penalties and administration are the means to assist governance, not what governance hinges upon. Only ritual is the standard of moral principle: when attained there is order, and when lost there is chaos. That by which the ruler transforms and guides the realm within the seas and extinguishes the sprouts of usurpation and disorder depends solely on this—among the things he ought to hold fast to, what indeed is greater than this? Laws and regulations are the means to maintain governance, not what is most urgent in governance. Only ritual is the rule of impartiality and correctness: when employed there is security, and when abandoned there is peril. That by which the ruler upholds the overarching order of the empire and checks the gradual onset of encroachment and decline relies uniquely on this—among the things he ought to devote himself to, what could be greater than this?

Alas! Such is ritual as the great handle of the ruler. One who uses an implement cannot let go of its handle for a single day; how could one who governs a state dispense with ritual for a single day? Yet ritual is also difficult to speak of. The gentleman must cultivate himself with reverence so that ritual without physical form is established; therefore, what difficulty is there in governing a state with ritual and deference? Otherwise, the ceremonies practiced with ropes and bundled grass are merely vulgar customs out in the open fields—what help could they truly be to governance? Thus, ritual is the great handle of the ruler, and reverence is the…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之權輿也圖治者其審諸
脩身及家平均天下此古樂之發也
舒應鳳
同考試官訓導吳批古樂和敬通於治道子獨
究本旨而詞能達意可與言樂矣取之
考試官教諭陳批體格嚴整
考試官教諭尹批明潔
賢者推君子端本之化而歸諸正樂焉甚矣樂
觀其深也以之脩已治人非正樂而能若是乎
===
子夏告文侯意曰樂之作非以其音也聽樂者
非徒聽其音也君子誠能於古樂語而道之而
明其和敬之理焉則涵濡深而性情之融化者
有自淪漸久而道德之和順者愈眞以之脩身
而身無不脩矣由是身者家國天下之本也身
脩以及家則宜其家人而一家於此乎齊焉家
齊以及天下則正是四國而天下於此乎均平
焉君子明樂之效至於如此夫豈今樂之可與
能哉蓋惟古樂之發也其聲足樂而不流故聆
punctuated:
之權輿也，圖治者其審諸。

脩身及家，平均天下。此古樂之發也。
舒應鳳
同考試官訓導吳批：古樂和敬通於治道，子獨究本旨而詞能達意，可與言樂矣，取之。
考試官教諭陳批：體格嚴整。
考試官教諭尹批：明潔。

賢者推君子端本之化，而歸諸正樂焉。甚矣，樂觀其深也！以之脩已治人，非正樂而能若是乎？子夏告文侯意曰：樂之作，非以其音也；聽樂者，非徒聽其音也。君子誠能於古樂語而道之，而明其和敬之理焉，則涵濡深而性情之融化者有自，淪漸久而道德之和順者愈眞，以之脩身而身無不脩矣。由是身者，家國天下之本也。身脩以及家，則宜其家人，而一家於此乎齊焉；家齊以及天下，則正是四國，而天下於此乎均平焉。君子明樂之效至於如此，夫豈今樂之可與能哉？蓋惟古樂之發也，其聲足樂而不流，故聆
translation_en:
…the very beginning of ritual. Those who plan for governance should examine this carefully.

"To cultivate the person and extend it to the family, and to bring equilibrium and peace to All under Heaven: this is the manifestation of ancient music."
Shu Yingfeng 舒應鳳
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wu 吳 comments: Ancient music, through harmony and reverence, connects with the way of governance. You alone have investigated the fundamental purport and your words are able to convey the meaning; one can discuss music with you! Selected.
Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳 comments: The structure and style are rigorous and well-ordered.
Examiner and Instructor Yin 尹 comments: Clear and concise.

The worthy traces the transformative influence by which the gentleman rectifies the root, and attributes it to proper music. Profound indeed is how music is observed in its depths! To use it to cultivate oneself and govern others—without proper music, could it be like this? Explaining his meaning to Marquis Wen 文侯, Zixia 子夏 said in effect: The creation of music is not merely on account of its sounds; those who listen to music do not merely listen to its sounds. If the gentleman can truly discuss and speak of ancient music, and illuminate its principles of harmony and reverence, then his immersion will be deep and the melting transformation of his nature and feelings will have its source; his saturation will be long-lasting and the harmonious compliance of his morality and virtue will become ever more genuine. Using this to cultivate his person, his person will never fail to be cultivated. From this, the person is the root of the family, the state, and All under Heaven. When the cultivation of the person is extended to the family, one does right by the members of one's family, and the whole family is thereby regulated; when the regulation of the family is extended to All under Heaven, one rectifies the states of the four quarters, and All under Heaven is thereby brought to equilibrium and peace. That the efficacy of the gentleman's illumination of music reaches such an extent—how could modern music possibly be capable of sharing in this? For this is solely the manifestation of ancient music! Its sounds are sufficient to give joy without degenerating into license, and therefore those who listen to…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其聲者足以平心而宣化其文足論而不息故
觀其文者足以同文而出治和矣而敬發焉此
敬德之化所以斂諸吾心而施之天下者翕如
也敬矣而和發焉此和德之化所以融諸吾心
而達之天下者藹如也咸英韶濩之音于今雖
不可復覩而唐虞三代之化于樂而實有明徵
矣古樂之發如此君子惟恐其語之不詳也又
安有聽之恐臥耶文侯可以自悟矣大抵古之
聖王心和氣和天地之和應焉故樂之作也盡
===
神而聽之者盡理後世新聲代變本之則無何
足言樂又何貴於聽也夫子曰人而不仁如樂
何噫知仁而後正樂可興脩齊均平之道在此
矣
第貳場
論
輔助德業而致太平
王應泰
同考試官教諭王批〔人君非賢輔無以成治而〕
punctuated:
其聲者，足以平心而宣化；其文足論而不息，故觀其文者，足以同文而出治。和矣而敬發焉，此敬德之化所以斂諸吾心，而施之天下者翕如也；敬矣而和發焉，此和德之化所以融諸吾心，而達之天下者藹如也。咸、英、韶、濩之音，于今雖不可復覩，而唐、虞、三代之化，于樂而實有明徵矣。古樂之發如此，君子惟恐其語之不詳也，又安有聽之恐臥耶？文侯可以自悟矣。大抵古之聖王，心和氣和，天地之和應焉，故樂之作也盡神，而聽之者盡理。後世新聲代變，本之則無，何足言樂？又何貴於聽也？夫子曰：「人而不仁，如樂何？」噫！知仁而後正樂可興，脩、齊、均、平之道在此矣。

第貳場
論
《輔助德業而致太平》
王應泰
同考試官教諭王批：〔人君非賢輔無以成治，而〕
translation_en:
… its sounds are able to calm their minds and spread transformative teaching; its patterns are worthy of discussion and never cease, so those who observe its patterns are able to unify culture and bring forth good governance. When there is harmony, reverence is expressed therein—this is how the transformation of reverent virtue is gathered within our minds and extended to all under heaven in complete unison. When there is reverence, harmony is expressed therein—this is how the transformation of harmonious virtue is blended within our minds and reaches all under heaven in gentle concord. Although the music of the Xianchi, Liuying, Shao, and Dahu can no longer be witnessed today, the transformative governance of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties truly has clear proof in their music. Such was the expression of ancient music; the superior man only feared that it would not be explained in sufficient detail—how could there be any fear of falling asleep while listening to it? Marquis Wen (Wenhou 文侯) could well come to this realization for himself. In general, with the sage kings of antiquity, their minds were harmonious and their vital energy was harmonious, and the harmony of Heaven and Earth responded to them; therefore, the creation of their music exhausted the numinous, and those who listened to it exhausted moral principle. In later ages, new sounds changed from era to era, yet when traced to their root there is nothing there—how are they worthy of being called music, and what value is there in listening to them? The Master said, "If a man be without humaneness, what has he to do with music?" Alas! Only when one understands humaneness can orthodox music be revived, and the Way of cultivating the self, regulating the family, and bringing equilibrium and peace to the world lies right here.

Second Session
Discourse
"Assisting in Virtue and Achievement to Bring About Great Peace"
Wang Yingtai 王應泰

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
好學又用賢之本也是作能發明之而構思精深摛
詞古雅殆非淺學可到宜錄為多士式
考試官教諭陳批平實中有古調佳作也
考試官教諭尹批氣充詞逸迥異諸作
論曰人君得賢以成天下之治者無他惟先之
好學而已矣夫聖主必得賢臣以弘治功賢臣
亦賴聖主以端治本是二人者未始不相須也
然而恒阻於相遇之疎者以上無好學之君故
下無弼直之臣所以明良不交德業未盛而治
===
道藐然卑卑無足論者是故君之圖治也莫急
於親賢而其親賢也莫先於好學君而好學則
天下稱聖主矣主聖則臣賢臣賢則君德益崇
君業益廣而開天下於太平者由此其致也輔
助德業而致太平請因范氏之論而申之今夫
人君以眇然之躬寄之乎巍然之上四海之廣
兆民之眾其所以待治於我者何可勝數近而
朝廷欲其正之内而中國欲其安之外而荒服
欲其撫之推而極於天地莫不欲其調燮而奠
punctuated:
好學又用賢之本也。是作能發明之，而構思精深，摛詞古雅，殆非淺學可到，宜錄為多士式。
考試官教諭陳批：平實中有古調，佳作也。
考試官教諭尹批：氣充詞逸，迥異諸作。
論曰：人君得賢以成天下之治者，無他，惟先之好學而已矣。夫聖主必得賢臣以弘治功，賢臣亦賴聖主以端治本，是二人者，未始不相須也。然而恒阻於相遇之疎者，以上無好學之君，故下無弼直之臣，所以明良不交，德業未盛，而治道藐然，卑卑無足論者。是故君之圖治也，莫急於親賢；而其親賢也，莫先於好學。君而好學，則天下稱聖主矣。主聖則臣賢，臣賢則君德益崇、君業益廣，而開天下於太平者，由此其致也。「輔助德業而致太平」，請因范氏之論而申之。
今夫人君以眇然之躬，寄之乎巍然之上，四海之廣，兆民之眾，其所以待治於我者，何可勝數？近而朝廷欲其正之，内而中國欲其安之，外而荒服欲其撫之，推而極於天地，莫不欲其調燮而奠
translation_en:
… love of learning is in turn the foundation of employing the worthy. This composition is able to elucidate this principle; its conception is refined and profound, and its phrasing is classical and elegant—something scarcely attainable by shallow scholarship. It ought to be recorded as a model for the many scholars.

Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: Within its plainness and solidity there is an ancient resonance; it is a fine composition.

Examiner and Instructor Yin comments: Its vital breath is full and its diction transcendent, vastly different from the other compositions.

The discourse reads: That by which a ruler of men obtains the worthy to accomplish the governance of All under Heaven is nothing other than first dedicating himself to the love of learning. Now, a sage ruler must obtain worthy ministers to broaden the achievements of governance, and worthy ministers likewise rely upon a sage ruler to rectify the foundation of governance; these two have never not depended on one another. Yet what constantly hinders them through the rarity of their meeting is that because there is no ruler who loves learning above, there are consequently no ministers who assist with uprightness below. Therefore, enlightened ruler and capable minister do not join together, virtue and achievement do not flourish, and the Way of governance remains slight and lowly, not worth discussing. For this reason, when a ruler plans for governance, nothing is more urgent than drawing close to the worthy; and in drawing close to the worthy, nothing comes before the love of learning. If the ruler loves learning, then All under Heaven will acclaim him as a sage ruler. When the ruler is sage, the ministers are worthy; when the ministers are worthy, the ruler's virtue becomes ever more exalted and the ruler's achievements ever more expansive, and opening All under Heaven unto grand peace is brought about by this means. "Assisting virtue and achievement so as to bring about grand peace"—allow me to build upon Master Fan's [Fan Zuyu 范祖禹] discourse and elaborate upon it.

Now then, the ruler of men places his minute person high above in a lofty position; across the breadth of the four seas and the multitude of the millions of people, how could the ways in which they await governance from him ever be fully counted? Near at hand, the court desires that he rectify it; within, the Central Lands desire that he pacify them; without, the distant wilderness zones desire that he soothe them; and extending all the way to Heaven and Earth, there is nothing that does not desire that he harmonize and settle…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
是惟精惟一允執厥中取堯舜之所以學者而
學焉學而好焉不矜不伐制事制心取禹湯之
所以學者而學焉學而好焉亦式亦入不泄不
忘取文武之所以學者而學焉學而好焉夫好
堯舜禹湯文武之學則其心即堯舜禹湯文武
之心也其道即堯舜禹湯文武之道也固不必
弓旌之招也蒲輪之聘也而物色之旁求也一
人元良則庶明勵翼當必有皐夔稷契伊呂周
召之儔出於其間焉之相導前後焉之左右夾
===
持由是近而朝廷則以法相序以禮相睦而朝
廷莫不正矣內而中國則禮樂明備刑政脩舉
而中國莫不安矣外而荒服則大小相維強弱
相守而荒服莫不撫矣上而經天則陰陽循序
日月順軌而天道莫不調變矣下而緯地則山
之不童澤之不涸而地道莫不奠麗矣將天下
之人稱之曰此協和風動之業也平成允殖之
休也攸同永清之績也太平極治之世不在唐
虞三代而復見於今日矣何其盛哉夫弓矢不
punctuated: 是「惟精惟一，允執厥中」，取堯、舜之所以學者而學焉，學而好焉；「不矜不伐」，「制事」、「制心」，取禹、湯之所以學者而學焉，學而好焉；「亦式亦入，不泄不忘」，取文、武之所以學者而學焉，學而好焉。夫好堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之學，則其心即堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之心也，其道即堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之道也。固不必弓旌之招也，蒲輪之聘也，而物色之旁求也。「一人元良」，則「庶明勵翼」，當必有皐、夔、稷、契、伊、呂、周、召之儔出於其間，焉之相導前後，焉之左右夾持。由是，近而朝廷，則以法相序，以禮相睦，而朝廷莫不正矣；內而中國，則禮樂明備，刑政脩舉，而中國莫不安矣；外而荒服，則大小相維，強弱相守，而荒服莫不撫矣；上而經天，則陰陽循序，日月順軌，而天道莫不調變矣；下而緯地，則山之不童，澤之不涸，而地道莫不奠麗矣。將天下之人稱之曰：「此協和、風動之業也，平成、允殖之休也，攸同、永清之績也。」太平極治之世，不在唐、虞、三代，而復見於今日矣，何其盛哉！夫弓矢不
translation_en:
…Thus, in "being refined and single-minded, sincerely holding fast to the Mean," one takes that whereby Yao and Shun learned and learns it, learning it and loving it; in "neither boasting nor bragging" and "regulating affairs" and "regulating the mind," one takes that whereby Yu and Tang learned and learns it, learning it and loving it; in "observing the model and entering into it, neither neglecting the near nor forgetting the distant," one takes that whereby Kings Wen and Wu learned and learns it, learning it and loving it. Now, if the sovereign loves the learning of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, then his mind is none other than the mind of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, and his Way is none other than the Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Surely there is no need to summon worthies with bows and banners, to invite them with rush-wrapped wheels, or to search far and wide by portrait! When "the One Man is supremely virtuous," then "the multitude of the enlightened will exert themselves as his wings," and there will surely emerge in their midst the likes of Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, Xie, Yi Yin, Lü Shang, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao, to guide him from before and behind and to support him on his left and right.

From this, near at hand in the royal court, officials will be ordered by law and harmonized by ritual, and nothing in the court will fail to be rectified; within the central states, rites and music will be illustrious and complete, punishments and governance will be cultivated and upheld, and nothing in the central states will fail to be at peace; without, in the wild domains, great and small will sustain one another, strong and weak will guard one another, and none in the wild domains will fail to be pacified; above, in ordering the heavens, yin and yang will follow their proper sequence, the sun and moon will keep to their courses, and nothing in the Way of Heaven will fail to be harmonized; below, in organizing the earth, the mountains will not be stripped bare, the marshes will not dry up, and nothing in the Way of Earth will fail to be settled and secure. Then the people of the world will praise it, saying: "This is the achievement of 'harmonizing the myriad states' and 'moving the people as if by wind' [under Yao and Shun]; this is the blessing of 'bringing water and land to peace and completion' and 'sincerely殖 [fostering livelihoods]' [under Yu and Tang]; this is the merit of 'all regions uniting as one' and 'making the world forever clear by a single donning of armor' [under Wen and Wu]!" An age of Great Peace and ultimate order will not reside only in the times of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, but will be seen again today—how magnificent indeed!

Now, if bow and arrow are not…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
調則后羿不能以中鵠驂服不馴則造父不能
以致遠上下不交則帝王無以治天下然則欲
致太平者可不好學以爲夾輔之本哉雖然日
與諸儒講論同異心非不顓也然雜以霸道卒
爲基禍之君耆舊如蕭望之宗正如劉更生可
謂左右有人矣然優游不斷何補於儒生之純
用由是而知明君以務學爲急務學以知道爲
先苟爲知道則精一數言何要約也然足以致
放勳之盛如不知道即白虎石渠徒滋聚訟耳
===
何裨於君德何益於治道哉此又君人所當知
表
擬宋龍圖閣學士孫奭進無逸圖表 天聖
五年
張孫念
同考試官敎諭嚴 批 措詞莊雅用意謹嚴而忠
懇之忱溢于言表深得臣子告君之體
考試官敎諭陳 批 不事雕鏤工緻自不可到
考試官敎諭尹 批 典則駢儷宛然宋人矩矱
punctuated:
調，則后羿不能以中鵠；驂服不馴，則造父不能以致遠；上下不交，則帝王無以治天下。然則欲致太平者，可不好學以爲夾輔之本哉！雖然，日與諸儒講論同異，心非不顓也，然雜以霸道，卒爲基禍之君；耆舊如蕭望之、宗正如劉更生，可謂左右有人矣，然優游不斷，何補於儒生之純用？由是而知明君以務學爲急，務學以知道爲先。苟爲知道，則「精一」數言，何要約也，然足以致放勳之盛；如不知道，即白虎、石渠，徒滋聚訟耳，何裨於君德，何益於治道哉？此又君人所當知。

表

擬宋龍圖閣學士孫奭進《無逸圖》表〔天聖五年〕

張孫念
同考試官敎諭嚴批：措詞莊雅，用意謹嚴，而忠懇之忱溢于言表，深得臣子告君之體。
考試官敎諭陳批：不事雕鏤，工緻自不可到。
考試官敎諭尹批：典則駢儷，宛然宋人矩矱。
translation_en:
… adjusted, then even Hou Yi 后羿 cannot hit the target; if the outside and inside horses of a team are not docile, then even Zaofu 造父 cannot reach afar; if those above and those below are not in communion, then emperors and kings have no means to govern All-under-Heaven. Such being the case, how could one who wishes to bring about Great Peace not love learning and take it as the foundation for assisting and supporting the ruler? Even so, one might daily discuss similarities and differences with the various Confucian scholars, with a mind that is by no means unfocused; yet if one mixes in the Way of the Hegemon, one will ultimately become a ruler who lays the foundation for disaster. Having a venerable elder such as Xiao Wangzhi 蕭望之, or a Director of the Imperial Clan (zongzheng 宗正) such as Liu Gengsheng 劉更生 [Liu Xiang 劉向], it could be said that there were capable men at one's side; yet if one is indecisive and irresolute, what help is that to the pure employment of Confucian scholars? From this we know that an enlightened ruler takes devoting himself to learning as his urgent task, and in devoting himself to learning, takes knowing the Way as his priority. If indeed he knows the Way, then how concise and summary are those few words on being "refined and single-minded" (jing yi 精一)! Yet they were sufficient to bring about the flourishing of Fangxun 放勳 [Emperor Yao 堯]. If he does not know the Way, then even the discussions at the White Tiger Hall (Baihu guan 白虎觀) and the Stone Conduit Pavilion (Shiqu ge 石渠閣) merely stir up contentious debate—what aid are they to the ruler's virtue, and what benefit to the Way of governance? This, too, is what one who rules over men ought to know.

Memorial (Biao 表)

Imitation of a Memorial by Sun Shi 孫奭, Academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion (Longtu ge xueshi 龍圖閣學士) of the Song, Presenting the "Illustrated 'Against Luxurious Ease'" (Wuyi tu 無逸圖) [Fifth Year of the Tiansheng 天聖 Era (1027)]

By Zhang Sunnian 張孫念.
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu 教諭) Yan 嚴 comments: The phrasing is dignified and elegant, the intent careful and strict, and a spirit of loyal sincerity overflows beyond the words; it deeply captures the proper form of a minister addressing his sovereign.
Examiner, Instructor Chen 陳 comments: It does not engage in artificial carving, yet its refined craftsmanship is naturally unattainable by others.
Examiner, Instructor Yin 尹 comments: Classical in standard and parallel in phrasing, it is the very image of Song-dynasty models and rules.

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天聖五年某月某日龍圖閣學士臣孫奭
謹以所繪無逸圖上
進者伏以
帝王懷保治之艱道存居敬臣子效匡時之略
志在納忠謹稽古以陳詞用繪圖而進
御上裨
睿覽下竭愚誠臣奭誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊惟
繼體守成當識王業艱難之自深居端拱
宜知小民稼穡之依自昔聖帝明王莫不
===
憂深慮遠迨成王爲有周之令主而姬公
陳無逸之良規謂治民者不敢荒寧以基
業者克自抑畏殷鑒不遠自祖甲而遡及
中宗周命維新由太王而傳及文考備述
前人之迪哲用匡厥后之持盈此元聖保
惠之謨乃萬世君人之鑑顧世多逸豫而
臣鮮憂危獻賦上林徒侈遊田之樂繪屏
長夜益增淫佚之資貞觀寶箴初聞讜論
開元金鑑僅見嘉言未能儆戒于無虞安
punctuated: 天聖五年某月某日，龍圖閣學士臣孫奭謹以所繪《無逸圖》上進者。伏以帝王懷保治之艱，道存居敬；臣子效匡時之略，志在納忠。謹稽古以陳詞，用繪圖而進御，上裨睿覽，下竭愚誠。臣奭誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟繼體守成，當識王業艱難之自；深居端拱，宜知小民稼穡之依。自昔聖帝明王，莫不憂深慮遠。迨成王爲有周之令主，而姬公陳《無逸》之良規，謂治民者不敢荒寧，以基業者克自抑畏。殷鑒不遠，自祖甲而遡及中宗；周命維新，由太王而傳及文考。備述前人之迪哲，用匡厥后之持盈。此元聖保惠之謨，乃萬世君人之鑑。顧世多逸豫，而臣鮮憂危：獻賦上林，徒侈遊田之樂；繪屏長夜，益增淫佚之資。《貞觀寶箴》，初聞讜論；《開元金鑑》，僅見嘉言。未能儆戒于無虞，安…
translation_en:
On a certain day of a certain month in the fifth year of the Tiansheng era [1027], your servant Sun Shi 孫奭, Academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, respectfully presents to the throne the Illustrated "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi tu 無逸圖) that has been painted.

Humbly, I reflect that when emperors and kings cherish the hardships of preserving good governance, the Way lies in dwelling in reverence; when ministers and subjects offer strategies for rectifying the age, their ambition lies in submitting loyal counsel. Respectfully examining antiquity to set forth my words, and thereby painting these illustrations to present to Your Majesty, above I hope to aid your sagely perusal, and below to exhaust my humble sincerity. Your servant Shi, in utmost fear and trepidation, bows his head to the ground again and again.

I venture to reflect that in succeeding to the dynastic line and preserving what has been achieved, one ought to recognize whence the hardships of the royal enterprise arose; dwelling deep in the palace and sitting in stately repose with folded hands, it is fitting to know the toil of sowing and reaping upon which the common people depend. Since antiquity, among sage emperors and enlightened kings, there were none who did not harbor deep concerns and far-reaching thoughts. Coming down to King Cheng 成王, who was a fine ruler of the house of Zhou, the Duke of Zhou (Ji Gong 姬公) set forth the admirable precepts of "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi 無逸), declaring that he who governs the people dares not indulge in idle ease, because those who laid the foundation of the enterprise were able to restrain themselves in awe and reverence. The mirror of the Yin dynasty was not far off, tracing back from Zu Jia 祖甲 to Zhongzong 中宗; the Mandate of Zhou was newly received, transmitted from King Tai 太王 down to the cultured late father, King Wen 文考. He recounted in full the enlightened wisdom of predecessors, so as to assist his sovereign in maintaining fullness without overflowing. This counsel of protective kindness from the Great Sage is indeed a mirror for rulers of men for ten thousand generations.

Yet ages have often inclined toward ease and pleasure, while ministers have rarely felt anxiety over peril: presenting rhapsodies on the Shanglin Park merely magnified the pleasures of excursion and hunting; painting screens for long nights of revelry only increased the means of licentious indulgence. In the Precious Admonitions of the Zhenguan Era (Zhenguan baozhen 貞觀寶箴), one first heard righteous discourse; in the Golden Mirror of the Kaiyuan Era (Kaiyuan jinjian 開元金鑑), one merely saw fine words. If one fails to maintain vigilance and caution when there is no apparent cause for alarm, how…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
望治平之有象欲輸忠悃實待
明時玆蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
仁孝性成
聰明天啓纘
祖宗之統心切時幾握參兩之權功勤日昃財
以不蓄爲富惠徧浹於閭閻兵以不用爲
威恩覃敷于寰宇
經筵
===
御講盛暑猶專
慈幄問安常朝必謹是
聖敬蓋已緝煕于宥密然臣愚毎欲啓沃於論
思伏念臣奭奮跡草茅獨諳田家之味致
身
廊廟誤沾仙仗之香封祀疏陳荷優容于
先帝學田請給蒙嘉納于
聖皇洊列儒紳叨陪近侍遭逢不偶忍謝葵傾
納約有階敢忘芹獻竊計豐亨之治當存
punctuated: 望治平之有象？欲輸忠悃，實待明時。玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，仁孝性成，聰明天啓。纘祖宗之統，心切時幾；握參兩之權，功勤日昃。財以不蓄爲富，惠徧浹於閭閻；兵以不用爲威，恩覃敷于寰宇。經筵御講，盛暑猶專；慈幄問安，常朝必謹。是聖敬蓋已緝煕于宥密，然臣愚毎欲啓沃於論思。伏念臣奭，奮跡草茅，獨諳田家之味；致身廊廟，誤沾仙仗之香。封祀疏陳，荷優容于先帝；學田請給，蒙嘉納于聖皇。洊列儒紳，叨陪近侍，遭逢不偶，忍謝葵傾？納約有階，敢忘芹獻？竊計豐亨之治，當存
translation_en: …hope for signs of peace and good governance? Wishing to pour forth my loyal sincerity, I have truly awaited an enlightened era. Now I humbly encounter Your Majesty [〇〇〇〇], whose benevolence and filial piety are innate by nature, and whose sagacity and intelligence are inspired by Heaven. Continuing the lineage of Your ancestors, Your mind is earnestly attentive to every timely juncture; wielding the authority that participates in the powers of Heaven and Earth, Your labors continue diligently until the sun inclines to the west. Taking the non-hoarding of wealth as true riches, Your beneficence thoroughly saturates the common hamlets; taking the non-use of arms as true majesty, Your grace extends widely throughout the realm. Attending the Classics Colloquium lectures in person, even in the height of summer You remain focused; inquiring after the well-being of the Empress Dowager's apartments, alongside regular court audiences You are unfailingly reverent. Thus Your sagely reverence already shines continuously in serene profundity, yet in my foolishness I ever wish to enlighten and enrich Your deliberations. Humbly I reflect that I, Your servant Shi, rose from rustic obscurity and alone know well the taste of the farming household; having devoted myself to the imperial court, I have undeservedly beenimbued with the fragrance of the immortal retinue. When I submitted a memorial opposing the Feng and Shan sacrifices, I received indulgent tolerance from the late Emperor; when I requested the bestowal of school lands, I was favored with gracious acceptance by Your Sacred Majesty. Repeatedly ranked among the Confucian gentry and undeservedly accompanying the close attendants, having met with such a rare conjunction of fortune, how could I bear to decline the sunflower's inclination toward the sun? Having a stepping-stone to offer counsel through a bond of trust, how would I dare forget the humble offering of wild celery? I privately reckon that in an era of abundance and prosperity, one ought to preserve…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
乾惕之心道已備於周書忠無加於姬旦
敬稽往蹟爰假丹青詳述前聞用加摹寫
上下數百年理亂之故編摩不遺先後六
七君脩短之由形容殆盡為商家為周室
懿範具在目中曰天命曰民情龜鑑可陳
掌上披雲補
袞祗輸一得之忱就日銘盤切冀
九重之矚儻蒙
燕暇時
===
賜監觀主善為師知其繪後于素惟敬作所察
其意不在圖則經史未披揖古人千載之
上堂階不下燭羣情萬里之餘雖不敢上
擬戶牖之銘亦庶幾下同韋弦之助也伏
願
治謹日中
憂先天下
罔于觀罔于逸恒思一日二日之煩
卽康功卽田功不忘匹婦匹夫之勝
punctuated: 乾惕之心。道已備於《周書》，忠無加於姬旦。敬稽往蹟，爰假丹青；詳述前聞，用加摹寫。上下數百年理亂之故，編摩不遺；先後六七君脩短之由，形容殆盡。為商家、為周室，懿範具在目中；曰天命、曰民情，龜鑑可陳掌上。披雲補袞，祗輸一得之忱；就日銘盤，切冀九重之矚。儻蒙燕暇，時賜監觀，主善為師，知其繪後于素；惟敬作所，察其意不在圖。則經史未披，揖古人千載之上；堂階不下，燭羣情萬里之餘。雖不敢上擬戶牖之銘，亦庶幾下同韋弦之助也。伏願治謹日中，憂先天下，罔于觀、罔于逸，恒思一日二日之煩；卽康功、卽田功，不忘匹婦匹夫之勝。
translation_en: … a mind of ceaseless vigilance. The Way is already fully set forth in the Book of Zhou (Zhou shu), and in loyalty none surpasses Ji Dan [the Duke of Zhou]. Respectfully examining past traces, I have therefore borrowed the painter's brush and colors; recounting in detail what was heard of old, I have thereby added pictorial depictions. The causes of order and disorder across several hundred years are compiled without omission; the reasons for the long or short reigns of six or seven successive rulers are portrayed almost exhaustively. Whether of the house of Shang or the royal house of Zhou, their admirable models are all before the eyes; whether termed the Mandate of Heaven or the sentiments of the people, the tortoise-shell and mirror of warning can be laid out upon the palm. Parting the clouds to mend the Imperial robes, I merely offer the sincerity of my single humble insight; approaching the sun to inscribe the washbasin, I earnestly hope for the gaze of the Ninefold Palace. Should I be favored, in Your moments of leisure, with Your timely inspection and contemplation—taking goodness as Your teacher, knowing that the painting comes after the plain silk; making reverence Your dwelling place, perceiving that the meaning lies beyond the pictures—then even before opening the Classics and Histories, You may bow to the ancients across a thousand years; without descending the hall steps, You may illuminate the conditions of the multitude beyond ten thousand li. Though I dare not compare this above to the inscriptions on doors and windows, below it may perhaps serve like the aid of soft leather and taut bowstring. I humbly pray that You will be谨 [vigilant] over governance when the sun is at its zenith, and worry before the rest of the world worries; neither indulging in sight-seeing nor indulging in ease, ever mindful of the myriad affairs of a single day or two; applying Yourself to the work of pacification and to the work of the fields, never forgetting that a common man or common woman may prevail over You…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭尹批事核詞雅非騁言說以為
奇者比宜錄以式
帝王之治天下也不能以一身勞天下而
不能不以其一身風天下其風天下者何
也政治之首務則農桑是也生民之大端
則衣食是也生民一日不得食則饑其饑
也聖人曰我饑之也一日不得衣則寒其
寒也聖人曰我寒之也民以衣食為天聖
人則以民為天民不得其所天聖人之心
===
則有遑遑不能自已者此非不知自逸也
其心誠慮四海之廣九州之衆一有不得
其所不得不以身嘗之也慮其無食也乃
身為之勸以導之耕慮其無衣也乃身為
之勸以導之蠶蓋聖人之所為天必與民
之所以為天者各相足而後已也此親農
親桑所以為風天下之道而我
太祖之開極
列聖之紹基
punctuated:
考試官教諭尹批：事核詞雅，非騁言說以為奇者比，宜錄以式。

帝王之治天下也，不能以一身勞天下，而不能不以其一身風天下。其風天下者何也？政治之首務，則農桑是也；生民之大端，則衣食是也。生民一日不得食則饑，其饑也，聖人曰：「我饑之也。」一日不得衣則寒，其寒也，聖人曰：「我寒之也。」民以衣食為天，聖人則以民為天。民不得其所天，聖人之心則有遑遑不能自已者，此非不知自逸也，其心誠慮四海之廣、九州之衆，一有不得其所，不得不以身嘗之也。慮其無食也，乃身為之勸以導之耕；慮其無衣也，乃身為之勸以導之蠶。蓋聖人之所為天，必與民之所以為天者各相足而後已也。此親農親桑所以為風天下之道，而我太祖之開極、列聖之紹基、
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Yin, Instructor: The facts are verified and the diction is refined; it is not comparable to those who indulge in empty rhetoric for the sake of novelty. It should be recorded as a model.

When emperors and kings govern the realm, they cannot toil for the entire realm in their own person, yet they cannot fail to inspire the realm through their own person. How do they inspire the realm? The foremost task of governance is agriculture and sericulture; the fundamental need of the people is clothing and food. If the people do not get food for a single day, they go hungry; of their hunger, the sage says, "It is I who have starved them." If they do not get clothing for a single day, they go cold; of their cold, the sage says, "It is I who have left them cold." The people regard clothing and food as their Heaven, whereas the sage regards the people as his Heaven. When the people do not obtain what they rely on as Heaven, the sage's heart is anxious and unable to rest. This is not because he does not know how to take his own ease; his heart truly worries that across the breadth of the Four Seas and the multitudes of the Nine Provinces, if even one person fails to find their proper place, he must experience it in his own person. Worrying that they lack food, he personally encourages them in order to lead them in plowing; worrying that they lack clothing, he personally encourages them in order to lead them in sericulture. Indeed, what the sage regards as Heaven and what the people regard as Heaven must each be mutually satisfied before he can rest. This is why personally attending to agriculture and personally attending to sericulture serve as the Way to inspire the realm, and why in our Grand Progenitor's founding of the imperial standard, the Successive Sages' continuation of the foundation, …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇上之御天必有以身勞之而風動四方也執
事策士首及乎此愚生耕而食織而衣者
也遊皞皞之中而誦法先王之道請以成
周之所以致盛治者為執事誦之人孰不
曰帝王以天下之食為食其所食者玉也
以天下之衣為衣其所衣者錦也乃曰必
身親為之耕而與民同食必身親為之蠶
而與民同衣此則許行之所以說神農者
堯舜且不暇為之乃不知聖人不能以一
===
身勞天下而不能不以一身風天下帝王
愛天下甚於愛其身誠不欲以天下食一
人必欲以一人為天下食也不欲以天下
衣一人必欲以一人為天下衣也以一人
為天下食乃天下之所取足以為食以一
人為天下衣乃天下之所取足以為衣吾
讀豳風七月之詩而歎周之君王身親耕
稼以勸天下耕其風天下以足食乎吾讀
葛覃之詩而歎周之后妃身治葛事以勸
punctuated: 皇上之御天，必有以身勞之而風動四方也。執事策士，首及乎此。愚生耕而食、織而衣者也，遊皞皞之中而誦法先王之道，請以成周之所以致盛治者為執事誦之。人孰不曰：「帝王以天下之食為食，其所食者玉也；以天下之衣為衣，其所衣者錦也。乃曰必身親為之耕而與民同食，必身親為之蠶而與民同衣，此則許行之所以說神農者，堯、舜且不暇為之。」乃不知聖人不能以一身勞天下，而不能不以一身風天下。帝王愛天下甚於愛其身，誠不欲以天下食一人，必欲以一人為天下食也；不欲以天下衣一人，必欲以一人為天下衣也。以一人為天下食，乃天下之所取足以為食；以一人為天下衣，乃天下之所取足以為衣。吾讀《豳風·七月》之詩，而歎周之君王身親耕稼以勸天下耕，其風天下以足食乎！吾讀《葛覃》之詩，而歎周之后妃身治葛事以勸
translation_en:
… and His Majesty's reigning over Heaven and Earth, surely involve laboring in person so as to inspire the four quarters like the wind. In putting policy questions to the scholars, Your Excellency has addressed this first of all. I, a humble student, am one who plows to eat and weaves to clothe himself; wandering amid the contented multitude of a harmonious realm and reciting and emulating the Way of the Former Kings, I beg to recite for Your Excellency how the accomplished Zhou dynasty achieved its flourishing governance.

Who among men does not say: "Emperors and kings take the food of the empire as their food—what they eat is like jade; they take the clothing of the empire as their clothing—what they wear is brocade. Yet to say that they must personally plow in order to eat alongside the people, and must personally tend silkworms in order to clothe themselves alongside the people—this is the doctrine of Shennong that Xu Xing許行 preached, something that even Yao and Shun had no leisure to do"? Yet they fail to understand that while a sage cannot labor for the whole empire with his single body, he cannot but inspire the whole empire with his single body. Emperors and kings love the empire more than they love their own persons. Truly, they do not wish to have the whole empire feed one man, but rather wish for one man to provide food for the whole empire; they do not wish to have the whole empire clothe one man, but rather wish for one man to provide clothing for the whole empire. When one man provides food for the whole empire, it is from this that the whole empire draws sufficiency in food; when one man provides clothing for the whole empire, it is from this that the whole empire draws sufficiency in clothing.

When I read the ode "Seventh Month" (Qiyue) in the "Airs of Bin" (Binfeng), I sigh in admiration at how the kings of Zhou personally engaged in plowing and sowing to encourage the empire to plow—was this not inspiring the empire to have sufficient food? When I read the ode "The Spreading Kudzu" (Getan), I sigh in admiration at how the queen and consorts of Zhou personally attended to the work of kudzu-linen to encourage …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
籍田有歌望耕有臺先農有壇東郊有儀
非不侈然具也乃吾獨有取於漢文之親
耕則以其躬儉爲天下先也蠶織有室先
蠶有祠躬蠶有壇養蠶有經非不侈然具
也乃吾獨有取於明德之濯龍則以其躬
儉爲六宮冠也我
太祖起自民間混一寰宇
思天下之無食欲有以食之
思天下之無衣欲有以衣之欲以一身風民
===
以農桑者何不至也洪武巳酉
太祖親耕籍田于南郊
太后親率內外命婦蠶于北郊
曰天子籍田千畝所以供粢盛備饙饎其率
天下以躬耕而導之足食者也
曰民間但有隙地皆令種桑其率天下以躬
蠶而導之足衣者也
諭廷臣則曰衣帛當思織女之勤食粟當念農
夫之苦
punctuated: 籍田有歌，望耕有臺，先農有壇，東郊有儀，非不侈然具也；乃吾獨有取於漢文之親耕，則以其躬儉爲天下先也。蠶織有室，先蠶有祠，躬蠶有壇，養蠶有經，非不侈然具也；乃吾獨有取於明德之濯龍，則以其躬儉爲六宮冠也。我太祖起自民間，混一寰宇，思天下之無食，欲有以食之；思天下之無衣，欲有以衣之；欲以一身風民以農桑者，何不至也！洪武巳酉，太祖親耕籍田于南郊，太后親率內外命婦蠶于北郊。曰：「天子籍田千畝，所以供粢盛，備饙饎。」其率天下以躬耕而導之足食者也。曰：「民間但有隙地，皆令種桑。」其率天下以躬蠶而導之足衣者也。諭廷臣則曰：「衣帛當思織女之勤，食粟當念農夫之苦。」
translation_en:
… There were songs for the imperial sacred field, terraces for viewing the plowing, altars to the First Agriculturist, and ceremonies in the eastern suburbs—these were by no means lacking in grand completeness; yet what I uniquely value is Emperor Wen of Han's personal plowing, because through his personal frugality he set an example for the entire realm. There were chambers for sericulture and weaving, shrines to the First Sericulturist, altars for personal silkworm-tending, and manuals on raising silkworms—these were by no means lacking in grand completeness; yet what I uniquely value is Empress Mingde's silkworm-tending at the Zhuolong Palace, because through her personal frugality she stood at the head of the Six Palaces.

Our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) rose from among the common people and unified the realm. Mindful that the people of the world lacked food, he wished to have the means to feed them; mindful that the people of the world lacked clothing, he wished to have the means to clothe them. In desiring to use his own person to inspire the people in agriculture and sericulture, to what lengths did he not go! In the jiyou year of the Hongwu reign (1369), the Grand Progenitor personally plowed the sacred field in the southern suburbs, and the Empress Dowager personally led the titled ladies of the inner court and outer officials in tending silkworms in the northern suburbs. He said: "The Son of Heaven's sacred field of a thousand mou is meant to supply the sacrificial millet and prepare the steamed grain offerings." In this way he led the world by personally plowing and guided it toward sufficiency in food. He said: "Wherever there is spare land among the people, order them all to plant mulberry trees." In this way he led the world by personal sericulture and guided it toward sufficiency in clothing. In instructing his court officials, he said: "When wearing silk, one should think of the diligence of the weaving woman; when eating grain, one should remember the hardship of the farmer." …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諭司農卿則曰自什一之制湮奇巧之技作而
後農桑之業廢其拳拳於天下作其勤起其
惰者也仍於
內苑置籍田蠶室以時觀省我
太祖所以垂範作則於前何一時一念不以此
二者以身勞之而風天下耶
列聖以來以
太祖之心爲心以
太祖之政爲政
===
成祖務本之訓因
仁宗巡道途而作也而天下之耕者勸
宣宗織婦之賦因見田間織婦而作也而天下
之蠶者勸
世宗更翼善冠
親耕臺下籍田
皇后親祀先蠶詣採桑臺乃
豳風無逸之詩
穀祗蠶壇之賦
punctuated: 諭司農卿則曰：「自什一之制湮，奇巧之技作，而後農桑之業廢。」其拳拳於天下，作其勤、起其惰者也。仍於內苑置籍田、蠶室，以時觀省。我太祖所以垂範作則於前，何一時一念不以此二者以身勞之，而風天下耶？列聖以來，以太祖之心爲心，以太祖之政爲政。成祖《務本之訓》，因仁宗巡道途而作也，而天下之耕者勸；宣宗《織婦之賦》，因見田間織婦而作也，而天下之蠶者勸。世宗更翼善冠，親耕臺下籍田，皇后親祀先蠶，詣採桑臺，乃《豳風》、《無逸》之詩，《穀祗》、《蠶壇》之賦，
translation_en:
… Instructing the Chief Minister of Agriculture (Sinong qing), he said: "Once the system of taxing one-tenth was lost and ingenious, extravagant crafts arose, thereafter the occupations of farming and sericulture fell into neglect." Thus was his earnest devotion to the realm, rousing its diligence and shaking off its indolence. Furthermore, he established the sacred field (jitian) and silkworm house within the Inner Park to observe and inspect them in season. In the way our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) handed down a model and set the standard in earlier times, was there ever a single moment or a single thought in which he did not personally toil at these two tasks so as to inspire the realm by example?

Throughout the reigns of the Successive Sages, they have taken the mind of the Grand Progenitor as their mind, and the governance of the Grand Progenitor as their governance. The Ancestral Founder's (Chengzu) Instructions on Attending to the Fundamental (Wuben zhi xun) was composed on the occasion of the Benevolent Ancestor (Renzong) inspecting the roads on tour, and thereby the tillers of the realm were encouraged; the Proclaiming Ancestor's (Xuanzong) Rhapsody on the Weaving Woman (Zhifu zhi fu) was composed upon seeing a weaving woman amid the fields, and thereby the sericulturists of the realm were encouraged. The Epochal Ancestor (Shizong) changed the design of the Yishan crown and personally plowed the sacred field below the terrace, while the Empress personally sacrificed to the First Sericulturist (Xiancan) and proceeded to the Mulberry-Picking Terrace (Caisang tai); and as for the poems on the "Airs of Bin" (Binfeng) and "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi), and the rhapsodies on the Spirit of Grain (Guzhi) and the Silkworm Altar (Cantan), …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
宸章燦爛不一而足我
列聖所以繼美承芳於後何一時一念不以此
二者以身先之而風天下耶肆我
皇上
冲年御宇四海向風雨暘愆期則
徹樂減膳露禱
宮中其祈農者何勤也淮徐水災則
遣官發賑蠲免公租其恤民者何急也東南
織造半減前額積逋絲絹竝從
===
除免何懇懇念民農桑之苦也以衣三澣以
事再思
親灑
宸翰以相警省何肔肔敦尚躬儉之風也邇者
特俞廷臣之請將舉籍禮未幾下
明旨期舉于來年則
親耕以風天下耕
親蠶以風天下桑所以供粢盛供祭服以輸
皇上之仁孝者四海將快覩之是孰非
punctuated: 宸章燦爛，不一而足。我列聖所以繼美承芳於後，何一時一念不以此二者以身先之而風天下耶？肆我皇上冲年御宇，四海向風。雨暘愆期，則徹樂減膳，露禱宮中，其祈農者何勤也！淮、徐水災，則遣官發賑，蠲免公租，其恤民者何急也！東南織造半減前額，積逋絲絹竝從除免，何懇懇念民農桑之苦也！以「衣三澣」、以「事再思」，親灑宸翰以相警省，何肔肔敦尚躬儉之風也！邇者特俞廷臣之請，將舉籍禮，未幾下明旨，期舉于來年。則親耕以風天下耕，親蠶以風天下桑，所以供粢盛、供祭服，以輸皇上之仁孝者，四海將快覩之。是孰非
translation_en:
… imperial compositions shone brilliantly, too numerous to recount in full. In the way our Successive Sacred Emperors inherited these fine models and carried forward their fragrant legacy in later times, when was there ever a single moment or a single thought in which they did not take the lead in person with these two tasks [agriculture and sericulture] so as to transform the realm by example?

Now our Majesty ascended the throne in his youth, and all within the Four Seas turn toward his transforming influence. When rain and sunshine fail to come in season, he suspends music, reduces his palace meals, and prays in the open air within the palace precincts—how diligent he is in praying for husbandry! When floods strike Huai and Xu, he dispatches officials to distribute relief and remits public land taxes—how urgent he is in showing compassion for the people! In the weaving establishments of the Southeast, he cuts the former quotas in half, and accumulated arrears of silk and taffeta are all alike remitted—how earnestly he bears in mind the people's hardships in farming and sericulture! With the maxims "wash garments thrice" and "think twice over affairs," he personally wields the imperial brush to admonish and encourage self-examination—how earnestly [?] he esteems the custom of personal frugality!

Recently he specially approved the request of his court ministers and was about to perform the ceremony of plowing the imperial sacred field; before long he handed down an explicit edict scheduling its performance for the coming year. Thus, plowing in person to inspire the realm to plow, and tending silkworms in person to inspire the realm to cultivate mulberry—thereby supplying the sacrificial millet and sacrificial vestments to express His Majesty's benevolence and filial piety—all within the Four Seas will soon rejoice to witness this. Which of these is not …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以淫巧相尚者何以禁也織造之有加而
東南之無以辦也何以節也兢乎其兢愼
乎其愼後無改于其前終無變于其始堯
舜端拱垂衣之化不在唐虞而在
今日此則葵藿書生所望於
聖天子者也
第二問
文立本
同考試官敎諭嚴批是作以
===
皇上考成為體天不息末復以
勤學為言是抱忠愛之誠者錄之
考試官敎諭陳批發明
皇上考成之意有關治體之大最為眞切可嘉
考試官敎諭尹批議論剴切格調古雅是通
達國體而有得者取之
天之所以為天者何也曰健也健者不息
也人君者奉天之不息以子民也人臣者
奉君之不息以共職也天唯不息故風雨
punctuated:
以淫巧相尚者，何以禁也？織造之有加，而東南之無以辦也，何以節也？兢乎其兢，愼乎其愼，後無改于其前，終無變于其始，堯、舜端拱垂衣之化，不在唐、虞而在今日，此則葵藿書生所望於聖天子者也。

第二問
文立本
同考試官敎諭嚴批：是作以皇上考成為體天不息，末復以勤學為言，是抱忠愛之誠者，錄之。
考試官敎諭陳批：發明皇上考成之意，有關治體之大，最為眞切可嘉。
考試官敎諭尹批：議論剴切，格調古雅，是通達國體而有得者，取之。

天之所以為天者何也？曰：健也。健者，不息也。人君者，奉天之不息以子民也；人臣者，奉君之不息以共職也。天唯不息，故風雨
translation_en:
…who vie with one another in extravagant and ingenious craftsmanship—how are they to be prohibited? As for the increases in imperial textile manufacturing that the southeast has no means to supply—how are they to be moderated? Being ever so cautious and ever so prudent, not altering later what was done before, nor changing at the end what was set at the beginning, the transformative rule of Yao and Shun sitting in composed dignity with robes hanging down will lie not in the eras of Tang and Yu, but in the present day. This is what a humble scholar, turning like the mallow and bean-leaf toward the sun, hopes for from the Sacred Son of Heaven.

Second Question
Wen Liben
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Yan comments: This essay takes His Majesty's verification of official performance (kaocheng) as embodying Heaven's ceaselessness, and at the end speaks further of diligent study. He is one who harbors the sincerity of loyalty and devotion; record it.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Chen comments: He elucidates the meaning of His Majesty's verification of official performance as it relates to the great essentials of governance; it is most genuine, incisive, and commendable.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Yin comments: The argument is trenchant and to the point, and the style is antique and elegant. He is one who thoroughly understands the essentials of statecraft and has attained true insight; select it.

What is it whereby Heaven is Heaven? It is said: vigor. To be vigorous is to be ceaseless. The ruler of men upholds the ceaselessness of Heaven in order to treat the people as his children; the ministers of men uphold the ceaselessness of the ruler in order to discharge their offices. Only because Heaven is ceaseless do wind and rain…

同考試官教諭嚴批是作以
===

勤學為言是抱忠愛之誠者錄之

皇上考成之意有關治體之大最為眞切可嘉

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
未甞不置書歎也曰旴者其所以致悔乎
裕者其所以成蠱乎至大有曰遏惡揚善
順天休命至乾曰終日乾乾夕惕若又悚
然懼躍然省也曰揚善遏惡者其君之所
以順天命保大有者乎曰乾乾惕若者其
臣之所以懷憂勤履危疑者乎爲人君者
一日二日有萬幾凛乎若朽索之馭六馬
則安得當六馬之逸而惟其索之朽是何
以齊萬幾爲人臣者進思盡忠退思補過
===
夙夜以事一人則安得進無所思退無所
補是何以事一人然後知發强剛毅明君
所以宰制六合而怠緩悅從且無以理一
身何以理天下爲也千古而上稱極治者
則孰過唐虞哉其所有五臣以相都俞吁
咈也何事詢何事省也乃堯之命舜曰詢
事考言乃言底可績其於臯陶曰屢省乃
成是其所詢者所省者卽所謂禹臯稷契
益之人也卽所謂平水土播百穀敷五敎
punctuated: 未甞不置書歎也，曰：「旴者，其所以致悔乎？裕者，其所以成蠱乎？」至《大有》曰：「遏惡揚善，順天休命。」至《乾》曰：「終日乾乾，夕惕若。」又悚然懼、躍然省也，曰：「揚善遏惡者，其君之所以順天命、保大有者乎！」曰：「乾乾惕若者，其臣之所以懷憂勤、履危疑者乎！」爲人君者，一日二日有萬幾，凛乎若朽索之馭六馬；則安得當六馬之逸，而惟其索之朽？是何以齊萬幾？爲人臣者，進思盡忠，退思補過，夙夜以事一人；則安得進無所思、退無所補？是何以事一人？然後知發强剛毅，明君所以宰制六合；而怠緩悅從，且無以理一身，何以理天下爲也？千古而上，稱極治者則孰過唐、虞哉？其所有五臣，以相都俞吁咈也，何事詢、何事省也？乃堯之命舜曰：「詢事考言，乃言底可績。」其於臯陶曰：「屢省乃成。」是其所詢者、所省者，卽所謂禹、臯、稷、契、益之人也，卽所謂平水土、播百穀、敷五敎、
translation_en: … I have never failed to set down the book and sigh, saying: "Is not gazing upwards in complacency that by which one brings on regret? Is not indulgent寬緩 (yu) tolerance that by which one allows decay to take form?" Coming to the hexagram Great Possession (Dayou), it says: "repressing evil and promoting good, thereby complying with the beneficent mandate of Heaven." Coming to the hexagram the Creative (Qian), it says: "All day long active and vigilant, and at evening still careful and apprehensive." Then again I am struck with awe and moved to keen reflection, saying: "Promoting good and repressing evil—is this not how a ruler complies with the Mandate of Heaven and preserves great possession?" And saying: "Being active, vigilant, and apprehensive—is this not how a minister harbors anxious diligence and treads through peril and doubt?" For one who is a ruler of men, in a single day or two there are ten thousandoli of state affairs, trembling as if driving six horses with rotten reins. How then could one face the bolting of the six horses while leaving the reins rotten? By what means could one then bring order to the myriad affairs? For one who is a minister to men, when advancing at court he thinks of exhausting his loyalty, and when retiring he thinks of repairing his faults, serving the One Man from dawn to night. How then could he advance without thought and retire without making amends? By what means could he then serve the One Man? Only after this does one know that vigorous strength and firm resolve are the means by which an enlightened ruler governs the six directions of the realm, whereas sluggish laxity and compliant flattery are insufficient even to govern one's own person—how then could they be used to govern the empire? Looking back over remote antiquity, among those praised for the pinnacle of good governance, who surpassed Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun]? They possessed five ministers with whom they exchanged expressions of agreement and admonition ("alas," "yes," "oh," "no")—what need was there for inquiry, and what need for inspection? Yet when Yao charged Shun, he said: "Inquire into affairs and examine words, and your words have been capable of yielding meritorious results." And regarding Gao Yao, it was said: "Frequently examine into achievements." Thus, those whom they inquired of and those whom they examined were none other than such men as Yu, Gao Yao, Hou Ji, Xie, and Boyi; and the affairs were none other than leveling the waters and land, sowing the hundred grains, spreading the five teachings, …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
明五刑共工朕虞之事也而帝之必詢之
必考之也乃四方之所以風動萬邦之所
以協和也唐虞而下稱極治者則孰過成
周哉其所有十臣以相疏附後先也則何
事計何事考也而春秋所紀王公卿士自
朝日至日入無不自計乃職者周禮所載
歲時月日無不有考者是其所計者所考
者則所謂周公旦召公奭散宜生南宮之
人也卽所謂勤王家脩有夏田功康功之
===
事也而周之必計之必考之也乃萬邦之
所以咸和四海之所以永清也吾於西漢
得一君焉曰宣帝是也則綜覈名實以為
治也吾於東漢得一君焉光武是也則總
攬威權以為治也吾於唐得一君焉德宗
是也則强明果斷更條格以為法也說者
謂漢業衰於宣帝察察之過也夫漢宣當
霍氏後乾剛倒持非綜覈無以起敝乃不
咎孝元之優柔而罪宣帝之明察耶說者
punctuated:
明五刑、共工、朕虞之事也。而帝之必詢之、必考之也，乃四方之所以風動、萬邦之所以協和也。唐虞而下，稱極治者，則孰過成周哉？其所有十臣，以相疏附後先也，則何事計、何事考也？而《春秋》所紀，王公卿士自朝日至日入，無不自計乃職者；《周禮》所載，歲時月日，無不有考者。是其所計者、所考者，則所謂周公旦、召公奭、散宜生、南宮之人也，卽所謂勤王家、脩有夏、田功、康功之事也。而周之必計之、必考之也，乃萬邦之所以咸和、四海之所以永清也。

吾於西漢得一君焉，曰宣帝是也，則綜覈名實以為治也；吾於東漢得一君焉，光武是也，則總攬威權以為治也；吾於唐得一君焉，德宗是也，則强明果斷、更條格以為法也。說者謂漢業衰於宣帝，察察之過也。夫漢宣當霍氏後，乾剛倒持，非綜覈無以起敝，乃不咎孝元之優柔，而罪宣帝之明察耶？說者
translation_en:
… clarifying the Five Punishments, and the duties of the Minister of Works and the Forester. That the Emperor invariably consulted them and invariably evaluated them is the very reason why the four quarters were moved as if by the wind and the myriad states were brought into harmony. After Tang and Yu [Yao and Shun], among those praised for the pinnacle of good governance, who surpassed the accomplished Zhou? They possessed ten ministers who assisted by drawing the distant near and by going before and following after—what need was there to reckon, what need was there to evaluate? Yet as recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), from daybreak until sunset, kings, dukes, high ministers, and noblemen without exception reckoned their own official duties; and as set down in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), by year, season, month, and day, none went without evaluation. Thus, those whom they reckoned and evaluated were none other than such men as Dan, the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong Dan 周公旦); Shi, the Duke of Shao (Shaogong Shi 召公奭); San Yisheng 散宜生; and Nangong 南宮 [Nangong Kuo]; and what was reckoned and evaluated was none other than laboring for the royal house, cultivating the ways of the lords of Xia, and the achievements in agriculture and in pacification. That the Zhou invariably reckoned them and invariably evaluated them is the very reason why the myriad states were all brought into harmony and the Four Seas were forever pacified.

In the Western Han I find one ruler, namely Emperor Xuan (Xuandi 宣帝), who governed by comprehensively verifying that names matched realities. In the Eastern Han I find one ruler, namely Guangwu 光武, who governed by gathering all authority and power into his own hands. In the Tang I find one ruler, namely Dezong 德宗, who established laws by being forceful, discerning, and resolute, and by altering regulations and ordinances. Commentators claim that the fortune of the Han declined under Emperor Xuan due to the fault of excessive scrutiny. Yet Emperor Xuan of the Han came after the Huo 霍 clan, when sovereign authority had been held upside down; without comprehensive verification there was no way to remedy the decay. How then can one not blame the indecisive softness of Emperor Yuan (Xiaoyuan 孝元), and instead fault the clear scrutiny of Emperor Xuan? Commentators…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
謂治體失于光武攬權之過也夫光武當
新莽後王綱解紐非總攬無以維風乃不
知光武之得而謂光武之失耶獨德宗剛
褊自用苛察爲明其所明者非所明而明
也其所察者非所察而察也此尚不足與
孝宣光武言而可語治天下之大道哉我
太祖肇造區夏設官分職我
列聖獨秉威權賞勤罰惰開濟作考功圖令所
司日記行事較勤惰
===
高皇帝賜第以旌其賢此非我
祖宗立考成之勸者哉顧佐糾不職三十人
章皇帝卽時罷斥賜
璽書褒美此非我
祖宗立考成之罰者哉薄海内外無不奉宣
德意遵行勿怠二百年來紀綱整肅法度脩明
則
太祖奉此不息者以立極於先
列聖奉此不息者以承美於後故有以駕唐虞
punctuated: 謂治體失于光武攬權之過也。夫光武當新莽後，王綱解紐，非總攬無以維風，乃不知光武之得，而謂光武之失耶？獨德宗剛褊自用，苛察爲明，其所明者，非所明而明也；其所察者，非所察而察也。此尚不足與孝宣、光武言，而可語治天下之大道哉？我太祖肇造區夏，設官分職；我列聖獨秉威權，賞勤罰惰。開濟作《考功圖》，令所司日記行事，較勤惰，高皇帝賜第以旌其賢，此非我祖宗立考成之勸者哉？顧佐糾不職三十人，章皇帝卽時罷斥，賜璽書褒美，此非我祖宗立考成之罰者哉？薄海内外，無不奉宣德意，遵行勿怠。二百年來，紀綱整肅，法度脩明，則太祖奉此不息者以立極於先，列聖奉此不息者以承美於後，故有以駕唐、虞，
translation_en:
… say that the substance of governance was lost under Emperor Guangwu (Guangwu 光武) through the fault of his monopolizing authority. Yet Emperor Guangwu came after Wang Mang's (Xin Mang 新莽) usurpation, when the royal cords of order had come undone; without concentrating power in his own hands, there would have been no way to uphold public morals. How then can one fail to recognize Emperor Guangwu's success and instead call it Emperor Guangwu's failure? Only Emperor Dezong (Dezong 德宗) was rigid, narrow-minded, and self-willed, taking petty scrutiny for discernment. What he was discerning about was not what ought to be discerned; what he scrutinized was not what ought to be scrutinized. He is not even worthy of being mentioned alongside Emperors Xiaoxuan (孝宣) and Guangwu—how could one speak with him of the great Way of governing the empire?

Our Grand Progenitor (Taizu 太祖) founded and ordered the Chinese realm, establishing offices and apportioning duties; our successive Sacred Emperors alone wielded august authority, rewarding diligence and punishing indolence. Kai Ji (開濟) drew up the Chart for Evaluating Merit (Kaogong tu 考功圖), ordering the competent authorities to record daily affairs and compare diligence and indolence; the Lofty Emperor (Gaohuangdi 高皇帝) bestowed a residence upon him to honor his worthiness. Was this not how our Imperial Ancestors established encouragement in the evaluation of performance? Gu Zuo (顧佐) impeached thirty delinquent officials; the Brilliant Emperor (Zhanghuangdi 章皇帝) immediately dismissed them and bestowed an imperial letter under the dynastic seal praising him. Was this not how our Imperial Ancestors established punishment in the evaluation of performance? Within and beyond the cuatro seas, none failed to uphold and proclaim the virtuous intentions of the throne, complying with and executing them without laxity. For two hundred years, discipline and order have been taut and solemn, and laws and regulations well-ordered and clear. Thus the Grand Progenitor upheld this unceasingly to establish the supreme standard beforehand, and the successive Sacred Emperors upheld this unceasingly to carry on its excellence afterward; therefore they have been able to surpass Tang (唐) and Yu (虞) …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
軼周室邁漢唐也邇年狃於治安樂於簡
便
章程顯布而奉行則稍習於媮安
約束嚴明而遵守則稍流於怠慢貪墨酷鷙
有定論也乃遲留不發則何所懲惡也功
賞虛冒有明徵也乃稽遲不上則何所懲
欺也錢穀額賦徵解有期也乃會計徒具
而輸輓後時何以充國計也刑獄擬議輕
重有律也乃停閣逾年而寃抑不白何以
===
重民命也條陳利病詳勘已定也乃徒取
文具而不亟下何以補民生也中外習以
爲常莫知其非此非所以脩臣職也此非
所以仰體
皇上奉
天不息以出治之心也
皇上俞輔臣之請下稽查之令沉章積牘起弊
維風按時之先後以定其限隨事之緩急
以考其成
punctuated: 軼周室、邁漢唐也。邇年狃於治安，樂於簡便。章程顯布，而奉行則稍習於媮安；約束嚴明，而遵守則稍流於怠慢。貪墨酷鷙有定論也，乃遲留不發，則何所懲惡也？功賞虛冒有明徵也，乃稽遲不上，則何所懲欺也？錢穀額賦徵解有期也，乃會計徒具而輸輓後時，何以充國計也？刑獄擬議輕重有律也，乃停閣逾年而寃抑不白，何以重民命也？條陳利病詳勘已定也，乃徒取文具而不亟下，何以補民生也？中外習以爲常，莫知其非。此非所以脩臣職也，此非所以仰體皇上奉天不息以出治之心也。皇上俞輔臣之請，下稽查之令，沉章積牘，起弊維風，按時之先後以定其限，隨事之緩急以考其成。
translation_en: … surpass the house of Zhou, and outstrip the Han and Tang. In recent years, however, officials have grown accustomed to peace and security and taken pleasure in convenience and ease. Regulations and statutes are clearly promulgated, yet in carrying them out they have gradually grown habituated to indolent comfort; restraints and rules are strict and explicit, yet in observing them they have gradually slipped into negligence. Corrupt and cruel officials have already been conclusively identified, yet action against them is delayed and left uninitiated—how then is evil to be punished? False and fraudulent claims to merit and reward have clear proof, yet reports on them are held back and not submitted—how then is deceit to be deterred? There are fixed deadlines for collecting and forwarding the quotas of grain and money taxes, yet accounting records are merely drawn up as a formality while transport and delivery fall behind schedule—how is the state's fiscal plan to be fulfilled? There are statutes governing the deliberation of light or heavy sentences in criminal cases, yet cases are shelved for over a year and grievances go unredressed—how is the life of the people to be valued? Itemized proposals on administrative benefits and abuses have been thoroughly investigated and settled, yet they are treated as mere paperwork and not promptly handed down for implementation—how is the livelihood of the people to be aided? Officials at court and in the provinces have grown accustomed to this as the norm, none recognizing that it is wrong. This is no way to fulfill the duties of a minister; this is no way to respectfully embody His Majesty's mind, which patterns itself on Heaven's unceasing activity in bringing forth governance. His Majesty approved the request of the Grand Secretaries and issued the order for auditing and inspection—clearing away submerged memorials and accumulated documents, remedying abuses and upholding the administrative ethos, fixing deadlines according to chronological sequence, and evaluating accomplishments according to the urgency of the affair. …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
內閣則總其綱也部院則分其事也臺省則
核其實也下之監司下之郡縣出之
九重之上達之萬里之遠若雷之震之也若風
之披之也此則以唐虞之所詢所省者詢
之省之也何過於明此則以成周之所計
所考者計之考之也何過于察內外臣工
罔不洗滌積玩夙夜秉公奉
詔書者惕惕然若
天語之臨也入
===
聖覽者兢兢然若
天顏之涖也論報嚴明故貪墨酷鷙無所匿也
報勘真實故功賞虛冒無所售也輸納有
限故錢穀額賦無後時也問理有條故刑
獄冤抑無覆盆也條別有章遵行不失故
利民生者無不舉也此則
皇上奉
天之不息以出治而內外臣工罔不若也羣臣
體
punctuated: 內閣則總其綱也，部院則分其事也，臺省則核其實也。下之監司，下之郡縣，出之九重之上，達之萬里之遠，若雷之震之也，若風之披之也。此則以唐、虞之所詢所省者詢之省之也，何過於明？此則以成周之所計所考者計之考之也，何過于察？內外臣工罔不洗滌積玩，夙夜秉公。奉詔書者惕惕然若天語之臨也，入聖覽者兢兢然若天顏之涖也。論報嚴明，故貪墨酷鷙無所匿也；報勘真實，故功賞虛冒無所售也；輸納有限，故錢穀額賦無後時也；問理有條，故刑獄冤抑無覆盆也；條別有章，遵行不失，故利民生者無不舉也。此則皇上奉天之不息以出治，而內外臣工罔不若也；羣臣體
translation_en: The Grand Secretariat oversees the general principles; the Ministries and the Censorate divide up the specific affairs; and the Censors and Supervising Secretaries verify their actual results. Sent down to the provincial surveillance and fiscal commissioners, and down to the prefectures and counties, issuing from above the ninefold gates of the palace and reaching ten thousand li into the distance, it is like thunder shaking them, like wind sweeping over them. This is making inquiries and inspections by means of what Tang and Yu inquired into and inspected—how could that be excessively clear-sighted? This is conducting evaluations and assessments by means of what the flourishing Zhou evaluated and assessed—how could that be overly scrutinizing? Officials inside and outside the capital all without exception cleanse away their accumulated laxity, upholding public-mindedness day and night. Those who receive imperial edicts are filled with awe, as though the words of Heaven had descended upon them; what enters for His Majesty's perusal is prepared with trembling caution, as though in the immediate presence of the Heavenly countenance. Evaluations and reports are strict and clear, so corrupt and ruthless officials have nowhere to hide; reports of investigations are truthful and accurate, so false and fraudulent claims for merit and reward cannot be peddled; tax deliveries have set deadlines, so the quota of money and grain taxes is never behind schedule; interrogations and trials follow proper procedures, so in criminal cases and litigation there are no unredressed wrongs hidden beneath an overturned basin; and itemized regulations are systematic and observed without fail, so everything that benefits the people's livelihood is carried out. Thus Your Majesty patterns Yourself on the ceaselessness of Heaven in bringing forth governance, and officials at court and in the provinces all conform to it; the assembled officials embody…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天之不息以從
上而乆遠章奏無不理也此以有爲爲無爲以
有事爲無事之道也雖然是不息也存之
爲內聖之心非勤學不足純此心也發之
爲外王之業非勤政不足弘此業也我
皇上日
御經筵講論不輟其所以爲
聖學者何勤也日
御朝宁寒暑不輟其所以爲
===
聖政者何勤也草莽之士則以爲勤學者其本
也勤政者其用也今天下華夷一統海宇
晏然稱極治矣此心少有所息則聲色貨
利得撓其眞也左右近習得抵其間也土
木遊佚得投其隙也非所以語純心也勤
學也誠願
皇上之愼之也
養之於不覩不聞之中
察之於莫見莫顯之際無怠朝也無怠夕也
punctuated: 天之不息以從上，而乆遠章奏無不理也。此以有爲爲無爲，以有事爲無事之道也。雖然，是不息也，存之爲內聖之心，非勤學不足純此心也；發之爲外王之業，非勤政不足弘此業也。我皇上日御經筵，講論不輟，其所以爲聖學者何勤也！日御朝宁，寒暑不輟，其所以爲聖政者何勤也！草莽之士，則以爲勤學者其本也，勤政者其用也。今天下華夷一統，海宇晏然，稱極治矣。此心少有所息，則聲色貨利得撓其眞也，左右近習得抵其間也，土木遊佚得投其隙也，非所以語純心也，勤學也。誠願皇上之愼之也，養之於不覩不聞之中，察之於莫見莫顯之際，無怠朝也，無怠夕也，
translation_en: … the unceasingness of Heaven in following His Majesty, so that even long-pending memorials are all attended to. This is the Way of taking action as non-action, and taking engagement in affairs as having no affairs. Even so, as for this unceasingness: preserved within, it is the mind of inner sageliness, and without diligent study one cannot purify this mind; manifested without, it is the enterprise of outer kingliness, and without diligent governance one cannot broaden this enterprise. Our Emperor daily attends the Classics Colloquium, lecturing and discussing without pause—how diligent He is in pursuing sagely learning! Daily He holds court in the audience hall, without pause through winter's cold and summer's heat—how diligent He is in conducting sagely governance! Yet a rustic scholar such as I considers that diligent study is the root, while diligent governance is its application. Today, Chinese and non-Chinese across the realm are united under one rule, and the world within the four seas is tranquil; it may be called the pinnacle of order. Yet if this mind slackens even slightly, then sensual pleasures, wealth, and profit will be able to disturb its genuineness; close attendants and favorites will be able to exploit its openings; and construction projects and idle excursions will be able to slip into its crevices. This is not what can be called purifying the mind or diligent study. I truly wish that His Majesty would be cautious in this: nurturing it amidst what is neither seen nor heard, examining it at the juncture where nothing is more visible or more manifest, without laxity in the morning and without laxity in the evening, …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
內外相孚始終無間將五帝不足帝三王
不足王也故曰天之所以爲天者何也曰
健也健者不息也天行健君子以自强不
息有味哉其言之也
第三問
劉延祚
同考試官教諭呂批邇來文武吏鮮實效以求
名多也子能爲覈實之論而筆力雄勁宜冠本房
考試官教諭陳批粵西需二者最亟子能劑
===
量不爽而敘論謹嚴宜錄以式
考試官教諭尹批課嚴名實法兼內外於大
計有裨錄之非徒尚其文也
天下有法內之材有法外之材法內之材
中材也待之法內而人知所勉法外之材
豪傑也待之法外而人競于勸何也豪傑
之士其志卓然所存遠也其猷廓然所施
弘也其氣浩然所挾持確而正也彼其身
視赤子家視郡縣疆場弗安且寧奮其三
punctuated:
內外相孚，始終無間，將五帝不足帝，三王不足王也。故曰：「天之所以爲天者何也？曰健也。」健者，不息也。「天行健，君子以自强不息」，有味哉其言之也！

第三問
劉延祚
同考試官教諭呂批：邇來文武吏鮮實效，以求名多也。子能爲覈實之論，而筆力雄勁，宜冠本房。
考試官教諭陳批：粵西需二者最亟，子能劑量不爽，而敘論謹嚴，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭尹批：課嚴名實，法兼內外，於大計有裨。錄之，非徒尚其文也。

天下有法內之材，有法外之材。法內之材，中材也，待之法內而人知所勉；法外之材，豪傑也，待之法外而人競于勸。何也？豪傑之士，其志卓然，所存遠也；其猷廓然，所施弘也；其氣浩然，所挾持確而正也。彼其身視赤子，家視郡縣，疆場弗安且寧，奮其三
translation_en:
…so that the inner and outer accord with one another and beginning and end are without interruption, then the Five Emperors will scarcely suffice to be called emperors, and the Three Kings will scarcely suffice to be called kings. Thus it is said: "What is it whereby Heaven is Heaven? It is vigor." Vigor means ceaselessness. "Heaven's movement is vigorous; the gentleman accordingly strengthens himself without ceasing"—how full of meaning are these words!

Third Question
Liu Yanzuo 劉延祚
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Lü: Lately civil and military officials have rarely achieved real results, because so many seek only reputation. You are able to advance an argument that verifies actualities, and the vigor of your brush is bold and strong; it deserves to top this ward.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Chen: Western Yue [Guangxi] needs both of these things most urgently. You are able to weigh and measure them without error, and your exposition and argument are rigorous and disciplined; this should be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yin: Its evaluation strictly distinguishes name and reality, and its methods encompass both inside and outside the rules, which is beneficial to great state plans. We record it not merely out of esteem for its literary style.

In the world there are talents within the rules, and there are talents beyond the rules. Talents within the rules are mediocre talents; treat them within the rules, and people know what to strive for. Talents beyond the rules are heroic men; treat them beyond the rules, and people vie to be encouraged. Why is this? Men of heroic stature have lofty aspirations, for what they harbor is far-reaching; their plans are expansive, for what they put into practice is grand; their vital spirit is vast, for what they hold fast to is firm and upright. They regard the infant-like common people as their own person and the commanderies and counties as their own family; when the frontiers are neither peaceful nor secure, they rouse these three…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者而爲之所非以上之法也而上之人不
以法外待之卽彼不爲沮亦豈所以鼓豪
傑而風天下乎若夫中材則異是矣各有
所用亦各有所偏明敏者戒於太察温良
者戒於無斷湛靜者戒於後時不齊之以
法察而不已則苛急矣斷而不足則庸懦
矣時而太後則事機僨矣故法者所以救
其偏而全其用胡可廢也以法之內外視
天下材而爲之待此帝王所以臨制海內
===
陶冶人羣之至術也執事以粵西文武吏
士策諸生計安邊方甚厚請撫所聞以對
自昔選吏任將若岳牧之命渭濱之載尚
矣在漢則神爵五鳳間郡國有治理效天
子爲下璽書勞問且不次徵入爲公卿此
其最著乃遣將之儀猶有古人推轂之風
一時揚旌之士皆能爲國家信威邊境蓋
漢世得人烝烝盛矣粵西固先秦所拓地
也稱藩則自漢始經略旣久稍視中州考
punctuated:
者而爲之所，非以上之法也。而上之人不以法外待之，卽彼不爲沮，亦豈所以鼓豪傑而風天下乎？若夫中材則異是矣：各有所用，亦各有所偏。明敏者戒於太察，温良者戒於無斷，湛靜者戒於後時。不齊之以法，察而不已，則苛急矣；斷而不足，則庸懦矣；時而太後，則事機僨矣。故法者，所以救其偏而全其用，胡可廢也？以法之內外，視天下材而爲之待，此帝王所以臨制海內、陶冶人羣之至術也。

執事以粵西文武吏士策諸生，計安邊方甚厚，請撫所聞以對。自昔選吏任將，若岳牧之命、渭濱之載，尚矣。在漢，則神爵、五鳳間，郡國有治理效，天子爲下璽書勞問，且不次徵入爲公卿，此其最著；乃遣將之儀，猶有古人推轂之風，一時揚旌之士，皆能爲國家信威邊境。蓋漢世得人，烝烝盛矣。粵西固先秦所拓地也，稱藩則自漢始。經略旣久，稍視中州。考
translation_en:
… [exert these three] qualities and provide for their needs—this is not because of the ruler's regulations. And if those above do not treat them beyond the confines of standard regulations, even though such men would not be discouraged by this, how could that serve to rouse heroic talents and inspire the world? As for men of average talent, they are different from this: each has his own usefulness, and each also has his own bias. Those who are perceptive and quick-witted must guard against being overly scrutinizing; those who are gentle and amiable must guard against lacking decisiveness; those who are calm and tranquil must guard against missing the opportune moment. If they are not regulated by law, then scrutinizing without end leads to harshness and urgency; insufficient decisiveness leads to mediocrity and timidity; and acting too late ruins opportunities for action. Therefore, regulations are the means to remedy their biases and preserve their usefulness in full—how could they be dispensed with? Observing the talents of the realm in terms of what lies within and beyond standard regulations, and treating them accordingly—this is the supreme art by which emperors and kings govern the realm within the seas and mold the multitude of men.

Your Excellency has posed a policy question to us students concerning the civil and military officials and officers of western Yue [Guangxi], showing deep concern for plans to pacify the frontier region. Allow me to gather what I have heard in order to reply. Since antiquity, in selecting officials and appointing generals, examples such as the commissioning of the Four Mountains and Twelve Pastors, or the bringing back [of Lü Shang] from the banks of the Wei River in a carriage, are of venerable memory. In the Han dynasty, during the Shenjue (61–58 BCE) and Wufeng (57–54 BCE) eras, when commanderies and principalities showed effective governance, the Son of Heaven would send down imperial letters under the royal seal to comfort and commend their administrators, and even summon them out of regular sequence to enter court as Excellency or Minister—this was most notable. Meanwhile, the ceremony for dispatching generals still retained the ancient custom of pushing the wheel-hub of the commander's chariot, so that the banner-raising warriors of that age were all able to extend the prestige of the state along the frontiers. Truly, the Han dynasty's success in obtaining capable men was thriving and abundant! Western Yue was originally territory opened up prior to the Qin, and its designation as a feudatory began with the Han. After long years of administration and development, it gradually came to be regarded like the central prefectures. Examining…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
覽往牒則其人聲實往往而在以守令言
之陸績守鬱林壓石歸舟人服其廉澤孰
茂焉嗣是則撫酋豪而定八州元結所以
刺容管挫彊禦而惠獨煢唐頌所以令布
山柳子厚順俗設理而俗化且授諸生以
經義人文興焉張敬夫諭夷釋怨而夷安
且為橫山革買馬宿蠹去焉皆號良吏也
而柳張其領袖乎以將帥言之馬援平交
阯標柱界地夷懾其威勳莫偉焉嗣是則
===
度尚一焚營鼓士而卜陽授首岳飛一縱
囚誤敵而曹成就俘軍士玩令狄青先斬
袁用以徇則智高之變靖矣懷遠要害和
斌先提步騎以據則世念之患銷矣皆號
良將也而岳狄其翹楚乎我
國家大簡天下文武吏士為億萬世計尤加
意於邊二百年來匪獨中州稱得人即粤
西亦皆彬彬質有其文武焉若何源若蕭
嘉祐及山雲輩未可一二數也庶幾哉其
punctuated: 覽往牒，則其人聲實往往而在。以守令言之，陸績守鬱林，壓石歸舟，人服其廉，澤孰茂焉？嗣是，則撫酋豪而定八州，元結所以刺容管；挫彊禦而惠獨煢，唐頌所以令布山；柳子厚順俗設理而俗化，且授諸生以經義，人文興焉；張敬夫諭夷釋怨而夷安，且為橫山革買馬，宿蠹去焉。皆號良吏也，而柳、張其領袖乎！以將帥言之，馬援平交阯，標柱界地，夷懾其威，勳莫偉焉！嗣是，則度尚一焚營鼓士，而卜陽授首；岳飛一縱囚誤敵，而曹成就俘；軍士玩令，狄青先斬袁用以徇，則智高之變靖矣；懷遠要害，和斌先提步騎以據，則世念之患銷矣。皆號良將也，而岳、狄其翹楚乎！我國家大簡天下文武吏士，為億萬世計，尤加意於邊。二百年來，匪獨中州稱得人，即粤西亦皆彬彬質有其文武焉。若何源、若蕭嘉祐及山雲輩，未可一二數也。庶幾哉！其
translation_en: … [Exam]ining past records, the reputations and real achievements of such men are everywhere to be found. Speaking of prefects and magistrates: when Lu Ji 陸績 served as Grand Administrator of Yulin 鬱林, he weighed down his returning boat with a stone, and people submitted to his incorruptibility—what beneficence could be more abundant than this? Thereafter, pacifying the chieftains and stabilizing the eight prefectures was how Yuan Jie 元結 served as Prefect of the Rongzhou Military Prefecture 容管; curbing the powerful and violent while showing kindness to the solitary and helpless was how Tang Song 唐頌 served as Magistrate of Bushan 布山; Liu Zihou 柳子厚 [Liu Zongyuan 柳宗元] established governance in accordance with local customs so that the customs were transformed, and moreover instructed the students in the meaning of the Classics, whereby cultural refinement flourished; Zhang Jingfu 張敬夫 [Zhang Shi 張栻] admonished the non-Chinese tribes to let go of their grievances so that they were pacified, and moreover reformed the horse-purchasing system at Hengshan 橫山, whereby long-standing abuses were eliminated. All of these were acclaimed as good officials, and were not Liu and Zhang their leaders? Speaking of generals and commanders: when Ma Yuan 馬援 pacified Jiaozhi 交阯 and erected bronze pillars to demarcate the territory, the non-Chinese tribes were awed by his majesty—no merit could be greater than this! Thereafter, as soon as Du Shang 度尚 burned the camps to rouse his soldiers, Bu Yang 卜陽 lost his head; as soon as Yue Fei 岳飛 released a prisoner to mislead the enemy, Cao Cheng 曹成 was taken captive; when the troops trifled with orders, Di Qing 狄青 first beheaded Yuan Yong 袁用 as a public warning, and thus the rebellion of [Nong] Zhigao 智高 was quelled; because Huaiyuan 懷遠 was a strategic strongpoint, He Bin 和斌 first led infantry and cavalry to occupy it, and thus the menace of [Cen] Shinian 世念 was dispelled. All of these were acclaimed as good generals, and were not Yue and Di their most outstanding figures? Our Dynasty has grandly selected civil and military officials and officers throughout the realm, planning for ten thousand generations, and has paid particular attention to the frontiers. Over the past two hundred years, not only has the Central Plain been praised for obtaining capable men, but even in western Yue [Guangxi] men have been refined and well-balanced in both civil and military accomplishments. Men such as He Yuan 何源, Xiao Jiayou 蕭嘉祐, and Shan Yun 山雲 cannot all be enumerated one by one. How close indeed are they…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
與昔人竝軌馳乎我
皇上
神明天授益廑民艱頃憂吏道稍稍耗廢
特詔廷臣嚴加甄别且舉增秩賜金故事行乆
任法以需厥成介胄有乗障破敵抵掌畫
策旋起徒歩建大將風聲所樹令天下士
有駕龔黃而凌韓白之氣何論粤西哉然
愚竊有異焉天下材品大都有三彼材之
墨而眊也酷烈也無論已其餘則中材也
===
豪傑也豪傑不數見而中材比比也今之
吏發奸擿伏鉤鉅不事有矣得無有淵察
爲明者乎敬老慈孤蒲鞭示辱有矣得無
有狐疑不决者乎雅風醇俗臥理自如有
矣得無有閣置廢事者乎此中材之吏之
所患也今之將開張押闔隨機應變或能
之而巧傷於竭澤不免也分甘損滋愛士
如子或能之而籌窘於前箸不免也審時
度勢老成持重或能之而膽怯於望風不
punctuated: 與昔人竝軌馳乎！我皇上神明天授，益廑民艱，頃憂吏道稍稍耗廢，特詔廷臣嚴加甄别，且舉增秩賜金故事，行乆任法以需厥成。介胄有乗障破敵、抵掌畫策，旋起徒歩建大將。風聲所樹，令天下士有駕龔、黃而凌韓、白之氣，何論粤西哉！然愚竊有異焉。天下材品大都有三：彼材之墨而眊也、酷烈也，無論已；其餘則中材也、豪傑也。豪傑不數見，而中材比比也。今之吏，發奸擿伏、鉤鉅不事，有矣，得無有淵察爲明者乎？敬老慈孤、蒲鞭示辱，有矣，得無有狐疑不决者乎？雅風醇俗、臥理自如，有矣，得無有閣置廢事者乎？此中材之吏之所患也。今之將，開張押闔、隨機應變，或能之，而巧傷於竭澤不免也；分甘損滋、愛士如子，或能之，而籌窘於前箸不免也；審時度勢、老成持重，或能之，而膽怯於望風不
translation_en:
… gallop abreast with the men of antiquity! Our August Emperor, endowed by Heaven with divine intelligence, is ever more solicitous of the people's hardships. Recently, concerned that the ways of officialdom have gradually deteriorated and grown lax, he specially decreed that court officials strictly screen and evaluate personnel; moreover, reviving the precedents of increasing ranks and bestowing gold, he implemented the policy of long tenure to await their ultimate success. Among armored soldiers, should there be those who mount the frontier barriers to shatter the enemy or clap their hands while devising strategies, they are swiftly raised from common foot soldiers to establish the banners of grand generals. The inspiring example thus set fills the gentlemen of the realm with the spirit to surpass Gong遂 (Gong Sui) and Huang霸 (Huang Ba) in civil governance, and to outstrip Han信 (Han Xin) and Bai起 (Bai Qi) in military prowess—what need is there to speak only of Guangxi!

Yet I humbly harbor a different reflection. The grades of talent in the world are generally three: as for those who are corrupt and muddled, or cruel and harsh, we need not even discuss them; the remainder are either of middling talent or heroic figures. Heroic figures are rarely seen, whereas men of middling talent are everywhere.
