Among today's civil officials, there are indeed those who expose villainy and uncover hidden crimes without resorting to devious traps, yet might there not also be those who mistake prying into the depths for true discernment? There are indeed those who respect the aged, show compassion to orphans, and use reed whips merely to display shame, yet might there not also be those who are suspicious and indecisive? There are indeed those who cultivate refined ways and pure customs, governing effortlessly from their couches, yet might there not also be those who shelve matters and neglect their duties? These are the failings to which civil officials of middling talent are prone. Among today's military commanders, some may be capable of deploying open and closed maneuvers and adapting to changing circumstances, yet they cannot avoid the flaw of cleverness that drains the pond to catch the fish; some may be capable of sharing sweet and bitter alike and loving their soldiers as their own sons, yet they cannot avoid being at a loss when devising plans at the council table; some may be capable of judging the times, weighing the situation, and acting with seasoned prudence, yet they cannot avoid losing their courage at the mere wind of the enemy's approach …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
免也此中材之將之所患也其材若彼其
患若此將胡以振之蓋昔者漢宣帝勵精
爲治有名實不相應必知其所以然故治
稱盛今覈吏非不詳也然巧吏每炫名以
最課上或徇名而課吏是故喜卓詭則狡
吏筩筩者顯矣美儇捷則奏成手中者先
矣事筐篋則禮義化俗者弗尚矣於郡縣
何裨焉今覈將非不密也然黠將恒買名
以邀功上或采名而任將是故快談辯則
===
能讀父書者售矣憑級報則性喜殺戮者
競矣竒征戰則坐困羌夷者見絀矣於疆
場奚賴焉此名實之覈不可不嚴也覈之
維何三年無囚不以無異見遺而戸口偽
增必斥也四璧堅守不以無功聽讒而馬
邑生事必誅也凡此覈之嚴矣然後視中
材之患懸其法整齊之有爵賞以誘乎其
前而不然者則奉三尺隨其後彼既有慕
於爵賞而又悚乎其黜罰則日兢兢焉惟
punctuated: 免也。此中材之將之所患也。其材若彼，其患若此，將胡以振之？蓋昔者漢宣帝勵精爲治，有名實不相應，必知其所以然，故治稱盛。今覈吏非不詳也，然巧吏每炫名以最課，上或徇名而課吏。是故喜卓詭，則狡吏筩筩者顯矣；美儇捷，則奏成手中者先矣；事筐篋，則禮義化俗者弗尚矣。於郡縣何裨焉？今覈將非不密也，然黠將恒買名以邀功，上或采名而任將。是故快談辯，則能讀父書者售矣；憑級報，則性喜殺戮者競矣；竒征戰，則坐困羌夷者見絀矣。於疆場奚賴焉？此名實之覈，不可不嚴也。覈之維何？三年無囚，不以無異見遺，而戸口偽增必斥也；四璧堅守，不以無功聽讒，而馬邑生事必誅也。凡此覈之嚴矣，然後視中材之患，懸其法整齊之。有爵賞以誘乎其前，而不然者，則奉三尺隨其後。彼既有慕於爵賞，而又悚乎其黜罰，則日兢兢焉惟
translation_en: … cannot be avoided. These are the failings that afflict generals of middling talent. With their talents being such as the former and their failings such as the latter, how are we to rouse them? In antiquity, when Emperor Xuan of the Han devoted his energies to governance, whenever reputation and reality did not correspond, he unfailingly found out the reason why; hence his rule was praised as flourishing. Today, the verification of civil officials is not lacking in detail, yet crafty officials often flaunt reputation to attain the highest service ratings, and their superiors sometimes evaluate officials by merely following reputation. Consequently, if one delights in the extraordinary and eccentric, then cunning officials who use informants and secret receptacles [?] become prominent; if one admires nimble promptness, then those who keep ready-made reports in hand are put first; if one relies on document boxes and registers, then those who transform customs through ritual and righteousness are not esteemed. What benefit is this to the commanderies and counties? Today, the verification of generals is not lacking in thoroughness, yet wily generals constantly buy reputation to angle for merit, and their superiors sometimes appoint generals by merely gathering reputations. Consequently, if one takes pleasure in eloquent debate, then those who can only read their father's books find favor; if one relies on reports of decapitated heads, then those whose nature delights in slaughter compete for advancement; if one prizes aggressive campaigning, then those who subdue the Qiang and Yi tribes by patiently hemming them in without fighting are dismissed. What reliance does this offer on the frontiers? Therefore, the verification of reputation and reality cannot but be strict. And how is this verification to be carried out? Having no prisoners for three years should not cause an official to be passed over for lacking extraordinary feats, whereas falsifying increases in registered households must be dismissed; holding firm behind four walls should not cause a general to suffer slander for lacking offensive merit, whereas provoking border trouble as at Mayi must be punished by execution. Once all such verification has been made strict, we may then examine the failings of those of middling talent and set up laws to regulate and bring them into line. There are ranks and rewards to entice them from ahead, and for those who fail to comply, the three-foot bamboo slips of the law follow closely behind them. Since they both yearn for ranks and rewards and stand in dread of demotion and punishment, day by day they will be anxiously cautious, only …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
君子之理財也豈能求之財之外哉求之
財之外者是謂蠹國是謂瘠民吾無取焉
吾惟順其財之所自生而講求其故劑量
于輕重變通于緩急因其賦之必不可加
稍有以充其賦因其用之必不可不足稍
有以足其用不病乎其私而有濟于其公
夫亦何所不可苟不察其所以而惟泥於
故常乃吾當縮乏之地處兵荒之交所需
四出莫知所應其於國計民瘼無裨萬分
===
一則何以善其後執事因粤西之縮於財
以近日所行之鹽筴錢法講求其無病于
公私可行于經久甚盛心也承學未與經
國之事則何所知然不可不有以復明問
今海內稱瘠土當多事者則孰過粤西哉
巖壑交錯水脉不生無可耕之地也谷箐
孤險雞犬不聞無可耕之民也為郡者九
不足當東南一二大郡也為邑者七十有
七不足當東南一二大邑也為土州為土
punctuated:
君子之理財也，豈能求之財之外哉？求之財之外者，是謂蠹國，是謂瘠民，吾無取焉。吾惟順其財之所自生而講求其故，劑量于輕重，變通于緩急。因其賦之必不可加，稍有以充其賦；因其用之必不可不足，稍有以足其用。不病乎其私，而有濟于其公，夫亦何所不可？苟不察其所以，而惟泥於故常，乃吾當縮乏之地，處兵荒之交，所需四出，莫知所應，其於國計民瘼無裨萬分一，則何以善其後？執事因粤西之縮於財，以近日所行之鹽筴、錢法，講求其無病于公私、可行于經久，甚盛心也。承學未與經國之事，則何所知？然不可不有以復明問。

今海內稱瘠土、當多事者，則孰過粤西哉？巖壑交錯，水脉不生，無可耕之地也；谷箐孤險，雞犬不聞，無可耕之民也。為郡者九，不足當東南一二大郡也；為邑者七十有七，不足當東南一二大邑也。為土州、為土
translation_en:
When a gentleman manages finances, how could he seek wealth outside of existing wealth itself? Seeking it outside of existing wealth is called consuming the state like a woodborer and impoverishing the people; I would adopt nothing of the sort. I would only follow the natural ways by which wealth is generated and investigate their underlying principles, balancing what is light and heavy, and adapting flexibly to what is urgent and what is not. Because the tax quotas absolutely cannot be increased, one finds modest ways to replenish those revenues; because expenditures absolutely cannot fall short, one finds modest ways to suffice for those needs. If it does not harm private interests while benefiting the public good, what could be objectionable about it? Yet if one fails to examine the reasons behind things and merely clings to old routines—when we are situated in a land of scarcity and depletion, amidst the twin crises of war and famine, with demands arising from all directions and no idea how to meet them, contributing not one part in ten thousand to state finances or the people's distress—then how could we manage the aftermath well? Because Guangxi (Yuexi) is straitened in finances, Your Excellency takes up the salt administration and coinage regulations recently put into practice, seeking ways that will bring no harm to public or private interests and can be sustained over the long term; this is a most magnanimous intention. As a junior scholar who has not participated in the affairs of governing the state, what could I know? Yet I cannot fail to offer a reply to your enlightened inquiry.

Today, among places within the seas known as barren lands facing constant troubles, which surpasses Guangxi? Crags and ravines interlock, water veins do not spring forth: there is no land fit for tilling. Valleys and bamboo thickets stand isolated and perilous, where the sounds of chickens and dogs are never heard: there are no people to till the land. Its nine prefectures are not enough to match one or two great prefectures of the southeast; its seventy-seven districts are not enough to match one or two great districts of the southeast. Those that are aboriginal departments, aboriginal…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
縣爲土司者環四面以居公租不入法令
不行一有事且嗷嗷望我以濟也是執事
之所謂賦之必不可加者也萬山盤錯道
路孤遠三江夾出舟楫艱難今日報劫路
則道路塞明日報劫江則舟楫阻某處議
鵰勦某處議夾勦日所需於軍餉者紛如
也某州告饑且云將盡出爲盜某縣告饑
且云將坐以待斃搜之民間無可貸搜之
倉庫無可發日所請於公帑者繹如也此
===
執事之所謂用之必不可不足者也賦必
不可加而又不可不加用必不可不足而
又不能足爲粵西籌者自古難之矣自近
日鹽筴行司庫稍有所貯乃公私輒又告
病蓋民生所不可一日缺者莫如鹽東南
煮于海西北產于池生于井永康崖鹽出
于木石決源釃流脉寫膏浸神液陰漉甘
鹵密起自管子謹正鹽筴計口食鹽始立
禁以佐兵賦而猗頓郭縱羅裒皆擅鹽之
punctuated:
縣、爲土司者，環四面以居，公租不入，法令不行，一有事，且嗷嗷望我以濟也。是執事之所謂賦之必不可加者也。萬山盤錯，道路孤遠，三江夾出，舟楫艱難。今日報劫路，則道路塞；明日報劫江，則舟楫阻。某處議鵰勦，某處議夾勦，日所需於軍餉者紛如也；某州告饑，且云將盡出爲盜，某縣告饑，且云將坐以待斃，搜之民間無可貸，搜之倉庫無可發，日所請於公帑者繹如也。此執事之所謂用之必不可不足者也。賦必不可加而又不可不加，用必不可不足而又不能足，爲粵西籌者，自古難之矣。

自近日鹽筴行，司庫稍有所貯，乃公私輒又告病。蓋民生所不可一日缺者，莫如鹽。東南煮于海，西北產于池、生于井，永康崖鹽出于木石，決源釃流，脉寫膏浸，神液陰漉，甘鹵密起。自管子謹正鹽筴，計口食鹽，始立禁以佐兵賦；而猗頓、郭縱、羅裒皆擅鹽之
translation_en:
…counties and chieftaincies (tusi) dwell all around us on four sides; they pay no public land tax, our laws and ordinances do not reach them, and yet the moment trouble arises, they clamor looking to us for relief. This is what Your Excellency refers to as taxes that absolutely cannot be increased. Myriad mountains twist and interlock, making the roads isolated and remote; the Three Rivers wind between cliffs, making boat navigation arduous. Today comes a report of highway robbery, and the roads are blocked; tomorrow comes a report of river piracy, and boat traffic is halted. One place deliberates on a swift, targeted raid (diaojiao), while another deliberates on a pincer campaign (jiajiao), so that the daily demands for military provisions are endless. One subprefecture reports famine and says its people will all go out to become bandits; one county reports famine and says its people will sit waiting for death. If we search among the people, there is nothing to borrow; if we search the granaries and treasuries, there is nothing to distribute; thus the daily requests upon the public treasury follow one after another in an unbroken stream. This is what Your Excellency refers to as expenditures that absolutely cannot fall short. Taxes absolutely cannot be increased and yet must be increased; expenditures absolutely cannot fall short and yet cannot be met—those who plan for Guangxi have found this difficult since antiquity!

Since the recent implementation of the salt administration measures, the provincial treasury has accumulated modest reserves, yet both the public and private sectors promptly report suffering from the drawbacks. Indeed, of the things the people cannot do without for a single day, none is more vital than salt. In the southeast it is boiled from the sea; in the northwest it is produced from salt lakes and drawn from wells; and the cliff salt of Yongkang emerges from wood and rock—tapping springs and channeling streams, seeping through veins and soaking like rich fat, its marvelous fluid secretly filtering down as sweet brine thickly rises. Ever since Master Guan (Guanzi) carefully regulated the salt policy and calculated salt consumption by head of population, monopolies were first established to subsidize military and fiscal levies; meanwhile, Yi Dun, Guo Zong, and Luo Pou all monopolized the [profits] of salt…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
利見于貨殖傳者可考也粤西非產鹽之
地鹽之由南海出湖湘也其路必由粤西
當事之臣因粤西公賦之縮得請于
朝出公帑之積轉鬻南海達于桂林召商上
納每二年可足三運每四運可得十萬本
息相半用助兵荒之需名曰官鹽商人出
私本由別路運其一由清遠縣至連州其
一由封川江至寧遠原額食熟鹽後乃改造生鹽越界變賣紊亂成規遂不可制名
===
曰私鹽官鹽轉輸頗難而其價亦稍高私
鹽乗便往返爲易而其價亦稍下以故私
鹽盛行官鹽阻滯今鹽場積至六百萬有
奇此公之所以病也官鹽滯不得不禁私
鹽羅兵譏察無所得縱私鹽之行非復往
昔之便湖湘之民籍鹽于粤西者不得不
告困此私之所以病也夫病之生也必有
所以爲病之原不究其原而欲救其病其
道無由也故欲通官鹽之滯不得不平官
punctuated: 利，見于《貨殖傳》者可考也。粤西非產鹽之地，鹽之由南海出湖湘也，其路必由粤西。當事之臣因粤西公賦之縮，得請于朝，出公帑之積，轉鬻南海，達于桂林，召商上納。每二年可足三運，每四運可得十萬，本息相半，用助兵荒之需，名曰「官鹽」。商人出私本，由別路運：其一由清遠縣至連州，其一由封川江至寧遠；原額食熟鹽，後乃改造生鹽，越界變賣，紊亂成規，遂不可制，名曰「私鹽」。官鹽轉輸頗難，而其價亦稍高；私鹽乗便往返爲易，而其價亦稍下。以故私鹽盛行，官鹽阻滯，今鹽場積至六百萬有奇，此公之所以病也。官鹽滯，不得不禁私鹽，羅兵譏察，無所得縱，私鹽之行非復往昔之便，湖湘之民籍鹽于粤西者不得不告困，此私之所以病也。夫病之生也，必有所以爲病之原；不究其原而欲救其病，其道無由也。故欲通官鹽之滯，不得不平官…
translation_en: …profits of salt, as can be verified in the "Biographies of Usurers" (Huozhi zhuan). Guangxi is not a salt-producing region, yet when salt from the Southern Sea (Guangdong) is transported out to Hunan and Hubei (Huxiang), its route must pass through Guangxi. Because of the shortfall in Guangxi's public revenues, the officials in charge obtained permission from the Court to draw upon accumulated public treasury funds to purchase salt in Guangdong and transport it to Guilin, summoning merchants to pay for and distribute it. Every two years suffices for three shipments, and every four shipments yields a hundred thousand [taels], half principal and half interest, which is used to aid the needs of military campaigns and famine relief; this is called "official salt." Merchants also put up private capital and transport salt by alternative routes—one from Qingyuan County to Lianzhou, and one by way of the Fengchuan River to Ningyuan. Originally the quota was for boiled salt, but later they switched to manufacturing raw salt, crossing jurisdictional boundaries to sell it off, throwing established regulations into disorder until it could no longer be controlled; this is called "private salt." The transport of official salt is quite difficult, and its price is also somewhat higher; private salt takes advantage of convenient routes to go back and forth easily, and its price is also somewhat lower. Consequently, private salt flourishes while official salt is obstructed and stagnant. Now over six million [catty/packs] have piled up in the salt yards—this is why the public sector suffers. Because official salt is stagnant, one cannot but prohibit private salt. Troops are deployed to inspect and intercept it so that none is allowed to pass; the movement of private salt no longer enjoys its former convenience, and the people of Hunan and Hubei who rely on Guangxi for their salt cannot help but cry out in distress—this is why the private sector suffers. Now, when an ailment arises, there must be a root cause that produces the ailment; if one does not investigate its root cause and yet wishes to cure the ailment, there is no way to do so. Therefore, if one wishes to clear the stagnation of official salt, one cannot but equalize the [price of] official…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
鹽之價使其價不甚遠於私則人何苦不
樂趨於官欲嚴私鹽之禁不得不重私鹽
之稅使其稅不甚遠於官則人何苦冒犯
于私通利于國而不病于民公利于商而
不病于國審如是而鹽有不行者乎此鹽
筴之不可不講者也自近日錢法行兵荒
稍有所需乃銅料又苦不繼蓋民生所利
用者莫如錢若布帛尺拆之則裂金銀細
分之則耗惟錢之為用寶於金利於刀流
===
於泉自太公立九府圜法而周則母子相
權秦則上下相等漢為八銖莢錢赤仄五
分理道夷陵有鵝眼綖環之别風飄水浮
之異大較錢重則病國錢輕則病民唯我
朝錢法輕重相等粵西僻在邊徼民便於錢
頃
皇上從廷臣之請令天下分省得各自鑄錢以
便行使粵西舊苦乏錢新錢一出鼓舞稱
便今所患者不在錢之不行而在錢之不
punctuated:
鹽之價。使其價不甚遠於私，則人何苦不樂趨於官？欲嚴私鹽之禁，不得不重私鹽之稅。使其稅不甚遠於官，則人何苦冒犯于私？通利于國而不病于民，公利于商而不病于國，審如是，而鹽有不行者乎？此鹽筴之不可不講者也。

自近日錢法行，兵荒稍有所需，乃銅料又苦不繼。蓋民生所利用者莫如錢：若布帛尺拆之則裂，金銀細分之則耗；惟錢之為用，寶於金，利於刀，流於泉。自太公立九府圜法，而周則母子相權，秦則上下相等，漢為八銖、莢錢、赤仄、五分。理道夷陵，有鵝眼、綖環之别，風飄、水浮之異。大較錢重則病國，錢輕則病民，唯我朝錢法，輕重相等。粵西僻在邊徼，民便於錢。頃皇上從廷臣之請，令天下分省得各自鑄錢，以便行使。粵西舊苦乏錢，新錢一出，鼓舞稱便。今所患者，不在錢之不行，而在錢之不…
translation_en:
… the price of government salt. If its price is not far from that of private salt, why would people not gladly turn to government salt? If one wishes to tighten the prohibition on private salt, one cannot but make the tax on private salt heavy. If its tax is not far from that of government salt, why would people go to the trouble of risking offense for private salt? When general benefit is brought to the state without harming the people, and public benefit is shared with the merchants without harming the state—if it is truly like this, could salt fail to circulate? This is why salt administration cannot go undiscussed.

Since the coinage regulations were recently put into effect, military expenses and famine relief have been somewhat supplied, yet the copper material suffers from a lack of continuous supply. Indeed, among the things useful for the people's livelihood, nothing compares to copper cash: if cloth and silk are torn foot by foot, they ruin; if gold and silver are finely divided, they suffer loss through wastage. Only cash in its utility is more precious than gold, sharper in advantage than knife-money, and flows like a spring. Ever since Taigong established the round-currency system of the Nine Treasuries, the Zhou balanced "mother" and "child" coins against each other, the Qin made upper and lower currencies equal, and the Han minted eight-zhu coins, elm-pod coins, red-rimmed coins, and five-fen coins. When principles of governance declined and decayed, there arose distinctions such as "goose-eye" and "thread-ring" coins, and anomalies so light they were "blown by the wind" or "floated on water." Broadly speaking, when coins are too heavy it harms the state, and when coins are too light it harms the people; only in our Dynasty's coinage system are heavy and light properly balanced. Guangxi (Yuexi) lies remote on the frontier, and the people find cash convenient. Recently His Majesty followed the request of court officials and ordered the provinces of the empire each to cast their own coins so as to facilitate circulation. Guangxi formerly suffered from a shortage of cash, and once the new coins came out, the people rejoiced and praised their convenience. What is cause for concern today is not that the coins do not circulate, but that the coins are not…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣不在錢之不廣而在銅之不繼開局之
初卽工作之具銅料之需俱取足粤東乃
粤東之銅亦取辦他省開局旣多用銅日
廣銅價高貴貿易爲難且在在有鬻銅出
省之禁此東路之銅有所不足恃也新錢
旣行舊錢遂閣原議以新易舊聽民自至
局兩平相易至者如流今則舊錢漸少不
及夙昔十之一二此舊錢之易有所不足
恃也不得已則以官吏齎銅價易於貴之
===
鎮遠乃道路孤遠時日曠久不足以應急
需則將柰何夫利之興也必有所以爲利
之原不得其原而欲興其利其道無由也
銅産於滇滇之由楚至粤也其路爲獨僻
商賈不至故得銅爲獨難今滇之廣南與
粤之田州其地爲接壤由廣南至田州江
從舟楫行也止半月程其路爲甚便滇人
議開官路置驛舍辦車馬惟以粤西應置
五驛費無所辦論大事者不計小費誠兩
punctuated: 廣；不在錢之不廣，而在銅之不繼。開局之初，卽工作之具、銅料之需，俱取足粤東。乃粤東之銅，亦取辦他省。開局旣多，用銅日廣，銅價高貴，貿易爲難，且在在有鬻銅出省之禁，此東路之銅有所不足恃也。新錢旣行，舊錢遂閣。原議以新易舊，聽民自至局兩平相易，至者如流。今則舊錢漸少，不及夙昔十之一二，此舊錢之易有所不足恃也。不得已，則以官吏齎銅價易於貴之鎮遠，乃道路孤遠，時日曠久，不足以應急需，則將柰何？夫利之興也，必有所以爲利之原。不得其原而欲興其利，其道無由也。銅産於滇，滇之由楚至粤也，其路爲獨僻，商賈不至，故得銅爲獨難。今滇之廣南與粤之田州，其地爲接壤，由廣南至田州江，從舟楫行也，止半月程，其路爲甚便。滇人議開官路、置驛舍、辦車馬，惟以粤西應置五驛，費無所辦。論大事者不計小費，誠兩
translation_en: … widespread; and not in their not being widespread, but in the copper supply not being sustained. When the mints were first opened, both the tools for the work and the required copper materials were obtained in full from Guangdong. Yet Guangdong's copper is also procured from other provinces. As more mints have opened and the use of copper has grown daily, the price of copper has become high and steep, making trade difficult; moreover, everywhere there are prohibitions against selling copper out of the province. Thus the copper from the eastern route cannot be relied upon. Once the new coins went into circulation, the old coins were shelved. The original proposal was to exchange the new for the old, allowing the people to come to the mints themselves to trade them at a fair rate, and those who came flowed like water. Now, however, the old coins have gradually dwindled to less than one- or two-tenths of what they were in the past. Thus the exchange of old coins cannot be relied upon. Having no alternative, officials and clerks are sent carrying the funds for copper to purchase it in Zhenyuan in Guizhou; yet the road is isolated and distant, taking a long stretch of time, so it is insufficient to meet urgent needs. What, then, is to be done? Now, in promoting a benefit, there must be a source from which the benefit arises. To wish to promote the benefit without securing its source leaves no way to achieve it. Copper is produced in Yunnan, but the route from Yunnan through Huguang to Guangxi is uniquely out of the way; merchants do not go there, and thus obtaining copper is uniquely difficult. Now, Guangnan in Yunnan and Tianzhou in Guangxi border one another. From Guangnan to the river at Tianzhou, traveling by boat, is a journey of only half a month, making the route very convenient. People in Yunnan have proposed opening an official road, establishing postal stations, and procuring carriages and horses, hesitating only because there are no funds to cover the expenses for the five postal stations that Guangxi ought to establish. Those who deliberate on great affairs do not calculate small expenses. Truly, if the two…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
省公議協通此道則銅至如流矣從而立
稅課廣錢局其利豈止於今日之費耶此
錢法之不可不講也雖然鹽價旣平公私
俱利故必大出公帑爲鹽本乃可以充公
家之用則轉運之法不可不行也由大舟
轉至梧州立場以頓由小舟運至桂林立
廠以發自梧州而上多立博淺之船自昭
平而上廣布哨守之卒則官鹽無滯轉運
不難其所積於司庫者豈止於今日之所
===
餘已哉南路旣通銅料日廣故必多開爐
以鑄錢乃可以備兵荒之需則私鑄之禁
不可不嚴也城中則
宗室私鑄以撓公家之權曠遠則土官私鑄
以擅公家之利請一切繩以法可行者禁
之以官不可行者請之於
上則官錢無滯流行日廣其所以備兵荒之需
者豈止於今日之所餘已哉嗚呼廣行鹽
之利是轉粤東之所生以充粤西之所積
punctuated: 省公議，協通此道，則銅至如流矣。從而立稅課、廣錢局，其利豈止於今日之費耶？此錢法之不可不講也。雖然，鹽價旣平，公私俱利，故必大出公帑爲鹽本，乃可以充公家之用，則轉運之法不可不行也。由大舟轉至梧州立場以頓，由小舟運至桂林立廠以發，自梧州而上多立博淺之船，自昭平而上廣布哨守之卒，則官鹽無滯，轉運不難，其所積於司庫者豈止於今日之所餘已哉？南路旣通，銅料日廣，故必多開爐以鑄錢，乃可以備兵荒之需，則私鑄之禁不可不嚴也。城中則宗室私鑄以撓公家之權，曠遠則土官私鑄以擅公家之利。請一切繩以法：可行者禁之以官，不可行者請之於上。則官錢無滯，流行日廣，其所以備兵荒之需者豈止於今日之所餘已哉？嗚呼！廣行鹽之利，是轉粤東之所生以充粤西之所積；
translation_en:
…provinces deliberate publicly and cooperate to open this route, then copper will arrive like a flowing stream. If we accordingly establish tax levies and expand the minting bureaus, how could the profit merely equal today's expenditures? This is why monetary policy must be thoroughly discussed.

Even so, once the price of salt is stabilized, both the public and private sectors benefit. Therefore, public funds must be expended on a large scale as capital for salt before it can suffice to meet the needs of the state; thus, a system of transport and distribution must be put into practice. Transport it by large vessels to Wuzhou 梧州, establishing depots there for storage, and carry it by small boats to Guilin 桂林, setting up yards there for distribution. Upstream from Wuzhou, maintain many shallow-draft lighters for transshipment; upstream from Zhaoping 昭平, widely deploy patrolling and guarding soldiers. Then government salt will suffer no bottlenecks, transport will not be difficult, and how could what is accumulated in the provincial treasury merely equal today's surplus?

Once the southern route is opened and copper supplies grow daily more abundant, we must set up more furnaces to cast coins in order to prepare for the exigencies of war and famine; thus, the prohibition against illicit minting must be made strict. Within the city walls, imperial clansmen mint illicitly, thereby disrupting the authority of the state; in remote expanses, native officials (tuguan 土官) mint illicitly, thereby monopolizing the profits of the state. I beg that all of them be restrained by law: where local action is feasible, let officials enforce the prohibition; where it is not feasible, let a petition be submitted to the Emperor. Then government coins will circulate without obstruction and spread ever more widely, and how could the reserves prepared for the exigencies of war and famine merely equal today's surplus?

Alas! Expanding the profits of the salt trade means transferring what is produced in eastern Guangdong to replenish the reserves of western Guangxi; …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
闢運銅之路是轉滇南之所有以濟粤西
之所無往來日衆財賦日生行之十年而
後之粤西非今之粤西比矣此百世之利
也不知執事者可採而見之施行否也
第五問
李時盛
同考試官訓導吳批粤西猺獞撫勦事宜具見
此篇讀至功級俘獲處令人惻然真仁人之言哉反
覆慨歎可深長思録之非徒以文辭之古雅也
===
考試官教諭陳批兵家事以不樂言不諱言
立柱而議論疊出區畫詳明籌粤西者尚有出此哉
考試官教諭尹批事情周悉敷敘詳明子其
有感時事而慨于衷者宜録以傳
君子未始樂言乎兵而亦未始諱言乎兵
樂言之則有用於其所不當用而何以全
吾之仁諱言之則有不用於其所不可不
用而何以行吾之義用於其所不可用是
疲民也其勢必至於弗戢不用於其所不
punctuated:
闢運銅之路，是轉滇南之所有以濟粤西之所無。往來日衆，財賦日生，行之十年，而後之粤西，非今之粤西比矣，此百世之利也。不知執事者可採而見之施行否也？

第五問
李時盛
同考試官訓導吳批：粤西猺獞撫勦事宜，具見此篇。讀至功級俘獲處，令人惻然，真仁人之言哉！反覆慨歎，可深長思。録之，非徒以文辭之古雅也。
考試官教諭陳批：兵家事以「不樂言」、「不諱言」立柱，而議論疊出，區畫詳明，籌粤西者尚有出此哉！
考試官教諭尹批：事情周悉，敷敘詳明，子其有感時事而慨于衷者，宜録以傳。

君子未始樂言乎兵，而亦未始諱言乎兵。樂言之，則有用於其所不當用，而何以全吾之仁？諱言之，則有不用於其所不可不用，而何以行吾之義？用於其所不可用，是疲民也，其勢必至於弗戢；不用於其所不
translation_en:
… and opening up a route for transporting copper is to transfer what southern Yunnan possesses in order to supply what Guangxi lacks. As travelers and merchants grow more numerous by the day and revenues are generated day by day, if this is practiced for ten years, the Guangxi of the future will no longer be comparable to the Guangxi of today. This is a benefit for a hundred generations. I do not know whether the examiners might adopt these views and see them put into practice?

Question Five
Li Shisheng

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Wu comments: The appropriate measures for pacifying and suppressing the Yao and Zhuang peoples of Guangxi are fully set forth in this essay. When reading to the passage on tallies of merit and captured prisoners, one is moved to pity—truly the words of a benevolent man! Repeatedly sighing with emotion, it invites deep and lasting reflection. We record it not merely for the archaic elegance of its diction.
Examiner, Instructor Chen comments: On military affairs, he sets up "not taking pleasure in speaking of them" and "not shying away from speaking of them" as his central pillars, while arguments unfold layer upon layer and his planning is detailed and clear. Among those who devise strategies for Guangxi, is there anyone who surpasses this!
Examiner, Instructor Yin comments: The circumstances are thoroughly understood and the exposition is detailed and clear. You are surely one who is moved by current affairs and feels deep emotion in your heart; it ought to be recorded and transmitted.

The gentleman has never taken pleasure in speaking of military force, yet neither has he ever shied away from speaking of military force. If one takes pleasure in speaking of it, one will employ it where it ought not to be employed—and how then can one preserve one's benevolence intact? If one shies away from speaking of it, one will fail to employ it where it cannot but be employed—and how then can one carry out one's righteousness? To employ it where it must not be employed is to exhaust the people, and the trend will inevitably lead to weapons never being laid down; to fail to employ it where it cannot…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
可不用是玩寇也其勢必至於棄民君子
爲之審輕重之辨酌先後之宜必有所用
以成其不用也必有所不用以全其用也
執事者有感於粵西之猺獞歲歲征勦弗
息也下策愚生愚生粵西人也請言粵西
猺獞之大略而後及所以處之者西粵猺
獞居萬山之中當三江之險深箐絕壑人
跡有所不通也古木懸崖日月有所不照
也層岡疊阜莫知其涯際也荒村遠落莫
===
窮其終始也種類莫可識別巢穴莫可跟
尋其所以爲室廬者則巖巔也其所以相
往來者則狼虎也其所以代耒耜者則鋒
鏑也殆天驕之若犬羊豺狼然莫可以人
理化也粵之西則有曰大藤曰八寨曰連
城曰六十三山曰七山等巢諸若此類莫
可枚舉也粵之東則有曰羅旁曰王母曰
雲稍曰母雞等巢諸若此類莫可枚舉也
濱于江者擾及舟楫濱于路者擾及行旅
punctuated: 可不用，是玩寇也，其勢必至於棄民。君子爲之審輕重之辨，酌先後之宜，必有所用以成其不用也，必有所不用以全其用也。執事者有感於粵西之猺、獞歲歲征勦弗息也，下策愚生。愚生，粵西人也，請言粵西猺、獞之大略，而後及所以處之者。西粵猺、獞居萬山之中，當三江之險。深箐絕壑，人跡有所不通也；古木懸崖，日月有所不照也；層岡疊阜，莫知其涯際也；荒村遠落，莫窮其終始也。種類莫可識別，巢穴莫可跟尋。其所以爲室廬者，則巖巔也；其所以相往來者，則狼虎也；其所以代耒耜者，則鋒鏑也。殆天驕之若犬羊豺狼然，莫可以人理化也。粵之西，則有曰大藤、曰八寨、曰連城、曰六十三山、曰七山等巢，諸若此類，莫可枚舉也；粵之東，則有曰羅旁、曰王母、曰雲稍、曰母雞等巢，諸若此類，莫可枚舉也。濱于江者，擾及舟楫；濱于路者，擾及行旅；
translation_en:
… cannot but be used, which is to treat bandits lightly, and its tendency must lead to abandoning the people. In handling this, the gentleman examines the distinction between what is weighty and what is light, and weighs the appropriateness of what comes first and what comes later; there must be occasions where he uses [force] in order to achieve not having to use it, and there must be occasions where he does not use [force] in order to keep its use intact.

You, the Examiner, moved by the fact that the Yao 猺 and Zhuang 獞 of Guangxi are subjected to punitive expeditions year after year without cease, have posed this policy question to your humble student. Your humble student is a native of Guangxi; allow me to speak of the general situation of the Yao and Zhuang of Guangxi, and then turn to the means of dealing with them.

The Yao and Zhuang of Guangxi dwell amidst ten thousand mountains and occupy the strategic passes of the Three Rivers (Sanjiang 三江). In their deep bamboo groves and sheer ravines, human footsteps cannot penetrate; beneath their ancient trees and overhanging cliffs, the sun and moon do not shine; across their layered ridges and piled hills, no one knows their bounds; among their desolate villages and distant settlements, no one can fathom where they begin or end. Their tribes and clans cannot be distinguished, and their lairs and dens cannot be tracked down. What they make into their houses and huts are the summits of crags; those with whom they go back and forth are wolves and tigers; what they use in place of plowshares are blades and arrowheads. Truly, Heaven indulges them like dogs, sheep, jackals, and wolves—they cannot be transformed by human principles.

In the west of Liangguang (i.e., Guangxi), there are lairs called Dateng 大藤, Bazhai 八寨, Liancheng 連城, the Sixty-Three Mountains (Liushisan Shan 六十三山), and the Seven Mountains (Qishan 七山); others of this sort are too numerous to recount one by one. In the east of Liangguang (i.e., Guangdong), there are lairs called Luopang 羅旁, Wangmu 王母, Yunshao 雲稍, and Muji 母雞; others of this sort are too numerous to recount one by one. Those who live along the rivers harass boats and oars; those who live along the roads harass travelers; …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
民財被劫虜且及公賦村落被剽略且及
城邑如是而猶曰兵不祥器也而吾諱言
之是居者無以爲居將棄編氓也行者無
以爲行將棄商賈也公賦無以爲公賦將
棄公賦也城邑無以爲城邑將棄城邑也
此必不可者也其動大衆者不得不動也
其興大役者不得不役也調兵數十萬不
得計其擾也費糧數十萬不得計其費也
何者誠計其大也誠不得不爲士民請命
===
也大兵一動風聲輒露其濱江濱路探知
內地消息者寧無有潛避遠匿脫然於鋒
鏑之外者耶其深山絕澗耕山而食結茅
而居不識內地言語不通者寧無有莫知
禍端駢首於鋒鏑之下者耶其所報功級
者果皆慣盜劇惡耶其所報俘獻者果皆
寇賊種類耶同生天地同稟血屬使其蠢
然無知莫知所謂而受俘獲罹刀鋸也此
又仁人之所隱而天地日月之恩有所不
punctuated: 民財被劫虜，且及公賦；村落被剽略，且及城邑。如是而猶曰：「兵，不祥器也」，而吾諱言之，是居者無以爲居，將棄編氓也；行者無以爲行，將棄商賈也；公賦無以爲公賦，將棄公賦也；城邑無以爲城邑，將棄城邑也。此必不可者也。其動大衆者，不得不動也；其興大役者，不得不役也。調兵數十萬，不得計其擾也；費糧數十萬，不得計其費也。何者？誠計其大也，誠不得不爲士民請命也。大兵一動，風聲輒露。其濱江濱路、探知內地消息者，寧無有潛避遠匿、脫然於鋒鏑之外者耶？其深山絕澗、耕山而食、結茅而居、不識內地、言語不通者，寧無有莫知禍端、駢首於鋒鏑之下者耶？其所報功級者，果皆慣盜劇惡耶？其所報俘獻者，果皆寇賊種類耶？同生天地，同稟血屬，使其蠢然無知，莫知所謂，而受俘獲、罹刀鋸也，此又仁人之所隱，而天地日月之恩有所不
translation_en: … The people's wealth is seized and plundered, and it even extends to public taxes; villages are pillaged and raided, and it even extends to walled cities and district seats. When things are like this, if one still says, "Weapons are instruments of ill omen," and we avoid speaking of them, then those who dwell at home will have no way to live, which would be to abandon the registered populace; those who travel will have no way to journey, which would be to abandon the merchants and traders; public taxes will have no way to be collected as public taxes, which would be to abandon public revenue; and walled cities and district seats will have no way to stand as cities and seats, which would be to abandon our cities and seats. This is categorically impermissible. When we mobilize a great host, it is because we have no choice but to mobilize it; when we launch a great campaign, it is because we have no choice but to undertake it. In calling up several hundred thousand troops, we cannot reckon the disruption; in expending several hundred thousand piculs of grain, we cannot reckon the cost. Why is this? Because we are truly reckoning what is of greater consequence, and we truly have no choice but to plead for the lives of the gentry and the people. Yet once a great army is set in motion, word of it inevitably leaks out. Among those along the rivers and roads who spy out news from the interior, could there not be some who secretly flee and hide far away, escaping altogether beyond the reach of blades and arrows? And among those in the deep mountains and cut-off ravines who till the hillsides for food and thatch huts for shelter, ignorant of the interior and unable to communicate in its language, could there not be some who, knowing nothing of how the disaster began, die side by side beneath the blades and arrows? Are the severed heads reported for merit truly all those of hardened bandits and heinous evildoers? Are the captives presented in triumph truly all of rebel and bandit stock? Born together between heaven and earth, endowed alike with flesh and blood, that they should in their simple ignorance, without knowing why, suffer capture and fall under the blade and saw—this in turn is what pains a humane person, and where the grace of heaven, earth, sun, and moon fails to…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
及也然則兵者將諱言之耶將樂言之耶
往歲督府重臣因粵東羅旁諸巢為地方
害且數十年動衆二十萬一舉殲之兵威
所震山谷為空計所得功級俘獻卽萬萬
勿計也乃西之六十三山等處逼近羅旁
畏威悔罪乞憐求生編里輸差盡從撫處
一時東西兩山並稱寧靖說者謂當時收
兵大早經略事宜尚未萬全逃匿餘黨尚
未搜捕乃不踰年舊日餘孽呼攜潜出盤
===
據舊巢劫掠水陸攻擾所城謂其藏匿者
在六十三山等巢然無實跡可考也謂其
糾合者為六十三山等獞亦無實跡可據
也卽日將東西夾剿滅此朝食而西之糧
餉稱乏八寨濱近之民又數數請兵將從
撫耶將從剿耶較之八寨將孰先耶將孰
後耶此執事者之所以私憂而過計之也
竊以為撫剿有定議而恩信不可失也兵
糧有定處而騷擾所當禁也行師有紀律
punctuated: 及也。然則兵者，將諱言之耶？將樂言之耶？往歲督府重臣因粵東羅旁諸巢為地方害且數十年，動衆二十萬，一舉殲之。兵威所震，山谷為空，計所得功級俘獻，卽萬萬勿計也。乃西之六十三山等處逼近羅旁，畏威悔罪，乞憐求生，編里輸差，盡從撫處，一時東西兩山並稱寧靖。說者謂當時收兵大早，經略事宜尚未萬全，逃匿餘黨尚未搜捕。乃不踰年，舊日餘孽呼攜潜出，盤據舊巢，劫掠水陸，攻擾所城。謂其藏匿者在六十三山等巢，然無實跡可考也；謂其糾合者為六十三山等獞，亦無實跡可據也。卽日將東西夾剿，滅此朝食，而西之糧餉稱乏，八寨濱近之民又數數請兵。將從撫耶？將從剿耶？較之八寨，將孰先耶？將孰後耶？此執事者之所以私憂而過計之也。竊以為撫剿有定議，而恩信不可失也；兵糧有定處，而騷擾所當禁也；行師有紀律，
translation_en: … reach. In that case, as for military force, should one treat it as a taboo subject, or should one speak of it with pleasure? In a past year, because the various strongholds of Luopang in eastern Guangdong (Yuedong) had plagued the region for nearly several decades, the senior official of the Supreme Commander's office mobilized a host of two hundred thousand and annihilated them at a single stroke. Shaken by the awe of our military might, the mountains and valleys were emptied; counting the decapitated heads taken for merit and the captives presented, they numbered in the tens of thousands beyond reckoning. Thereupon, in the west, the Sixty-three Mountains (Liushisan Shan) and other places closely bordering Luopang feared our might and repented their crimes, begging for pity and seeking to live. They were organized into tithing-communities (li) to render labor services and taxes, and all were dealt with through pacification; for a time, the mountains of both east and west were alike acclaimed as peaceful and quiet. Yet commentators say that the troops were withdrawn too early at the time, that the measures for strategic regulation were not yet completely thorough, and that the fleeing and hiding remnants of the gangs had not yet been hunted down and seized. Indeed, before a year had passed, the surviving miscreants of former days called to one another and stealthily emerged, occupying their old strongholds, plundering by water and land, and attacking and harassing the battalion towns (suocheng). Some say that those hiding them are in the strongholds of the Sixty-three Mountains and elsewhere, yet there is no concrete evidence to verify this; some say that those banding together with them are the Zhuang (Tong) tribesmen of the Sixty-three Mountains and elsewhere, yet there is no concrete evidence to rely on for this either. Now, we are about to launch a pincer extermination campaign from both east and west to "destroy these before breakfast," yet in the west the grain and provisions are reported to be lacking, while the people living near the Eight Stockades (Bazhai) also repeatedly request troops. Shall we pursue pacification, or shall we pursue extermination? Compared with the Eight Stockades, which should come first, and which should come later? This is why the Examiner privately worries and takes such anxious thought over it. I venture to consider that pacification and extermination have a fixed principle, and benevolence and good faith must not be lost; troops and provisions have fixed arrangements, and harassment and disturbance ought to be prohibited; marching an army has discipline, …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而玉石所當辨也善後有長策而犬羊不
可無統也地方有緩急而機宜不可失也
此今日爲粵西籌者誠無以過之也夫曰
撫勦有定論而恩信不可失者何也蓋六
十三山連城等山與羅旁相去不遠其所
藏匿其所糾合誠不知其有無夾勦之師
欲杜禍根收全功誠不可已也然昔之受
招安當編差者尚未有叛逆顯迹也一旦
使之一槩受鋒鏑何以示往日之恩信開
===
後日之悔悟也大兵一出願察其素受招
處者許立旗挿牌以保其生其怙惡不悛
素未招撫者必誅無赦則畏威感恩忠信
行于蠻貊矣此以勦行撫之道也夫曰兵
糧有定處而騷擾所當禁者何也蓋粵西
司庫所入不支所出興師十萬支糧三月
欲取辦粵西難矣兩廣用兵調粵西之兵
食粵東之糧舊有定額無議也但近日右
江一帶饑歉特甚狼兵一調勢必騷動窮
punctuated:
而玉石所當辨也；善後有長策，而犬羊不可無統也；地方有緩急，而機宜不可失也。此今日爲粵西籌者，誠無以過之也。

夫曰「撫勦有定論，而恩信不可失」者，何也？蓋六十三山、連城等山，與羅旁相去不遠，其所藏匿，其所糾合，誠不知其有無。夾勦之師，欲杜禍根、收全功，誠不可已也。然昔之受招安、當編差者，尚未有叛逆顯迹也。一旦使之一槩受鋒鏑，何以示往日之恩信、開後日之悔悟也？大兵一出，願察其素受招處者，許立旗挿牌以保其生；其怙惡不悛、素未招撫者，必誅無赦。則畏威感恩，忠信行于蠻貊矣。此以勦行撫之道也。

夫曰「兵糧有定處，而騷擾所當禁」者，何也？蓋粵西司庫所入不支所出，興師十萬，支糧三月，欲取辦粵西，難矣。兩廣用兵，調粵西之兵，食粵東之糧，舊有定額，無議也。但近日右江一帶，饑歉特甚，狼兵一調，勢必騷動，窮
translation_en:
… while jade and stone must be distinguished; there must be long-term strategies for postwar reconstruction, as the dog-and-sheep-like tribes cannot be left without governance; and regions have differing degrees of urgency, so opportune moments must not be missed. For anyone planning for Guangxi today, truly nothing can surpass these principles.

Why do I say that "there must be a settled policy on pacification and suppression, yet grace and good faith must not be lost"? The Sixty-three Mountains, Liancheng, and other mountains are not far from Luopang. Whether they are harboring fugitives or banding together with rebels is truly impossible to know for certain. A joint pincer campaign to eradicate the root of trouble and achieve complete success truly cannot be dispensed with. Yet those who previously accepted amnesty and submitted to registration and corvée service have not yet shown any overt signs of rebellion. If one morning we subject them all indiscriminately to the blade and arrow, how could we demonstrate the grace and good faith of the past or open the way for repentance in the future? Once the grand army marches out, I would wish that we investigate those who have long accepted pacification and settlement, permitting them to erect flags and plant placards to preserve their lives; as for those who persist in evil without repentance and have never submitted to pacification, they must be executed without pardon. Thus they will fear our majesty and feel gratitude for our grace, and loyalty and good faith will prevail even among the barbarian tribes. This is the way to carry out pacification by means of suppression.

Why do I say that "there must be fixed arrangements for military provisions, while disturbances and exactions must be prohibited"? The revenues of the provincial treasuries in Guangxi cannot cover their expenditures. To mobilize an army of a hundred thousand and supply them with rations for three months—if we seek to procure all of this from Guangxi, it will be difficult indeed. When military operations are conducted in the Two Guangs, mobilizing troops from Guangxi and feeding them with grain from Guangdong has long been an established quota, beyond dispute. However, recently the Youjiang region has suffered exceptionally severe famine and crop failure. Once the native wolf-troops (langbing) are mobilized, it will inevitably cause turmoil, and in the destitute…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
山空谷乘時將起而爲盜請出公帑之積
預買糧食分布大兵所過州縣以備行糧
饑荒處所大加賑恤以安反側兵一出境
一切糧食取濟粵東則閭里寧輯民得安
生糧餉有藉不至告乏此動衆安民之道
也夫曰行師有紀律而玉石所當辨者何
也蓋東西猺獞其相濱大江州邑浪人糾
合出沒焚燒劫殺無歲無之誠不可不誅
乃其在遠地與華人絕不相聞一槩取而
===
殺戮俘獲之以爲功無乃傷天地之和虧
好生之德也今之用兵誠不以殺戮爲功
而以安集爲功不以俘獲爲功而以制馭
爲功使兇惡醜類無所逃於
天罰而無辜羣生得保全於
太和之世豈不恩威並著哉此則神武不殺之
道也夫曰善後有長策而犬羊不可無統
者何也蓋夷性獷悍難馴惟自服其酋長
今宇內疆土與夷爲界者不知幾千萬里
punctuated: 山空谷，乘時將起而爲盜。請出公帑之積，預買糧食，分布大兵所過州縣，以備行糧；饑荒處所，大加賑恤，以安反側。兵一出境，一切糧食取濟粵東。則閭里寧輯，民得安生，糧餉有藉，不至告乏。此動衆安民之道也。夫曰「行師有紀律，而玉石所當辨」者，何也？蓋東西猺獞，其相濱大江州邑，浪人糾合出沒，焚燒劫殺，無歲無之，誠不可不誅；乃其在遠地，與華人絕不相聞，一槩取而殺戮俘獲之以爲功，無乃傷天地之和，虧好生之德也？今之用兵，誠不以殺戮爲功，而以安集爲功；不以俘獲爲功，而以制馭爲功。使兇惡醜類無所逃於天罰，而無辜羣生得保全於太和之世，豈不恩威並著哉？此則神武不殺之道也。夫曰「善後有長策，而犬羊不可無統」者，何也？蓋夷性獷悍難馴，惟自服其酋長。今宇內疆土與夷爲界者，不知幾千萬里
translation_en:
…those in remote mountains and empty valleys will seize the opportunity to rise up and become bandits. I beg that accumulated public treasury funds be disbursed to purchase grain in advance and distribute it among the subprefectures and counties through which the grand army will pass, so as to provide marching rations; and that in famine-stricken areas, generous relief and aid be granted in order to pacify the restless and wavering. Once the troops cross the border, all grain supplies should be drawn from Guangdong. Thus, the villages and neighborhoods will be tranquil and harmonious, the people will be able to live in peace, and military provisions will have a reliable source without running short. This is the way to mobilize the multitude while keeping the people secure.

Why do I say that "in marching an army there must be discipline, and jade and stone must be distinguished"? Among the Yao and Zhuang of the east and west, those who border the subprefectures and counties along the great rivers join forces with rootless vagabonds to appear and disappear unpredictably, burning, plundering, and killing—not a year goes by without this, and they truly must be executed. Yet as for those in distant lands who have no contact whatsoever with the Chinese people, if we indiscriminately seize, slaughter, and capture them to claim merit, would this not injure the harmony of Heaven and Earth and impair the virtue of cherishing life? In employing troops today, we should truly not regard slaughter as merit, but rather pacification and settlement as merit; we should not regard taking captives as merit, but rather control and management as merit. If we cause the fierce and wicked cliques to have no escape from Heaven's punishment, while innocent living beings are preserved intact in an era of Supreme Harmony, will not grace and authority both be made manifest? This is the way of divine martial prowess that does not resort to killing.

Why do I say that "for post-war reconstruction there are long-term strategies, and the barbarous tribes must not be without governance"? The nature of the non-Chinese tribes is fierce, unruly, and difficult to tame; they submit only to their own chieftains. Today, the territories within the empire that border upon non-Chinese tribes stretch for no one knows how many tens of thousands of li…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也獨有土官者制服爲易而其莫相君長
自相種類者則剽掠出沒莫可制也大功
旣成請以猺獞所居之山川畫地分區擇
其衆所推服者令其招出遺黨分地以居
官給以名色不徵其租稅行之三年地方
無事立爲土司等官令其約束地方聽調
徵發仍增置哨堡廣添兵卒則地方永永
無虞也此以夷治夷之道也夫曰地方有
緩急而機宜不可失者何也蓋六十三山
===
等山當粵西之一隅乃八寨患在腹心士
民數數請兵緩急之辨亦旣較然矣顧一
省所急者在八寨兩省所急者在夾勦欲
獨舉之則不可欲兼舉之則不能願且置
八寨於不論兵威一振八寨諸獞果能悔
罪輸誠分土立官自同齊民豈不能略其
旣往許其將來如其怙罪不悛爲害地方
則乘此餘威以殲滅之特摧朽也此則酌
量緩急之道也嗚呼兵者豈得已哉將樂
punctuated:
也。獨有土官者，制服爲易；而其莫相君長、自相種類者，則剽掠出沒，莫可制也。大功旣成，請以猺、獞所居之山川，畫地分區，擇其衆所推服者，令其招出遺黨，分地以居。官給以名色，不徵其租稅。行之三年，地方無事，立爲土司等官，令其約束地方，聽調徵發；仍增置哨堡，廣添兵卒，則地方永永無虞也。此以夷治夷之道也。
夫曰地方有緩急，而機宜不可失者，何也？蓋六十三山等山，當粵西之一隅；乃八寨患在腹心，士民數數請兵，緩急之辨，亦旣較然矣。顧一省所急者在八寨，兩省所急者在夾勦。欲獨舉之則不可，欲兼舉之則不能。願且置八寨於不論。兵威一振，八寨諸獞果能悔罪輸誠，分土立官，自同齊民，豈不能略其旣往、許其將來？如其怙罪不悛，爲害地方，則乘此餘威以殲滅之，特摧朽也。此則酌量緩急之道也。
嗚呼！兵者豈得已哉？將樂
translation_en:
… Only where there are native officials (tuguan) is it easy to keep them under control; whereas those who have no rulers or chieftains over one another and simply group together by their own kind plunder and raid, appearing and disappearing unpredictably, so that there is no way to control them. Once the great campaign is accomplished, I beg that the mountains and streams inhabited by the Yao and Zhuang be demarcated into distinct districts, and that those whom the multitude respects and submits to be selected and ordered to summon forth the remaining bands, dividing the land for them to settle. The authorities should grant them nominal titles without levying land taxes upon them. After this has been practiced for three years, if the region remains peaceful, they should be established as Native Office (tusi) officials and the like, charged with restraining and policing the locality and answering calls for troop mobilization and requisitions. If at the same time we establish additional sentry posts and forts and widely increase the garrison troops, the region will forever be free from anxiety. This is the way of using barbarians to govern barbarians.

Now, why is it said that regions have relative urgencies and that opportune moments must not be lost? The Sixty-three Mountains (Liushisan Shan) and other mountains lie in one corner of western Yue [Guangxi], whereas the Eight Stockades (Bazhai) are an affliction in the very heartland. Because the gentry and commoners have repeatedly petitioned for military action, the distinction between what is urgent and what can wait is already crystal clear. Yet what is urgent for a single province lies in the Eight Stockades, whereas what is urgent for both provinces [Guangxi and Guangdong] lies in a joint pincer campaign. To launch a campaign on our own is inadvisable; to undertake both campaigns simultaneously is beyond our capacity. I would ask that for the time being we set the Eight Stockades aside without discussion. Once our military might has been displayed, if the various Zhuang of the Eight Stockades are truly able to repent their crimes and pledge their sincerity—dividing the land, establishing native officials, and making themselves the same as ordinary registered subjects—how could we not overlook their past offenses and grant them a future? If, however, they persist in their crimes without remorse and continue to harm the region, then riding on the remaining momentum of our martial awe to annihilate them will be no more than crushing dry rot. This, then, is the way of weighing relative urgency.

Alas! How could weapons of war be used if there were any alternative? Shall we delight in…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
言之耶將諱言之耶樂言之而所謂寡人
妻孤人子獨人父母見聞所不及者獨不
足念耶諱言之而近日古田之復城邑府
江之通往來可以無兵得之耶酌量於緩
急之間識察於輕重之勢以撫爲勦則其
不用也猶用也爲雨露爲日星而莫非天
地之仁也以勦爲撫則其用也猶不用也
爲雷霆爲霜雪而莫非天地之義也仁義
竝行恩威兼著此兵家之善道也愚生書
===
生也何所知因明問而陳其一得者如此
惟執事者進教之
punctuated: 言之耶？將諱言之耶？樂言之，而所謂寡人妻、孤人子、獨人父母，見聞所不及者，獨不足念耶？諱言之，而近日古田之復城邑、府江之通往來，可以無兵得之耶？酌量於緩急之間，識察於輕重之勢，以撫爲勦，則其不用也猶用也，爲雨露、爲日星，而莫非天地之仁也；以勦爲撫，則其用也猶不用也，爲雷霆、爲霜雪，而莫非天地之義也。仁義竝行，恩威兼著，此兵家之善道也。愚生，書生也，何所知？因明問而陳其一得者如此，惟執事者進教之。
translation_en: … speaking of it? Or shall we treat speaking of it as taboo? If we delight in speaking of it, are the so-called widowed wives, orphaned children, and bereaved parents—even those beyond the reach of our own sight and hearing—not worthy of our concern? Yet if we treat speaking of it as taboo, could the recent recovery of the walled town of Gutian 古田 and the reopening of traffic along the Fu River (Fujiang 府江) have been achieved without troops? By weighing the balance between what is urgent and what can wait, and discerning the relative gravity of the situation, when pacification is used as a means of suppression, then not employing troops is just like employing them: it acts as rain and dew, as sun and stars, and is nothing other than the benevolence of Heaven and Earth. When suppression is used as a means of pacification, then employing troops is just like not employing them: it acts as thunderbolts, as frost and snow, and is nothing other than the righteousness of Heaven and Earth. For benevolence and righteousness to proceed together, and grace and martial awe to be manifested simultaneously—this is the best way of the military strategists. I, a foolish student, am merely a bookish scholar; what do I know? In response to your enlightened inquiry, I have set forth my humble understanding thus; I pray only that Your Excellency will summon me forward and instruct me.

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
萬曆巳卯秋巡按廣西御史
顧鈐奉
皇帝典制賓士于澤宮闋歌謂志
頤曰士且駕矣若亦何言志
頤伏内忖泳游
恩澤如海未知所報而告所愧以
===
訓人越鷄伏鵠難矣雖然使
誨規矩者必班倕離朱然後
可匠將微乎告諸士曰有司
之求士甚于士之求有司也
比者玄黃以志頤而來以爲
權衡以爲律量揣銖黍度毫
末瞠乎其視芒也手其編中
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序
萬曆巳卯秋，巡按廣西御史顧鈐奉皇帝典制，賓士于澤宮。闋歌，謂志頤曰：「士且駕矣，若亦何言？」志頤伏内忖：泳游恩澤如海，未知所報，而告所愧以訓人，越鷄伏鵠，難矣！雖然，使誨規矩者必班、倕、離朱然後可，匠將微乎？告諸士曰：「有司之求士，甚于士之求有司也。比者玄黃以志頤而來，以爲權衡，以爲律量，揣銖黍，度毫末，瞠乎其視芒也！手其編，中
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination
In the autumn of the yimao year of the Wanli era (1579), the Regional Inspector of Guangxi, Censor Gu Qian 顧鈐, upholding the Emperor's statutory institutions, entertained the scholars as guests at the Archery Pavilion. When the singing concluded, he said to me, Zhiyi 志頤: "The scholars are about to set out on their journey; what words do you have for them?" I, Zhiyi, humbly reflected to myself: swimming in imperial grace that is as vast as the sea, I do not yet know how to repay it; to speak of what I am ashamed of in order to instruct others is like a small chicken of Yue trying to hatch a swan's egg—how difficult! Even so, if those who teach the compass and square had to be Gongshu Ban 公輸班, Chui 倕, or Li Zhu 離朱 before they were permitted to do so, would artisans not become scarce indeed? I therefore say to the scholars: "The authorities' quest for scholars is even more urgent than the scholars' quest for the authorities. Recently, ceremonial silks of black and yellow were sent to bring me, Zhiyi, here, taking me as the balance and scale, taking me as the pitch-pipe and measure, to weigh grains and millet-seeds and to gauge hair-tips—staring wide-eyed until my vision grew dim! Taking a paper in hand, when it met…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
程𫉬矣竟蒐之而殊患其愉
也此何愛而不忍哉曰人才
實難脫一不終安得以瑕瑜
不掩爲解而汙賢能書蓋其
慎也士由此進于
天子矣譬則貢焉明金焠羽英犀
澤象雖遐裔之林不數數產
===
也日月而獲之意駭色動置
驛而上而不知都市之駢闐
天府之委擲直奇贏已耳士無自
謂英英奇矣而妄驅馳脫一
不終猶汙今日賢能書也其
慎自愛哉且夫取士以藝法
之窮也豈無他科自周漢以
punctuated: 程𫉬矣，竟蒐之，而殊患其愉也。此何愛而不忍哉？曰：人才實難，脫一不終，安得以瑕瑜不掩爲解，而汙賢能書？蓋其慎也。士由此進于天子矣，譬則貢焉。明金、焠羽、英犀、澤象，雖遐裔之林，不數數產也。日月而獲之，意駭色動，置驛而上，而不知都市之駢闐、天府之委擲，直奇贏已耳。士無自謂英英奇矣而妄驅馳，脫一不終，猶汙今日賢能書也，其慎自愛哉！且夫取士以藝，法之窮也，豈無他科？自周、漢以
translation_en: …meets the standard and is measured, we examine it to the end and yet remain deeply worried that it might prove shallow or lax. Why do we cherish them so and yet find ourselves unable to be lenient? It is because true talent is genuinely hard to find; if even one among them fails to carry through to the end, how could we excuse ourselves on the grounds that flaws and virtues do not conceal one another, and thereby sully the register of the worthy and able? Such is our caution. From here, scholars will be presented to the Son of Heaven—much like tribute goods. Bright gold, kingfisher feathers, fine rhinoceros horn, and lustrous ivory: even in the forests of the distant borderlands, such things are not produced in abundance. When one acquires them after days and months of searching, one’s mind is startled and one’s countenance moved, and one sends them up by post-relay—not realizing that amid the thronging markets of the capital and the heaped-up stores of the imperial treasury, they are treated as mere surplus curiosities! Let the scholars not consider themselves brilliantly extraordinary and recklessly gallop ahead; should they once fail to maintain their integrity to the end, they will still stain today's register of the worthy and able. Let them be cautious and cherish their own honor! Moreover, selecting scholars through literary craft comes from the exhaustion of institutional methods. Were there no other avenues of recruitment? Since the Zhou and Han…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
來置罷罷置凡以十數
明興要氐六經之言以爲卒亡
以踰而已昔孔子觀於上古
患其言不皆爾雅削觚裁方
所存者廑廑止此爲萬世程
授學者習之雖才不逮猶堪
自植訓詁之興棼如絲毛至
===
===
朱子乃有條貫六經之旨復
章章著明我
聖朝統一道眞塞岐旁示周行令
學者尊尚師說不悖亦足以
脩行先王之道矣由此言之
雖有超觀冥覽秪嘵嘵亂羣
無益今所不取而況俗化彫
punctuated: 來，置罷、罷置，凡以十數。明興，要氐六經之言，以爲卒亡以踰而已。昔孔子觀於上古，患其言不皆爾雅，削觚裁方，所存者廑廑止此，爲萬世程。授學者習之，雖才不逮，猶堪自植。訓詁之興，棼如絲毛，至朱子乃有條貫，六經之旨復章章著明。我聖朝統一道眞，塞岐旁，示周行，令學者尊尚師說不悖，亦足以脩行先王之道矣。由此言之，雖有超觀冥覽，秪嘵嘵亂羣無益，今所不取，而況俗化彫
translation_en: … [From the Zhou and Han dynasties] onward, they have been established and abolished, abolished and established, dozens of times in all. With the rise of the Ming, the essentials have been grounded in the words of the Six Classics, on the view that ultimately nothing can surpass them. In antiquity, when Confucius surveyed the distant past, he was troubled that its words were not all refined and proper; he pared away the corners and trimmed the squares, and what he preserved amounted barely to this much, to serve as a standard for ten thousand generations. Handed down for scholars to practice, even those whose talents fall short are still able to establish themselves. When exegetical commentaries arose, they were as tangled as silk fibers and hair; only when we reached Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] was there a coherent thread, and the purport of the Six Classics shone forth clearly once again. Our Sacred Dynasty has unified the true Way, blocked off diverging side-paths, and pointed out the great highway, commanding scholars to revere and uphold the explanations of the masters without deviation—which is likewise sufficient for cultivating and practicing the Way of the former kings. Viewed in this light, even if someone possesses transcendent insight and abstruse erudition, it merely creates a clamorous din that throws the flock into confusion to no avail, and today it is not selected—how much less so when vulgar fashions carve and…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
文樂難攻之書而弋獨用之
言以飾其瑣譎謬悠之論讀
之如太上靈檢絕域重譯非
同文之化而罔施于用文章
道喪渰渰下矣此世之所謂
千金而有司方敝帚棄者也
士無寧詆有司眊哉士第以
===
故業往即經緯
國華康賛
聖功無匱用已毋更謁師不信有
司將謂聖賢掌不然之辯以
迷世而有司張無目之羅以
招不制之羽也必非指矣劉
邵有言人之質量中和最貴
punctuated: 文，樂難攻之書，而弋獨用之言，以飾其瑣譎謬悠之論。讀之如太上靈檢、絕域重譯，非同文之化，而罔施于用。文章道喪，渰渰下矣。此世之所謂千金，而有司方敝帚棄者也。士無寧詆有司眊哉？士第以故業往，即經緯國華、康賛聖功，無匱用已，毋更謁師、不信有司。將謂聖賢掌不然之辯以迷世，而有司張無目之羅以招不制之羽也，必非指矣。劉邵有言：「人之質量，中和最貴。
translation_en: …embellish prose, delighting in books that are hard to penetrate and hunting after idiosyncratic words to adorn their petty, deceitful, and absurdly far-fetched arguments. Reading them is like reading the esoteric talismanic scriptures of the Most High or texts multiply translated from remote lands: they do not belong to a culture of unified script, and they cannot be applied to practical use. The Way of literary composition is lost, sinking ever lower in gloom. What the world calls worth a thousand pieces of gold, the authorities cast aside right now like a worn-out broom. Would scholars not rather slander the authorities as dim-sighted? If scholars simply proceed on the basis of their established studies, then in weaving the splendor of the state and peacefully assisting in the sacred achievements, there will be no lack of utility; let them not seek out other masters or distrust the authorities. To claim that the sages and worthies wielded specious arguments to delude the world, or that the authorities spread a meshless net to summon untamable birds, is certainly not the true intention. Liu Shao 劉邵 once said: “In the substance and measure of a person, equilibrium and harmony are most prized…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄序
萬曆巳卯天下復當賓興士
御史顧鈴以
上命按廣西得監臨試事遵故事
聘禮繼及教諭陳志頤為考
試官教諭嚴思恭呂朝陽王
元弼訓導徐雲山吳道東為
===
同考試官以左布政使吳椿
右布政使盧仲佃司提調按
察使林澄源副使歐陽模司
監試暨百執事遴選咸稱入
鎖院御史進禮繼等而盟之
曰簾以內諸文學典之惟衡
乃平惟鑑乃明慎之哉又進
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄序

萬曆巳卯，天下復當賓興士。御史顧鈴以皇命按廣西，得監臨試事。遵故事，聘禮繼及教諭陳志頤為考試官，教諭嚴思恭、呂朝陽、王元弼，訓導徐雲山、吳道東為同考試官。以左布政使吳椿、右布政使盧仲佃司提調，按察使林澄源、副使歐陽模司監試，暨百執事遴選咸稱。入鎖院，御史進禮繼等而盟之曰：「簾以內，諸文學典之，惟衡乃平，惟鑑乃明，慎之哉！」又進
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the jimao year of the Wanli reign (1579), the empire once again reached the time for honoring and recommending scholars for the provincial examinations. Investigating Censor Gu Ling 顧鈴, inspecting Guangxi by imperial command, served as Supervising Official of the examination affairs. Following precedent, he invited me, Liji 禮繼, together with County Director of Studies Chen Zhiyi 陳志頤 to serve as Examiners, and County Directors of Studies Yan Sigong 嚴思恭, Lü Chaoyang 呂朝陽, and Wang Yuanbi 王元弼, along with Assistant Instructors Xu Yunshan 徐雲山 and Wu Daodong 吳道東, to serve as Associate Examiners. Left Administration Commissioner Wu Chun 吳椿 and Right Administration Commissioner Lu Zhongtian 盧仲佃 were placed in charge of proctoring (as Proctors), while Surveillance Commissioner Lin Chengyuan 林澄源 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Ouyang Mo 歐陽模 were placed in charge of monitoring the examination; all the various functionaries selected were likewise well suited to their posts. Upon entering the locked examination compound, the Censor summoned me, Liji, and the others before him and administered an oath, saying: "Within the curtain, you men of letters are in charge. Only the balance is level; only the mirror is clear. Be conscientious in this!" He then summoned…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諸司而盟之曰簾以外諸大
夫百執事典之科指具存矩
矱必飭亦自盟也曰予所不
虔毖以詒子大夫憂則有
昭昭之監在焉約已罔弗兢兢祗
厥事乃合提學副使鍾繼英
所程士一千四百有奇三試
===
之得士五十有五人梓其文
以
獻禮繼不佞以職事宜敘首簡
乃颺言於諸士曰爾諸士亦
知今日之奇遘乎夫桂林百
粤之地幅隕二千里夷獠之
族錯編氓而居者殆半其誦
punctuated:
諸司而盟之曰：「簾以外，諸大夫百執事典之。科指具存，矩矱必飭。」亦自盟也，曰：「予所不虔毖以詒子大夫憂，則有昭昭之監在焉。」約已，罔弗兢兢祗厥事。乃合提學副使鍾繼英所程士一千四百有奇，三試之，得士五十有五人，梓其文以獻。
禮繼不佞，以職事宜敘首簡，乃颺言於諸士曰：「爾諸士亦知今日之奇遘乎？夫桂林百粤之地，幅隕二千里，夷獠之族錯編氓而居者殆半。其誦
translation_en:
… the various officials and bound them by oath, saying: "Outside the screen, the various grandees and hundred functionaries are in charge. The statutory guidelines are all extant, and the rules and regulations must be strictly observed." He also bound himself by oath, saying: "Should I fail to be reverent and cautious, thereby leaving cause for concern to you grandees, there is the bright watching of Heaven above." Once the covenant was concluded, there was no one who did not attend to his duties with trembling caution. Thus they gathered the more than one thousand four hundred scholars examined and selected by the Education-intendant Vice Commissioner Zhong Jiying 鍾繼英, tested them in three sessions, and obtained fifty-five men. Their essays were cut onto woodblocks to be presented to the Throne.
Unworthy as I, [Chen] Liji, am, by virtue of my official duties it falls to me to write the preface for the opening pages. Accordingly, I proclaim to the scholars: "Do all you scholars understand the extraordinary opportunity of today? Now, this land of Guilin and the Hundred Yue spans two thousand li in breadth, and the Yi and Liao tribes who live interspersed among the registered commoners make up nearly half the population. For them to recite…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
法詩書羣黌校之間得號爲
士斯已難矣矧去
天萬里士白首牖下無繇望見
帝閽者何限而一旦舉之奧渫彈
冠出里待對
大廷抑又難焉至於
聖人御極山海廓清諸士處得脩
===
其故業出得覲其
耿光翺翔天衢若升虚邑則何
啻難之蓋千載一遘耳禮繼
故曰奇也然竊有過計焉夫
士者民所則也舉於千萬人
之中爲
明時用天下所環指而竊睨也是
punctuated: 法《詩》、《書》，羣黌校之間，得號爲士，斯已難矣。矧去天萬里，士白首牖下，無繇望見帝閽者何限？而一旦舉之奧渫，彈冠出里，待對大廷，抑又難焉。至於聖人御極，山海廓清，諸士處得脩其故業，出得覲其耿光，翺翔天衢，若升虚邑，則何啻難之，蓋千載一遘耳！禮繼故曰奇也。然竊有過計焉：夫士者，民所則也；舉於千萬人之中，爲明時用，天下所環指而竊睨也。是
translation_en: …and emulating the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, gathering among the state schools so as to be called scholars—this in itself is already difficult. How much more so when, ten thousand li distant from Heaven, there is no limit to the number of scholars who grow white-haired beneath their windows with no means of ever gazing upon the imperial gates! Yet once raised up from obscurity and lowliness, to dust off one's cap and leave one's village to await examination in the Great Court—this is harder still. And now that a Sage sits upon the throne and the mountains and seas are swept clear, for you gentlemen in retirement to be able to cultivate your accustomed studies, and in coming forth to be able to behold His radiant glory, soaring along the avenues of Heaven as easily as ascending an unguarded town—how is this merely difficult? Indeed, it is an encounter that comes once in a thousand years! That is why I, Liji (禮繼), call it extraordinary. Yet privately I harbor an anxious concern: a scholar is one whom the common people take as a model; selected from among tens of thousands to be employed by an enlightened age, he is the one at whom the whole world points from all sides and secretly watches. Therefore…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
故負超俗之望則標準難蒙
國士之遇則稱塞難際治平
之時則表見難一不當人將
求多而疵瑕之亡論諸士卽
主司者有餘責矣諸士其何
以自效乎夫鉅細異材淺深
異智方圓異器强弱異力稟
===
有固然弗可强也乃心之精
神則無不可自盡者要在本
之以愨耳故弓調而後求勁
馬服而後求良士必愨而後
智能著蓋愨則精專而神定
誠之所極金石爲糜卽智能
稍不及彼固足以辦之况其
punctuated: 故負超俗之望，則標準難；蒙國士之遇，則稱塞難；際治平之時，則表見難。一不當，人將求多而疵瑕之，亡論諸士，卽主司者有餘責矣。諸士其何以自效乎？夫鉅細異材，淺深異智，方圓異器，强弱異力，稟有固然，弗可强也。乃心之精神，則無不可自盡者，要在本之以愨耳。故弓調而後求勁，馬服而後求良，士必愨而後智能著。蓋愨則精專而神定，誠之所極，金石爲糜。卽智能稍不及，彼固足以辦之，况其
translation_en:
…Therefore, when one bears expectations that transcend the ordinary, it is difficult to serve as a standard; when one receives the treatment due a scholar of the realm, it is difficult to live up to and fulfill those expectations; and when one encounters an era of peace and good order, it is difficult to distinguish oneself. Should there be a single misstep, people will demand much and find fault with it; not to mention the gentlemen themselves, even the examiners will bear leftover blame. How, then, are these gentlemen to prove themselves?

Now, great and small differ in talent, shallow and deep differ in wisdom, square and round differ in capacity, and strong and weak differ in strength; natural endowments are inherently so and cannot be forced. Yet as for the vital spirit of the mind, there is nothing in which one cannot fully exert oneself; the key lies simply in grounding it in earnestness. Thus, only after a bow is well-adjusted does one seek stiffness in it; only after a horse is broken in does one seek excellence in it; and a scholar must first be earnest before his wisdom and ability can become manifest. For when one is earnest, one's vital energy is focused and one's spirit is settled; at the utmost point of sincerity, even metal and stone are pulverized. Even if one's wisdom and ability fall slightly short, such earnestness is certainly sufficient to accomplish the task—how much more so for those whose…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
過人者耶今
廟堂作則垂範專尚本實思得忠
信樸茂之士布列有位而棄
浮脩實在中土稍難之何則
其所漸者深也乃廣右越在
西南僻徼士生其間類多恂
恂悃愊無一切靡麗之觀即
所爲文大都發明理奧宗本
經訓斤斤守其尺寸雖光采
崛奇差遜中土禮繼等無寧
收之意所謂忠信樸茂之士
不出此耳語云社樹之峩峩
不如茗柯之細實侈言無當
固不若簡樸者之適用也且
punctuated: 過人者耶？今廟堂作則垂範，專尚本實，思得忠信樸茂之士布列有位。而棄浮脩實，在中土稍難之，何則？其所漸者深也。乃廣右越在西南僻徼，士生其間，類多恂恂悃愊，無一切靡麗之觀。即所爲文，大都發明理奧，宗本經訓，斤斤守其尺寸。雖光采崛奇差遜中土，禮繼等無寧收之，意所謂忠信樸茂之士不出此耳。語云：「社樹之峩峩，不如茗柯之細實。」侈言無當，固不若簡樸者之適用也。且
translation_en: …surpasses others? Today the imperial court establishes standards and hands down models, exclusively prizing what is fundamental and substantial, and longing to obtain loyal, trustworthy, plain, and solid scholars to fill the official ranks. Yet abandoning superficiality and cultivating substance is somewhat more difficult in the Central Plains—why is that? Because what they have been steeped in runs deep. By contrast, Guangxi lies far off on the remote southwestern frontier. The scholars born in this region are mostly respectful, modest, and sincere, utterly devoid of any ostentatious or florid pretensions. Even the essays they compose generally elucidate the profound principles and take as their foundation the teachings of the Classics, scrupulously adhering to their rules and measures. Although in brilliance and striking originality they are slightly inferior to those of the Central Plains, I, Liji, and my colleagues would rather select them, thinking that what are called loyal, trustworthy, plain, and solid scholars are none other than these. As the saying goes: "The towering height of the altar tree is not as good as the fine substance of the tea branch." Extravagant words without appropriateness are certainly not as suited for practical use as that which is simple and plain. Moreover,…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諸士不見桂嶺諸山終古巍
巍乎氣從崑崙自北徂南而
極于西粵則其基厚也又不
見湘漓諸水終古洋洋乎勢
從海陽支分為二而瀠洄數
千里則其源深也士躡雲霄
之會將楨榦
===
王國恢弘
帝猷以建巍巍洋洋之業而使基
弗厚源弗深則胡以應之忠
信樸茂固士之基與源也操
玆往焉而益以閱天下之義
理習
國家之典刑精神所注何事弗
punctuated: 諸士不見桂嶺諸山，終古巍巍乎？氣從崑崙，自北徂南，而極于西粵，則其基厚也。又不見湘、漓諸水，終古洋洋乎？勢從海陽，支分為二，而瀠洄數千里，則其源深也。士躡雲霄之會，將楨榦王國，恢弘帝猷，以建巍巍洋洋之業，而使基弗厚、源弗深，則胡以應之？忠信樸茂，固士之基與源也。操玆往焉，而益以閱天下之義理，習國家之典刑，精神所注，何事弗
translation_en: … Do you scholars not see the mountains of the Guiling range, towering aloft through all antiquity? Their vital force comes from the Kunlun Mountains, coursing from north to south until it reaches its limit here in Western Yue [Guangxi]—thus their foundation is thick. And do you not see the waters of the Xiang and Li rivers, flowing vast and boundless through all antiquity? Their momentum comes from Mount Haiyang, dividing into two branches and eddying across thousands of li—thus their source is deep. When scholars ascend to the occasion of reaching the clouds, they are about to become the supporting pillars of the royal realm and enlarge the imperial plan, so as to establish towering and boundless achievements; if their foundation is not thick and their source is not deep, how then could they answer this call? Loyalty, trustworthiness, and unadorned substance are indeed the foundation and the source of a scholar. Hold fast to these as you go forth, and further enrich yourselves by examining the moral principles of the world and familiarizing yourselves with the statutory models of the state; wherever your spirit and energy are focused, what task could you not…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
任所以標準天下稱知已而
報
明時端在是矣脫或出見紛華弁
髦本質靡然改玉初終若兩
人則不惟負此舉負此時回
視閭里編氓且非故我安所
貴士矣諸士勉哉是舉也先
===
總督兩廣都察院右都御史
兼兵部左侍郎今晉南京兵
部尚書凌雲翼治教兼弘肅
清嶺海總督兩廣兵部右侍
郎兼都察院右僉都御史劉
堯誨威德並楙興起髦先
巡撫廣西都察院右副都御
punctuated:
任？所以標準天下、稱知已而報明時，端在是矣。脫或出見紛華，弁髦本質，靡然改玉，初終若兩人，則不惟負此舉、負此時，回視閭里編氓，且非故我，安所貴士矣！諸士勉哉！
是舉也，先總督兩廣都察院右都御史兼兵部左侍郎、今晉南京兵部尚書凌雲翼，治教兼弘，肅清嶺海；總督兩廣兵部右侍郎兼都察院右僉都御史劉堯誨，威德並楙，興起髦先；巡撫廣西都察院右副都御
translation_en:
…shoulder? That whereby one sets a standard for the realm, lives up to those who recognize one's worth, and repays this enlightened age lies precisely in this. Should you perhaps go out and see the splendor and luxury of the world, cast aside your fundamental substance as a useless cap, and yieldingly change your jade-like conduct so that from beginning to end you are like two different people, then you would not only betray this examination and betray this era, but when you look back upon the registered commoners of your home villages, you would no longer even be your former selves—wherein, then, would lie the value of a scholar! Gentlemen, exert yourselves!
In this examination, the former Supreme Commander of Liangguang, Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate concurrently serving as Left Vice Minister of War, now promoted to Nanjing Minister of War, Ling Yunyi 凌雲翼, broadly advanced both governance and education, bringing order and peace to the Mountain Ranges and the Coast; the Supreme Commander of Liangguang, Right Vice Minister of War concurrently serving as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, Liu Yaohui 劉堯誨, caused both majesty and virtue to flourish, inspiring and raising up outstanding talents; the former Grand Coordinator of Guangxi, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
史今晉戶部右侍郎吳文華
握憲經文甄陶素洽巡撫廣
西都察院右副都御史張任
壯猷崇雅綱紀聿新鎮守廣
西總兵官署都督僉事王尚
文詰戎靖遠章縫樂業其襄
試事于外者左參政彭文質
===
右參政王原相右參政兼僉
事陳應春副使陳俊侯國治
右參議姜忻右參議兼僉事
李一迪參將于嵩倪中化李
應祥韓文啓張榜咸與有力
焉副使周舜岳左參議毛爲
光署都指揮僉事呂應暘則
punctuated: 史今晉戶部右侍郎吳文華，握憲經文，甄陶素洽；巡撫廣西都察院右副都御史張任，壯猷崇雅，綱紀聿新；鎮守廣西總兵官、署都督僉事王尚文，詰戎靖遠，章縫樂業。其襄試事于外者，左參政彭文質、右參政王原相、右參政兼僉事陳應春、副使陳俊、侯國治、右參議姜忻、右參議兼僉事李一迪、參將于嵩、倪中化、李應祥、韓文啓、張榜，咸與有力焉。副使周舜岳、左參議毛爲光、署都指揮僉事呂應暘，則
translation_en: … [former Grand Coordinator of Guangxi and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate,] now promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, Wu Wenhua (吳文華), held the canons of law and ordered literary culture, his molding and nurturing influence having long been pervasive; the Grand Coordinator of Guangxi and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, Zhang Ren (張任), with grand plans and esteem for elegance, renewed the laws and discipline; and the Regional Commander Defender of Guangxi and Acting Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief, Wang Shangwen (王尚文), kept the military in order and pacified the distant marches, so that scholars in their robes could rejoice in their studies. As for those who assisted with the examination affairs from the outside: Left Administration Vice Commissioner Peng Wenzhi (彭文質), Right Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Yuanxiang (王原相), Right Administration Vice Commissioner concurrently Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Chen Yingchun (陳應春), Surveillance Vice Commissioners Chen Jun (陳俊) and Hou Guozhi (侯國治), Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Jiang Xin (姜忻), Right Assistant Administration Commissioner concurrently Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Li Yidi (李一迪), and Assistant Regional Commanders Yu Song (于嵩), Ni Zhonghua (倪中化), Li Yingxiang (李應祥), Han Wenqi (韓文啓), and Zhang Bang (張榜) all contributed their efforts to it. Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhou Shunyue (周舜岳), Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Mao Weiguang (毛爲光), and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Lü Yingyang (呂應暘), who…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以入
賀行右參政莊國禎則以遷秩
行亦與襄始事法得竝書
福建福州府福清縣儒學教
諭尹禮繼謹序
punctuated:
以入賀行，右參政莊國禎則以遷秩行，亦與襄始事，法得竝書。
福建福州府福清縣儒學教諭尹禮繼謹序。
translation_en:
… had departed to attend the court congratulations, while Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhuang Guozhen 莊國禎 had departed upon promotion in rank; as they also assisted in initiating the affairs of the examination, by regulation they are recorded together here.

Respectfully prefaced by Yin Liji 尹禮繼, Instructor of the Confucian School of Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian.

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萬曆七年廣西鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史顧鈴〔朝肅浙江仁和縣人辛酉貢士〕
提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司左布政使吳椿〔壽卿江西新建縣人已未進士〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司右布政使盧仲佃〔田叔浙江東陽縣人丙辰進士〕

廣西等處提刑按察司副使歐陽模〔宏甫福建南安縣人已未進士〕
===
考試官
福建福州府福清縣儒學教諭尹禮繼〔世敬浙江龍游縣人戊午貢士〕
江西吉安府廬陵縣儒學教諭陳志頤〔吉甫廣東海陽縣人癸酉貢士〕
同考試官
直隸鎭江府丹陽縣儒學教諭嚴思恭〔子安雲南後衛籍浙江嘉興縣人庚午貢士〕
江西饒州府餘干縣儒學教諭呂朝陽〔相明廣東順德縣人壬子貢士〕
湖廣黃州府黃安縣儒學教諭王元弼〔汝諧江西新建縣人丁卯貢士〕

湖廣常德府龍陽縣儒學訓導吳道東〔傳之貴州思州府人庚午貢士〕
punctuated:
萬曆七年廣西鄉試

巡按廣西監察御史顧鈴〔朝肅，浙江仁和縣人，辛酉貢士〕。

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
居敬而行簡以臨其民不亦可乎居簡而
行簡無乃大簡乎子曰雍之言然
唯天下至誠爲能經綸天下之大經
日月有明容光必照焉
易
君子進德脩業忠信所以進德也脩辭立
其誠所以居業也知至至之可與幾也
===
知終終之可與存義也
說而巽孚乃化邦也
然則聖人之意其不可見乎子曰聖人立
象以盡意設卦以盡情僞繫辭焉以盡
其言變而通之以盡利鼓之舞之以盡
神乾坤其易之縕耶乾坤成列而易立
乎其中矣
大有衆也同人親也
書
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

「居敬而行簡，以臨其民，不亦可乎？居簡而行簡，無乃大簡乎？」子曰：「雍之言然。」
唯天下至誠，爲能經綸天下之大經。
日月有明，容光必照焉。

易

君子進德脩業。忠信，所以進德也；脩辭立其誠，所以居業也。知至至之，可與幾也；知終終之，可與存義也。
說而巽，孚乃化邦也。
然則聖人之意，其不可見乎？子曰：聖人立象以盡意，設卦以盡情僞，繫辭焉以盡其言，變而通之以盡利，鼓之舞之以盡神。乾坤其易之縕耶？乾坤成列，而易立乎其中矣。
大有，衆也。同人，親也。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"To abide in reverence and practice simplicity in governing one's people—is that not acceptable? To abide in simplicity and practice simplicity—is that not overly simple?" The Master said: "What Yong says is right."
Only one who is possessed of the utmost sincerity in the world is able to order and adjust the great invariable relations of the world.
The sun and moon have their brightness, so that every chink that admits light is illuminated by them.

Book of Changes (Yi)

The noble man advances in virtue and cultivates his enterprise. Loyalty and trustworthiness are the means by which he advances in virtue; cultivating his words to establish his sincerity is the means by which he abides in his enterprise. Knowing the point to be reached and reaching it, he can deal with the subtle springs of things; knowing the end and ending with it, he can preserve rightness.
Joyous and yet penetratingly compliant, his trustworthiness thus transforms the states.
Then can the intent of the sages not be seen? The Master said: The sages established the images in order to express their intent fully; they set up the hexagrams in order to express the true and false conditions of things fully; they appended the judgments to them in order to express their words fully; they changed and made them pass through in order to express the benefit fully; they drummed and danced them in order to express the spirit-like fully. Are not Qian and Kun the secret store of the Changes? When Qian and Kun are set in array, the Changes are established in their midst.
Da You (Great Possession) means abundance; Tong Ren (Fellowship with Men) means affection.

Book of Documents (Shu)

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
臣哉鄰哉鄰哉臣哉禹曰俞帝曰臣作朕
股肱耳目
王忱不艱允協于先王成德
其汝克敬德明我俊民
澤潤生民四夷左衽罔不咸賴
詩
坎坎伐檀兮寘之河之干兮河水清且漣
猗
俾爾多益以莫不庶
===
思齊大任文王之母思媚周姜京室之婦
大姒嗣徽音則百斯男
王釐爾成來咨來茹嗟嗟保介維莫之春
亦又何求如何新畬於皇來牟將受厥
明明昭上帝迄用康年命我眾人庤乃
錢鎛奄觀銍艾
春秋
祭公來遂逆王后于紀桓公八年春紀季
姜歸于京師桓公九年
punctuated:
「臣哉鄰哉！鄰哉臣哉！」禹曰：「俞。」帝曰：「臣作朕股肱耳目。」
「王忱不艱，允協于先王成德。」
「其汝克敬德，明我俊民。」
「澤潤生民，四夷左衽，罔不咸賴。」

《詩》
「坎坎伐檀兮，寘之河之干兮，河水清且漣猗。」
「俾爾多益，以莫不庶。」
「思齊大任，文王之母，思媚周姜，京室之婦。大姒嗣徽音，則百斯男。」
「王釐爾成，來咨來茹。嗟嗟保介，維莫之春，亦又何求？如何新畬？於皇來牟，將受厥明。明昭上帝，迄用康年。命我眾人，庤乃錢鎛，奄觀銍艾。」

《春秋》
「祭公來，遂逆王后于紀。」桓公八年。「春，紀季姜歸于京師。」桓公九年。
translation_en:
"Ministers indeed! Associates indeed! Associates indeed! Ministers indeed!" Yu said, "Yes!" The Emperor said, "My ministers act as my legs and arms, my ears and eyes."
"The King's sincerity is not beset by difficulty; it truly accords with the accomplished virtue of the Former Kings."
"May you be able to revere virtue and bring to light our eminent men."
"His beneficence moistens the living people; the four barbarian tribes who fasten their garments on the left all without exception rely on him."

Book of Odes (Shi)
"Kan-kan go the blows as they chop the sandalwood, and place it on the bank of the River; the waters of the River are clear and rippling."
"May He grant you abundant increase, so that there is nothing not plentiful."
"Reverent and莊 [composed] was Tairen, the mother of King Wen; lovingly she served Zhou Jiang, as the wife of the royal house. Taisi succeeded to her admirable renown, and a hundred sons were born to her."
"The King has granted you the completed achievement; come to consult, come to deliberate. Ah, the assistant officers of husbandry! It is now the end of spring—what more do you seek? How is it with the new fields and the fields of the third year? Oh, splendid are the wheat and barley; we shall soon receive their bright bounty. Bright and glorious is the Lord on High, who will bring us a year of plenty. Order all our multitude to prepare their spades and hoes; soon we shall see the sickles reaping."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"The Duke of Zhai came, and thereupon went to meet the Queen in Ji" (8th year of Duke Huan). "In spring, Ji Jiang of Ji went as bride to the capital" (9th year of Duke Huan).

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
冬楚子使椒來聘〔文公九年〕
楚人執鄭行人良霄〔襄公十有一年〕夏楚
子蔡侯陳侯鄭伯許男徐子滕子頓子
胡子沈子小邾子宋世子佐淮夷會于
申〔昭公四年〕
秋晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年〕
禮記
是故禮者君之大柄也
近者說服而遠者懷之此大學之道也
===
脩身及家平均天下此古樂之發也
子民如父母有憯怛之愛有忠利之教親
而尊安而敬威而愛富而有禮惠而能
散其君子尊仁畏義恥費輕實忠而不
犯義而順文而靜寬而有辨甫刑曰德
威惟威德明惟明非虞帝其孰能如此
乎
第貳塲
論
punctuated:
冬，楚子使椒來聘。〔文公九年〕
楚人執鄭行人良霄。〔襄公十有一年〕夏，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申。〔昭公四年〕
秋，晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞。〔昭公十有五年〕

禮記
是故禮者，君之大柄也。
近者說服而遠者懷之，此大學之道也。
脩身及家，平均天下，此古樂之發也。
子民如父母，有憯怛之愛，有忠利之教，親而尊，安而敬，威而愛，富而有禮，惠而能散。其君子尊仁畏義，恥費輕實，忠而不犯，義而順，文而靜，寬而有辨。《甫刑》曰：「德威惟威，德明惟明。」非虞帝其孰能如此乎？

第貳塲
論
translation_en:
In winter, the Viscount of Chu sent Jiao on a mission of friendly inquiries to our court. [9th year of Duke Wen]
The people of Chu seized Liang Xiao, the messenger of Zheng. [11th year of Duke Xiang] In summer, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Viscount of Xu, the Viscount of Teng, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Shen, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, Heir Apparent Zuo of Song, and the Huai Yi met at Shen. [4th year of Duke Zhao]
In autumn, Xun Wu of Jin led an army to attack Xianyu. [15th year of Duke Zhao]

Record of Rites (Liji)
Therefore, ritual is the great handle of the ruler.
Those who are near are pleased and submit, while those who are distant cherish him: this is the Way of the Great Learning.
Cultivating the person, extending it to the family, and bringing equilibrium and peace to all under Heaven: this is the manifestation of ancient music.
Treating the people as children just as parents do, possessing a deeply sympathetic love and a teaching of loyalty and benefit, they are intimate yet revered, at ease yet respected, awe-inspiring yet loved, wealthy yet observant of ritual, and beneficent yet able to distribute their bounty. Their gentlemen honor benevolence and stand in awe of righteousness, are ashamed of extravagance and think lightly of material wealth, are loyal without offending, righteous and compliant, accomplished and tranquil, magnanimous yet discerning. The "Punishments of Fu" (Fu xing) says: "Through the majesty of virtue they are held in awe; through the brilliance of virtue they are enlightened." Who but the Emperor of Yu (Shun) could be like this?

Second Session
Discourse

和十年
