Five Policy Questions (ce):
Question: For the foundation of kingly enterprise, nothing is more important than agriculture and sericulture. In the Zhou dynasty, from the time Hou Ji 后稷 laid the foundation and Kings Wen 文 and Wu 武 continued the line, they personally plowed and personally tended silkworms to set an example for the world. The established laws of that era are preserved in the canonical texts; can they be recounted in full? Examining what the Book of Odes (Shi 詩) and the Book of Documents (Shu 書) say about the former dukes…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
先王未聞親耕親蠶之禮乃王業實肇
基是時其故何歟自漢而後亦有足稱
者歟我
太祖高皇帝再造區寰軫念民瘼伏讀元年之
詔與
廷諭諸臣孰非萬世當服膺者可得而恭述歟
列聖繼體崇實嗣徽務本有
訓織婦有
詞穀祇蠶壇有
===
賦悉心於民依之念說者謂軼周室而過之
亦可陳其槩歟我
皇上
冲年御宇卹災蠲賦加
惠黎元至渥也是歲仲春
俞廷臣之請脩籍禮有日矣未幾有
旨期於來年意必有待將二者並舉以重
盛典歟頃因春雨特廑
天語令農夫乘時力田無惰業聞者莫不舉手
punctuated: 先王，未聞親耕、親蠶之禮，乃王業實肇基是時，其故何歟？自漢而後，亦有足稱者歟？我太祖高皇帝再造區寰，軫念民瘼。伏讀元年之詔，與廷諭諸臣，孰非萬世當服膺者？可得而恭述歟？列聖繼體，崇實嗣徽：務本有訓，織婦有詞，穀祇、蠶壇有賦，悉心於民依之念，說者謂軼周室而過之，亦可陳其槩歟？我皇上冲年御宇，卹災蠲賦，加惠黎元至渥也。是歲仲春，俞廷臣之請，脩籍禮有日矣。未幾，有旨期於來年，意必有待，將二者並舉以重盛典歟？頃因春雨，特廑天語，令農夫乘時力田，無惰業。聞者莫不舉手
translation_en:
… and former kings, one does not hear of the rites of personal plowing and personal sericulture, yet the royal enterprise truly laid its foundation at that time—what is the reason for this? From the Han dynasty onward, were there also those worthy of praise?

Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), recreated the realm and showed deep concern for the distress of the people. Humbly reading the Edict of the First Year and his court admonitions to the various officials, which of them is not something to be cherished for ten thousand generations? Can you reverently recount them? Successive sacred emperors inherited the throne, esteeming practical substance and continuing this fine legacy: there were instructions on attending to the fundamentals, lyrics on weaving women, and rhapsodies on the Altar of Grain and the Altar of Silkworms. Wholeheartedly devoted to thought for the people's livelihood, commentators say they surpassed and exceeded the house of Zhou—can you also set forth the general outline of this?

Our August Emperor ascended the throne in his youth, relieving disasters and remitting taxes, bestowing most generous favor upon the common people. In the second month of spring this year, he approved the request of the court officials, and a date had been set for performing the ritual plowing of the imperial field. Before long, an imperial decree postponed it until next year. Surely there is something awaited—will both rites be held together so as to give added weight to the grand ceremony? Recently, on account of the spring rains, he specially issued imperial words ordering farmers to seize the season to work the fields and not be lazy in their occupations. Among those who heard this, none failed to raise their hands…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
加額思見
仁政之成真千載一時也多士躬逢
盛世沐浴太和願颺言之以附於豳風無逸之
歌
問天下之事未有不玩於習而作於明主
者授人以官而不考其成是權不懸而
欲輕重辨也堯命舜曰詢事考成乃言
底可績臯陶曰屢省乃成此在後世且
以為督責之術而唐虞行之輒成無為
===
之治何歟春秋所紀有自朝日至日入
無不自計乃職者周禮所紀有歲時月
日無不有考者此悉遵唐虞之遺以致
盛治而後之稱綜核稱總攬稱强明果
敢者又卒不免有遺議也抑又何歟我
祖宗
列聖以來法紀嚴明稽核整肅上下奉行至兢
兢也乃近者狃於治平日就媮安即所
上計簿入
punctuated:
加額，思見仁政之成，真千載一時也。多士躬逢盛世，沐浴太和，願颺言之，以附於《豳風》、《無逸》之歌。

問：天下之事，未有不玩於習而作於明主者。授人以官而不考其成，是權不懸而欲輕重辨也。堯命舜曰：「詢事考成，乃言底可績。」臯陶曰：「屢省乃成。」此在後世且以為督責之術，而唐、虞行之，輒成無為之治，何歟？《春秋》所紀，有自朝日至日入無不自計乃職者；《周禮》所紀，有歲、時、月、日無不有考者。此悉遵唐、虞之遺以致盛治；而後之稱綜核、稱總攬、稱强明果敢者，又卒不免有遺議也，抑又何歟？我祖宗列聖以來，法紀嚴明，稽核整肅，上下奉行至兢兢也。乃近者狃於治平，日就媮安，即所上計簿入
translation_en:
… [raise their hands] to their foreheads in joy, longing to see the perfection of benevolent governance—truly a once-in-a-thousand-years opportunity! You gentlemen have personally encountered a flourishing age and bathed in great harmony; I hope you will set forth your views at length, so as to append them to the songs of the "Odes of Bin" (Binfeng) and "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi).

Question: Among the affairs of the world, there are none that do not grow lax through habit and become invigorated under an enlightened ruler. To confer office upon men without evaluating their achievements is like wishing to distinguish light from heavy without suspending the steelyard weight. When Yao charged Shun, he said: "Inquire into affairs and examine achievements [standard text: words], and your words can be brought to accomplishment." Gao Yao said: "Frequently examine into their achievements." In later ages, this would even be regarded as a technique for harsh supervision and责 (accountability-enforcement), yet when practiced in the Tang and Yu eras [of Yao and Shun], it invariably achieved governance through non-action (wuwei). Why is this? In what is recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) [or rather, Guoyu], there were those who from morning until sunset never failed to take account of their own duties; in what is recorded in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), there were evaluations for every year, season, month, and day. All of these followed the legacy of Tang and Yu to bring about flourishing governance; yet those in later times who were praised for comprehensive verification, for gathering all authority into their own hands, or for being forceful, incisive, and resolute, ultimately could not avoid lingering criticism. Why, again, is this? Since the time of Our Imperial Ancestors and Successive Sacred Emperors, laws and discipline have been strict and clear, and auditing and verification orderly and solemn; superiors and inferiors have carried them out with the utmost circumspection. Yet recently, accustomed to peace and order, officials daily sink into indolent ease, so that even with the account registers submitted for…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖覽者每廢時日我
皇上從輔臣請稽査積年章奏立限考成非唐
虞詢事考言意哉中外臣工罔不滌玩
愒改觀聽月有成歲有報矣欲自今行
之永永不替不知此外尚有當講可以
佐此者歟諸士行且服官聽任使者請
先言之以觀用世之具
問守令者民之師帥繫焉而建威銷萌則
在良將二者所需至亟矣粤西去
===
天萬里地瘠民貧且夷落盤錯其間時出爲患
所需二者不尤亟歟乃談達不羈之士
謂此地不足起名則何昔之垂聲西土
彬彬盛也試質所聞彼鬱林之廉石伏
波之銅柱爛然睹已有刺容管而綏定
八州有令布山而惠及𡠾嫠有順俗設
敎禁而士人得師有睦鄰諭酋豪而蠻
夷歸命均稱良吏矣孰爲優歟有紿士
焚營而卜陽破有誑諜逸囚而曹成遯
punctuated:
聖覽者，每廢時日。我皇上從輔臣請，稽査積年章奏，立限考成，非唐、虞詢事考言意哉？中外臣工，罔不滌玩愒、改觀聽，月有成、歲有報矣。欲自今行之，永永不替，不知此外尚有當講可以佐此者歟？諸士行且服官聽任使者，請先言之，以觀用世之具。
問：守令者，民之師帥繫焉；而建威銷萌，則在良將。二者所需至亟矣。粤西去天萬里，地瘠民貧，且夷落盤錯其間，時出爲患，所需二者不尤亟歟？乃談達不羈之士，謂此地不足起名，則何昔之垂聲西土，彬彬盛也？試質所聞：彼鬱林之廉石、伏波之銅柱，爛然睹已。有刺容管而綏定八州，有令布山而惠及𡠾嫠，有順俗設敎禁而士人得師，有睦鄰諭酋豪而蠻夷歸命，均稱良吏矣，孰爲優歟？有紿士焚營而卜陽破，有誑諜逸囚而曹成遯，
translation_en:
… for His Majesty's perusal often waste time and drag on for days. Our Sovereign has followed the request of the Grand Secretaries to inspect the memorials accumulated over the years and to establish deadlines for evaluating their completion—is this not the very intent of Tang and Yu in inquiring into affairs and examining words? Officials at court and in the provinces have all cleansed themselves of negligence and complacency, renewing what they see and hear, so that every month there are accomplishments and every year there are reports. If we wish to carry this out from now on forever without decline, I wonder whether beyond this there are still other matters that ought to be discussed to assist in this effort? You gentlemen are about to take office and await appointment and service; please speak of this first, so that we may observe your wherewithal for serving the world.

Question: On prefects and magistrates depends the leadership and guidance of the people; whereas establishing awe and nipping rebellion in the bud rests with good generals. The need for both is extremely urgent. Western Yue [Guangxi] is ten thousand li distant from the imperial court; its soil is barren and its people are poor, and moreover non-Chinese settlements are intertwined throughout the region, emerging from time to time to cause trouble. Is not the need for both even more urgent here? Yet unrestrained men who talk of advancement claim that this region is insufficient for making a name for oneself—why then were those who left behind a reputation in this western land in times past so flourishing and illustrious? Let us examine what we have heard: that "Stone of Integrity" at Yulin and the bronze pillars of the Wave-Subduing General [Ma Yuan 馬援] are already brilliantly visible. There was one who served as Prefect of the Rong District Command and pacified eight prefectures; there was one who served as Magistrate of Bushan and whose benevolence reached widows; there was one who established teachings and prohibitions in accordance with local customs so that scholars and the people gained a teacher; and there was one who maintained harmony with neighbors and instructed the chieftains so that the southern tribespeople submitted to authority. All of these are praised as good officials—which of them was superior? There was one who tricked his soldiers into burning the camp and thereby defeated Bu Yang; there was one who deceived spies and let prisoners escape and thereby caused Cao Cheng to flee; …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有斬袁用而儂智高敗走有趙懷遠而
羅世念請降均稱良將矣孰最奇歟今
主上神聖加意宇内大簡文武吏士計安元元
嚴且悉矣頃
徵郡國縣道治行最者增秩優異之介胄有乘
一障畫一策卽拔起戎行爲軍鋒冠士
生斯時有不自矜奮者非夫也果人人
各抒所抱卓有昔人風歟抑溺其職者
未盡無歟玆欲宣
===
德振威民安閭里夷戢疆埸則何所施設哉諸
士其悉意陳之母遜
問善理財者不加賦而國自足說者謂無
是理然至於賦必不可加而用必不可
不足也則謂之何今之稱瘠土者孰過
粤西乃其備征勦急歳用也又孰過粤
西吾於此得二策焉鹽筴者籌國長計
也自管子制鹽禁一切生于木産于池
煑于海者俱掌之官爲經國之助粤西
punctuated:
有斬袁用而儂智高敗走，有趙懷遠而羅世念請降，均稱良將矣，孰最奇歟？今主上神聖，加意宇内，大簡文武吏士，計安元元，嚴且悉矣。頃徵郡國縣道治行最者，增秩優異之；介胄有乘一障、畫一策，卽拔起戎行，爲軍鋒冠。士生斯時，有不自矜奮者，非夫也。果人人各抒所抱，卓有昔人風歟？抑溺其職者未盡無歟？玆欲宣德振威，民安閭里，夷戢疆埸，則何所施設哉？諸士其悉意陳之，母遜。
問：善理財者，不加賦而國自足，說者謂無是理。然至於賦必不可加，而用必不可不足也，則謂之何？今之稱瘠土者，孰過粤西？乃其備征勦、急歳用也，又孰過粤西？吾於此得二策焉。鹽筴者，籌國長計也。自管子制鹽禁，一切生于木、産于池、煑于海者，俱掌之官，爲經國之助。粤西
translation_en:
… there was one who executed Yuan Yong 袁用 and caused Nong Zhigao 儂智高 to be defeated and flee; and there was one who rushed to Huaiyuan 懷遠 [趙懷遠, for 趨懷遠?] so that Luo Shinian 羅世念 begged to surrender. All of these are acclaimed as fine generals—which of them was the most extraordinary?

Today, our Sovereign is divinely sage and pays close heed to the entire realm, conducting a grand selection of civil and military officials and officers to devise plans for giving peace to the common people, with both strictness and thoroughness. Recently, those in the commanderies, principalities, counties, and marches whose administrative performance was rated the best were summoned and specially distinguished with increased ranks; and among armored soldiers, anyone who guarded a single fort or devised a single plan has been immediately promoted out of the ranks to lead the vanguard of the army. For a gentleman born in such times not to take pride in rousing himself to action would be unworthy of a true man. Does everyone indeed pour forth what he cherishes within, standing out with the air of the ancients? Or are those who fail in their duties not yet entirely absent? Now, if we wish to proclaim virtue and project awe, so that the people live in peace in their villages and the non-Chinese tribes are restrained on the frontiers, what measures should be instituted? Let you gentlemen set forth your thoughts in full, and do not hold back.

Question: That one who is skilled at managing finances can make the state sufficient in itself without increasing taxes is something commentators say makes no sense. Yet when one reaches a point where taxes absolutely cannot be increased, and expenditures absolutely cannot fall short, what is to be said of it? Among the places today called barren lands, which surpasses Guangxi (Yuexi 粤西)? And yet in preparing for punitive expeditions and pressing for annual expenditures, which again surpasses Guangxi? On this matter I have obtained two policies. The salt monopoly is a long-term plan for financing the state. Ever since Master Guan (Guanzi 管子) established salt prohibitions, all salt—whether grown on trees, produced in salt ponds, or boiled from the sea—has been managed by officials as an aid in governing the state. Guangxi…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
非產鹽之地近議出公帑轉鬻南海輸
之湖湘計歲入可當常賦一二矣比聞
湘湖之間稍稍稱苦鹽食國計既不可
廢而民困又不可不理也將何道以處
之而使公私兩利耶泉布自然之利自
周立圜府而八兩五銖鵞眼綖環制益
紛紛比歲海宇開局鑄錢乃粤西錢法
流行獨易即今稍有贏羨可備兵荒需
矣但地處極邊無所得銅以故開爐為
===
獨少今且苦於銅之不繼銅不繼將至
廢局將何道以通之而使經久可行耶
此二者粤西以縮為盈之術也子多士
留心世務日久况桑梓哉願有以相告
問兵者不得已而用也然亦有不可不用
粤西猺獞雜居山谷盤錯深箐陰木莫
知涯際固盜賊之所必穴也胡可無兵
勿論往事姑以近日言之無古田之舉
胡以成永寧無府江之舉胡以安平樂
punctuated:
非產鹽之地。近議出公帑轉鬻南海，輸之湖湘，計歲入可當常賦一二矣。比聞湘湖之間稍稍稱苦鹽食，國計既不可廢，而民困又不可不理也，將何道以處之，而使公私兩利耶？泉布，自然之利，自周立圜府，而八兩、五銖、鵞眼、綖環，制益紛紛。比歲海宇開局鑄錢，乃粤西錢法流行獨易，即今稍有贏羨，可備兵荒需矣。但地處極邊，無所得銅，以故開爐為獨少。今且苦於銅之不繼，銅不繼將至廢局，將何道以通之，而使經久可行耶？此二者，粤西以縮為盈之術也。子多士留心世務日久，况桑梓哉，願有以相告。

問：兵者，不得已而用也；然亦有不可不用。粤西猺獞雜居，山谷盤錯，深箐陰木，莫知涯際，固盜賊之所必穴也，胡可無兵？勿論往事，姑以近日言之：無古田之舉，胡以成永寧？無府江之舉，胡以安平樂？
translation_en:
… is not a salt-producing region. Recently it was proposed to disburse public funds to buy salt for resale from Nanhai and transport it to the Huxiang region, with the estimated annual revenue amounting to one or two tenths of the regular tax quota. Lately, however, we hear that people in the Xiang and Hu area are beginning to complain of hardships regarding salt consumption. Since state fiscal planning cannot be abandoned and the distress of the people cannot go unaddressed, by what method should we manage this so that both public and private interests benefit? Coinage is a natural source of profit. Ever since the Zhou established the Treasury of Round Money (Huanfu), systems such as the eight-liang, five-zhu, goose-eye (eyan), and string-ring (yanhuan) coins have proliferated in great variety. In recent years, mints have been opened across the empire to cast coins, yet in Guangxi alone the circulation of coinage has been unusually smooth; right now there is even a modest surplus that can be held in reserve for military needs and famine relief. However, because the region lies on the far frontier, there is nowhere to obtain copper, and for this reason the number of furnaces opened is uniquely small. Now we are furthermore plagued by the failure of copper supplies to keep up, and if copper supplies fail to keep up, it will lead to the closing of the mints. By what method can we resolve this bottleneck so that the practice remains viable over the long term? These two measures are techniques for turning scarcity into surplus in Guangxi. You gentlemen have long paid close attention to worldly affairs—all the more so when they concern your own native homeland! I hope you will have advice to offer.

Question: Military force is used only when there is no alternative; yet there are also times when it cannot but be used. In Guangxi, the Yao and Zhuang peoples live intermingled; the mountains and valleys twist and interlock, with dense bamboo thickets and dark woods whose limits no one knows. It is naturally a place where bandits and rebels are bound to make their lairs—how could one do without troops? Leaving aside past events, let us speak only of recent days: without the campaign in Gutian, how could Yongning have been established? Without the campaign along the Fu River (Fujiang), how could Pingle have been pacified? …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
信哉荆棘必剪而後嘉禾可生也比歲
粵東大征羅旁并議及粵西之六十三
山七山等巢時以兵糧弗繼暫從撫處
今西之諸巢未聞叛迹東之餘孽旋肆
跳梁撫與勦孰為長算耶說者謂東西
賊巢彼此藏匿非一時夾勦難語全功
而兵興糧從費且鉅萬粵西空乏何以
辦此耶狼兵一調騷擾村邑大眾一動
玉石俱焚何以戢悍卒保善類耶舉事
===
不難難於善後根株不拔勢必滋蔓功
旣告成何以揷羣黎成久安耶然諸巢
與粵東為鄰阻在一隅乃八寨稱腹心
患征勦之師果孰所當先孰所當後耶
多士生于其鄉籌之已熟其詳著于篇
此旦夕見之施行者毋虛談
punctuated: 信哉！荆棘必剪，而後嘉禾可生也。比歲粵東大征羅旁，并議及粵西之六十三山、七山等巢，時以兵糧弗繼，暫從撫處。今西之諸巢未聞叛迹，東之餘孽旋肆跳梁，撫與勦孰為長算耶？說者謂東西賊巢彼此藏匿，非一時夾勦，難語全功；而兵興糧從，費且鉅萬，粵西空乏，何以辦此耶？狼兵一調，騷擾村邑；大眾一動，玉石俱焚，何以戢悍卒、保善類耶？舉事不難，難於善後；根株不拔，勢必滋蔓。功旣告成，何以揷羣黎、成久安耶？然諸巢與粵東為鄰，阻在一隅，乃八寨稱腹心患，征勦之師，果孰所當先、孰所當後耶？多士生于其鄉，籌之已熟，其詳著于篇。此旦夕見之施行者，毋虛談。
translation_en:
Truly, the brambles and thorns must be cut away before the fine grain can grow! In recent years, when Guangdong launched a major campaign against Luopang 羅旁, deliberations also extended to the strongholds in Guangxi such as the Sixty-Three Mountains (Liushisan shan 六十三山) and Seven Mountains (Qishan 七山). At that time, because troops and provisions could not be sustained, a policy of pacification and settlement was temporarily adopted. Now, no signs of rebellion have been heard from the various strongholds in the west, yet the remaining miscreants in the east have soon begun to rampage recklessly again. Between pacification and extermination, which is the superior long-term strategy?

Some argue that the bandit strongholds in the east and west harbor one another, and that unless they are caught in a simultaneous pincer attack, it will be difficult to speak of complete success. Yet when troops are mobilized, provisions must follow, at a cost of tens of thousands. Given the exhaustion and scarcity in Guangxi, how can this be managed? Once the native "wolf troops" (langbing 狼兵) are requisitioned, they harass the villages and towns; once a great force is set in motion, jade and stone are burned alike. How can we restrain fierce soldiers and protect the good people? Initiating an action is not difficult; what is difficult is the post-war reconstruction. If the roots and stumps are not pulled up, the weeds will inevitably spread again. Once the campaign is declared a success, how should we settle the common people and achieve lasting peace? Moreover, while those strongholds bordering Guangdong are isolated in one corner, the Eight Stockades (Bazhai 八寨) are known as an affliction in our very heartland. In dispatching forces for punitive extermination, which should indeed come first, and which should come later?

You gentlemen were born in this region and have long pondered these matters thoroughly. Set forth your detailed views in your essays. These are measures to be put into practice at any moment—do not indulge in empty talk!
