title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
居敬而行簡以臨其民不亦可乎居簡而
行簡無乃大簡乎子曰雍之言然
王應泰
同考試官教諭王批君子執簡御煩惟在一敬
是作說理明透詞約意足殆可與論簡者宜錄以式
考試官教諭陳批簡當得體
考試官教諭尹批醇雅可誦
===
賢者以敬論簡而聖人與之也蓋簡主於敬而
一於簡焉不可也聖人所以然賢者之言與仲
弓見夫子可伯子之簡而言曰簡一也行之在
天下而居之在吾心論簡者顧所以居之何如
耳居之以敬吾心之自治嚴矣而行之以簡順
其所無事焉是我有執而民無擾也或者其可
乎居之以簡吾心之自治疎矣而所行又簡廢
其所有事焉是我無執而民斯玩也無乃太簡
乎是夫子之可伯子微詞也仲弓未之喻也而
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「居敬而行簡，以臨其民，不亦可乎？居簡而行簡，無乃大簡乎？」子曰：「雍之言然。」

王應泰

同考試官教諭王批：「君子執簡御煩，惟在一敬。是作說理明透，詞約意足，殆可與論簡者，宜錄以式。」
考試官教諭陳批：「簡當得體。」
考試官教諭尹批：「醇雅可誦。」

賢者以敬論簡，而聖人與之也。蓋簡主於敬，而一於簡焉，不可也，聖人所以然賢者之言與！仲弓見夫子可伯子之簡而言曰：「簡一也，行之在天下，而居之在吾心，論簡者顧所以居之何如耳。居之以敬，吾心之自治嚴矣，而行之以簡，順其所無事焉，是我有執而民無擾也，或者其可乎？居之以簡，吾心之自治疎矣，而所行又簡，廢其所有事焉，是我無執而民斯玩也，無乃太簡乎？」是夫子之可伯子，微詞也，仲弓未之喻也；而
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

"To abide in reverence and practice simplicity in governing one's people, is that not acceptable? To abide in simplicity and practice simplicity, is that not overly simple?" The Master said, "What Yong says is right."

Wang Yingtai 王應泰

Associate Examiner Instructor Wang 王 comments: "A gentleman holds to simplicity in governing complexity, and this rests solely on reverence. This essay explains the principle with clarity and penetration; its words are concise yet its meaning is full. One can indeed discuss simplicity with its author, and it ought to be recorded as a model."
Examiner Instructor Chen 陳 comments: "Concise, fitting, and proper in form."
Examiner Instructor Yin 尹 comments: "Pure and elegant, worthy of recitation."

The worthy discusses simplicity by means of reverence, and the Sage approves of him. Indeed, simplicity must be grounded in reverence, whereas being wholly given over to simplicity will not do; is this not why the Sage affirmed the worthy's words! When Zhonggong 仲弓 saw that the Master had approved of Bozi's 伯子 simplicity, he said: "Simplicity is one, yet practicing it lies in the world at large, whereas abiding in it lies within one's own mind; one who discusses simplicity need only look to how one abides within. If one abides in reverence, the self-governance of one's mind is strict; and when one practices simplicity, following along smoothly without making trouble, then I hold fast to a standard and the people are not disturbed—perhaps that is acceptable? If one abides in simplicity, the self-governance of one's mind is lax; and when what one practices is also simple, neglecting the affairs that ought to be attended to, then I hold to no standard and the people consequently grow trifling—is that not overly simple?" Now the Master's approval of Bozi was subtly phrased, and Zhonggong had not grasped its nuance; yet…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
仲弓之論簡確論也聖人不能易也故曰雍之
言然蓋治以有本而立雍不尚夫簡而尚夫居
敬之簡論治斯有本也率斯言而帝王垂裳之
化不外是矣道以無弊而行雍不病夫簡而病
夫居簡之簡議道斯無弊也率斯言而帝王恭
己之道不越是矣信乎其可使南面也然此乃
仲弓受之夫子者非自爲之言也其問仁也曰
見賓承祭敬也不欲勿施簡也孔門論學皆治
論治皆學非有二也南面之使亦知其請事斯
===
語者深乎故曰受之夫子也
唯天下至誠爲能經綸天下之大經
劉延祚
同考試官教諭吕批
講經綸處明析而統貫於
一誠甚得本旨非造理精到之士不能
考試官教諭陳批詞旨瑩徹
考試官教諭尹批體認精邃
中庸論至誠之盡倫所以明天道也夫大經未
易盡也非天下至誠其孰能經綸之哉中庸論
punctuated:
仲弓之論簡，確論也，聖人不能易也，故曰「雍之言然」。蓋治以有本而立，雍不尚夫簡，而尚夫居敬之簡，論治斯有本也。率斯言，而帝王垂裳之化不外是矣。道以無弊而行，雍不病夫簡，而病夫居簡之簡，議道斯無弊也。率斯言，而帝王恭己之道不越是矣。信乎其「可使南面」也！然此乃仲弓受之夫子者，非自爲之言也。其問仁也，曰「見賓、承祭」，敬也；「不欲勿施」，簡也。孔門論學皆治，論治皆學，非有二也。「南面」之使，亦知其「請事斯語」者深乎！故曰受之夫子也。

唯天下至誠爲能經綸天下之大經。
劉延祚
同考試官教諭吕批：講經綸處明析，而統貫於一誠，甚得本旨，非造理精到之士不能。
考試官教諭陳批：詞旨瑩徹。
考試官教諭尹批：體認精邃。

《中庸》論至誠之盡倫，所以明天道也。夫大經未易盡也，非天下至誠，其孰能經綸之哉？《中庸》論
translation_en:
… Zhonggong's (Ran Yong 冉雍) discourse on simplicity is a definitive judgment that even the Sage could not alter; hence he said, "Yong's words are right." Indeed, governance is established by having a foundation: Yong did not esteem simplicity in itself, but esteemed the simplicity rooted in abiding in reverence—thus his discussion of governance possessed a foundation. Follow these words, and the transformative rule of the sovereigns of antiquity who governed by merely letting their robes hang down is nothing other than this. The Way is practiced by being free of defects: Yong did not fault simplicity in itself, but faulted the simplicity rooted in abiding in simplicity—thus his deliberation on the Way was free of defects. Follow these words, and the Way of the sovereigns of antiquity who merely held themselves in reverent composure does not go beyond this. Truly, he "might be made to face south [as a ruler]"! Yet this was something Zhonggong received from the Master, not words of his own making. When he asked about humaneness (ren), the Master said, "[Go abroad as if] receiving a great guest, [employ the people as if] assisting at a great sacrifice"—that is reverence; "what you do not wish for yourself, do not impose on others"—that is simplicity. In the school of Confucius, every discussion of learning is governance, and every discussion of governance is learning; they are not two separate things. In deeming him fit to "face south," did the Master not also recognize how deeply he had taken to heart his pledge, "I beg to put these words into practice"? Therefore, I say he received it from the Master.

"Only he who is possessed of the utmost sincerity under heaven can warp and woof the great invariable relations of all under heaven."
By Liu Yanzuo 劉延祚.
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Lü comments: The explanation of warping and woofing (jinglun) is clear and analytical, while unifying everything through single-minded sincerity. It grasps the fundamental purport exceedingly well; none but a scholar who has penetrated principle with precision could achieve this.
Examiner, Instructor Chen comments: The diction and purport are luminous and penetrating.
Examiner, Instructor Yin comments: The personal realization of the truth is refined and profound.

The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) discusses how he who possesses the utmost sincerity fulfills human relationships, thereby illuminating the Way of Heaven. Now, the great invariable relations are not easily fulfilled; unless one possesses the utmost sincerity under heaven, who could warp and woof them? When the Doctrine of the Mean discusses…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
至誠功用若曰大哉倫乎其理一誠而已誠有
未至者斯倫有未盡耳唯天下至誠實理完於
天賦一心有以涵秩叙之精真機率於性成一
身有以會倫物之極大經有不得不分者唯至
誠為能經之因天下自然之等為天下而區别
焉若緒之有理而不亂也大經有不得不合者
唯至誠為能綸之因天下自然之類為天下而
聯屬焉若系之有統而無間也天合人合經雖
不一然皆本一誠以品節之則既辨其異復統
===
其同天經地誼之懿固獨惇於此矣所以為天
下立人極其在斯乎主恩主敬經雖不同然皆
本一誠以範圍之則既分其羣復聚其類民彝
物則之常固獨全於此矣所以為萬世正人紀
其在斯乎此脩道之教也而盡性至命該之矣
噫斯其為天道歟大抵至誠經綸非二也存之
聖心皆大經也發之大經皆聖心也外心以求
經綸非也中庸一書自造端夫婦及武周制作
三重九經莫非經綸地也莫非心也學者求諸
punctuated: 至誠功用，若曰：大哉倫乎！其理一誠而已。誠有未至者，斯倫有未盡耳。唯天下至誠，實理完於天賦，一心有以涵秩叙之精；真機率於性成，一身有以會倫物之極。大經有不得不分者，唯至誠為能經之，因天下自然之等，為天下而區别焉，若緒之有理而不亂也。大經有不得不合者，唯至誠為能綸之，因天下自然之類，為天下而聯屬焉，若系之有統而無間也。天合、人合，經雖不一，然皆本一誠以品節之，則既辨其異，復統其同，天經地誼之懿，固獨惇於此矣。所以為天下立人極，其在斯乎！主恩、主敬，經雖不同，然皆本一誠以範圍之，則既分其羣，復聚其類，民彝物則之常，固獨全於此矣。所以為萬世正人紀，其在斯乎！此脩道之教也，而盡性至命該之矣。噫！斯其為天道歟！大抵至誠、經綸非二也。存之聖心，皆大經也；發之大經，皆聖心也。外心以求經綸，非也。《中庸》一書，自造端夫婦，及武、周制作，三重、九經，莫非經綸地也，莫非心也。學者求諸…
translation_en: …the efficacy of utmost sincerity, as if to say: Great indeed are human relationships! Their principle is nothing more than a single sincerity. Where sincerity has not reached the utmost, these relationships cannot be fully realized. Only in one of utmost sincerity in the world is true principle complete by heavenly endowment, so that his single mind can encompass the essence of order and sequence; true vitality follows his inborn nature, so that his single person can embody the ultimate standard of human relationships and affairs. Where the great invariable relations must be differentiated, only one of utmost sincerity is able to arrange them as warp threads—following the natural gradations of the world, he distinguishes them for the sake of the world, just like silk threads that are ordered and unentangled. Where the great invariable relations must be united, only one of utmost sincerity is able to bind them together—following the natural categories of the world, he connects them for the sake of the world, just like a cord that is unified and seamless. Whether joined by Heaven or joined by man, although the invariable relations are not uniform, all are graded and regulated on the basis of a single sincerity; thus, having distinguished their differences, he again unifies their commonalities, and the beauty of Heaven's invariable relations and Earth's righteousness is uniquely upheld herein. Is it not here that the ultimate standard of humanity is established for the world? Whether governed by affection or governed by respect, although the invariable relations differ, all are encompassed and molded on the basis of a single sincerity; thus, having divided their groups, he again gathers their kinds, and the constancy of the people's moral norms and the rules of things is uniquely preserved intact herein. Is it not here that the human moral order is rectified for ten thousand generations? This is the instruction of cultivating the Way, and fulfilling one's nature and reaching Heaven's decree are encompassed within it. Alas! Is this not the Way of Heaven? In general, utmost sincerity and the ordering and binding of the great relations are not two separate things. Preserved within the sage's mind, all are the great invariable relations; manifested in the great invariable relations, all are the sage's mind. To seek to order and bind the great relations outside the mind is wrong. Throughout the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), from taking its beginning in husband and wife, to the institutions created by King Wu and the Duke of Zhou, the three things of prime importance, and the nine standard rules, there is nothing that is not a realm of ordering and binding the great relations, and nothing that is not the mind. If scholars seek it in…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
心而誠焉則經綸可幾矣
日月有明容光必照焉
文立本
同考試官教諭嚴批發揮聖道有本深切著明
而醞藉自別可以式矣
考試官教諭陳批脫去塵俗
考試官教諭尹批明潔可取
觀天象之明無遺照而聖道之有本可知矣夫
日月之無微不照者以其明之有本也觀聖道
===
者亦稽諸此而已孟子欲學聖者探其本也若
曰大哉聖人之道非自爲大也必有所似本之
者不觀諸日月乎彼日月懸象而明著焉分陰
分陽是各一其明也日月相禪而明生焉根陰
根陽是合一其明也明著而不息則光普而不
遺苟可容其光者皆其照之所必及明生而不
窮則光遠而不禦苟得容其光者皆其照之所
必徹其在四表光被之矣卽一隙之小亦旁燭
焉何光輝之盛若斯乎然則明者彰矣而所以
punctuated:
心而誠焉，則經綸可幾矣。

日月有明，容光必照焉。

文立本

同考試官教諭嚴批：發揮聖道有本，深切著明，而醞藉自別，可以式矣。

考試官教諭陳批：脫去塵俗。

考試官教諭尹批：明潔可取。

觀天象之明無遺照，而聖道之有本可知矣。夫日月之無微不照者，以其明之有本也；觀聖道者，亦稽諸此而已。孟子欲學聖者探其本也，若曰：大哉聖人之道！非自爲大也，必有所似本之者，不觀諸日月乎？彼日月懸象而明著焉，分陰分陽，是各一其明也；日月相禪而明生焉，根陰根陽，是合一其明也。明著而不息，則光普而不遺，苟可容其光者，皆其照之所必及；明生而不窮，則光遠而不禦，苟得容其光者，皆其照之所必徹。其在四表，光被之矣，卽一隙之小，亦旁燭焉，何光輝之盛若斯乎？然則明者彰矣，而所以
translation_en:
… mind and makes it sincere, then such ordering and governance can be attained.

"The sun and moon have their brightness, so that wherever light is admitted, they inevitably shine upon it." [Mencius 7A.24]

Wen Liben 文立本

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Yan 嚴: He expounds upon how the Way of the Sages has a fundamental source in a manner that is profound, incisive, and crystal clear, while its refined depth sets it apart; it may serve as a model.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Chen 陳: Free from vulgarity and worldly dust.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Yin 尹: Lucid, pure, and worthy of selection.

When one observes how the brightness of the celestial bodies leaves nothing unilluminated, one can know that the Way of the Sages has a fundamental source. Now, the reason the sun and moon leave even the tiniest crevice unilluminated is that their brightness has a fundamental source; those who observe the Way of the Sages need only examine it in light of this. Mencius wished for those learning from the Sages to seek out their fundamental source, as if to say: Great indeed is the Way of the Sages! Yet it does not become great of itself; there must be something whereby it is rooted—do you not see this in the sun and moon? Those sun and moon hang forth their images and their brightness becomes manifest: dividing yin and yang, each possesses its own distinct brightness; the sun and moon succeed one another in turn and brightness is generated: rooted in yin and rooted in yang, they unite into a single brightness. Because their brightness is manifest and unceasing, their light is universal and leaves nothing out; wherever there is a space that can admit their light, their illumination inevitably reaches it. Because their brightness is generated and inexhaustible, their light reaches afar and cannot be stopped; wherever there is a space able to admit their light, their illumination inevitably penetrates it. Throughout the four quarters of the world, their light covers all, and even into a crevice as small as a crack, it shines on all sides—how is the abundance of their radiance as great as this? Thus their brightness is made manifest, yet as for that whereby…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
運其明者孰主宰是哉其在萬古光垂之矣卽
一閒之微亦洞達焉何光昭之大若斯乎然則
明者見矣而所以貞其明者孰根柢是哉故觀
容光之必照而知日月之明之有本矣孔子之
道其大則日月之明中天者也而人皆仰之其
有本則日月之精得天者也而人孰窺之善學
者亦惟探其本而已矣本者何誠是已誠故大
語誠則孔子之一貫堯舜之執中天地之不貳
皆是道也何論日月哉噫非私淑有得者不能
===
推本言之故曰孟子之學獨識其大
易
君子進德脩業忠信所以進德也脩辭立
其誠所以居業也知至至之可與幾也
知終終之可與存義也
張孫念
同考試官敎諭嚴批講進脩處卓有定見是深
於易者允宜高薦
考試官敎諭陳批明簡可誦
punctuated:
運其明者，孰主宰是哉？其在萬古，光垂之矣，卽一閒之微，亦洞達焉，何光昭之大若斯乎？然則明者見矣，而所以貞其明者，孰根柢是哉？故觀容光之必照，而知日月之明之有本矣。孔子之道，其大則日月之明中天者也，而人皆仰之；其有本則日月之精得天者也，而人孰窺之？善學者，亦惟探其本而已矣。本者何？誠是已。誠故大。語誠，則孔子之一貫、堯舜之執中、天地之不貳，皆是道也，何論日月哉！噫！非私淑有得者，不能推本言之。故曰：孟子之學，獨識其大。

易
君子進德脩業。忠信，所以進德也；脩辭立其誠，所以居業也。知至至之，可與幾也；知終終之，可與存義也。
張孫念
同考試官敎諭嚴批：講進脩處，卓有定見，是深於《易》者，允宜高薦。
考試官敎諭陳批：明簡可誦。
translation_en:
…operates their brightness—who is the master of this? Across ten thousand ages, their light has shone down, and even the tiniest crevice is thoroughly penetrated by it—how is the greatness of their shining brilliance like this? Thus, the brightness is visible, yet as for that by which their brightness is sustained in constancy—what is the root and foundation of this? Therefore, by observing how wherever light is admitted it invariably illuminates, one knows that the brightness of the sun and moon has a fundamental source. As for the Way of Confucius, in its greatness it is like the brightness of the sun and moon in mid-heaven, which all people look up to; in its having a fundamental source, it is like the essence of the sun and moon obtained from Heaven, which who among men can fathom? Those who are good at learning simply seek out its fundamental source, and nothing more. What is this source? It is sincerity. Because it is sincere, it is great. Speaking of sincerity, the single thread of Confucius, the holding fast to the Mean of Yao and Shun, and the non-duality of Heaven and Earth are all this Way—what need is there even to speak of the sun and moon! Alas! Were one not a person who had gained insight through private emulation as a disciple, one could not trace it back to its source and speak of it thus. Therefore it is said: the learning of Mencius alone recognized what was great in him.

Book of Changes (Yi)
"The superior man advances in virtue and cultivates his sphere of duty. Loyalty and faithfulness are the means by which he advances in virtue; cultivating his words so as to establish his sincerity is the means by which he abides in his sphere of duty. Knowing what is to be reached and reaching it, he is worthy to deal with the subtle springs of things; knowing what is to be brought to an end and bringing it to an end, he is worthy to preserve righteousness."

Zhang Sunnian 張孫念
Associate Examiner, Instructor Yan 嚴 comments: Where he expounds upon advancing in virtue and cultivating one's sphere of duty, he shows an outstanding and settled view; he is one deeply versed in the Book of Changes, and truly deserves a high recommendation.
Examiner, Instructor Chen 陳 comments: Clear and concise, worthy of recitation.

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭尹批潔淨得旨
文言於君子而詳其進脩之實焉蓋君子以進
德脩業爲心者也然非忠信立誠亦何以造其
極哉文言論乾九三若謂君子者天下所由以
觀德業焉其責不易盡其心恒不自逸也九三
所以日乾而夕惕者果何心哉亦以德吾性也
業吾職也此理之合一者本無一息之或間德
欲其進也業欲其脩也此心之交儆者自無一
時之或違德何如而進耶忠信者實心也有實
===
心而實理可凝也非所以進德乎業何如而脩
耶脩詞立誠者實言也有實言而實行可履也
非所以居業乎忠信雖可以進德未可語德之
至也知其至而忠信以至之則一心有以窮其
神而幾微之理晰矣德之底於日新也不在是
歟立誠雖可以居業未可語業之終也知其終
而立誠以終之則一身有以體其化而時出之
義裕矣業之臻於富有也不在是歟噫君子進
脩之功必如是而後造其極也則其心之憂勤
punctuated:
考試官敎諭尹批：潔淨得旨。
《文言》於君子，而詳其進脩之實焉。蓋君子以進德脩業爲心者也，然非忠信立誠，亦何以造其極哉？《文言》論《乾》九三，若謂：君子者，天下所由以觀德業焉，其責不易盡，其心恒不自逸也。九三所以日乾而夕惕者，果何心哉？亦以德，吾性也；業，吾職也。此理之合一者，本無一息之或間。德欲其進也，業欲其脩也。此心之交儆者，自無一時之或違。德何如而進耶？忠信者，實心也；有實心而實理可凝也，非所以進德乎？業何如而脩耶？脩詞立誠者，實言也；有實言而實行可履也，非所以居業乎？忠信雖可以進德，未可語德之至也。知其至而忠信以至之，則一心有以窮其神，而幾微之理晰矣。德之底於日新也，不在是歟？立誠雖可以居業，未可語業之終也。知其終而立誠以終之，則一身有以體其化，而時出之義裕矣。業之臻於富有也，不在是歟？噫！君子進脩之功，必如是而後造其極也，則其心之憂勤，
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Yin's comment: Pure and clean; grasps the main import.

The Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan), with regard to the superior man, sets forth in detail the substance of his advancement and cultivation. For the superior man is one who makes advancing in virtue and cultivating his task his heart's aim; yet without loyalty, trustworthiness, and establishing sincerity, how could he ever reach the ultimate? In discussing the nine in the third place of the hexagram Qian, the Commentary on the Words of the Text seems to say: The superior man is he through whom all under heaven observe virtue and tasks; his responsibility is not easily fulfilled, and his mind never allows itself ease. Wherefore the nine in the third place is active all day and vigilantly apprehensive at night—what indeed is in his mind? It is simply that virtue is my nature, and the task is my duty. In the unity of this principle, there is originally not a single breath's interruption. Virtue he desires to advance; his task he desires to cultivate. In the mutual admonition of this mind, there is naturally not a single moment's departure. How does virtue advance? Loyalty and trustworthiness are a genuine mind; having a genuine mind, genuine principle can be consolidated—is this not the means to advance in virtue? How is the task cultivated? Cultivating words to establish sincerity is genuine speech; having genuine speech, genuine conduct can be practiced—is this not the means to abide in one's task? Although loyalty and trustworthiness can advance virtue, one cannot yet speak of the ultimate point of virtue. When one knows that ultimate point and reaches it through loyalty and trustworthiness, then with a single mind one is able to fathom its spirit, and the principles of subtle incipient tendencies become clear. Does not virtue's arriving at daily renewal lie in this? Although establishing sincerity can enable one to abide in one's task, one cannot yet speak of the completion of the task. When one knows its completion and brings it to completion by establishing sincerity, then in one's own person one is able to embody its transformations, and the righteousness brought forth at the proper time becomes abundant. Does not the task's attaining to rich possession lie in this? Ah! The effort of the superior man in advancing and cultivating must be like this before it reaches its ultimate; how then could the anxious diligence of his mind …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
寧自已哉抑是心也正君子所以法天之學也
蓋天地之德業一誠也聖人之德業亦一誠也
无妄以剛自外來而為主於內言誠大畜以剛
健篤實言日新故君子之求誠主於剛而已剛
則能誠誠故不息而憂勤惕厲之心自有所不
容已耳於戲此聖學也亦乾道也
然則聖人之意其不可見乎子曰聖人立
象以盡意設卦以盡情偽繫辭焉以盡
其言變而通之以盡利鼓之舞之以盡
===
神乾坤其易之縕耶乾坤成列而易立
乎其中矣
呂興齊
同考試官教諭嚴批發立象盡意明徹無遺
子其言足盡意者耶宜錄以式
考試官教諭陳批詞意明順
考試官教諭尹批簡淨得體
聖人所以盡意者於乾坤盡之而已蓋易不外
乎乾坤也然則盡聖人之意者舍乾坤其奚以
punctuated:
寧自已哉？抑是心也，正君子所以法天之學也。蓋天地之德業，一誠也；聖人之德業，亦一誠也。《无妄》以「剛自外來而為主於內」言誠，《大畜》以「剛健篤實」言日新。故君子之求誠，主於剛而已。剛則能誠，誠故不息，而憂勤惕厲之心，自有所不容已耳。於戲！此聖學也，亦乾道也。

「然則聖人之意，其不可見乎？子曰：聖人立象以盡意，設卦以盡情偽，繫辭焉以盡其言，變而通之以盡利，鼓之舞之以盡神。乾坤，其易之縕耶？乾坤成列，而易立乎其中矣。」

呂興齊
同考試官教諭嚴批：發「立象盡意」明徹無遺。子其言足盡意者耶！宜錄以式。
考試官教諭陳批：詞意明順。
考試官教諭尹批：簡淨得體。

聖人所以盡意者，於乾坤盡之而已。蓋《易》不外乎乾坤也，然則盡聖人之意者，舍乾坤其奚以
translation_en:
… how could it ever cease of itself? Moreover, this mind is precisely the learning by which the superior man models himself on Heaven. Indeed, the virtue and achievement of Heaven and Earth consist in a single sincerity; the virtue and achievement of the sage likewise consist in a single sincerity. The hexagram Wuwang (Innocence) speaks of sincerity in terms of "the firm coming from without and becoming master within," while the hexagram Daxu (Great Accumulation) speaks of daily renewal in terms of "firmness, strength, and substantiality." Therefore, the superior man's pursuit of sincerity centers simply on firmness. Being firm, he can be sincere; being sincere, he is unceasing, and his mind of anxious diligence and vigilant caution naturally cannot stop itself. Alas! This is the learning of the sages, and it is also the Way of Qian.

"Then can the intentions of the sages not be seen? The Master said: The sages established the images in order to express their intentions fully; they set up the hexagrams in order to express the true and the false fully; they appended the explanations in order to express their words fully; they changed and adapted them in order to express the benefit fully; they drummed and danced them in order to express the spirit fully. Are not Qian and Kun the secret store of the Changes? When Qian and Kun are set in array, the Changes are established within them."

Lü Xingqi 呂興齊
Associate Examiner and Instructor Yan 嚴 comments: He elucidates "establishing the images to express the intentions fully" with thorough clarity, leaving nothing out. Are not your words sufficient to express the intentions fully? This should be recorded as a model.
Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳 comments: The diction and meaning are clear and smooth.
Examiner and Instructor Yin 尹 comments: Concise, clean, and fitting in style.

That by which the sages expressed their intentions fully was simply to express them fully in Qian and Kun. For the Book of Changes (Yi) does not go beyond Qian and Kun; if so, in expressing the intentions of the sages fully, apart from Qian and Kun how could one…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
哉大傳若曰甚矣哉聖人覺民之意無窮也然
意無窮而言有限聖人蓋有不能恝然者是豈
終無可見哉亦以聖人之意盡於象象之理盡
於乾坤故仰觀俯察而聖心之擬議者旣立夫
奇偶之畫斯類情體撰而聖意之包涵者自洩
於形象之表由是重之而爲卦而情僞盡焉發
之而爲辭而言盡焉莫非象也亦莫非意之所
由盡也由是通變于民而利盡焉鼓舞于民而
神盡焉莫非象也亦莫非意之所由盡也夫乾
===
坤未立意固以默而藏乾坤旣立意遂以象而
顯則乾坤也一易之縕也何也乾列于左而凡
陽之易而爲陰者胥立本于其中坤列于右而
凡陰之易而爲陽者悉肇端乎其內所以設卦
繫辭者從此出也所以通變鼓舞者從此推也
易之縕不歸於乾坤而何吁此乾坤之象所以
立也此聖人之意所以盡也善學易者因其象
之立求其意之存其於易也思過半矣雖然易
一陰陽也陰陽一太極也反求諸心而各足也
punctuated: 哉？大傳若曰：甚矣哉，聖人覺民之意無窮也！然意無窮而言有限，聖人蓋有不能恝然者，是豈終無可見哉？亦以聖人之意盡於象，象之理盡於乾坤。故仰觀俯察，而聖心之擬議者，旣立夫奇偶之畫；斯類情體撰，而聖意之包涵者，自洩於形象之表。由是重之而爲卦，而情僞盡焉；發之而爲辭，而言盡焉。莫非象也，亦莫非意之所由盡也。由是通變于民，而利盡焉；鼓舞于民，而神盡焉。莫非象也，亦莫非意之所由盡也。夫乾坤未立，意固以默而藏；乾坤旣立，意遂以象而顯。則乾坤也，一易之縕也。何也？乾列于左，而凡陽之易而爲陰者，胥立本于其中；坤列于右，而凡陰之易而爲陽者，悉肇端乎其內。所以設卦繫辭者，從此出也；所以通變鼓舞者，從此推也。易之縕不歸於乾坤而何？吁！此乾坤之象所以立也，此聖人之意所以盡也。善學易者，因其象之立，求其意之存，其於易也，思過半矣。雖然，易一陰陽也，陰陽一太極也，反求諸心而各足也。
translation_en:
… [apart from Qian and Kun, how else could it be done]?

It is as though the Great Commentary (Dazhuan) were saying: How profound indeed is the boundless intention of the sages to awaken the people! Yet while their intention is boundless, words are finite; the sages could not remain unconcerned about this, so how could their intention ultimately remain invisible? It is simply because the intention of the sages is fully expressed in the images (xiang), and the principle of the images is fully expressed in Qian and Kun. Therefore, gazing up to contemplate and looking down to examine, what the sages pondered and deliberated in their minds was established in the odd and even lines; thus, categorizing the dispositions of things and embodying the operations of the world, what was encompassed within the sages' intention naturally revealed itself beyond physical forms and appearances. From this, the lines were doubled to form the hexagrams, and the true and false dispositions of things were fully expressed therein; they were articulated as the appended verbalizations, and words were fully expressed therein. None of this is anything other than the images, and none of it is anything other than the means by which the intention is fully expressed. From this, transformations were communicated to the people, and benefit was fully realized therein; the people were inspired and set in motion, and the numinous was fully realized therein. None of this is anything other than the images, and none of it is anything other than the means by which the intention is fully expressed.

Now, before Qian and Kun were established, the intention was indeed silently hidden away; once Qian and Kun were established, the intention was thereupon made manifest through the images. Thus Qian and Kun are the very essence (yun) of the Changes (Yi). Why is this? Qian is arrayed on the left, and all cases in which yang changes and becomes yin establish their root within it; Kun is arrayed on the right, and all cases in which yin changes and becomes yang originate within it. That by which the hexagrams are set up and the verbalizations appended issues forth from this; that by which transformations are communicated and the people are inspired is extended from this. If the essence of the Changes does not come down to Qian and Kun, then to what does it come down?

Ah! This is why the images of Qian and Kun were established, and this is how the intention of the sages was fully expressed. Those who excel at studying the Changes base themselves on the establishment of its images to seek the preservation of its intention; as for the Changes, their understanding will be more than halfway there. Even so, the Changes are nothing other than yin and yang, and yin and yang are nothing other than the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji); when one turns within to seek it in the mind, each person finds it complete in himself. …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
使天下皆能於心焉求之則何俟於象之立而
意之盡也奈之何百姓之愚不能得意而忘象
此易書所以不得不作也噫立象盡意豈聖人
得已哉
書
臣哉鄰哉鄰哉臣哉禹曰俞帝曰臣作朕
股肱耳目
戴九有
同考試官教諭呂批發明君臣一體意甚切而
詞復整肅不浮可以式矣
考試官教諭陳批精邃典雅
考試官教諭尹批婉切有味
===
聖君咏臣職之重因明其義之切也甚矣臣之
關於君者重也觀諸一體之相須而其義之切
不益見哉帝舜感禹弼直之語遂為之咏曰臣
哉鄰哉鄰哉臣哉夫臣而繫之鄰則凡服在大
僚而為保治之佐者孰無後先疏附之責乎信
乎弼之不容不直也鄰而屬之臣則凡左右厥
punctuated:
使天下皆能於心焉求之，則何俟於象之立而意之盡也？奈之何百姓之愚，不能得意而忘象，此《易》書所以不得不作也。噫！立象盡意，豈聖人得已哉！
《書》
「臣哉鄰哉！鄰哉臣哉！」禹曰：「俞。」帝曰：「臣作朕股肱耳目。」
戴九有
同考試官、教諭呂批：發明君臣一體，意甚切而詞復整肅不浮，可以式矣。
考試官、教諭陳批：精邃典雅。
考試官、教諭尹批：婉切有味。
聖君咏臣職之重，因明其義之切也。甚矣，臣之關於君者重也！觀諸一體之相須，而其義之切不益見哉！帝舜感禹弼直之語，遂為之咏曰：「臣哉鄰哉！鄰哉臣哉！」夫臣而繫之鄰，則凡服在大僚而為保治之佐者，孰無後先疏附之責乎？信乎弼之不容不直也。鄰而屬之臣，則凡左右厥…
translation_en:
If everyone in the world were able to seek it within their own minds, what need would there be to establish images in order to fully express the meaning? Yet what can be done when the common people, in their ignorance, cannot grasp the meaning and forget the images? This is why the Book of Changes (Yi) had to be composed. Alas! In establishing images to fully express his meaning, how could the sage have helped doing so?

Book of Documents (Shu)
"Ministers! Close associates! Close associates! Ministers!" Yu said, "Yes!" The Sovereign said, "My ministers act as my legs and arms, my ears and eyes."

Dai Jiuyou 戴九有
Associate Examiner, Instructor Lü's comment: It elucidates the principle of ruler and minister forming a single body; the thought is most pertinent and the diction, moreover, is orderly, solemn, and free of superficiality. It may serve as a model.
Examiner, Instructor Chen's comment: Profound, abstruse, and classically elegant.
Examiner, Instructor Yin's comment: Graceful, pertinent, and rich in flavor.

The sage ruler chants of the weightiness of the ministerial office, and thereby clarifies the closeness of its bond of duty. Great indeed is the importance of the minister in relation to the ruler! When we observe their mutual dependence as parts of a single body, is not the closeness of this bond of duty seen all the more clearly? Sovereign Shun, moved by Yu's words on assisting with uprightness, thereupon chanted of it, saying: "Ministers! Close associates! Close associates! Ministers!" Now, when "minister" is linked with "close associate," then among all those who serve in high office and act as aides in preserving good governance, who does not bear the responsibility of attending before and behind and drawing the distant near? Truly, their assistance cannot fail to be upright! And when "close associate" is referred back to "minister," then all those who flank their…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
辟以賛保治之業者不在宅揆亮工之選乎信
乎直之必藉於弼也夫弼直之語自禹陳之既
啓帝之所未發而臣鄰之職自帝咏之益契禹
之所欲言宜其感之深而遂俞之也帝復從而
申之曰汝知臣所以爲鄰之義乎彼人非股肱
無以運行朕不能自運行乎天下所資以爲馮
翼者臣也其作朕之股肱乎人非耳目無以視
聽朕不能自視聽乎天下所資以達聞見者臣
也其作朕之耳目乎四體效職而後元首尊良
===
臣交脩而後君治廣玆其相須爲至切而臣鄰
之義見矣有弼直之責者其尚無負斯託哉抑
論帝王通天下爲一身其視天下之大呼吸癢
疴靡不相關非獨股肱其臣而已故其精神日
加于四海而無壅閼何者一體故也舜甞明四
目矣達四聰矣而四方從欲應若指臂非一體
之明驗歟
澤潤生民四夷左衽罔不咸賴
譚汝講
punctuated:
辟以賛保治之業者，不在宅揆亮工之選乎？信乎直之必藉於弼也。夫「弼直」之語，自禹陳之，既啓帝之所未發；而「臣鄰」之職，自帝咏之，益契禹之所欲言。宜其感之深而遂俞之也。帝復從而申之曰：「汝知臣所以爲鄰之義乎？彼人非股肱無以運行，朕不能自運行乎天下，所資以爲馮翼者臣也，其作朕之股肱乎！人非耳目無以視聽，朕不能自視聽乎天下，所資以達聞見者臣也，其作朕之耳目乎！」四體效職而後元首尊，良臣交脩而後君治廣，玆其相須爲至切，而臣鄰之義見矣。有弼直之責者，其尚無負斯託哉！抑論帝王通天下爲一身，其視天下之大，呼吸癢疴靡不相關，非獨股肱其臣而已。故其精神日加于四海而無壅閼，何者？一體故也。舜甞明四目矣，達四聰矣，而四方從欲，應若指臂，非一體之明驗歟？

澤潤生民，四夷左衽，罔不咸賴。
譚汝講
translation_en:
…sovereign in assisting the enterprise of preserving good governance—are they not chosen to occupy the post of prime minister and bring achievements to light? Truly, uprightness must rely upon corrective assistance! Now, the words on "assisting toward uprightness," as set forth by Yu, opened up what the Emperor had not yet expressed; and the duty of "ministers as close associates," as chanted by the Emperor, agreed all the more with what Yu wished to say. No wonder Yu was deeply moved and immediately assented! The Emperor then went on to elaborate on it, saying: "Do you understand the meaning of why ministers act as close associates? Without limbs, a person has no means to move and act; I cannot by myself move and act throughout the realm—those upon whom I rely as my support and wings are my ministers. Let them act as my limbs! Without ears and eyes, a person has no means to see and hear; I cannot by myself see and hear throughout the realm—those upon whom I rely to extend my hearing and sight are my ministers. Let them act as my ears and eyes!" Only when the four limbs fulfill their functions is the head honored; only when worthy ministers mutually cultivate their duties is the ruler's governance broadened. Herein their mutual dependence is most intimate, and the meaning of ministers as close associates becomes manifest. May those who bear the responsibility of assisting toward uprightness not fail this trust! Furthermore, if we consider that emperors and kings unite the entire realm into a single body, in viewing the vastness of the world, there is not a single breath, itch, or ailment with which they are not connected—it is not merely that they treat their ministers as limbs. Therefore, their vital spirit daily reaches throughout the Four Seas without obstruction. Why is this? Because they form a single body. Shun once illumined the eyes of the four quarters and opened the ears of the four quarters, and the four directions followed his desires, responding as fingers to the arm—is this not clear proof of their being a single body?

"Benefits moisten the living people, and the four夷 (yi) tribes who fold their robes to the left all without exception rely on them."
Tan Rujiang

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭呂批發揮明透而語更俊雅殆
非騁蔓詞者
考試官敎諭陳批鬯達可誦
考試官敎諭尹批雅潔
賢王期大臣化殷而澤及于無外焉蓋殷民化
而四夷攸賴此王者無外之治也非大臣成終
而能然歟昔康王期畢公之意若曰惟茲殷士
非獨係邦之安危亦四夷所視以休戚者也我
公繼二公以化殷旣道洽而政治矣由是道乆
===
而澤益流其及民也溥政敷而仁愈沛其入人
也深昔甞旌淑以示之勸矣茲則淪濡於道化
殆盡人而可旌焉羣然徧德之風也昔甞別慝
以導之趨矣茲則漸摩於治敎殆無慝之可別
焉熙然遵義之俗也此殷民所以永賴也而其
所及寧有限耶吾知王畿安則天下舉安而德
自施乎無外殷民順則遠邇俱順而化自被于
無方不獨環四封者賴之也雖四夷之遠亦皆
沐餘澤以恬熙太和之景象由東郊而達之華
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭呂批：發揮明透，而語更俊雅，殆非騁蔓詞者。
考試官敎諭陳批：鬯達可誦。
考試官敎諭尹批：雅潔。
賢王期大臣化殷，而澤及于無外焉。蓋殷民化而四夷攸賴，此王者無外之治也；非大臣成終，而能然歟？昔康王期畢公之意，若曰：惟茲殷士，非獨係邦之安危，亦四夷所視以休戚者也。我公繼二公以化殷，旣道洽而政治矣。由是道乆而澤益流，其及民也溥；政敷而仁愈沛，其入人也深。昔甞旌淑以示之勸矣，茲則淪濡於道化，殆盡人而可旌焉，羣然徧德之風也；昔甞別慝以導之趨矣，茲則漸摩於治敎，殆無慝之可別焉，熙然遵義之俗也。此殷民所以永賴也，而其所及寧有限耶？吾知王畿安則天下舉安，而德自施乎無外；殷民順則遠邇俱順，而化自被于無方。不獨環四封者賴之也，雖四夷之遠，亦皆沐餘澤以恬熙，太和之景象由東郊而達之華
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Lü's comment: The exposition is clear and thorough, and the phrasing is even more refined and elegant; this is hardly someone who indulges inrambling verbiage.
Examiner and Instructor Chen's comment: Fluent and expressive, worthy of recitation.
Examiner and Instructor Yin's comment: Elegant and concise.
A worthy king expects his great minister to transform the people of Yin so that his beneficence extends without bound. Indeed, when the people of Yin are transformed and the four barbarian tribes rely upon them, this is the boundless governance of a true king; without a great minister to bring the task to completion, how could it be so? In the past, King Kang's intention in placing his hopes in the Duke of Bi was as if to say: "These officers of Yin not only bear upon the security and peril of our state, but are also whom the four barbarian tribes look to in sharing our weal and woe. Your Grace succeeds the two previous dukes in transforming Yin, and already the Way has soaked in and governance is well-ordered. From this, as the Way endures for long, its beneficence flows ever further, reaching the people broadly; as governance is spread wide, benevolence surges ever more abundantly, entering into people deeply. Formerly, the good were honored with insignia to show encouragement; now, steeped and moistened in the transformation of the Way, nearly every person is worthy of being honored—a collective climate of universal virtue! Formerly, the wicked were set apart to guide the people's direction; now, gradually molded by orderly instruction, there is scarcely any wickedness left to be set apart—a harmonious custom of following righteousness! This is whereby the living people forever rely upon it; yet how could its reach have any limit? I know that when the royal domain is at peace, all under Heaven is at peace, and virtue naturally extends without bound; when the people of Yin are compliant, both far and near are compliant, and transformation naturally reaches in every direction. Not only do those within the four borders rely upon it; even the distant four barbarian tribes all bathe in the overflowing beneficence to live in calm and harmony, as the spectacle of great concord extends from the Eastern Suburb to reach the Chinese…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
夏廓如矣不獨列編氓者賴之也雖左衽之俗
亦皆霑餘潤以寧謐大順之休風自下都而通
之宇宙蕩如矣必至是而保釐之託副三后之
功成予小子殆永有慶也公其圖諸抑論成周
盛時九夷重譯中國聖人之化窮極天壤何有
于蕞爾之殷民哉乃成康之君周畢君陳之佐
相繼綏輯猶然廑安危之慮焉此見周家忠厚
之至而商先王之德澤結于人心而不可解者
亦足徵矣
===
詩
思齊大任文王之母思媚周姜京室之婦
大姒嗣徽音則百斯男
王應泰
同考試官教諭王批推本聖德處具見精蘊而
聖德不專藉于人尤知所本者可與言詩矣
考試官教諭陳批詞旨瑩徹
考試官教諭尹批莊雅之作
觀周家內德相承則聖德為有自矣甚矣內治
punctuated:
夏，廓如矣；不獨列編氓者賴之也，雖左衽之俗，亦皆霑餘潤以寧謐，大順之休風，自下都而通之宇宙，蕩如矣。必至是而保釐之託副，三后之功成，予小子殆永有慶也，公其圖諸！抑論成周盛時，九夷重譯，中國聖人之化，窮極天壤，何有于蕞爾之殷民哉？乃成、康之君，周、畢、君陳之佐，相繼綏輯，猶然廑安危之慮焉。此見周家忠厚之至，而商先王之德澤結于人心而不可解者，亦足徵矣。

《詩》
「思齊大任，文王之母，思媚周姜，京室之婦。大姒嗣徽音，則百斯男。」
王應泰
同考試官教諭王批：推本聖德處，具見精蘊；而聖德不專藉于人，尤知所本者。可與言《詩》矣。
考試官教諭陳批：詞旨瑩徹。
考試官教諭尹批：莊雅之作。

觀周家內德相承，則聖德為有自矣。甚矣！內治
translation_en:
… the central lands—how vast! Not only will those enrolled among the registered commoners rely upon it; even the peoples of left-fastening robes will all be moistened by its surplus grace and rest in tranquility, as the auspicious风 (influence) of great obedience spreads from the Lower Capital throughout the universe—how boundless! Only when this is reached will the charge of protecting and regulating be fulfilled, the achievements of the Three Rulers be brought to completion, and I, the Little Child, perhaps enjoy enduring felicity. May the Duke plan for this! Yet if we consider the flourishing age of Chengzhou, when the Nine Yi tribes came through repeated interpretations and the transforming influence of the Sage of the Central Kingdom reached the ends of heaven and earth, what difficulty could there have been with the tiny remnant of the people of Yin? Nevertheless, sovereigns such as Kings Cheng and Kang, and assisting ministers such as the Dukes of Zhou and Bi and Junchen, successively pacified and harmonized them, still harboring anxious concern over safety and peril. From this we see the utmost loyalty and generosity of the House of Zhou, while the fact that the virtuous bounty of the former kings of Shang was bound so fast to people's hearts that it could not be loosed is also sufficiently attested here.

Classic of Poetry (Shijing)
"Reverent was Tai Ren, the mother of King Wen; loving was she toward Tai Jiang of Zhou, a wife in the capital house. Tai Si inherited her admirable renown, and so bore a hundred sons."
Wang Yingtai
Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang's comment: Where he traces the origin of sagely virtue, the subtle essence is fully revealed; and in showing that sagely virtue does not rely solely upon others, he especially understands what is fundamental. One can speak of the Odes with him!
Examiner and Instructor Chen's comment: Diction and purport are crystal clear.
Examiner and Instructor Yin's comment: A dignified and elegant composition.

When we observe how domestic virtue was passed down within the House of Zhou, we see that sagely virtue had its source. How profound indeed is the…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有關于君德也天啓文德而所賴于聖母賢妃
者豈其微哉此詩人詠歌文王之德而推本之
曰文王之德固天縱之而其所由盛尤有獨際
其隆者彼自古帝王君臨天下每難于母后之
聖維此大任乃文王之母焉齊莊本于性生而
祗服明于婦順執之以事周姜凡致慤而慤致
愛而愛允乎媚茲之忱而婦道其克稱矣蓋天
將啓一人明聖之資故先于篤生者而厚其眷
母以德聖則子以母聖淵源所漸夫豈偶然之
===
故哉自古人君正位於外每難于內助之賢維
此太姒乃文王之妃焉貞靜協于思齊而孝敬
嗣乎思媚由之以昌姬籙凡繼體而聖克肖而
賢莫非盛德之徵而多男以百計矣蓋天將翼
我周明聖之運故先于配德者而發其祥后以
德承則君以德顯贊助所及豈曰小補之哉吁
此文王之德之純有以夫雖然文王亦不專藉
乎此也成以聖母助以賢妃天之所以開聖人
也小心翼翼聖人之所以事天也事天至則天
punctuated: 有關于君德也。天啓文德，而所賴于聖母賢妃者，豈其微哉？此詩人詠歌文王之德而推本之，曰：文王之德，固天縱之，而其所由盛，尤有獨際其隆者。彼自古帝王君臨天下，每難于母后之聖。維此大任，乃文王之母焉，齊莊本于性生，而祗服明于婦順，執之以事周姜，凡致慤而慤、致愛而愛，允乎媚茲之忱，而婦道其克稱矣。蓋天將啓一人明聖之資，故先于篤生者而厚其眷。母以德聖，則子以母聖，淵源所漸，夫豈偶然之故哉？自古人君正位於外，每難于內助之賢。維此太姒，乃文王之妃焉，貞靜協于思齊，而孝敬嗣乎思媚，由之以昌姬籙，凡繼體而聖、克肖而賢，莫非盛德之徵，而多男以百計矣。蓋天將翼我周明聖之運，故先于配德者而發其祥。后以德承，則君以德顯，贊助所及，豈曰小補之哉？吁！此文王之德之純，有以夫！雖然，文王亦不專藉乎此也。成以聖母，助以賢妃，天之所以開聖人也；小心翼翼，聖人之所以事天也。事天至則天
translation_en: …has a bearing on the virtue of the ruler! When Heaven initiates cultured virtue, how could what depends on a sage mother and a worthy consort be slight? Thus the poet sings in praise of the virtue of King Wen and traces its root, saying: The virtue of King Wen was assuredly bestowed by Heaven, yet that whereby it flourished especially met with uniquely magnificent circumstances. Since antiquity, when emperors and kings have ruled over All under Heaven, it has always been difficult to have a sage queen mother. Now this Tairen 太任 was the mother of King Wen. Reverent composure was rooted in her inborn nature, and respectful compliance was manifest in her wifely obedience. Holding fast to this in serving Jiang of Zhou 周姜, in all things where she devoted her sincerity there was sincerity, and where she devoted her love there was love; truly she possessed the earnestness of loving devotion, and the way of a wife was thereby fulfilled. Indeed, because Heaven was about to open up the enlightened and sagely endowment of the One Man, it first lavished its favor upon the one who gave him birth. When the mother is sagely through her virtue, the son is sagely through his mother; imbued from this deep source, how could it be an accidental matter? Since antiquity, when a ruler has occupied his rightful position in the outer court, it has always been difficult to have a worthy helper within. Now this Taisi 太姒 was the consort of King Wen. Chaste and tranquil, she harmonized with the reverent composure [of Tairen], and filial and respectful, she succeeded to her loving devotion. Through this she made prosperous the mandate of the Ji 姬 clan; all those who succeeded to the line and were sagely, or who took after their parents and were worthy, were without exception tokens of abundant virtue, and her many sons were counted by the hundred. Indeed, because Heaven was about to assist the enlightened and sagely destiny of our Zhou, it first sent down its auspicious signs upon the one who matched him in virtue. When the queen carries on with virtue, the ruler becomes illustrious through virtue; as for the reach of her assistance, how could it be called a mere minor supplement? Ah! That the virtue of King Wen was so pure had its cause in this! Even so, King Wen did not rely exclusively on this. To be brought to completion by a sage mother and assisted by a worthy consort was how Heaven opened the way for the sage; to be warily reverent was how the sage served Heaven. When the service of Heaven reaches the utmost, then Heaven…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
純而天在我矣故繼之曰亦保亦臨事天也亦
式亦入純天也故聖人不恃其得天而脩其所
以純天者
王釐爾成來咨來茹嗟嗟保介維莫之春
亦又何求如何新畬於皇來牟將受厥
明明昭上帝迄用康年命我眾人庤乃
錢鎛奄觀銍艾
曹學程
同考試官教諭王批說出成王勤民重本之意
===
宛然在目蓋究心經義而有得者取之
考試官教諭陳批格調高古讀之灑然
考試官教諭尹批嚴整精密
周王詳戒農官惟欲求成法而已蓋乗時治田
成法具在也明農者可自緩于咨度哉周王戒
農官若曰我周以農事開國固立之官以董其
事又嘗釐之法以受其成矣世相授守允為畫
一之規法當講求非直循行之具凡爾臣工欲
敬有位其尚來咨焉以詢其實來茹焉以度其
punctuated:
純而天在我矣。故繼之曰：「亦保亦臨」，事天也；「亦式亦入」，純天也。故聖人不恃其得天，而脩其所以純天者。

《王釐爾成，來咨來茹。嗟嗟保介，維莫之春，亦又何求？如何新畬？於皇來牟，將受厥明。明昭上帝，迄用康年。命我眾人，庤乃錢鎛，奄觀銍艾。》
曹學程
同考試官教諭王批：說出成王勤民重本之意，宛然在目，蓋究心經義而有得者。取之。
考試官教諭陳批：格調高古，讀之灑然。
考試官教諭尹批：嚴整精密。

周王詳戒農官，惟欲求成法而已。蓋乗時治田，成法具在也，明農者可自緩于咨度哉？周王戒農官若曰：我周以農事開國，固立之官以董其事，又嘗釐之法以受其成矣。世相授守，允為畫一之規；法當講求，非直循行之具。凡爾臣工，欲敬有位，其尚來咨焉以詢其實，來茹焉以度其
translation_en:
… becomes pure, and Heaven is within oneself. Therefore the poem continues by saying: "Protected and watched over"—this is serving Heaven; "Conforming to the model and entering into virtue"—this is purifying oneself to be one with Heaven. Thus the sage does not presume upon having obtained Heaven's favor, but cultivates that by which he makes his virtue pure like Heaven's.

"The king has given you perfect rules; come and consult, come and deliberate. Ah, you attendant officers! It is now the end of spring; what more do you seek? How are the newly tilled fields and the fields of the third year? Oh, magnificent are the wheat and barley; we shall soon receive their bright賜 [bounty]. The bright and glorious Lord on High will bring us a year of豐稔 [abundance]. Order all our people to prepare their spades and hoes; soon we shall see the sickles reaping." [Classic of Poetry, Ode "Chen Gong"]
Cao Xuecheng 曹學程
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor (jiaoyu): It brings out King Cheng's intention of being diligent for the people and valuing the fundamental occupation [agriculture] so vividly that it seems right before one's eyes. This is someone who has delved deeply into the meaning of the Classics and gained true insight. Selected.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: The style is lofty and antique; reading it is refreshing.
Comment by Examiner Yin, Instructor: Rigorous, orderly, and precise.

The Zhou king admonished his agricultural officials in detail, wishing only that they seek out the established laws. Indeed, for seizing the season to cultivate the fields, the established laws are all present; how could those who oversee agriculture allow themselves to be remiss in consulting and deliberating? In admonishing the agricultural officials, the Zhou king spoke as if to say: Our Zhou dynasty founded the state upon agriculture; we certainly established officials to supervise the affair, and we also formulated laws to hand down the completed standards. Passed down and guarded from generation to generation, they truly serve as uniform regulations; these laws ought to be studied and sought into, and are not merely instruments for routine compliance. All you officials and ministers, if you wish to revere your offices, you should come and consult to inquire into their substance, and come and deliberate to measure their…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
詳誠莫有急於今日者咨茹維何嗟嗟保介職
副農官然皆以勸農爲責均當於成法是求也
一歲之計在于春仰觀天時春則暮矣三農之
務秉乎春俯察新畬今何如哉毋但曰田之難
治而時可後也試觀來牟明昭之賜將受於上
帝而豐穰之利可必于新畬失今不治非法也
何以承天之休乎毋但曰效之難獲而力可懈
也率時農夫錢鎛之興方勤于俶載而銍艾之
舉奄觀於新畬失今不治非法也何以察地之
===
利乎此皆成法所在賜於王者爲甚重而繫於
民者爲不輕也汝農官尚其敬之哉吁周王亦
可謂善訓迪者歟抑務農重穀明王寶之故躬
先耕籍訓官飭務勤民重本之精意固有不專
在於成法者是以咨嗟勸勉洋洋乎盈廟堂徹
閰野宣之史館被之金石後世猶可想見其盛
徒法云乎哉昔人以農事爲帝王傳心之要詎
不信夫
春秋
punctuated:
詳，誠莫有急於今日者。咨茹維何？嗟嗟保介，職副農官，然皆以勸農爲責，均當於成法是求也。一歲之計在于春，仰觀天時，春則暮矣；三農之務秉乎春，俯察新畬，今何如哉？毋但曰田之難治而時可後也。試觀來牟明昭之賜，將受於上帝，而豐穰之利，可必于新畬。失今不治，非法也，何以承天之休乎？毋但曰效之難獲而力可懈也。率時農夫，錢鎛之興，方勤于俶載；而銍艾之舉，奄觀於新畬。失今不治，非法也，何以察地之利乎？此皆成法所在，賜於王者爲甚重，而繫於民者爲不輕也，汝農官尚其敬之哉！吁！周王亦可謂善訓迪者歟！抑務農重穀，明王寶之，故躬先耕籍，訓官飭務。勤民重本之精意，固有不專在於成法者，是以咨嗟勸勉，洋洋乎盈廟堂、徹閰野，宣之史館，被之金石，後世猶可想見其盛，徒法云乎哉！昔人以農事爲帝王傳心之要，詎不信夫！
《春秋》
translation_en:
…details, for truly nothing is more urgent today. What is it that you must consult and deliberate upon? Ah, you assistant agricultural officers! Though your post is deputy to the agricultural officials, you all share the responsibility of encouraging farming, and all alike should seek out the established methods. The planning for the whole year lies in spring; looking up to observe the season of Heaven, spring is now drawing to a close. The labors of the three classes of farmers depend upon the spring; looking down to examine the two- and three-year-old fields, how do they stand today? Do not merely say that the fields are difficult to cultivate and that the season may be delayed. Just look at the wheat and barley—that bright and glorious gift is about to be received from the Lord on High, and the benefit of an abundant harvest can be assured in the two- and three-year-old fields. To let the present moment slip by without cultivating them is contrary to the established methods; how then could one receive the blessings of Heaven? Do not merely say that results are hard to achieve and that effort may be slackened. Lead these farmers: the wielding of spades and hoes is just now diligent in the first commencement of spring work, and the reaping with sickles will soon be seen across the two- and three-year-old fields. To let the present moment slip by without cultivating them is contrary to the established methods; how then could one realize the advantages of the earth? In all these matters lie the established methods; what is bestowed by the true king is weighty indeed, and what is bound up with the people is far from light. May you agricultural officials revere this! Ah, the King of Zhou may truly be called skillful in instructing and guiding! Yet devoting oneself to agriculture and valuing grain are what enlightened kings treasure; therefore they personally lead the way in plowing the sacred field, instructing officials and putting affairs in order. The profound intent of working for the people and emphasizing the fundamental occupation inherently does not lie solely in established laws. Thus, his sighing exhortations and encouragements filled the court and reached the village lanes in grand abundance; proclaimed in the historiography institute and inscribed on metal and stone, later generations can still envision that flourishing age. Could it be a matter of mere laws alone? The ancients regarded agriculture as the essential mind-to-mind transmission of emperors and kings—how could that not be true!

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
冬楚子使椒來聘文公九年
胡天霞
同考試官訓導徐批發春秋進楚之意明盡且
筆力謹嚴宜冠本房
考試官教諭陳批詞義凜然典則可式
考試官教諭尹批格正詞明
春秋於遠人之脩禮而特等之於中國焉夫楚
爲聖賢之後聖人常欲其進於善也况以禮而
自通焉安得不中國之哉昔楚僭稱王經甞以
===
號舉矣亦以人書矣椒之來聘一進而中國之
遂無嫌乎蓋聖人以謹嚴訓天下故純於夷者
不輕進以决其防而尤以忠恕待天下故變於
夷者不輕絶以隘其量楚何人哉越章之僭雖
流入於夷狄而祝融之烈猶未泯於宗周惟其
執迷不返則雖欲引之而不能耳乃者共玉帛
以告虔深懲乎爲讎之暴命越椒以脩禮益堅
乎慕義之心聘以結好惟中國之君能然而穆
之令其臣者以之則去逆効順視先世之元德
punctuated:
「冬，楚子使椒來聘。」〔文公九年〕
胡天霞
同考試官訓導徐批：發《春秋》進楚之意，明盡，且筆力謹嚴，宜冠本房。
考試官教諭陳批：詞義凜然，典則可式。
考試官教諭尹批：格正詞明。

《春秋》於遠人之脩禮，而特等之於中國焉。夫楚爲聖賢之後，聖人常欲其進於善也，况以禮而自通焉，安得不中國之哉？昔楚僭稱王，經甞以號舉矣，亦以人書矣。椒之來聘，一進而中國之，遂無嫌乎？蓋聖人以謹嚴訓天下，故純於夷者不輕進，以决其防；而尤以忠恕待天下，故變於夷者不輕絶，以隘其量。楚何人哉？越章之僭，雖流入於夷狄；而祝融之烈，猶未泯於宗周。惟其執迷不返，則雖欲引之而不能耳。乃者，共玉帛以告虔，深懲乎爲讎之暴；命越椒以脩禮，益堅乎慕義之心。聘以結好，惟中國之君能然，而穆之令其臣者以之，則去逆効順，視先世之元德⋯⋯
translation_en:
"In winter, the Viscount of Chu sent Jiao to come on a mission of friendly inquiries." [Ninth year of Duke Wen]
By Hu Tianxia

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Xu comments: It brings out the intention of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) in advancing Chu clearly and exhaustively; moreover, its brushwork is rigorous and disciplined—it ought to head this examination ward.
Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: The diction and meaning are awe-inspiring; its classical standards can serve as a model.
Examiner and Instructor Yin comments: The structure is upright and the diction clear.

When men from afar cultivated ritual propriety, the Spring and Autumn Annals specially ranked them on a par with the Central States. Now, Chu was descended from sages and worthies, and the Sage always wished for it to advance toward goodness; how much more so when it communicated on its own initiative through ritual propriety—how could he not treat it as one of the Central States? In the past, when Chu usurped the title of king, the Classic sometimes referred to it simply by its state name, and sometimes recorded its rulers merely as "men." With Jiao's coming on a mission of friendly inquiries, was there then no suspicion in advancing it all at once and treating it as one of the Central States? Indeed, the Sage instructed the world with rigor and strictness, so those who were purely barbarian he did not lightly advance, lest he breach the defenses; yet even more did he treat the world with conscientiousness and reciprocity, so those who had degenerated into barbarians he did not lightly cut off, lest he narrow his capacity for tolerance. What sort of people were those of Chu? Although through the usurpation at Yuezhang they had lapsed into the ways of the Yi and Di barbarians, the illustrious merit of Zhurong had still not perished in the ancestral Zhou house. It was only because they persisted in their delusion without turning back that even though one wished to draw them in, one could not. Now, however, they presented jade and silk to declare their reverence, deeply repenting of their past violence in acting as enemies; and ordered Yue Jiao to cultivate ritual propriety, further strengthening their heart of admiration for righteousness. Sending missions of friendly inquiries to conclude amity is something only a ruler of the Central States is able to do, yet when King Mu commanded his minister by this means, in abandoning rebellion and rendering obedience, compared to the primal virtue of his ancestors…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
爲有光矣安可追其旣往而絶之乎聘以獻物
惟中國之臣能然而椒之承其君者以之則思
善悔過視先代之顯功爲無忝矣安可逆其將
來而棄之乎聖人以爲楚之類旣如此而其行
又如此故其君書爵其臣書名而稱使亦愼用
刑重絶人之意歟抑是聘也其狼淵之後乎楚
之聘何爲者以商臣之逆而濟以范山之謀志
在北方久矣特以魯爲人望之國竊慕義之名
以自文耳自是楚日驕中國日狎至於主會主
===
盟而天下大勢駸在楚矣春秋之進楚者其憂
楚也夫
楚人執鄭行人良霄襄公十有一年夏楚
子蔡侯陳侯鄭伯許男徐子滕子頓子
胡子沈子小邾子宋世子佐淮夷會于
申昭公四年
文希信
同考試官訓導徐 批 晉悼之賢具見此文是擅
塲之作也錄之
punctuated:
爲有光矣，安可追其旣往而絶之乎？聘以獻物，惟中國之臣能然，而椒之承其君者以之，則思善悔過，視先代之顯功爲無忝矣，安可逆其將來而棄之乎？聖人以爲楚之類旣如此，而其行又如此，故其君書爵，其臣書名而稱使，亦愼用刑、重絶人之意歟！抑是聘也，其狼淵之後乎？楚之聘何爲者？以商臣之逆，而濟以范山之謀，志在北方久矣，特以魯爲人望之國，竊慕義之名以自文耳。自是楚日驕，中國日狎，至於主會、主盟，而天下大勢駸在楚矣。《春秋》之進楚者，其憂楚也夫！

「楚人執鄭行人良霄」襄公十有一年，「夏，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申」昭公四年。
文希信
同考試官訓導徐批：晉悼之賢，具見此文，是擅塲之作也，錄之。
translation_en:
… adds luster to it! How could one pursue its past misdeeds and cut it off? Paying a court visit to present offerings is something only a minister of the Central States is capable of doing; yet Jiao, in carrying out his ruler's command, did so by this means. Thus, in contemplating goodness and repenting of faults, he brought no shame upon the illustrious achievements of earlier generations—how could one anticipate his future conduct and cast him aside? The Sage considered that since Chu's pedigree was already such, and its conduct was now also such, he therefore recorded its ruler by his noble rank and its minister by his personal name while styling him an envoy; was this not also the intent of being cautious in applying punishments and reluctant to cut people off? Or was this mission of friendly inquiry after the campaign at Langyuan? What was the purpose of Chu's mission of friendly inquiry? With the rebellion of Shangchen, abetted by the counsel of Fan Shan, its ambitions had long been set on the northern lands; it merely took advantage of Lu's being a state held in high esteem by men, stealing the reputation of admiring righteousness in order to gloss over itself. From this point on, Chu grew daily more arrogant and the Central States grew daily more contemptuous and familiar, until it came to preside over assemblies and preside over covenants, and the great balance of power in the realm shifted swiftly to Chu. When the Spring and Autumn Annals elevates Chu, it is out of anxiety over Chu indeed!

"The men of Chu seized Liang Xiao, messenger of Zheng" (Eleventh year of Duke Xiang); "In summer, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Viscount of Xu, the Viscount of Teng, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Shen, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, Heir Apparent Zuo of Song, and the Huai Yi met at Shen" (Fourth year of Duke Zhao).

By Wen Xixin 文希信.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Xu: The worthiness of Duke Dao of Jin is fully revealed in this essay; it is a work that dominates the examination compound, and so we record it for publication.

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭陳批詞氣謹嚴格調高古
考試官教諭尹批詞簡格整
春秋紀內外之屈服而伯主之績見矣此悼之
駕楚服鄭以謀勝以誠感也春秋所以與之歟
晉至中葉悼公復霸命昭糾逖之勳業紹館穀
之烈其功伐著於春秋何踔絕也彼外之强而
撓霸者莫如楚于汜振旅之後屢爭而不可制
其誰能威之東門三駕而北圖遽寢豈其以力
屈之哉蓋惟謀可以制勝楚非屈於晉也屈於
===
謀也息民聽於魏絳還師聽於知罃分軍逆來
楚且疲於奔命矣及至良霄之遣執一行人而
其憤已洩不然會伐之師方興告絕之使復至
馮二廣之力以臨之其不夷為縣鄙乎觀楚之
屈而知謀之能制敵也內之攜而背霸者莫如
鄭于戲要言之後屢盟而不可信其誰能懷之
蕭魚一會而南轅遽挽豈其以力服之哉蓋惟
誠可以動物鄭非服於晉也服於誠也入盟命
於趙武遣告命於叔肸赦囚禮歸鄭且懷其明
punctuated:
考試官教諭陳批：詞氣謹嚴，格調高古。
考試官教諭尹批：詞簡格整。
《春秋》紀內外之屈服，而伯主之績見矣。此悼之駕楚服鄭，以謀勝，以誠感也，《春秋》所以與之歟！晉至中葉，悼公復霸，命昭糾逖之勳，業紹館穀之烈，其功伐著於《春秋》，何踔絕也！彼外之强而撓霸者，莫如楚；于汜振旅之後，屢爭而不可制，其誰能威之？東門三駕而北圖遽寢，豈其以力屈之哉？蓋惟謀可以制勝，楚非屈於晉也，屈於謀也。息民聽於魏絳，還師聽於知罃，分軍逆來，楚且疲於奔命矣。及至良霄之遣，執一行人而其憤已洩；不然，會伐之師方興，告絕之使復至，馮二廣之力以臨之，其不夷為縣鄙乎？觀楚之屈，而知謀之能制敵也。內之攜而背霸者，莫如鄭；于戲要言之後，屢盟而不可信，其誰能懷之？蕭魚一會而南轅遽挽，豈其以力服之哉？蓋惟誠可以動物，鄭非服於晉也，服於誠也。入盟命於趙武，遣告命於叔肸，赦囚禮歸，鄭且懷其明…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: The diction and tone are rigorous and strict; the style is lofty and ancient.
Examiner and Instructor Yin comments: The wording is concise and the structure is orderly.

The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records the submission of both external and internal powers, and thereby the achievements of the hegemon are made manifest. This was how Duke Dao of Jin (Jin Daogong) overwhelmed Chu and won over Zheng—prevailing through strategy and moving others through sincerity; is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals praises him? When Jin reached its middle period, Duke Dao restored the hegemony. His charge illuminated the merit of uniting and pacifying the distant, and his enterprise continued the illustrious deeds of the provisioning at Guangu; how extraordinary are his achievements recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals! Among external powers that were strong and disrupted the hegemony, none matched Chu. After the triumphant return of troops from Fan, it contended repeatedly and could not be checked—who could overawe it? Yet after the three campaigns reaching the Eastern Gate (Dongmen), its northern ambitions suddenly ceased; was it forced into submission by mere strength? Indeed, only strategy can secure victory; Chu did not submit to Jin, it submitted to strategy. In resting the people, he listened to Wei Jiang; in withdrawing the army, he listened to Zhi Ying. By dividing his forces to meet them as they came, Chu was exhausted from rushing about at his command. By the time Liang Xiao was sent, Chu seized a single envoy and its anger was already vented; otherwise, just as the allied expeditionary forces were rising, an envoy announcing the severance of relations arrived again—had Chu relied on the strength of its Two Broad Chariot Divisions (Erguang) to descend upon Zheng, would it not have been razed into prefectures and borderlands? Observing the submission of Chu, one knows that strategy can subdue the enemy. Among internal states that were alienated and turned against the hegemony, none matched Zheng. After the coerced covenant at Xi, it made repeated alliances that could not be trusted—who could win its allegiance? Yet after a single meeting at Xiaoyu, its southward-bound chariots were suddenly turned back; was it won over by mere force? Indeed, only sincerity can move others; Zheng was not won over by Jin, it was won over by sincerity. Entering to make the covenant was ordered to Zhao Wu, and dispatching the announcement was ordered to Shu Xi; by pardoning prisoners and sending them back with courtesy, Zheng came to cherish his illustrious…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
德矣及至申之會歷二十四年而其志始攜不
然紓民之謀孔多擇疆之歌猶在勤二境之使
以待之其不渝此載書乎觀鄭之服而知誠之
能感人也悼其霸之賢者乎然晉所以霸蓋有
繇也悼以君子之資而得賢人之輔君明臣睦
夫是以九合諸侯而繼三覲之績耳彼二國謀
臣曰晉不可敵曰晉不棄鄭其亦豫見於此乎
禮記
是故禮者君之大柄也
===
李時盛
同考試官訓導吳 批 治國莫急乎禮是作發揮
透徹而講大柄處語尤不俗宜錄以式
考試官教諭陳 批 詞理精到
考試官教諭尹 批 雅健
記者重禮而指其切於治也夫人君之治國必
有爲之柄也然其大者孰有過於禮哉記禮運
者蓋曰甚哉人君之道不可無所執而在明其
所執之大吾嘗自禮之得失觀之而知禮之於
punctuated:
德矣。及至申之會，歷二十四年而其志始攜。不然，紓民之謀孔多，擇疆之歌猶在，勤二境之使以待之，其不渝此載書乎？觀鄭之服，而知誠之能感人也。悼其霸之賢者乎！然晉所以霸，蓋有繇也。悼以君子之資，而得賢人之輔，君明臣睦，夫是以九合諸侯，而繼三覲之績耳。彼二國謀臣，曰「晉不可敵」，曰「晉不棄鄭」，其亦豫見於此乎？

禮記

是故禮者君之大柄也
李時盛
同考試官訓導吳 批：治國莫急乎禮，是作發揮透徹，而講大柄處語尤不俗，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭陳 批：詞理精到。
考試官教諭尹 批：雅健。

記者重禮，而指其切於治也。夫人君之治國，必有爲之柄也，然其大者孰有過於禮哉？記《禮運》者蓋曰：甚哉！人君之道不可無所執，而在明其所執之大。吾嘗自禮之得失觀之，而知禮之於
translation_en:
… virtue. Down to the meeting at Shen, twenty-four years passed before its resolve first wavered. Otherwise, with plenty of schemes to give respite to its people and the song of "choosing which neighbor to follow" still echoing, when emissaries from both borders were kept busy in attendance upon it, would it not have betrayed the written covenant? Observing the submission of Zheng, one knows that sincerity can move people. Was Duke Dao not a worthy hegemon! Yet there was a reason why Jin achieved hegemony. Endowed with the qualities of a gentleman, Dao obtained the assistance of worthy men; the ruler was enlightened and his ministers were harmonious, and therefore he was able to assemble the feudal lords repeatedly and carry on the achievement of being received three times in royal audience. When the counseling ministers of those two states said "Jin cannot be rivaled" and "Jin will not abandon Zheng," did they not foresee it in this?

Record of Rites (Liji)

"Therefore ritual is the great handle of the ruler."

By Li Shisheng 

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wu comments: In governing a state, nothing is more urgent than ritual. This composition expounds the theme thoroughly, and where it discusses the "great handle," the language is especially free of vulgarity. It ought to be recorded as a model.
Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: The diction and reasoning are precise and thorough.
Examiner and Instructor Yin comments: Elegant and vigorous.

The chronicler attaches great weight to ritual and points out how essential it is to governance. When a ruler governs a state, there must be something that serves as his handle; yet among its greatest aspects, what can surpass ritual? The author of the "Ceremonial Usages" (Liyun) chapter is saying in effect: Indeed! The Way of the ruler cannot be without something to grasp, and it lies in understanding the greatness of what he grasps. I have observed this from the gain and loss of ritual, and know that to…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
治爲最切矣蓋禮者先王以承天之道也而君
之凝承天命者必以是爲持循之要務禮者先
王以治人之情也而君之統理民物者必以是
爲運量之要樞經禮三百秩然示人序矣隆而
由之則所守者至約而可以定天下之民志曲
禮三千燦然示人文矣敬而守之則所持者至
簡而可以立斯世之大防刑政所以輔治而非
治之所關也惟禮爲義理之準得則治而失則
亂人君所以化導海內而消其僭亂之萌者賴
===
有此耳其所當執者果孰大於此哉法度所以
維治而非治之所急也惟禮爲中正之規用則
安而舍則危人君所以綱維天下而杜其陵替
之漸者特有此耳其所當務者孰能爲之大哉
噫禮爲君之大柄如此用器者不可一日而舍
乎柄治國者獨可一日而廢乎禮哉然禮亦難
言矣君子必脩己以敬而無體之禮立故能以
禮讓爲國乎何有否則綿蕞之儀野外之陋習
也果何補於治云是禮者君之大柄也敬者禮
punctuated: 治爲最切矣。蓋禮者，先王以承天之道也，而君之凝承天命者，必以是爲持循之要務；禮者，先王以治人之情也，而君之統理民物者，必以是爲運量之要樞。經禮三百，秩然示人序矣，隆而由之，則所守者至約，而可以定天下之民志；曲禮三千，燦然示人文矣，敬而守之，則所持者至簡，而可以立斯世之大防。刑政所以輔治，而非治之所關也。惟禮爲義理之準，得則治而失則亂，人君所以化導海內而消其僭亂之萌者，賴有此耳。其所當執者，果孰大於此哉？法度所以維治，而非治之所急也。惟禮爲中正之規，用則安而舍則危，人君所以綱維天下而杜其陵替之漸者，特有此耳。其所當務者，孰能爲之大哉？噫！禮爲君之大柄如此。用器者，不可一日而舍乎柄；治國者，獨可一日而廢乎禮哉？然禮亦難言矣。君子必脩己以敬，而無體之禮立，故能以禮讓爲國乎何有？否則綿蕞之儀，野外之陋習也，果何補於治云？是禮者，君之大柄也；敬者，禮
translation_en: … governance is most urgent. For ritual is that by which the former kings received the Way of Heaven, and the ruler who consolidates and receives the Mandate of Heaven must take this as the essential task of his adherence and observance; ritual is that by which the former kings governed human feelings, and the ruler who directs and orders the people and things must take this as the essential pivot of his deliberation and management. The three hundred cardinal ceremonies orderly display rank and sequence to mankind; if one exalts and follows them, what is maintained is most concise, yet it suffices to settle the minds of the people throughout the realm. The three thousand detailed rules of demeanor brilliantly display cultural refinement to mankind; if one reverently guards them, what is upheld is most simple, yet it suffices to establish the great bulwark of this world. Punishments and administrative measures are the means to assist governance, not what governance hinges upon. Only ritual is the standard of moral principle: attained, there is order; lost, there is chaos. That by which the ruler transforms and guides the realm within the seas and extinguishes the sprouts of usurpation and rebellion depends solely on this. Among the things he ought to hold fast to, what indeed is greater than this? Laws and regulations are the means to maintain governance, not what is most urgent in governance. Only ritual is the rule of impartiality and correctness: employed, there is security; abandoned, there is peril. That by which the ruler holds together the world and checks the gradual onset of encroachment and decline relies exclusively on this. Among the things he ought to devote himself to, what could be greater than this? Alas! Such is ritual as the great handle of the ruler. One who uses a tool cannot for a single day let go of its handle; how could one who governs a state alone abolish ritual for a single day? Yet ritual is also difficult to speak of. The noble man must cultivate himself with reverence so that formless ritual is established; therefore, what difficulty is there in governing a state with ritual and deference? Otherwise, the ceremonies marked out by ropes and bundles of grass are merely rustic customs of the open country—what aid do they truly offer to governance? Thus ritual is the great handle of the ruler, and reverence is the…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之權輿也圖治者其審諸
脩身及家平均天下此古樂之發也
舒應鳳
同考試官訓導吳批古樂和敬通於治道子獨
究本旨而詞能達意可與言樂矣取之
考試官教諭陳批體格嚴整
考試官教諭尹批明潔
賢者推君子端本之化而歸諸正樂焉甚矣樂
觀其深也以之脩己治人非正樂而能若是乎
===
子夏告文侯意曰樂之作非以其音也聽樂者
非徒聽其音也君子誠能於古樂語而道之而
明其和敬之理焉則涵濡深而性情之融化者
有自淪漸久而道德之和順者愈眞以之脩身
而身無不脩矣由是身者家國天下之本也身
脩以及家則宜其家人而一家於此乎齊焉家
齊以及天下則正是四國而天下於此乎均平
焉君子明樂之效至於如此夫豈今樂之可與
能哉蓋惟古樂之發也其聲足樂而不流故聆
punctuated:
之權輿也。圖治者其審諸。

「脩身及家，平均天下。此古樂之發也。」
舒應鳳
同考試官訓導吳批：古樂和敬，通於治道。子獨究本旨，而詞能達意，可與言樂矣。取之。
考試官教諭陳批：體格嚴整。
考試官教諭尹批：明潔。

賢者推君子端本之化，而歸諸正樂焉。甚矣，樂觀其深也！以之脩己治人，非正樂而能若是乎？子夏告文侯意曰：樂之作，非以其音也；聽樂者，非徒聽其音也。君子誠能於古樂語而道之，而明其和敬之理焉，則涵濡深而性情之融化者有自，淪漸久而道德之和順者愈眞。以之脩身，而身無不脩矣。由是身者，家、國、天下之本也。身脩以及家，則宜其家人，而一家於此乎齊焉；家齊以及天下，則正是四國，而天下於此乎均平焉。君子明樂之效至於如此，夫豈今樂之可與能哉？蓋惟古樂之發也，其聲足樂而不流，故聆
translation_en:
…is the beginning of ritual. Those who plan for governance should examine this carefully.

"Cultivating the person and extending it to the family, bringing equilibrium and order to All under Heaven: this is the manifestation of ancient music." (Book of Rites, "Record of Music" [Liji, Yueji])
Shu Yingfeng 舒應鳳
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Wu 吳 comments: The harmony and reverence of ancient music communicate with the way of governance. You alone have investigated the fundamental purport, and your words are able to convey the meaning; one can discuss music with you! Selected.
Examiner, Instructor Chen 陳 comments: The structure is rigorous and well-ordered.
Examiner, Instructor Yin 尹 comments: Clear and concise.

The worthy traces the transformative influence by which the noble man rectifies the root, and attributes it to orthodox music. Profound indeed is the observation of music in its depths! Using it to cultivate oneself and govern others—if it were not orthodox music, could it be like this? Explaining his meaning to Marquis Wen 文侯, Zixia 子夏 said in effect: The creation of music is not merely on account of its sounds; those who listen to music do not merely listen to its sounds. If the noble man is truly able to discuss and discourse upon ancient music, and illuminate its principles of harmony and reverence, then through deep immersion the melting and transformation of his nature and emotions will have a source, and through long permeation the harmony and compliance of his moral virtue will become ever more genuine. Using this to cultivate his person, his person will in no respect fail to be cultivated. From this, the person is the root of the family, the state, and All under Heaven. When the person is cultivated and this is extended to the family, he will harmonize his family members, and the whole family will thereby be regulated; when the family is regulated and this is extended to All under Heaven, he will rectify the states of the four quarters, and All under Heaven will thereby be brought into equilibrium and peace. That the efficacy of the noble man's illumination of music reaches such an extent—how could contemporary music be capable of participating in this? For this is solely the manifestation of ancient music! Its sounds are sufficient to give joy without degenerating into license; therefore, those who listen to…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其聲者足以平心而宣化其文足論而不息故
覩其文者足以同文而出治和矣而敬發焉此
敬德之化所以斂諸吾心而施之天下者翕如
也敬矣而和發焉此和德之化所以融諸吾心
而達之天下者藹如也咸英韶濩之音于今雖
不可復覩而唐虞三代之化于樂而實有明徴
矣古樂之發如此君子惟恐其語之不詳也又
安有聽之恐臥耶文侯可以自悟矣大抵古之
聖王心和氣和天地之和應焉故樂之作也盡
===
神而聽之者盡理後世新聲代變本之則無何
足言樂又何貴於聽也夫子曰人而不仁如樂
何噫知仁而後正樂可興脩齊均平之道在此
矣
第貳場
論
輔助德業而致太平
王應泰
同考試官教諭王 批 人君非賢輔無以成治而
punctuated:
其聲者，足以平心而宣化；其文足論而不息，故覩其文者，足以同文而出治。和矣而敬發焉，此敬德之化所以斂諸吾心，而施之天下者翕如也；敬矣而和發焉，此和德之化所以融諸吾心，而達之天下者藹如也。咸、英、韶、濩之音，于今雖不可復覩，而唐、虞、三代之化，于樂而實有明徴矣。古樂之發如此，君子惟恐其語之不詳也，又安有聽之恐臥耶？文侯可以自悟矣。大抵古之聖王，心和氣和，天地之和應焉，故樂之作也盡神，而聽之者盡理。後世新聲代變，本之則無，何足言樂？又何貴於聽也？夫子曰：「人而不仁，如樂何？」噫！知仁而後正樂可興，脩、齊、均、平之道在此矣。

第貳場
論
輔助德業而致太平
王應泰
同考試官教諭王批：人君非賢輔無以成治，而
translation_en:
…its sounds are enabled to calm their minds and propagate moral transformation; its patterned form is worthy of discussion without cease, and therefore those who observe its patterned form are enabled to unify culture and bring forth good governance. When there is harmony, reverence emanates from it; this is why the transformation of reverent virtue is gathered within our minds and extended to the world in complete concord. When there is reverence, harmony emanates from it; this is why the transformation of harmonious virtue is blended within our minds and reaches throughout the world in geniality. Although the music of the Xianchi, Liuying, Shao, and Dahu can no longer be witnessed today, the moral transformations of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties truly find clear verification in their music. Since the manifestation of ancient music is such as this, the gentleman only fears that his discussion of it may not be thorough enough—how could there be any fear of falling asleep while listening to it? Marquis Wen (Wenhou) might well have awakened to this himself! In general, the sage kings of antiquity were harmonious in mind and harmonious in vital energy, and the harmony of Heaven and Earth responded to them; thus, in the creation of music they exhausted the spirit, and those who listened to it exhausted the principle. In later ages, new sounds changed from generation to generation, lacking any root—how are they worthy of being called music, and what value is there in listening to them? The Master said, "If a man be without humaneness, what has he to do with music?" Alas! Only when one understands humaneness can orthodox music be revived, and the Way of cultivating the person, regulating the family, and bringing equilibrium and peace to the world lies right here.

考試官敎諭陳批平實中有古調佳作也
考試官敎諭尹批氣充詞逸逈異諸作
論曰人君得賢以成天下之治者無他惟先之
好學而已矣夫聖主必得賢臣以弘治功賢臣
亦賴聖主以端治本是二人者未始不相須也
然而恒阻於相遇之疎者以上無好學之君故
下無弼直之臣所以明良不交德業未盛而治
===
道藐然卑卑無足論者是故君之圖治也莫急
於親賢而其親賢也莫先於好學君而好學則
天下稱聖主矣主聖則臣賢臣賢則君德益崇
君業益廣而開天下於太平者由此其致也輔
助德業而致太平請因范氏之論而申之今夫
人君以眇然之躬寄之乎巍然之上四海之廣
兆民之衆其所以待治於我者何可勝數近而
朝廷欲其正之内而中國欲其安之外而荒服
欲其撫之推而極於天地莫不欲其調燮而奠
punctuated:
好學，又用賢之本也。是作能發明之，而構思精深，摛詞古雅，殆非淺學可到，宜錄爲多士式。
考試官敎諭陳批：平實中有古調，佳作也。
考試官敎諭尹批：氣充詞逸，逈異諸作。
論曰：人君得賢以成天下之治者，無他，惟先之好學而已矣。夫聖主必得賢臣以弘治功，賢臣亦賴聖主以端治本，是二人者，未始不相須也。然而恒阻於相遇之疎者，以上無好學之君，故下無弼直之臣，所以明良不交，德業未盛，而治道藐然卑卑無足論者。是故君之圖治也，莫急於親賢；而其親賢也，莫先於好學。君而好學，則天下稱聖主矣。主聖則臣賢，臣賢則君德益崇，君業益廣，而開天下於太平者，由此其致也。「輔助德業而致太平」，請因范氏之論而申之。
今夫人君以眇然之躬，寄之乎巍然之上，四海之廣，兆民之衆，其所以待治於我者，何可勝數？近而朝廷欲其正之，内而中國欲其安之，外而荒服欲其撫之，推而極於天地，莫不欲其調燮而奠
translation_en:
…devotion to learning is in turn the foundation of employing the worthy. This composition manages to elucidate this point; its conception is refined and profound, and its phrasing possesses an antique elegance. This is hardly something shallow learning could attain, and it ought to be recorded as a model for the many scholars.

Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: Within its plainness and solidity there is an antique tone; it is an excellent piece.

Examiner and Instructor Yin comments: Its vital breath is full and its phrasing transcendent, vastly different from the other compositions.

The discourse states: The means by which a ruler obtains worthy men to accomplish the governance of the world is none other than first devoting himself to learning. Now, a sage ruler must obtain worthy ministers in order to broaden the achievements of governance, and worthy ministers likewise rely on a sage ruler to rectify the fundamental root of governance; these two have never not depended on one another. Yet what constantly hinders them through the rarity of their meeting is that because there is no ruler devoted to learning above, there are consequently no ministers who assist and correct below. Therefore, when an enlightened ruler and fine ministers do not come together, virtue and grand enterprises do not flourish, and the Way of governance remains puny, base, and unworthy of discussion. For this reason, when a ruler plans for governance, nothing is more urgent than drawing close to the worthy; and in drawing close to the worthy, nothing comes before devotion to learning. If the ruler is devoted to learning, then the world will acclaim him as a sage ruler. When the ruler is sage, the ministers are worthy; when the ministers are worthy, the ruler's virtue becomes ever more exalted and his enterprises ever more expansive, and opening the world unto Great Peace is brought about by this means. "Assisting in virtue and enterprise to bring about Great Peace"—allow me to build upon Master Fan's [Fan Zuyu 范祖禹] discourse and elaborate upon it.

Now then, the ruler places his solitary person high atop a lofty position. Across the vastness of the Four Seas and the multitude of the millions of people, how could all the matters awaiting governance from him possibly be counted? Near at hand, the court desires that he rectify it; within, the Central States desire that he pacify them; without, the wild domains desire that he soothe them; and extending all the way to Heaven and Earth, there is nothing that does not desire that he harmonize and settle…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
麗之其責何重也人君以一人之身而當紛紜
艱大之務如必自爲而後太平之業始成吾懼
其力不勝而日不給也已易曰首出庶物萬國
咸寧言聖人得位行道致太平之占也書曰野
無遺賢萬邦咸寧言羣材畢集而後天下各得
其理也夫崇臺峻宇非一木之材也洪流巨浸
非一勺之潤也盛德大業非一己之能也所由
致者衆矣故天將興太平之治必篤生聖人爲
斯世之主又必降生賢哲以供斯世之用然自
===
古聖明之君未始不欲得賢以官天地府萬物
共建不世之治而賢哲之士亦未始不欲得聖
明之君以彰道德顯事業翊成太平之功然而
千百載乃一相遇焉此其故何也蓋人君好尚
關天下之耳目繫天下之安危而天下之人亦
各挟其術而投於人主之好衆好交攻則君心
日蔽君心日蔽則賢士日疎矣安望其輔助德
業而弼成至治哉誠使人君知德業不自隆也
而本於賢才知賢才不自輔也而由於好學於
punctuated: 麗之，其責何重也！人君以一人之身，而當紛紜艱大之務，如必自爲而後太平之業始成，吾懼其力不勝而日不給也已。《易》曰：「首出庶物，萬國咸寧。」言聖人得位行道，致太平之占也。《書》曰：「野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。」言羣材畢集，而後天下各得其理也。夫崇臺峻宇，非一木之材也；洪流巨浸，非一勺之潤也；盛德大業，非一己之能也，所由致者衆矣。故天將興太平之治，必篤生聖人爲斯世之主，又必降生賢哲以供斯世之用。然自古聖明之君，未始不欲得賢以官天地、府萬物，共建不世之治；而賢哲之士，亦未始不欲得聖明之君，以彰道德、顯事業，翊成太平之功。然而千百載乃一相遇焉，此其故何也？蓋人君好尚，關天下之耳目，繫天下之安危，而天下之人，亦各挟其術而投於人主之好。衆好交攻，則君心日蔽；君心日蔽，則賢士日疎矣。安望其輔助德業，而弼成至治哉？誠使人君知德業不自隆也，而本於賢才；知賢才不自輔也，而由於好學。於
translation_en: …and settle them in their proper places—how heavy is this responsibility! When a ruler, in his single person, faces such multitudinous, difficult, and great affairs, if he must do everything himself before the enterprise of Great Peace can be accomplished, I fear that his strength will not suffice and his days will not be enough. The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Rising above the multitude of things, the myriad states all enjoy peace." This speaks of the auspice of a sage gaining the throne, practicing the Way, and bringing about Great Peace. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "When no worthy men are left neglected in the wilds, the myriad states all enjoy peace." This means that only after all talents are gathered together does everything in the world attain its proper order. Indeed, a lofty terrace or a towering hall is not built from the timber of a single tree; a mighty river or a vast lake is not filled by the moisture of a single spoonful; glorious virtue and a great enterprise are not achieved by the ability of a single individual—those by whom they are brought about are many. Therefore, when Heaven is about to raise up an era of Great Peace, It must surely give birth to a sage to be the lord of that age, and must also send down worthy and wise men to serve the needs of that age. Yet since antiquity, sage and enlightened rulers have never not wished to obtain worthies in order to govern Heaven and Earth and store up the myriad things, jointly establishing an extraordinary rule; and worthy and wise scholars have likewise never not wished to find a sage and enlightened ruler in order to manifest their moral way, distinguish their achievements, and assist in accomplishing the work of Great Peace. Yet they meet only once in a hundred or a thousand years—what is the reason for this? It is because the preferences of a ruler engage the eyes and ears of the world and are tied to the security and peril of the world, while the people of the world each clutch their own arts to cater to the ruler's fondness. When competing attractions assail him from all sides, the ruler's mind becomes daily more obscured; as the ruler's mind becomes daily more obscured, worthy scholars become daily more estranged. How then can one hope for them to assist his virtue and enterprise and help bring about supreme governance? If only the ruler truly understands that virtue and enterprise do not flourish of themselves, but are rooted in worthy talents; and understands that worthy talents do not come to assist of themselves, but are drawn through a love of learning. Thereupon…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
是惟精惟一允執厥中取堯舜之所以學者而
學焉學而好焉不矜不伐制事制心取禹湯之
所以學者而學焉學而好焉亦式亦入不泄不
忘取文武之所以學者而學焉學而好焉夫好
堯舜禹湯文武之學則其心卽堯舜禹湯文武
之心也其道卽堯舜禹湯文武之道也固不必
弓旌之招也蒲輪之聘也而物色之旁求也一
人元良則庶明勵翼當必有臯夔稷契伊吕周
召之儔出於其間爲之相導前後爲之左右夾
===
===
持由是近而朝廷則以法相序以禮相睦而朝
廷莫不正矣內而中國則禮樂明備刑政脩舉
而中國莫不安矣外而荒服則大小相維强弱
相守而荒服莫不撫矣上而經天則隂陽循序
日月順軌而天道莫不調燮矣下而緯地則山
之不童澤之不涸而地道莫不奠麗矣將天下
之人稱之曰此協和風動之業也平成允殖之
休也攸同永清之績也太平極治之世不在唐
虞三代而復見於今日矣何其盛哉夫弓矢不
punctuated: 是惟精惟一、允執厥中，取堯、舜之所以學者而學焉，學而好焉；不矜不伐、制事制心，取禹、湯之所以學者而學焉，學而好焉；亦式亦入、不泄不忘，取文、武之所以學者而學焉，學而好焉。夫好堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之學，則其心卽堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之心也，其道卽堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之道也。固不必弓旌之招也、蒲輪之聘也，而物色之旁求也。一人元良，則庶明勵翼，當必有臯、夔、稷、契、伊、吕、周、召之儔出於其間，爲之相導前後，爲之左右夾持。由是近而朝廷，則以法相序、以禮相睦，而朝廷莫不正矣；內而中國，則禮樂明備、刑政脩舉，而中國莫不安矣；外而荒服，則大小相維、强弱相守，而荒服莫不撫矣；上而經天，則隂陽循序、日月順軌，而天道莫不調燮矣；下而緯地，則山之不童、澤之不涸，而地道莫不奠麗矣。將天下之人稱之曰：「此協和風動之業也，平成允殖之休也，攸同永清之績也。」太平極治之世，不在唐、虞、三代，而復見於今日矣，何其盛哉！夫弓矢不
translation_en:
…this, by being discerning and single-minded, and sincerely holding fast to the Mean, he takes that by which Yao and Shun learned and learns it, learning it and delighting in it; by neither boasting nor bragging, and regulating affairs through righteousness and the mind through rites, he takes that by which Yu and Tang learned and learns it, learning it and delighting in it; by observing both admonition and compliance, neither neglecting the near nor forgetting the distant, he takes that by which Kings Wen and Wu learned and learns it, learning it and delighting in it. Now, if he delights in the learning of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, then his mind is none other than the mind of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, and his Way is none other than the Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Truly, there will be no need for summonses with bows and banners, or invitations with rush-wrapped wheels, or searching far and wide by descriptions of appearance. When the One Man is supremely virtuous, the many enlightened ones exert themselves to assist him; there will surely emerge among them the likes of Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, Xie, Yi Yin, Lü Shang, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao, to guide him from before and behind, and to support him on the left and right.

From this, near at hand in the royal court, officials will be ordered by law and harmonized by ritual, so that nothing in the court will not be rectified; within, throughout the Central States, rites and music will be brilliantly complete and punishments and governance well-maintained, so that nothing in the Central States will not be at peace; without, in the wild domains, great and small will hold together and strong and weak will mutually defend, so that nothing in the wild domains will not be pacified; above, in ordering Heaven, yin and yang will follow their sequence and the sun and moon will keep to their paths, so that nothing in the Way of Heaven will not be harmonized; below, in organizing Earth, the mountains will not be stripped bare and the marshes will not dry up, so that nothing in the Way of Earth will not be settled and arrayed. Then the people of the world will praise it, saying: "This is the enterprise of harmony and wind-like transformation; this is the blessing of peace, order, and flourishing; this is the achievement of universal unity and eternal peace." An era of Great Peace and supreme governance will not be confined to Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, but will be seen again today—how glorious indeed! Now, if bow and arrow are not…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
調則后羿不能以中鵠驂服不馴則造父不能
以致遠上下不交則帝王無以治天下然則欲
致太平者可不好學以為夾輔之本哉雖然日
與諸儒講論同異心非不顓也然雜以霸道卒
為基禍之君耆舊如蕭望之宗正如劉更生可
謂左右有人矣然優游不斷何補於儒生之純
用由是而知明君以務學為急務學以知道為
先苟為知道則精一數言何要約也然足以致
放勳之盛如不知道即白虎石渠徒滋聚訟耳
===
何裨於君德何益於治道哉此又君人所當知
表
擬宋龍圖閣學士孫奭進無逸圖表〔天聖五年〕
張孫念
同考試官教諭嚴批措詞莊雅用意謹嚴而忠
懇之忱溢于言表深得臣子告君之體
考試官教諭陳批不事雕鏤工緻自不可到
考試官教諭尹批典則駢儷宛然宋人矩矱
punctuated:
調，則后羿不能以中鵠；驂服不馴，則造父不能以致遠；上下不交，則帝王無以治天下。然則欲致太平者，可不好學以為夾輔之本哉？雖然，日與諸儒講論同異，心非不顓也，然雜以霸道，卒為基禍之君；耆舊如蕭望之、宗正如劉更生，可謂左右有人矣，然優游不斷，何補於儒生之純用？由是而知：明君以務學為急，務學以知道為先。苟為知道，則「精一」數言，何要約也？然足以致放勳之盛。如不知道，即白虎、石渠，徒滋聚訟耳，何裨於君德？何益於治道哉？此又君人所當知。

表

擬宋龍圖閣學士孫奭進《無逸圖》表〔天聖五年〕
張孫念

同考試官教諭嚴批：措詞莊雅，用意謹嚴，而忠懇之忱，溢于言表，深得臣子告君之體。
考試官教諭陳批：不事雕鏤，工緻自不可到。
考試官教諭尹批：典則駢儷，宛然宋人矩矱。
translation_en:
… well-adjusted, then even Houyi could not hit the bull's-eye; if the outer and inner team-horses are not well-trained, then even Zaofu could not reach distant places; and if ruler and subjects do not commune with one another, then emperors and kings have no means by which to govern the world. This being so, how could anyone who desires to bring about Great Peace not love learning as the foundation of mutual assistance and support? Even so, someone who daily discusses similarities and differences with the various Confucian scholars is not lacking in single-minded devotion; yet if he mixes it with the Way of the Hegemon (badao), he will ultimately become a ruler who lays the foundations of disaster. With a venerable elder like Xiao Wangzhi 蕭望之 and a Director of the Imperial Clan (Zongzheng) like Liu Gengsheng 劉更生 [Liu Xiang 劉向], he could be said to have capable men at his side; yet if he is indecisive and irresolute, what avail is there in the pure employment of Confucian scholars? From this we know that an enlightened ruler takes devotion to learning as his urgent task, and in devoting himself to learning he takes understanding the Way as his first priority. If indeed he understands the Way, then how concise and essential are those few words on being "refined and single-minded" (jing yi)! Yet they were sufficient to bring about the flourishing of Fangxun [Emperor Yao]. If he does not understand the Way, then even the conferences at the White Tiger Hall (Baihu) and the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiqu) merely multiply contentious debates—of what benefit are they to the ruler's virtue, and of what advantage to the Way of governance? This, too, is what one who rules over men ought to know.

Memorial (Biao)

An Imitation of the Memorial by Sun Shi 孫奭, Academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion (Longtuge xueshi) of the Song Dynasty, Presenting the Illustrated "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi tu) [Fifth Year of the Tiansheng Era (1027)]
By Zhang Sunnian 張孫念

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor (Jiaoyu) Yan 嚴: The phrasing is dignified and elegant, the intent careful and rigorous, and a spirit of loyal sincerity overflows beyond the words—it deeply captures the proper form of a minister addressing his sovereign.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳: Without engaging in artificial carving, its refined craftsmanship is naturally unattainable by others.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yin 尹: Classical in standard and balanced in parallel prose, it has the exact measure and style of a Song-dynasty writer.

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天聖五年某月某日龍圖閣學士臣孫奭
謹以所繪無逸圖上
進者伏以
帝王懷保治之艱道存居敬臣子效匡時之略
志在納忠謹稽古以陳詞用繪圖而進
御上裨
睿覽下竭愚誠臣奭誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊惟
繼體守成當識王業艱難之自深居端拱
宜知小民稼穡之依自昔聖帝明王莫不
===
