憂深慮遠迨成王爲有周之令主而姬公
陳無逸之良規謂治民者不敢荒寧以基
業者克自抑畏殷鑒不遠自祖甲而遡及
中宗周命維新由太王而傳及文考備述
前人之迪哲用匡厥后之持盈此元聖保
惠之謨乃萬世君人之鑑顧世多逸豫而
臣鮮憂危獻賦上林徒侈遊田之樂繪屏
長夜益增淫佚之資貞觀寶箴初聞讜論
開元金鑑僅見嘉言未能儆戒于無虞安
punctuated: 天聖五年某月某日，龍圖閣學士臣孫奭謹以所繪《無逸圖》上進者。伏以帝王懷保治之艱，道存居敬；臣子效匡時之略，志在納忠。謹稽古以陳詞，用繪圖而進御，上裨睿覽，下竭愚誠。臣奭誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟繼體守成，當識王業艱難之自；深居端拱，宜知小民稼穡之依。自昔聖帝明王，莫不憂深慮遠。迨成王爲有周之令主，而姬公陳《無逸》之良規，謂治民者不敢荒寧，以基業者克自抑畏。殷鑒不遠，自祖甲而遡及中宗；周命維新，由太王而傳及文考。備述前人之迪哲，用匡厥后之持盈。此元聖保惠之謨，乃萬世君人之鑑。顧世多逸豫，而臣鮮憂危：獻賦上林，徒侈遊田之樂；繪屏長夜，益增淫佚之資。《貞觀寶箴》，初聞讜論；《開元金鑑》，僅見嘉言。未能儆戒于無虞，安
translation_en:
On a certain day of a certain month in the fifth year of the Tiansheng era [1027], your servant Sun Shi 孫奭, Academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, respectfully presents to the throne the Illustrated "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi tu) that he has had painted.

Humbly I reflect that when emperors and kings cherish the difficulties of preserving good governance, the Way lies in abiding in reverence; when ministers and subjects offer strategies for rectifying the age, their ambition lies in tendering loyalty. I respectfully examine antiquity to set forth my words, and by means of a painted illustration present them to the throne, above to aid Your sagely perusal, and below to exhaust my humble sincerity. Your servant Shi, in utmost fear and trepidation, bows his head to the ground again and again.

I privately reflect that in succeeding to the line and conserving what has been achieved, a ruler ought to recognize whence the hardships of the royal enterprise arose; dwelling deep within the palace with hands folded in ceremonial ease, he should know the sowing and reaping upon which the common people depend. Since antiquity, there have been no sage emperors or enlightened kings who did not harbor deep anxieties and far-reaching concerns. When King Cheng became a worthy sovereign of the House of Zhou, the Duke of Zhou set forth the fine precepts of "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi), saying that those who govern the people dare not indulge in荒wildness or repose, and that those who lay the foundations of an enterprise are able to restrain themselves in awe. The mirror of Yin was not far off, tracing back from Zu Jia to Zhongzong; the Mandate of Zhou was made new, transmitted from King Tai down to the Cultured Father [King Wen]. He recounted in full how predecessors walked in wisdom, thereby assisting his sovereign in preserving fullness. This counsel of protective kindness from the Great Sage is indeed a mirror for rulers of ten thousand generations.

Yet in later ages there has been much idle pleasure, and ministers have rarely felt anxiety over peril: presenting rhapsodies on the Shanglin Park merely magnified the pleasures of excursion and hunting; painting screens of the Long Night only added to the resources of licentiousness and dissipation. In the Precious Admonitions of the Zhenguan Era (Zhenguan baozhen), one first heard honest discourse; in the Golden Mirror of the Kaiyuan Era (Kaiyuan jinjian), one merely saw fine words. If one is unable to maintain caution and vigilance when there is no apparent cause for alarm, how can one…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
望治平之有象欲輸忠悃實待
明時玆蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
仁孝性成
聰明天啓纘
祖宗之統心切時幾握參兩之權功勤日昃財
以不蓄爲富惠徧浹於閭閻兵以不用爲
威恩覃敷于寰宇
經筵
===
御講盛暑猶專
慈幄問安常朝必謹是
聖敬蓋已緝熈于宥密然臣愚每欲啓沃於論
思伏念臣奭奮跡草茅獨諳田家之味致
身
廊廟誤沾仙仗之香封祀疏陳荷優容于
先帝學田請給蒙嘉納于
聖皇洊列儒紳叨陪近侍遭逢不偶忍謝葵傾
納約有階敢忘芹獻竊計豐亨之治當存
punctuated: 望治平之有象？欲輸忠悃，實待明時。玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，仁孝性成，聰明天啓。纘祖宗之統，心切時幾；握參兩之權，功勤日昃。財以不蓄爲富，惠徧浹於閭閻；兵以不用爲威，恩覃敷于寰宇。經筵御講，盛暑猶專；慈幄問安，常朝必謹。是聖敬蓋已緝熈于宥密，然臣愚每欲啓沃於論思。伏念臣奭，奮跡草茅，獨諳田家之味；致身廊廟，誤沾仙仗之香。封祀疏陳，荷優容于先帝；學田請給，蒙嘉納于聖皇。洊列儒紳，叨陪近侍。遭逢不偶，忍謝葵傾？納約有階，敢忘芹獻？竊計豐亨之治，當存
translation_en:
…how can one hope for the signs of order and peace? Wishing to pour forth one’s loyal sincerity, one must truly await an enlightened age.

Now, I humbly encounter Your Majesty [〇〇〇〇]: your benevolence and filial piety are formed by nature, and your intelligence and clarity are inspired by Heaven. Succeeding to the lineage of the ancestors, your heart is earnestly attentive to every timely incipient tendency; grasping the authority that participates in the triad of Heaven and Earth, your labors are diligent until the sun declines. Regarding wealth as residing in not hoarding resources, your beneficence thoroughly saturates the village lanes; regarding martial awe as residing in not resorting to arms, your grace spreads widely across the entire realm. At the Classics Colloquia and Imperial Lectures, even in the height of summer you remain single-mindedly focused; in inquiring after the well-being of the Empress Dowager at the Maternal Curtain, at every regular audience you are unfailingly reverent. Thus Your Sacred Reverence already shines continuously in deep serenity; yet in my foolishness I ever wish to offer enlightenment and nourishment in deliberation and reflection.

I humbly reflect that I, Your Servant Shi (Wuyi Shi 無逸奭, i.e., Song Jing 宋璟 / Cui Zhimian 崔植 / Wu Jing 吳兢 or rather Song Jing / Han Xiu / Cui Shi / rather Song Jing 宋璟? No, 臣奭 is Song Jing's or rather someone named Shi — here "Your Servant Shi"), rose from humble rustic origins and alone understand the taste of the farming household; having devoted my person to the imperial court, I have undeservedly beenimbued with the fragrance of the immortal cortège. When I presented a memorial regarding the Feng and Shan sacrifices, I received indulgent tolerance from the Late Emperor; when I requested the bestowal of school lands, I was favored with gracious acceptance by Your Sacred Majesty. Repeatedly ranked among the Confucian gentry, I have undeservedly accompanied the close attendants. Having met with such an extraordinary encounter, how could I bear to decline the sunflower’s inclination toward the sun? Since there is a path for introducing candid counsel, how could I dare forget the humble offering of wild celery? I privately reckon that in an era of abundance and prosperity, one ought to preserve…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
乾惕之心道已備於周書忠無加於姬旦
敬稽往蹟爰假丹青詳述前聞用加摹寫
上下數百年理亂之故編摩不遺先後六
七君脩短之由形容殆盡為商家為周室
懿範具在目中曰天命曰民情龜鑑可陳
掌上排雲補
袞祗輸一得之忱就日銘盤切冀
九重之矚儻蒙
燕暇時
===
賜監觀主善為師知其繪後于素惟敬作所察
其意不在圖則經史未披揖古人千載之
上堂階不下燭羣情萬里之餘雖不敢上
擬戶牖之銘亦庶幾下同韋弦之助也伏
願
治謹日中
憂先天下
罔于觀罔于逸恒思一日二日之煩
卽康功卽田功不忘匹婦匹夫之勝
punctuated: 乾惕之心；道已備於《周書》，忠無加於姬旦。敬稽往蹟，爰假丹青；詳述前聞，用加摹寫。上下數百年理亂之故，編摩不遺；先後六七君脩短之由，形容殆盡。為商家、為周室，懿範具在目中；曰天命、曰民情，龜鑑可陳掌上。排雲補袞，祗輸一得之忱；就日銘盤，切冀九重之矚。儻蒙燕暇，時賜監觀：主善為師，知其繪後于素；惟敬作所，察其意不在圖。則經史未披，揖古人千載之上；堂階不下，燭羣情萬里之餘。雖不敢上擬戶牖之銘，亦庶幾下同韋弦之助也。伏願治謹日中，憂先天下。罔于觀、罔于逸，恒思一日二日之煩；卽康功、卽田功，不忘匹婦匹夫之勝。
translation_en: … a mind of tireless vigilance; this Way is already fully set forth in the Book of Zhou, and in loyalty none can surpass Ji Dan [the Duke of Zhou]. Reverently examining past traces, I have therefore borrowed the painter's colors; recounting in detail what was heard of old, I have thereby made this depiction. The causes of order and disorder spanning several hundred years are compiled and traced without omission; the reasons for the long or short reigns of six or seven successive rulers are portrayed nearly in full. Whether the house of Shang or the royal house of Zhou, their admirable models are all before the eyes; whether the Mandate of Heaven or the sentiments of the people, this mirror of warning can be laid out upon the palm. Parting the clouds to mend the imperial robes, I merely offer the sincerity of my humble insight; approaching the sun to engrave the washbasin, I earnestly hope for the gaze of the Ninefold Palace. Should I be favored, in Your moments of leisure, with Your timely inspection and reflection—taking goodness as Your teacher, knowing that the painting comes after the plain silk; making reverence Your dwelling place, perceiving that the meaning lies beyond the picture itself—then even before opening the Classics and Histories, You may bow to the ancients across a thousand years; without descending the hall steps, You may illuminate the conditions of the multitude beyond ten thousand miles. Though I dare not compare this above to the inscriptions on doors and windows, below it may perhaps serve like the aid of soft leather and taut bowstring. I humbly pray that You will be cautious of governance when the sun is at its zenith, and be anxious before the rest of the world is anxious; neither indulging in sightseeing nor indulging in ease, ever mindful of the myriad affairs of a single day or two; applying Yourself to peaceful achievements and to agricultural achievements, never forgetting that a common man or common woman may prevail over You…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
學古訓而有獲
監成憲以無愆
寶曆縣長凝命軼景員之盛金甌鞏固卜年邁
郊鄏之隆臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所繪無逸圖隨
表上
進以
聞
===
第叁場
策五道
第一問
王應泰
同考試官教諭王批農桑生民首務我
祖宗家法之美
皇上勤民之誠是作發揚殆盡
考試官教諭陳批我
國家良法美意子能闡揚之非夙抱經濟者耶敬服敬服
punctuated:
學古訓而有獲，監成憲以無愆。寶曆縣長，凝命軼景員之盛；金甌鞏固，卜年邁郊鄏之隆。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹以所繪《無逸圖》隨表上進以聞。

第叁場

策五道

第一問

王應泰

同考試官教諭王批：農桑，生民首務。我祖宗家法之美，皇上勤民之誠，是作發揚殆盡。
考試官教諭陳批：我國家良法美意，子能闡揚之，非夙抱經濟者耶？敬服，敬服！
translation_en:
…study the ancient lessons and reap their rewards; observe the established statutes and commit no error. May the precious calendar stretch on endlessly, consolidating the Mandate to surpass the flourishing of the vast domain of Yin; may the golden vessel of the state remain firmly secure, its divined years exceeding the prosperity of the settlement at Jiaoru. Your servant is overcome with the utmost awe and anxious reverence in looking up to Heaven and beholding Your Sacred Majesty, and respectfully presents the painted Illustrations of "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi tu) along with this memorial for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session

Five Policy Essays

First Question

Wang Yingtai

Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: Farming and sericulture are the foremost tasks for the livelihood of the people. The beauty of our Imperial Ancestors' family statutes and the sincerity of His Majesty's diligence on behalf of the people are brought to light almost exhaustively in this composition.
Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: You have been able to elucidate the fine laws and admirable intentions of our dynasty—are you not one who has long cherished the art of statecraft? Truly admirable, truly admirable!

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭尹批事核詞雅非騁言說以為
奇者比宜錄以式
帝王之治天下也不能以一身勞天下而
不能不以其一身風天下其風天下者何
也政治之首務則農桑是也生民之大端
則衣食是也生民一日不得食則饑其饑
也聖人曰我饑之也一日不得衣則寒其
寒也聖人曰我寒之也民以衣食為天聖
人則以民為天民不得其所天聖人之心
===
則有遑遑不能自已者此非不知自逸也
其心誠慮四海之廣九州之衆一有不得
其所不得不以身嘗之也慮其無食也乃
身為之勸以導之耕慮其無衣也乃身為
之勸以導之蠶蓋聖人之所為天必與民
之所以為天者各相足而後已也此親農
親桑所以為風天下之道而我
太祖之開極
列聖之紹基
punctuated:
考試官敎諭尹批：「事核詞雅，非騁言說以為奇者比，宜錄以式。」

帝王之治天下也，不能以一身勞天下，而不能不以其一身風天下。其風天下者何也？政治之首務，則農桑是也；生民之大端，則衣食是也。生民一日不得食則饑，其饑也，聖人曰：「我饑之也。」一日不得衣則寒，其寒也，聖人曰：「我寒之也。」民以衣食為天，聖人則以民為天。民不得其所天，聖人之心則有遑遑不能自已者。此非不知自逸也，其心誠慮四海之廣、九州之衆，一有不得其所，不得不以身嘗之也。慮其無食也，乃身為之勸以導之耕；慮其無衣也，乃身為之勸以導之蠶。蓋聖人之所為天，必與民之所以為天者各相足而後已也。此親農親桑，所以為風天下之道，而我太祖之開極、列聖之紹基、
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Yin comments: "The facts are verified and the diction is elegant. This is not comparable to those who merely give free rein to rhetoric for the sake of novelty; it should be recorded as a model."

In governing the empire, emperors and kings cannot toil for the entire empire with their own single person, yet they cannot fail to inspire the empire with their own single person. What is it by which they inspire the empire? The foremost priority of governance is agriculture and sericulture; the fundamental need of the people is clothing and food. If the people go a single day without food, they hunger; when they hunger, the sage says, "It is I who have caused them to hunger." If they go a single day without clothing, they are cold; when they are cold, the sage says, "It is I who have caused them to be cold." The people regard clothing and food as their Heaven, whereas the sage regards the people as his Heaven. When the people do not obtain what they rely upon as Heaven, the sage's heart is anxious and unable to rest. This is not because he does not know how to take his own ease; his heart truly worries that across the breadth of the Four Seas and the multitudes of the Nine Provinces, if even one person fails to find their proper place, he must personally experience their hardship. Worrying that they lack food, he personally encourages them so as to guide them in plowing; worrying that they lack clothing, he personally encourages them so as to guide them in tending silkworms. Indeed, what the sage regards as his Heaven and what the people regard as their Heaven must each be mutually satisfied before he will rest. This is why personally practicing agriculture and personally practicing sericulture serve as the Way to inspire the empire, and why in our Grand Progenitor's (Taizu) founding of the imperial standard, the Successive Sages' continuation of the foundation, …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇上之御天必有以身勞之而風動四方也執
事策士首及乎此愚生耕而食織而衣者
也遊皞皞之中而誦法先王之道請以成
周之所以致盛治者為執事誦之人孰不
曰帝王以天下之食為食其所食者玉也
以天下之衣為衣其所衣者錦也乃曰必
身親為之耕而與民同食必身親為之蠶
而與民同衣此則許行之所以說神農者
堯舜且不暇為之乃不知聖人不能以一
===
身勞天下而不能不以一身風天下帝王
愛天下甚於愛其身誠不欲以天下食一
人必欲以一人為天下食也不欲以天下
衣一人必欲以一人為天下衣也以一人
為天下食乃天下之所取足以為食以一
人為天下衣乃天下之所取足以為衣吾
讀豳風七月之詩而歎周之君王身親耕
稼以勸天下耕其風天下以足食乎吾讀
葛覃之詩而歎周之后妃身治葛事以勸
punctuated: 皇上之御天，必有以身勞之而風動四方也。執事策士，首及乎此。愚生耕而食、織而衣者也，遊皞皞之中，而誦法先王之道，請以成周之所以致盛治者，為執事誦之。人孰不曰：「帝王以天下之食為食，其所食者玉也；以天下之衣為衣，其所衣者錦也。」乃曰：「必身親為之耕而與民同食，必身親為之蠶而與民同衣。」此則許行之所以說神農者，堯、舜且不暇為之。乃不知聖人不能以一身勞天下，而不能不以一身風天下。帝王愛天下甚於愛其身，誠不欲以天下食一人，必欲以一人為天下食也；不欲以天下衣一人，必欲以一人為天下衣也。以一人為天下食，乃天下之所取足以為食；以一人為天下衣，乃天下之所取足以為衣。吾讀《豳風·七月》之詩，而歎周之君王身親耕稼以勸天下耕，其風天下以足食乎！吾讀《葛覃》之詩，而歎周之后妃身治葛事以勸
translation_en: … and the reigning Emperor's governance of the realm—have surely involved personally toiling at these tasks so as to inspire the four quarters by example. In putting policy questions to the candidates, Your Excellency has addressed this very matter first of all. I, this foolish student, am one who plows to eat and weaves to be clothed; wandering amid the serene contentment of a well-ruled age and reciting and modeling myself on the Way of the Former Kings, I beg leave to recite for Your Excellency the means by which the flourishing rule of the Zhou at its height was achieved. Who among men does not say: "Emperors and kings take the food of All under Heaven as their food, and what they eat is like jade; they take the clothing of All under Heaven as their clothing, and what they wear is brocade"? Yet if someone then says: "They must personally plow for themselves and eat together with the common people, and must personally tend silkworms for themselves and dress together with the common people," this is what Xu Xing 許行 claimed of the Divine Husbandman (Shennong 神農)—something that even Yao 堯 and Shun 舜 had no leisure to do. Such people fail to understand that while the sages cannot labor for All under Heaven with their own single bodies, they cannot fail to inspire All under Heaven by the example of their own single bodies. Emperors and kings love All under Heaven more than they love their own persons. Truly, they do not wish to have All under Heaven feed one man, but rather wish that one man provide food for All under Heaven; they do not wish to have All under Heaven clothe one man, but rather wish that one man provide clothing for All under Heaven. When one man provides food for All under Heaven, therein lies that from which All under Heaven draws sufficiency in food; when one man provides clothing for All under Heaven, therein lies that from which All under Heaven draws sufficiency in clothing. When I read the ode "Seventh Month" (Qiyue 七月) in the "Airs of Bin" (Binfeng 豳風), I sigh in admiration at how the kings of Zhou personally engaged in plowing and sowing to encourage All under Heaven to plow—did they not inspire All under Heaven so as to make food sufficient? When I read the ode "Spreading Kudzu" (Getan 葛覃), I sigh in admiration at how the queen and consorts of Zhou personally attended to the work of kudzu linen to encourage…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天下蠶其風天下以足衣乎何者彼誠不
愛一身之勞而欲以所勞者風天下也以
躬籍之禮考之周則曰孟春天子為籍千
畝冕而朱紘躬秉耒措之于參保介之御
間天子三推以時入之以供粢盛乃王后
則率六宮而生穜稑之種獻之于王此則
躬籍之禮先天下以勸農者也以親蠶之
禮考之周則曰季春王后薦鞠衣於先帝
齋戒親東鄉躬桑禁婦女毋觀蠶事既登
===
分繭稱絲以供郊廟之服而天子則作居
范宮以觀桑者飲于桑中此則親蠶之禮
先天下以勸桑者也夫親耕者帝也而后
則獻種玆父道也亦猶乎母道也親蠶者
后也而帝則觀桑玆母道也亦猶乎父道
也以宗廟粢盛必曰帝所親籍以郊廟之
服必曰后所親蠶玆勸民也亦所以饗帝
也所以饗親也玆二者所以為風天下之
道也而仁孝之大端畢舉之矣自周而後
punctuated: 天下蠶，其風天下以足衣乎！何者？彼誠不愛一身之勞，而欲以所勞者風天下也。以躬籍之禮考之周，則曰：孟春，天子為籍千畝，冕而朱紘，躬秉耒，措之于參保介之御間。天子三推，以時入之，以供粢盛；乃王后則率六宮而生穜稑之種，獻之于王。此則躬籍之禮，先天下以勸農者也。以親蠶之禮考之周，則曰：季春，王后薦鞠衣於先帝，齋戒，親東鄉躬桑，禁婦女毋觀，蠶事既登，分繭稱絲，以供郊廟之服；而天子則作居范宮以觀桑者，飲于桑中。此則親蠶之禮，先天下以勸桑者也。夫親耕者帝也，而后則獻種，玆父道也，亦猶乎母道也；親蠶者后也，而帝則觀桑，玆母道也，亦猶乎父道也。以宗廟粢盛，必曰帝所親籍；以郊廟之服，必曰后所親蠶。玆勸民也，亦所以饗帝也，所以饗親也。玆二者，所以為風天下之道也，而仁孝之大端畢舉之矣。自周而後，
translation_en:
… all under Heaven to rear silkworms; was this not inspiring all under Heaven by example to have sufficient clothing? Why was this? Because they truly did not begrudge the toil of their own persons, wishing instead to use their own toil to inspire all under Heaven by example.

If we examine the rite of personal plowing in the Zhou, it states: In the first month of spring, the Son of Heaven establishes a sacred field of a thousand mou. Wearing the ceremonial cap with red cords, he personally holds the plow, placing it between the third man in the chariot—the Assistant to the Protector—and the charioteer. The Son of Heaven pushes the plow three times, harvesting the grain in season to supply the sacrificial millet for the vessels; meanwhile, the Queen leads the Six Palaces to sprout the early-ripening and late-ripening seeds and presents them to the King. Such was the rite of personal plowing, setting an example before all under Heaven to encourage agriculture.

If we examine the rite of personal sericulture in the Zhou, it states: In the last month of spring, the Queen presents the yellow mulberry-picking robe to the Former Emperors, fasts and purifies herself, and personally faces east to pick mulberry leaves with her own hands. Women are forbidden from merely looking on as spectators. When the silkworm work is completed, the cocoons are distributed and the silk weighed in order to supply the vestments for the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temples; meanwhile, the Son of Heaven builds and resides in the Fan Palace [?] to observe the mulberry-pickers, drinking amidst the mulberry groves. Such was the rite of personal sericulture, setting an example before all under Heaven to encourage mulberry cultivation.

Now, the one who personally plows is the Emperor, yet the Queen presents the seeds—this is the way of a father, and yet it partakes of the way of a mother as well. The one who personally tends silkworms is the Queen, yet the Emperor observes the mulberry picking—this is the way of a mother, and yet it partakes of the way of a father as well. Regarding the sacrificial grain for the ancestral temple, it must be said to come from what the Emperor personally plowed; regarding the vestments for the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temple, they must be said to come from the silkworms the Queen personally tended. This is encouraging the people, and it is also the means of making offerings to the Lord on High, and the means of making offerings to one's ancestors. These two rites are the way to inspire all under Heaven by example, and in them the great principles of benevolence and filial piety are fully encompassed. From the Zhou onward, …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
籍田有歌望耕有臺先農有壇東郊有儀
非不侈然具也乃吾獨有取於漢文之親
耕則以其躬儉爲天下先也蠶織有室先
蠶有祠躬蠶有壇養蠶有經非不侈然具
也乃吾獨有取於明德之濯龍則以其躬
儉爲六宮冠也我
太祖起自民間混一寰宇
思天下之無食欲有以食之
思天下之無衣欲有以衣之欲以一身風民
===
以農桑者何不至也洪武巳酉
太祖親耕籍田于南郊
太后親率內外命婦蠶于北郊
曰天子籍田千畝所以供粢盛備饙饌其率
天下以躬耕而導之足食者也
曰民間但有隙地皆令種桑其率天下以躬
蠶而導之足衣者也
諭廷臣則曰衣帛當思織女之勤食粟當念農
夫之苦
punctuated: 籍田有歌，望耕有臺，先農有壇，東郊有儀，非不侈然具也；乃吾獨有取於漢文之親耕，則以其躬儉爲天下先也。蠶織有室，先蠶有祠，躬蠶有壇，養蠶有經，非不侈然具也；乃吾獨有取於明德之濯龍，則以其躬儉爲六宮冠也。我太祖起自民間，混一寰宇，思天下之無食，欲有以食之；思天下之無衣，欲有以衣之。欲以一身風民以農桑者，何不至也！洪武巳酉，太祖親耕籍田于南郊，太后親率內外命婦蠶于北郊。曰：「天子籍田千畝，所以供粢盛、備饙饌。」其率天下以躬耕而導之足食者也。曰：「民間但有隙地，皆令種桑。」其率天下以躬蠶而導之足衣者也。諭廷臣則曰：「衣帛當思織女之勤，食粟當念農夫之苦。」
translation_en:
…there were odes for the sacred field, terraces for viewing the plowing, altars to the First Husbandman, and ceremonies in the eastern suburb—all of these were provided in grand fashion. Yet I single out for praise Emperor Wen of Han's personal plowing, because he practiced frugality in his own person to set an example for the entire realm. There were chambers for sericulture and weaving, shrines to the First Sericulturist, altars for personal sericulture, and manuals on raising silkworms—all of these were provided in grand fashion. Yet I single out for praise Empress Mingde's sericulture at the Zhuolong Palace, because she practiced frugality in her own person to stand at the head of the Six Palaces.

Our Grand Progenitor rose from among the common people and unified the realm. Mindful of those in the world without food, he wished to provide them with food; mindful of those in the world without clothes, he wished to provide them with clothes. In wishing through his own person to inspire the people to agriculture and sericulture, what stone did he leave unturned? In the jiyou year of the Hongwu reign (1369), the Grand Progenitor personally plowed the sacred field in the southern suburb, and the Empress Dowager personally led the titled women of the inner court and outer court to tend silkworms in the northern suburb. He declared: "The Son of Heaven's sacred field of a thousand mu is meant to supply the sacrificial grain and prepare the steamed offerings"—thus leading the world in personal plowing and guiding it toward sufficiency in food. He declared: "Wherever there is spare land among the people, let them all plant mulberries"—thus leading the world in personal sericulture and guiding it toward sufficiency in clothing. Instructing his court officials, he said: "When wearing silk, one should think of the toil of the weaving woman; when eating grain, one should remember the hardship of the farmer." Instructing…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諭司農卿則曰自什一之制湮奇巧之技作而
後農桑之業廢其拳拳於天下作其勤起其
惰者也仍於
內苑置籍田蠶室以時觀省我
太祖所以垂範作則於前何一時一念不以此
二者以身勞之而風天下耶
列聖以來以
太祖之心爲心以
太祖之政爲政
===
成祖務本之訓因
仁宗巡道途而作也而天下之耕者勸
宣宗織婦之賦因見田間織婦而作也而天下
之蠶者勸
世宗更翼善冠
親耕臺下籍田
皇后親祀先蠶詣採桑臺乃
豳風無逸之詩
穀祗蠶壇之賦
punctuated: 諭司農卿則曰：「自什一之制湮，奇巧之技作，而後農桑之業廢。」其拳拳於天下，作其勤、起其惰者也。仍於內苑置籍田、蠶室，以時觀省。我太祖所以垂範作則於前，何一時一念不以此二者以身勞之而風天下耶？列聖以來，以太祖之心爲心，以太祖之政爲政。成祖《務本之訓》，因仁宗巡道途而作也，而天下之耕者勸；宣宗《織婦之賦》，因見田間織婦而作也，而天下之蠶者勸；世宗更翼善冠，親耕臺下籍田，皇后親祀先蠶，詣採桑臺，乃《豳風》《無逸》之詩、《穀祗》《蠶壇》之賦，
translation_en:
… In instructing the Chief Minister of Agriculture (Sinong qing), he said: "Once the system of the one-tenth tax fell into oblivion and ingenious, extravagant crafts arose, the occupations of farming and sericulture fell into neglect." Such was his earnest devotion to the realm, rousing its diligence and shaking off its indolence. Furthermore, within the Inner Park he established the sacred field (jitian) and the silkworm house, inspecting them at the proper seasons. In thus setting down a model and establishing a standard in former times, was there ever a single moment or a single thought in which Our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) did not personally toil at these two tasks so as to inspire the realm by his example?

Throughout the reigns of the Successive Sages, they have taken the mind of the Grand Progenitor as their mind, and the governance of the Grand Progenitor as their governance. The "Instructions on Attending to the Fundamental" (Wuben zhi xun) of the Ancestor of Accomplishment (Chengzu, the Yongle Emperor) was composed on the occasion of the Benevolent Ancestor (Renzong, the Hongxi Emperor) travelling along the roads, and thereby the tillers of the realm were encouraged. The "Rhapsody on the Weaving Woman" (Zhifu zhi fu) of the Propagating Ancestor (Xuanzong, the Xuande Emperor) was composed upon seeing a woman weaving amid the fields, and thereby the silkworm-rearers of the realm were encouraged. The Epochal Ancestor (Shizong, the Jiajing Emperor) changed the Design of the Winged Philanthropy Cap (yishanguan) and personally plowed the sacred field beneath the terrace, while the Empress personally sacrificed to the First Sericulturist (Xian Can) and proceeded to the Mulberry-Picking Terrace (Caisang tai); and as for the poems on the "Airs of Bin" (Binfeng) and "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi), and the rhapsodies on the "Spirit of the Grain" (Guzhi) and the "Sericulture Altar" (Cantan), …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
宸章燦爛不一而足我
列聖所以繼美承芳於後何一時一念不以此
二者以身先之而風天下耶肆我
皇上
冲年御宇四海向風雨暘愆期則
徹樂減膳露禱
宮中其祈農者何勤也淮徐水災則
遣官發賑蠲免公租其恤民者何急也東南
織造半減前額積逋絲絹並從
===
除免何懇懇念民農桑之苦也以衣三澣以
事再思
親灑
宸翰以相警省何肫肫敦尚躬儉之風也邇者
特俞廷臣之請將舉籍禮未幾下
明旨期舉于來年則
親耕以風天下耕
親蠶以風天下桑所以供粢盛供祭服以輸
皇上之仁孝者四海將快覩之是孰非
punctuated: 宸章燦爛，不一而足。我列聖所以繼美承芳於後，何一時一念不以此二者以身先之而風天下耶？肆我皇上冲年御宇，四海向風。雨暘愆期，則徹樂減膳，露禱宮中，其祈農者何勤也！淮徐水災，則遣官發賑，蠲免公租，其恤民者何急也！東南織造，半減前額，積逋絲絹，並從除免，何懇懇念民農桑之苦也！以衣三澣，以事再思，親灑宸翰以相警省，何肫肫敦尚躬儉之風也！邇者特俞廷臣之請，將舉籍禮；未幾，下明旨期舉于來年。則親耕以風天下耕，親蠶以風天下桑，所以供粢盛、供祭服以輸皇上之仁孝者，四海將快覩之。是孰非
translation_en:
… the imperial compositions shone brilliantly, more than one could recount. In the way our successive sage emperors inherited this beauty and carried on this virtuous fragrance in later times, what moment or what thought was not devoted to taking the lead in person in these two matters so as to inspire the realm?

Thus our Emperor ascended the throne in his youth, and all within the four seas turned toward his influence. When rain and sunshine failed to come in season, he suspended music, reduced his meals, and prayed in the open air within the palace—how diligent he is in praying for husbandry! When floods struck the Huai and Xuzhou regions, he dispatched officials to distribute relief and remitted public taxes—how urgent he is in showing compassion for the people! In the imperial weaving establishments of the southeast, he reduced the previous quotas by half, and accumulated arrears of silk and taffeta were altogether remitted—how earnestly he bears in mind the hardships of the people's farming and sericulture! Taking "washing garments thrice" and "thinking twice in affairs" as his themes, he personally brushed imperial calligraphy for mutual admonition and reflection—how sincerely he esteems the custom of personal frugality!

Recently, he specially approved the request of the court officials and was about to perform the ritual of the sacred field; shortly thereafter, he issued an explicit decree scheduling its performance for the coming year. Then, by plowing in person to inspire the realm to plow, and by tending silkworms in person to inspire the realm to cultivate mulberry, the means of supplying sacrificial grain and sacrificial vestments so as to express the Emperor's benevolence and filial piety will soon be joyfully witnessed by all within the four seas. Is not all of this…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇上以一人足天下之食以一人足天下之衣
而風天下者耶是孰非
皇上之敬
天尊
親備仁孝之大端者耶是孰非周家之七月葛
覃所以成有道之長者耶是孰非遵
太祖之開極垂範而百世不改者耶是孰非守
列聖之紹美承芳而奕世無斁者耶抑愚有說
焉
===
===
皇上以
冲睿之年秉
天縱之聖華夷一統中外一心卽堯舜垂衣
端拱之化奚讓焉乃治理不難于其始而
難于其終不貴于其文而貴于其實勸農
以耕是也乃民之不耕而食者何以驅也
又民之無所得耕者何以恤也大司農之
數數告乏者何以充也勸民以桑是也乃
民之不織而衣者何以易也風俗之侈靡
punctuated:
皇上以一人足天下之食，以一人足天下之衣，而風天下者耶？是孰非皇上之敬天尊親，備仁孝之大端者耶？是孰非周家之《七月》、《葛覃》所以成有道之長者耶？是孰非遵太祖之開極垂範而百世不改者耶？是孰非守列聖之紹美承芳而奕世無斁者耶？

抑愚有說焉。皇上以冲睿之年，秉天縱之聖，華夷一統，中外一心，卽堯、舜垂衣端拱之化，奚讓焉？乃治理不難于其始而難于其終，不貴于其文而貴于其實。勸農以耕，是也；乃民之不耕而食者，何以驅也？又民之無所得耕者，何以恤也？大司農之數數告乏者，何以充也？勸民以桑，是也；乃民之不織而衣者，何以易也？風俗之侈靡，
translation_en:
… His Majesty, through his own single person, providing sufficient food for the world and sufficient clothing for the world, thereby inspiring the entire realm by his example? How is any of this not His Majesty revering Heaven and honoring his parents, fulfilling the great essentials of benevolence and filial piety? How is any of this not that whereby the "Seventh Month" (Qiyue) and "Spreading Kudzu" (Getan) odes of the house of Zhou achieved the enduring longevity of a state possessing the Way? How is any of this not following the founding standard and enduring model of the Grand Progenitor (Taizu), not to be altered for a hundred generations? How is any of this not upholding the inherited excellence and fragrant legacy of the successive sacred emperors, never to be wearied of for generation after generation?

Yet this humble one has something further to say. In his youthful and sagacious years, endowed with Heaven-bestowed sageness, His Majesty has unified Chinese and non-Chinese alike, with court and provinces of one mind; even compared to the transformative rule of Yao and Shun, who governed withrobes hanging down and hands folded in composure, how does this yield anything to them? Still, in governance and order, what is difficult is not the beginning but the end; what is valued is not the outward form but the substance. To encourage farming through plowing is indeed right; yet as for those among the people who eat without plowing, how are they to be driven back to the fields? Moreover, as for those among the people who have no land to plow, how are they to be relieved? And as for the Grand Minister of Agriculture (Dasinong, i.e., the Ministry of Revenue) repeatedly reporting shortages, how are the granaries and treasuries to be replenished? To encourage the people in sericulture is indeed right; yet as for those among the people who wear clothes without weaving, how are their habits to be changed? When customs are extravagant and wasteful, …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以淫巧相尚者何以禁也織造之有加而
東南之無以辦也何以節也兢乎其兢愼
乎其愼後無改于其前終無變于其始堯
舜端拱垂衣之化不在唐虞而在
今日此則葵藿書生所望於
聖天子者也
第二問
文立本
同考試官教諭嚴批是作以
===
皇上孝敬為體天不息末復以
聖學為言是抱忠愛之誠者錄之
考試官教諭陳批發明
皇上孝敬之意有關治體之大最為真切可嘉
考試官教諭尹批議論剴切格調古雅是通
達國體而有得者取之
天之所以為天者何也曰健也健者不息
也人君者奉天之不息以子民也人臣者
奉君之不息以共職也天唯不息故風雨
punctuated:
以淫巧相尚者，何以禁也？織造之有加，而東南之無以辦也，何以節也？兢乎其兢，愼乎其愼，後無改于其前，終無變于其始，堯舜端拱垂衣之化，不在唐虞而在今日。此則葵藿書生所望於聖天子者也。

第二問
文立本
同考試官教諭嚴批：是作以皇上孝敬為體天不息，末復以聖學為言，是抱忠愛之誠者，錄之。
考試官教諭陳批：發明皇上孝敬之意，有關治體之大，最為真切，可嘉。
考試官教諭尹批：議論剴切，格調古雅，是通達國體而有得者，取之。

天之所以為天者，何也？曰：健也。健者，不息也。人君者，奉天之不息以子民也；人臣者，奉君之不息以共職也。天唯不息，故風雨
translation_en:
…and competing with one another in extravagant contrivances—how is this to be prohibited? As for the quotas for imperial textile production being increased while the Southeast has no means to supply them—how is this to be moderated? If the ruler is ever so cautious and ever so prudent, so that what comes later does not alter what went before, and the end does not change from the beginning, then the transformative governance of Yao and Shun, ruling with folded hands and hanging robes, will lie not in the eras of Tang and Yu, but in the present day. This is what this humble scholar, turning like the sunflower toward the sun, hopes for from the Sacred Son of Heaven.

Second Policy Question
Wen Liben (文立本)
Associate Examiner and Instructor Yan (嚴) comments: This essay takes His Majesty's filial piety and reverence as embodying Heaven's unceasing nature, and at the end speaks further of the Sacred Learning. It is the work of one who cherishes a sincere loyalty and affection; record it for selection.
Examiner and Instructor Chen (陳) comments: It elucidates the meaning of His Majesty's filial piety and reverence, touching upon the great essentials of the structure of governance. It is most genuine and earnest, and worthy of praise.
Examiner and Instructor Yin (尹) comments: The discussion is incisive and to the point, and the style is ancient and elegant. It is the work of one who thoroughly understands the principles of statecraft and has attained true insight; select it.

What is it whereby Heaven is Heaven? It is said: vigor. To be vigorous is to be unceasing. The ruler of men upholds Heaven's unceasingness in order to treat the people as his children; the minister of men upholds the ruler's unceasingness in order to discharge his official duties. Because Heaven alone is unceasing, wind, rain,…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
露雷鼓舞萬物者弗窮也君唯不息故慶
賞刑威鼓舞萬民者弗已也臣唯不息故
章程約束竭力以效之君者匪懈也是何
也必有所為乃可以無為必有所事乃可
以無事也君曰我無為也舉所謂慶賞刑
威且敝帚視之其敝必將至於有所不可
為臣曰我無事也舉所謂章程約束且瓦
礫視之其勢必至於多事而且僨事是故
上下交相警以有成也其成者君奉此不
===
息以成天也臣奉此不息以成君也書曰
元首明哉股肱良哉庶事康哉是明也良
也乃其所以康也非執事者之所謂作於
明者哉元首叢脞哉股肱惰哉萬事墮哉
是叢也惰也乃其所以墮也非執事者之
所謂玩於習者哉觀此則我
皇上之稽查章奏隨事考成奉
天之不息以鼓舞天下臣工者可得而言也愚
生讀易至豫曰盱豫悔至蠱曰裕父之蠱
punctuated: 露雷鼓舞萬物者弗窮也；君唯不息，故慶賞刑威鼓舞萬民者弗已也；臣唯不息，故章程約束竭力以效之君者匪懈也。是何也？必有所為，乃可以無為；必有所事，乃可以無事也。君曰：「我無為也。」舉所謂慶賞刑威，且敝帚視之，其敝必將至於有所不可為。臣曰：「我無事也。」舉所謂章程約束，且瓦礫視之，其勢必至於多事而且僨事。是故上下交相警以有成也。其成者，君奉此不息以成天也，臣奉此不息以成君也。《書》曰：「元首明哉，股肱良哉，庶事康哉。」是明也、良也，乃其所以康也，非執事者之所謂作於明者哉？「元首叢脞哉，股肱惰哉，萬事墮哉。」是叢也、惰也，乃其所以墮也，非執事者之所謂玩於習者哉？觀此，則我皇上之稽查章奏，隨事考成，奉天之不息以鼓舞天下臣工者，可得而言也。愚生讀《易》，至〈豫〉曰「盱豫悔」，至〈蠱〉曰「裕父之蠱」，
translation_en:
… dew, and thunder rouse and animate the myriad things without exhaustion. Because the ruler alone never ceases, rewards, commendations, punishments, and awe rouse and animate the myriad people without end. Because the ministers alone never cease, they exert their utmost strength in upholding regulations and restraints to serve the ruler without slackening. Why is this so? Only when there is purposeful action can one attain non-action; only when affairs are attended to can one attain freedom from affairs. If the ruler says, "I practice non-action," and regards all that are called rewards, commendations, punishments, and awe as mere worn-out brooms, the resulting decay will inevitably reach a point where nothing can be done. If the ministers say, "We are free from affairs," and regard all that are called regulations and restraints as mere broken tiles and rubble, the situation will inevitably lead to a proliferation of troubles and the ruin of affairs. Therefore, superiors and inferiors mutually admonish one another in order to achieve success. In such success, the ruler upholds this unceasingness to fulfill the work of Heaven, and the ministers uphold this unceasingness to fulfill the work of the ruler.

The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "When the head is enlightened, the limbs are good, and all affairs are prosperous." This enlightenment and goodness are precisely the means by which prosperity is achieved—is this not what Your Excellency refers to as "arising through enlightenment"? "When the head is petty and vexatious, the limbs are lazy, and all affairs are ruined." This pettiness and laziness are precisely the means by which ruin comes about—is this not what Your Excellency refers to as "growing negligent through habit"? Viewing it from this perspective, we may proceed to speak of how Our Emperor inspects memorials, evaluates performance according to each matter, and upholds the unceasingness of Heaven in order to rouse and animate the officials of the empire.

When I, a humble student, read the Book of Changes (Yi), upon reaching the hexagram Yu ("Enthusiasm"), where it says "Looking upward for gratification brings regret," and upon reaching the hexagram Gu ("Decay"), where it says "Tolerating the decay left by the father," …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
未嘗不置書歎也日旴者其所以致悔乎
裕者其所以成蠱乎至大有曰遏惡揚善
順天休命至乾曰終日乾乾夕惕若又悚
然懼躍然省也曰揚善遏惡者其君之所
以順天命保大有者乎曰乾乾惕若者其
臣之所以懷憂勤履危疑者乎為人君者
一日二日有萬幾凜乎若朽索之馭六馬
則安得當六馬之逸而惟其索之朽是何
以齊萬幾為人臣者進思盡忠退思補過
===
夙夜以事一人則安得進無所思退無所
補是何以事一人然後知發强剛毅明君
所以宰制六合而怠緩悅從且無以理一
身何以理天下為也千古而上稱極治者
則孰過唐虞哉其所有五臣以相都俞吁
咈也何事詢何事省也乃堯之命舜曰詢
事考言乃言底可績其於臯陶曰屢省乃
成是其所詢者所省者卽所謂禹臯稷契
益之人也卽所謂平水土播百穀敷五敎
punctuated: 未嘗不置書歎也，日：「旴者，其所以致悔乎？裕者，其所以成蠱乎？」至《大有》曰：「遏惡揚善，順天休命。」至《乾》曰：「終日乾乾，夕惕若。」又悚然懼、躍然省也，曰：「揚善遏惡者，其君之所以順天命、保大有者乎？」曰：「乾乾惕若者，其臣之所以懷憂勤、履危疑者乎？」為人君者，一日二日有萬幾，凜乎若朽索之馭六馬，則安得當六馬之逸而惟其索之朽？是何以齊萬幾？為人臣者，進思盡忠，退思補過，夙夜以事一人，則安得進無所思、退無所補？是何以事一人？然後知發强剛毅，明君所以宰制六合；而怠緩悅從，且無以理一身，何以理天下為也！千古而上，稱極治者則孰過唐、虞哉？其所有五臣以相都俞吁咈也，何事詢？何事省也？乃堯之命舜曰：「詢事考言，乃言底可績。」其於臯陶曰：「屢省乃成。」是其所詢者、所省者，卽所謂禹、臯、稷、契、益之人也，卽所謂平水土、播百穀、敷五敎、
translation_en:
… I have never failed to set down the book and sigh, saying: "Is not gazing upward in complacency that which brings about regret? Is not indulgence that which allows decay to take hold?" Coming to the Dayou (Great Possession) hexagram, which says, "repress evil and promote good, and so comply with the beneficent mandate of Heaven," and to the Qian (Creative) hexagram, which says, "all day long active and vigilant, and at evening still apprehensive," I am again struck with awe and moved to reflection, saying: "Is not promoting good and repressing evil the means by which a ruler complies with the Mandate of Heaven and preserves great possession?" And saying: "Is not being active, vigilant, and apprehensive the means by which a minister cherishes anxious diligence and treads through peril and doubt?" For one who is a ruler of men, in a single day or two there are ten thousand affairs of state, and he is filled with awe as if driving six horses with rotten reins—how then can he face the bolting of the six horses while letting his reins remain rotten? How could that suffice to regulate the ten thousand affairs? For one who is a minister, when advancing to court he thinks of exhausting his loyalty, and when retiring he thinks of making up for his faults, serving the One Man from dawn to night—how then can he advance without thought and retire without making amends? How could that suffice to serve the One Man? Only then does one know that vigorous strength and resolute firmness are the means by which an enlightened ruler governs the six directions of the realm, whereas sluggish laxity and compliant flattery are insufficient even to govern one's own person—how then could they serve to govern the Empire?

Looking back across all antiquity, in speaking of supreme governance, what age surpassed that of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun]? They possessed five ministers with whom they exchanged expressions of agreement and admonition—what need was there to inquire, and what need to inspect? Yet when Yao charged Shun, he said: "Inquire into affairs and examine words, and your words have been capable of achieving results." And in speaking with Gao Yao, it was said: "Frequently inspect what has been accomplished." Thus those whom they inquired of and those whom they inspected were none other than the men Yu, Gao Yao, Hou Ji, Xie, and Yi, and their affairs were none other than leveling the waters and lands, sowing the hundred grains, spreading the five teachings, …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
明五刑共工朕虞之事也而帝之必詢之
必考之也乃四方之所以風動萬邦之所
以協和也唐虞而下稱極治者則孰過成
周哉其所有十臣以相疏附後先也則何
事計何事考也而春秋所紀王公卿士自
朝日至日入無不自計乃職者周禮所載
歲時月日無不有考者是其所計者所考
者則所謂周公旦召公奭散宜生南宮适
人也即所謂勤王家脩有夏田功康功之
===
事也而周之必計之必考之也乃萬邦之
所以咸和四海之所以永清也吾於西漢
得一君焉曰宣帝是也則綜覈名實以為
治也吾於東漢得一君焉光武是也則總
攬威權以為治也吾於唐得一君焉德宗
是也則强明果斷更條格以為法也說者
謂漢業衰於宣帝察察之過也夫漢宣當
霍氏後乾剛倒持非綜覈無以起敝乃不
咎孝元之優柔而罪宣帝之明察耶說者
punctuated: 明五刑、共工朕虞之事也。而帝之必詢之、必考之也，乃四方之所以風動，萬邦之所以協和也。唐虞而下，稱極治者則孰過成周哉？其所有十臣以相疏附後先也，則何事計？何事考也？而《春秋》所紀，王公卿士自朝日至日入，無不自計乃職者；《周禮》所載，歲、時、月、日無不有考者。是其所計者、所考者，則所謂周公旦、召公奭、散宜生、南宮适人也；即所謂勤王家、脩有夏、田功、康功之事也。而周之必計之、必考之也，乃萬邦之所以咸和，四海之所以永清也。吾於西漢得一君焉，曰宣帝是也，則綜覈名實以為治也；吾於東漢得一君焉，光武是也，則總攬威權以為治也；吾於唐得一君焉，德宗是也，則强明果斷、更條格以為法也。說者謂漢業衰於宣帝察察之過也。夫漢宣當霍氏後，乾剛倒持，非綜覈無以起敝，乃不咎孝元之優柔，而罪宣帝之明察耶？說者
translation_en:
… clarifying the five punishments, and overseeing the public works and the royal mountains and marshes. And the reason why the sovereigns insisted on inquiring into them and testing them was precisely how the four quarters were moved as by the wind and the myriad states were brought into harmony. After Tang and Yu, among those eras praised for reaching the pinnacle of governance, what could surpass Accomplished Zhou (Cheng Zhou)? Since it possessed ten ministers who mutually drew the distant near and assisted from before and behind, what need was there to reckon accounts? What need was there to evaluate performance? Yet as recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) [or rather, Discourses of the States], kings, dukes,卿 (chief ministers), and 士 (servicemen), from daybreak until sunset, none failed to reckon their own official duties; and as set down in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), by year, season, month, and day, none went without evaluation. Thus, those whom they reckoned and evaluated were none other than such men as Dan, Duke of Zhou (Zhougong Dan), Shi, Duke of Shao (Shaogong Shi), San Yisheng, and Nangong Kuo; and the matters involved were none other than toiling for the royal house, cultivating the ways of Xia, agricultural works, and works of pacification. And the reason why the Zhou insisted on reckoning them and evaluating them was precisely how the myriad states were all brought into harmony and the four seas were made forever tranquil.

In the Western Han, I find one ruler—namely, Emperor Xuan—who governed by comprehensively verifying names and realities. In the Eastern Han, I find one ruler—namely, Emperor Guangwu—who governed by gathering all authority and power into his own hands. In the Tang, I find one ruler—namely, Emperor Dezong—who established laws by being forceful, discerning, resolute, and altering regulations and ordinances. Commentators claim that the Han enterprise declined due to the fault of Emperor Xuan's overly fastidious scrutiny. Now, Emperor Xuan of Han came after the Huo clan's dominance, when sovereign authority had been held upside down; without comprehensive verification of performance, there was no way to remedy the decay. How then can one not blame the weak indecisiveness of Emperor Yuan, and instead fault the clear scrutiny of Emperor Xuan? Commentators…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
謂治體失于光武攬權之過也夫光武當
新莽後王綱解紐非總攬無以維風乃不
知光武之得而謂光武之失耶獨德宗剛
褊自用苛察為明其所明者非所明而明
也其所察者非所察而察也此尚不足與
孝宣光武言而可語治天下之大道哉我
太祖肇造區夏設官分職我
列聖獨秉威權賞勤罰惰開濟作考功圖令所
司日記行事較勤惰
===
高皇帝賜第以旌其賢此非我
祖宗立考成之勸者哉顧佐糾不職三十人
章皇帝即時罷斥賜
璽書褒美此非我
祖宗立考成之罰者哉薄海內外無不奉宣
德意遵行勿怠二百年來紀綱整肅法度脩明
則
太祖奉此不息者以立極於先
列聖奉此不息者以承美於後故有以駕唐虞
punctuated: 謂治體失于光武，攬權之過也。夫光武當新莽後，王綱解紐，非總攬無以維風，乃不知光武之得，而謂光武之失耶？獨德宗剛褊自用，苛察為明，其所明者，非所明而明也；其所察者，非所察而察也。此尚不足與孝宣、光武言，而可語治天下之大道哉！我太祖肇造區夏，設官分職；我列聖獨秉威權，賞勤罰惰。開濟作《考功圖》，令所司日記行事，較勤惰，高皇帝賜第以旌其賢，此非我祖宗立考成之勸者哉？顧佐糾不職三十人，章皇帝即時罷斥，賜璽書褒美，此非我祖宗立考成之罰者哉？薄海內外，無不奉宣德意，遵行勿怠。二百年來，紀綱整肅，法度脩明，則太祖奉此不息者以立極於先，列聖奉此不息者以承美於後，故有以駕唐虞、
translation_en:
…say that the proper form of governance was lost under Guangwu, through the fault of his monopolizing authority. Now, Guangwu came after Wang Mang's Xin dynasty, when the royal cords of state had come undone; without gathering all authority into his own hands, there was no way to uphold the political order. How then can they fail to recognize Guangwu's success and instead call it Guangwu's failure? Only Emperor Dezong was obstinate, narrow-minded, and self-willed, taking petty scrutiny for discernment. What he treated as discernment was discerning what ought not to be discerned; what he treated as scrutiny was scrutinizing what ought not to be scrutinized. Such a ruler is not even worthy of being spoken of alongside Emperor Xuan and Guangwu—how could one discuss with him the great Way of governing the realm!

Our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) founded the realm in the central lands, establishing offices and apportioning duties; our successive sacred emperors alone wielded majestic authority, rewarding the diligent and punishing the indolent. Kai Ji (開濟) drew up the Chart for the Evaluation of Merit (Kaogong tu), ordering the competent authorities to record daily performance so as to compare diligence and indolence, and the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi, the Hongwu Emperor) bestowed a residence upon him to honor his worthiness—was this not how our imperial ancestors established encouragement in the evaluation of official performance? Gu Zuo (顧佐) impeached thirty officials who were derelict in their duties, and the Accomplished Emperor (Zhang Huangdi, the Xuande Emperor) immediately dismissed and expelled them, bestowing an imperial letter under the dynastic seal to praise him—was this not how our imperial ancestors established punishment in the evaluation of official performance? Within and beyond the four seas, there were none who did not reverently proclaim their virtuous intentions and comply with them without slackening. For two hundred years, state discipline has been orderly and strict, and laws and institutions well-maintained and clear. This is because the Grand Progenitor upheld this unceasing principle to establish the supreme standard first, and the successive sacred emperors upheld this unceasing principle to carry on its excellence thereafter; thus they have been able to surpass Tang and Yu,…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
軼周室邁漢唐也邇年狃於治安樂於簡
便
章程顯布而奉行則稍習於媮安
約束嚴明而遵守則稍流於怠慢貪墨酷鷙
有定論也乃遲留不發則何所懲惡也功
賞虛冒有明徵也乃稽遲不上則何所懲
欺也錢穀額賦徵解有期也乃會計徒具
而輸輓後時何以充國計也刑獄擬議輕
重有律也乃停閣逾年而寃抑不白何以
===
重民命也條陳利病詳勘巳定也乃徒取
文具而不亟下何以補民生也中外習以
爲常莫知其非此非所以脩臣職也此非
所以仰體
皇上奉
天不息以出治之心也
皇上俞輔臣之請下稽查之令沉章積牘起弊
維風按時之先後以定其限隨事之緩急
以考其成
punctuated: 軼周室、邁漢唐也。邇年狃於治安，樂於簡便，章程顯布，而奉行則稍習於媮安；約束嚴明，而遵守則稍流於怠慢。貪墨酷鷙有定論也，乃遲留不發，則何所懲惡也？功賞虛冒有明徵也，乃稽遲不上，則何所懲欺也？錢穀額賦徵解有期也，乃會計徒具而輸輓後時，何以充國計也？刑獄擬議輕重有律也，乃停閣逾年而寃抑不白，何以重民命也？條陳利病詳勘巳定也，乃徒取文具而不亟下，何以補民生也？中外習以爲常，莫知其非，此非所以脩臣職也，此非所以仰體皇上奉天不息以出治之心也。皇上俞輔臣之請，下稽查之令，沉章積牘，起弊維風，按時之先後以定其限，隨事之緩急以考其成。
translation_en: …surpass the House of Zhou, and outstrip the Han and Tang dynasties. In recent years, however, officials have grown accustomed to peace and order and fond of ease and convenience. Statutes and regulations are clearly promulgated, yet in carrying them out they have gradually grown habituated to indolent comfort; injunctions and restraints are strict and explicit, yet in observing them they have gradually lapsed into negligence. That certain officials are corrupt, rapacious, cruel, and ruthless is a settled matter, yet action is delayed and not initiated—how then is evil to be punished? That rewards for merit have been falsely claimed is clearly evidenced, yet reports are held back and not submitted—how then is deceit to be penalized? The collection and forwarding of grain and revenue quotas have fixed deadlines, yet accounting is a mere formality and transport falls behind schedule—how then are the state finances to be supplied? The deliberation and sentencing of criminal cases according to their gravity are governed by statutes, yet cases are shelved for over a year and grievances go unredressed—how then are the lives of the people to be valued? Itemized proposals on advantages and abuses have been thoroughly investigated and settled, yet they are treated as mere paperwork and not promptly handed down for implementation—how then is the livelihood of the people to be aided? Inside and outside the court, officials have grown accustomed to this as the norm, none recognizing that it is wrong. This is not the way to fulfill the duties of a minister; this is not the way to reverently embody Your Majesty's mind, which emulates Heaven's ceaselessness in bringing forth governance. Your Majesty has approved the request of the Grand Secretaries and handed down the order for auditing and inspection—clearing away submerged memorials and accumulated documents, remedying abuses and upholding the administrative ethos, setting deadlines according to chronological priority, and evaluating performance according to the urgency of each affair…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
內閣則總其綱也部院則分其事也臺省則
核其實也下之監司下之郡縣出之
九重之上達之萬里之遠若雷之震之也若風
之披之也此則以唐虞之所詢所省者詢
之省之也何過於明此則以成周之所計
所考者計之考之也何過于察內外臣工
罔不洗滌積玩夙夜秉公奉
詔書者惕惕然若
天語之臨也入
===
聖覽者兢兢然若
天顏之涖也論報嚴明故貪墨酷鷙無所匿也
報勘眞實故功賞虛冒無所售也輸納有
限故錢穀額賦無後時也問理有條故刑
獄冤抑無覆盆也條別有章遵行不失故
利民生者無不舉也此則
皇上奉
天之不息以出治而內外臣工罔不若也羣臣
體
punctuated: 內閣則總其綱也，部院則分其事也，臺省則核其實也，下之監司，下之郡縣，出之九重之上，達之萬里之遠，若雷之震之也，若風之披之也。此則以唐虞之所詢、所省者詢之、省之也，何過於明？此則以成周之所計、所考者計之、考之也，何過于察？內外臣工罔不洗滌積玩，夙夜秉公。奉詔書者惕惕然若天語之臨也，入聖覽者兢兢然若天顏之涖也。論報嚴明，故貪墨酷鷙無所匿也；報勘眞實，故功賞虛冒無所售也；輸納有限，故錢穀額賦無後時也；問理有條，故刑獄冤抑無覆盆也；條別有章，遵行不失，故利民生者無不舉也。此則皇上奉天之不息以出治，而內外臣工罔不若也；羣臣體
translation_en: …The Grand Secretariat summarizes their main principles; the Ministries and Censorate divide their administration; the Censors and Supervising Secretaries verify their reality; and they are handed down to the Surveillance Commissions and Circuits, and down to the prefectures and counties. Issuing from above the Ninefold Palace and reaching to a distance of ten thousand li, it is like thunder shaking them, like wind sweeping over them. This is to inquire into and examine them by means of what Tang and Yu inquired into and examined—how could this be overly acute? This is to reckon and evaluate them by means of what the accomplished Zhou reckoned and evaluated—how could this be overly scrutinizing? Officials inside and outside the capital all without exception cleanse away accumulated laxity, upholding public-mindedness day and night. Those who receive imperial edicts are filled with awe, as though the words of Heaven were descending upon them; those whose reports enter for His Majesty's perusal are tremblingly cautious, as though they were in the presence of the imperial countenance. Because evaluations and reports are strict and clear, the greedy, corrupt, cruel, and rapacious have nowhere to hide; because reports and investigations are genuine and truthful, false and fraudulent claims to merit and reward have no way to pass; because deliveries and payments have deadlines, money, grain, and fixed tax quotas are never behind schedule; because interrogations and adjudications are orderly, in criminal cases and litigation there are no unredressed wrongs hidden beneath an overturned basin; because itemized regulations have clear statutes that are observed without fail, everything that benefits the people's livelihood is carried out. Thus Your Majesty models himself on Heaven's unceasingness to bring forth governance, and officials at court and in the provinces all without exception conform; the body of officials embodies…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天之不息以從
上而久遠章奏無不理也此以有爲爲無爲以
有事爲無事之道也雖然是不息也存之
爲內聖之心非勤學不足純此心也發之
爲外王之業非勤政不足弘此業也我
皇上日
御經筵講論不輟其所以爲
聖學者何勤也日
御朝宁寒暑不輟其所以爲
===
聖政者何勤也草莽之士則以爲勤學者其本
也勤政者其用也今天下華夷一統海宇
晏然稱極治矣此心少有所息則聲色貨
利得撓其眞也左右近習得抵其間也土
木遊佚得投其隙也非所以語純心也勤
學也誠願
皇上之愼之也
養之於不覩不聞之中
察之於莫見莫顯之際無怠朝也無怠夕也
punctuated: 天之不息以從上，而久遠章奏無不理也。此以有爲爲無爲，以有事爲無事之道也。雖然，是不息也，存之爲內聖之心，非勤學不足純此心也；發之爲外王之業，非勤政不足弘此業也。我皇上日御經筵，講論不輟，其所以爲聖學者，何勤也！日御朝宁，寒暑不輟，其所以爲聖政者，何勤也！草莽之士，則以爲勤學者，其本也；勤政者，其用也。今天下華夷一統，海宇晏然，稱極治矣。此心少有所息，則聲色貨利得撓其眞也，左右近習得抵其間也，土木遊佚得投其隙也，非所以語純心也、勤學也。誠願皇上之愼之也，養之於不覩不聞之中，察之於莫見莫顯之際，無怠朝也，無怠夕也，
translation_en:
…the unceasingness of Heaven in order to follow the Sovereign, so that even long-pending memorials are all attended to. This is the Way of taking purposeful action as non-action, and taking engagement in affairs as having no affairs.

Even so, as for this unceasingness, when preserved within, it is the mind of inner sageliness, yet without diligence in learning one cannot keep this mind pure; when manifested without, it is the enterprise of outer kingliness, yet without diligence in governance one cannot broaden this enterprise. Our Emperor daily attends the Classics Colloquium, expounding and discussing without cease—how diligent he is in pursuing sagely learning! He daily presides over the court audience, never ceasing in winter's cold or summer's heat—how diligent he is in conducting sagely governance! Yet as a rustic scholar, I consider diligence in learning to be the root, and diligence in governance to be its application. Today, Chinese and non-Chinese throughout the realm are unified, and all within the seas is peaceful and tranquil; it may be called the pinnacle of good order. Yet if this mind relaxes even slightly, then sensual pleasures, music, and material wealth will be able to disturb its genuineness; close attendants and favorites will be able to exploit the opening; and construction projects and idle excursions will be able to slip into the breach. This is no way to speak of purifying the mind or of diligence in learning. I truly wish that Your Majesty will be cautious regarding this: nurturing it amidst what is neither seen nor heard, examining it at the juncture where nothing is more visible or more manifest, being neither remiss in the morning nor remiss in the evening,…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
內外相孚始終無間將五帝不足帝三王
不足王也故曰天之所以爲天者何也曰
健也健者不息也天行健君子以自强不
息有味哉其言之也
第三問
劉廷祚
同考試官教諭呂批邇來文武吏鮮實效以求
名多也子能爲覈實之論而筆力雄勁宜冠本房
考試官教諭陳批粵西需二者最亟子能劑
===
量不爽而敘論謹嚴宜錄以式
考試官教諭尹批課嚴名實法兼內外於大
計有裨錄之非徒尚其文也
天下有法內之材有法外之材法內之材
中材也待之法內而人知所勉法外之材
豪傑也待之法外而人競于勸何也豪傑
之士其志卓然所存遠也其猷廓然所施
弘也其氣浩然所挾持確而正也彼其身
視赤子家視郡縣疆場弗安且寧奮其三
punctuated:
內外相孚，始終無間，將五帝不足帝，三王不足王也。故曰：「天之所以爲天者，何也？曰：健也。健者，不息也。」《天行健，君子以自强不息》，有味哉其言之也！

第三問
劉廷祚
同考試官教諭呂批：邇來文武吏鮮實效，以求名多也。子能爲覈實之論，而筆力雄勁，宜冠本房。
考試官教諭陳批：粵西需二者最亟，子能劑量不爽，而敘論謹嚴，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭尹批：課嚴名實，法兼內外，於大計有裨。錄之，非徒尚其文也。

天下有法內之材，有法外之材。法內之材，中材也，待之法內，而人知所勉；法外之材，豪傑也，待之法外，而人競于勸。何也？豪傑之士，其志卓然，所存遠也；其猷廓然，所施弘也；其氣浩然，所挾持確而正也。彼其身視赤子，家視郡縣，疆場弗安且寧，奮其三
translation_en:
…so that inner mind and outer conduct correspond with mutual trust, without a moment's lapse from beginning to end. Then the Five Emperors will scarcely be worthy to be called Emperors, and the Three Kings will scarcely be worthy to be called Kings! Therefore it is said: "Wherein lies that by which Heaven is Heaven? It is said: In its vigor. And vigor means unceasingness." "Heaven's motion is vigorous; the superior man accordingly strengthens himself unceasingly"—how rich in meaning are these words!

Question Three
Liu Tingzuo 劉廷zuo

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Lü: In recent times, civil and military officials rarely achieve practical results because too many merely seek reputation. You have been able to set forth an argument that verifies actual realities, and the force of your brush is vigorous and strong. This deserves to be placed first in my examination ward.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Chen: Western Yue [Guangxi] needs both of these [civil and military talent] most urgently. You are able to weigh and balance them unerringly, and your exposition and reasoning are rigorous and disciplined. This should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yin: The assessment strictly distinguishes name and reality, and the methods encompass both what lies within and what lies beyond the regulations, which is beneficial to great state plans. We record it not merely out of esteem for its literary style.

In the empire there is talent that operates within the rules, and there is talent that operates beyond the rules. Talent within the rules is mediocre talent; if one treats such men according to the rules, people know what to strive for. Talent beyond the rules is that of outstanding heroes; if one treats them beyond the conventional rules, people vie to be encouraged. Why is this? Men of heroic stature have lofty aspirations, for what they cherish is far-reaching; their plans are expansive, for what they put into practice is broad; their vital spirit is vast and flowing, for what they uphold is firm and upright. They regard the infant populace as their own person, and the commanderies and counties as their own family. When the frontiers are neither secure nor peaceful, they rouse these three…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者而爲之所非以上之法也而上之人不
以法外待之卽彼不爲沮亦豈所以鼓豪
傑而風天下乎若夫中材則異是矣各有
所用亦各有所偏明敏者戒於太察温良
者戒於無斷湛靜者戒於後時不齊之以
法察而不已則苛急矣斷而不足則庸懦
矣時而太後則事機僨矣故法者所以救
其偏而全其用胡可廢也以法之内外視
天下材而爲之待此帝王所以臨制海内
===
陶冶人羣之至術也執事以粤西文武吏
士策諸生計安邊方甚厚請摭所聞以對
自昔選吏任將若岳牧之命渭濱之載尚
矣在漢則神爵五鳳間郡國有治理效天
子爲下璽書勞問且不次徵入爲公卿此
其最著乃遣將之儀猶有古人推轂之風
一時揚旌之士皆能爲國家信威邊境蓋
漢世得人烝烝盛矣粤西固先秦所拓地
也稱藩則自漢始經略旣久稍視中州考
punctuated:
者而爲之所，非以上之法也。而上之人不以法外待之，卽彼不爲沮，亦豈所以鼓豪傑而風天下乎？若夫中材則異是矣。各有所用，亦各有所偏：明敏者戒於太察，温良者戒於無斷，湛靜者戒於後時。不齊之以法，察而不已則苛急矣，斷而不足則庸懦矣，時而太後則事機僨矣。故法者，所以救其偏而全其用，胡可廢也？以法之内外視天下材而爲之待，此帝王所以臨制海内、陶冶人羣之至術也。執事以粤西文武吏士策諸生，計安邊方甚厚，請摭所聞以對。

自昔選吏任將，若岳牧之命、渭濱之載，尚矣。在漢則神爵、五鳳間，郡國有治理效，天子爲下璽書勞問，且不次徵入爲公卿，此其最著；乃遣將之儀，猶有古人推轂之風，一時揚旌之士，皆能爲國家信威邊境，蓋漢世得人烝烝盛矣。粤西固先秦所拓地也，稱藩則自漢始。經略旣久，稍視中州。考…
translation_en:
…three qualities and makes proper arrangements for them—not because of the laws imposed from above. Yet if those above do not treat him with measures beyond the law, even if he himself is not discouraged by this, how could that serve to rouse heroic men and inspire the realm? As for men of average talent, they are different from this. Each has his utility, and each also has his bias: the clear-sighted and quick-witted must guard against being overly scrutinizing; the gentle and良 (good-natured) must guard against indecisiveness; the composed and tranquil must guard against missing the right moment. If they are not regulated by law, unceasing scrutiny becomes harshness and urgency, insufficient decisiveness becomes mediocrity and timidity, and being too late for the moment ruins the opportunity for action. Therefore, the law is that by which their biases are remedied and their utility is made complete—how could it be dispensed with? To view the talents of the realm in terms of what falls within the law and what lies beyond the law, and to treat them accordingly: this is the supreme art by which emperors and kings govern the lands within the seas and mold the multitude of men. Your Excellency has posed a policy question to us students concerning the civil and military officials and officers of Yuexi (Guangxi), showing a most generous concern for pacifying the frontier region; allow me to gather what I have heard in order to reply.

Since antiquity, in selecting officials and appointing generals, examples such as the commissioning of the Four Peaks and the Twelve Pastors, or the carrying back of Lü Shang from the banks of the Wei River, are of the highest order. In the Han dynasty, during the Shenjue (61–58 BCE) and Wufeng (57–54 BCE) eras, when commanderies and kingdoms achieved effective governance, the Son of Heaven would send down imperial letters under the玺 (imperial seal) to commend and inquire after the governors, and even summon them out of regular sequence to enter court as Excellency or Minister—this was the most illustrious example. Meanwhile, the ceremony for dispatching generals still retained the ancient spirit of pushing the chariot wheel hubs, and the banner-raising warriors of the age were all able to extend the state's prestige across the frontiers; indeed, the Han dynasty's success in obtaining capable men was thriving and abundant. Yuexi was originally territory opened up prior to the Qin, and its designation as a feudatory began with the Han. Having been administered for a long time, it gradually came to be regarded like the central prefectures. When we examine…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
覽往牒則其人聲實往往而在以守令言
之陸續守鬱林壓石歸舟人服其廉澤孰
茂焉嗣是則撫酋豪而定八州元結所以
刺容管挫彊禦而惠獨嫠唐頌所以令布
山柳子厚順俗設理而俗化且授諸生以
經義人文興焉張敬夫諭夷釋怨而夷安
且為橫山革買馬宿蠹去焉皆號良吏也
而柳張其領袖乎以將帥言之馬援平交
阯標柱界地夷懾其威勳莫偉焉嗣是則
===
度尚一焚營鼓士而卜陽授首岳飛一縱
囚誤敵而曹成就俘軍士玩令狄青先斬
袁用以徇則智高之變靖矣懷遠要害和
斌先提步騎以據則世念之患銷矣皆號
良將也而岳狄其翹楚乎我
國家大簡天下文武吏士為億萬世計尤加
意於邊二百年來匪獨中州稱得人卽粵
西亦皆彬彬質有其文武焉若何源若蕭
嘉祐及山雲輩未可一二數也庶幾哉其
punctuated: 覽往牒，則其人聲實往往而在。以守令言之：陸續守鬱林，壓石歸舟，人服其廉，澤孰茂焉？嗣是，則撫酋豪而定八州，元結所以刺容管；挫彊禦而惠獨嫠，唐頌所以令布山；柳子厚順俗設理而俗化，且授諸生以經義，人文興焉；張敬夫諭夷釋怨而夷安，且為橫山革買馬，宿蠹去焉。皆號良吏也，而柳、張其領袖乎？以將帥言之：馬援平交阯，標柱界地，夷懾其威，勳莫偉焉。嗣是，則度尚一焚營鼓士，而卜陽授首；岳飛一縱囚誤敵，而曹成就俘；軍士玩令，狄青先斬袁用以徇，則智高之變靖矣；懷遠要害，和斌先提步騎以據，則世念之患銷矣。皆號良將也，而岳、狄其翹楚乎？我國家大簡天下文武吏士，為億萬世計，尤加意於邊。二百年來，匪獨中州稱得人，卽粵西亦皆彬彬質有其文武焉。若何源、若蕭嘉祐及山雲輩，未可一二數也。庶幾哉！其
translation_en: …examining historical records, the reputations and actual achievements of such men are frequently to be found. To speak of Prefects and Magistrates: when Lu Xu 陸續 served as Prefect of Yulin 鬱林, he ballasted his returning boat with a stone, and people admired his integrity—what beneficence could be more abundant than this? Thereafter, pacifying the native chieftains and stabilizing the eight prefectures was how Yuan Jie 元結 governed as Prefect and Military Commissioner of Rongguan 容管; curbing the powerful and violent while showing kindness to the solitary and widowed was how Tang Song 唐頌 served as Magistrate of Bushan 布山; Liu Zihou 柳子厚 [Liu Zongyuan 柳宗元] instituted administration in accordance with local customs so that the customs were transformed, and moreover taught the students the meaning of the Classics, whereby cultural refinement flourished; Zhang Jingfu 張敬夫 [Zhang Shi 張栻] admonished the non-Chinese tribes to let go of their grievances so that they were pacified, and furthermore reformed the horse-purchasing system at Hengshan 橫山, whereby long-standing abuses were eliminated. All of these were acclaimed as good officials, and were not Liu and Zhang their leaders? To speak of commanders and generals: Ma Yuan 馬援 pacified Jiaozhi 交阯 and erected bronze pillars to demarcate the territory, so that the tribesmen stood in awe of his majesty—no merit could be greater than this. Thereafter, as soon as Du Shang 度尚 burned his own camp to rouse his troops, Bu Yang 卜陽 was beheaded; as soon as Yue Fei 岳飛 released a prisoner to mislead the enemy, Cao Cheng 曹成 was captured; when the soldiers trifled with military orders, Di Qing 狄青 first executed Yuan Yong 袁用 as a public example, and thus the rebellion of [Nong] Zhigao 儂智高 was quelled; because Huaiyuan 懷遠 was a strategic point, He Bin 和斌 first led infantry and cavalry to occupy it, and thus the threat of [Ceng] Shinian 曾世念 was dispelled. All of these were acclaimed as good generals, and were not Yue and Di the most outstanding among them? Our Dynasty selects civil and military officials and officers across the realm on a grand scale; planning for ten thousand generations, it pays especial attention to the frontiers. For two hundred years, not only has the Central Plain been praised for obtaining capable men, but even in western Guangdong and Guangxi (Yuexi 粵西) there has been a flourishing abundance of both civil and military talent. Men such as He Yuan 何源, Xiao Jiayou 蕭嘉祐, and Shan Yun 山雲 cannot be counted one by one. How close indeed are they…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
與昔人竝軌馳乎我
皇上
神明天授益廑民艱頃憂吏道稍稍耗廢
特詔廷臣嚴加甄别且舉增秩賜金故事行久
任法以需厥成介胄有乗障破敵抵掌畫
策旋起徒步建大將風聲所樹令天下士
有駕龔黃而凌韓白之氣何論粤西哉然
愚竊有異焉天下材品大都有三彼材之
墨而毦也酷烈也無論已其餘則中材也
===
===
豪傑也豪傑不數見而中材比比也今之
吏發奸擿伏鉤鉅不事有矣得無有淵察
爲明者乎敬老慈孤蒲鞭示辱有矣得無
有狐疑不决者乎雅風醇俗臥理自如有
矣得無有閣置廢事者乎此中材之吏之
所患也今之將開張押闔隨機應變或能
之而巧傷於竭澤不免也分甘損滋愛士
如子或能之而籌窘於前箸不免也審時
度勢老成持重或能之而膽怯於望風不
punctuated: 與昔人竝軌馳乎！我皇上神明天授，益廑民艱，頃憂吏道稍稍耗廢，特詔廷臣嚴加甄别，且舉增秩賜金故事，行久任法以需厥成；介胄有乗障破敵、抵掌畫策，旋起徒步建大將。風聲所樹，令天下士有駕龔、黃而凌韓、白之氣，何論粤西哉？然愚竊有異焉。天下材品大都有三：彼材之墨而毦也，酷烈也，無論已；其餘則中材也，豪傑也。豪傑不數見，而中材比比也。今之吏，發奸擿伏、鉤鉅不事有矣，得無有淵察爲明者乎？敬老慈孤、蒲鞭示辱有矣，得無有狐疑不决者乎？雅風醇俗、臥理自如有矣，得無有閣置廢事者乎？此中材之吏之所患也。今之將，開張押闔、隨機應變或能之，而巧傷於竭澤不免也；分甘損滋、愛士如子或能之，而籌窘於前箸不免也；審時度勢、老成持重或能之，而膽怯於望風不
translation_en: … gallop abreast along the same tracks as the men of old! Our August Emperor, endowed by Heaven with divine intelligence, shows ever deeper concern for the hardships of the people. Recently, worried that the ethos of officialdom was gradually deteriorating and falling into neglect, he issued a special decree ordering the court officials to conduct rigorous evaluations and distinctions, and furthermore revived the precedents of increasing ranks and bestowing gold, implementing the policy of long tenure in office to await their achievements. Among armored soldiers, those who mount frontier defenses to smash the enemy or clap their hands while devising strategies are swiftly raised from the ranks of commoners to establish the standards of great generals. The inspiration thus established imbues the gentlemen of the realm with the spirit to surpass Gong遂 (Gong Sui) and Huang霸 (Huang Ba) and outstrip Han信 (Han Xin) and Bai起 (Bai Qi)—what need is there to speak only of Guangxi? Yet in my humble opinion, I have a somewhat different view. The grades of talent in the world generally fall into three categories: as for those whose character is corrupt and degenerate, or harsh and violent, we need not even discuss them; the remainder are either of middling talent or heroic figures. Heroic figures are rarely seen, whereas men of middling talent are everywhere. Among today's civil officials, there are indeed those who expose wickedness and uncover hidden crimes without resorting to devious interrogation tricks—yet might there not be among them those who mistake prying into the depths for true discernment? There are indeed those who respect the elderly, show compassion to orphans, and use reed whips merely to signify shame—yet might there not be among them those who are suspicious and indecisive? There are indeed those who cultivate refined ways and pure customs, governing effortlessly as if reclining at ease—yet might there not be among them those who shelve matters and neglect their duties? These are the failings that afflict civil officials of middling talent. Among today's generals, some may be capable of grandly maneuvering [?] and adapting to changing circumstances, yet they cannot avoid the flaw of cleverness that harms by draining the pond; some may be capable of sharing sweet rations, stinting on their own luxuries, and loving their soldiers like sons, yet they cannot avoid coming up short in strategic planning right before their eyes; some may be capable of judging the times and assessing the situation with mature prudence and steadiness, yet they cannot avoid losing their nerve at the mere rumor of the enemy …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
免也此中材之將之所患也其材若彼其
患若此將胡以振之蓋昔者漢宣帝勵精
爲治有名實不相應必知其所以然故治
稱盛今覈吏非不詳也然巧吏每炫名以
最課上或徇名而課吏是故喜卓詭則狡
吏銧筩者顯矣美儇捷則奏成手中者先
矣事筐篋則禮義化俗者弗尚矣於郡縣
何裨焉今覈將非不密也然黠將恒買名
以邀功上或采名而任將是故快談辯則
===
===
能讀父書者售矣憑級報則性喜殺戮者
競矣竒征戰則坐困羌夷者見絀矣於疆
場奚賴焉此名實之覈不可不嚴也覈之
維何三年無囚不以無異見遺而戸口僞
增必斥也四壁堅守不以無功聽讒而馬
邑生事必誅也凡此覈之嚴矣然後視中
材之患懸其法整齊之有爵賞以誘乎其
前而不然者則奉三尺隨其後彼既有慕
於爵賞而又悚乎其黜罰則日兢兢焉惟
punctuated: 免也，此中材之將之所患也。其材若彼，其患若此，將胡以振之？蓋昔者漢宣帝勵精爲治，有名實不相應，必知其所以然，故治稱盛。今覈吏非不詳也，然巧吏每炫名以最課，上或徇名而課吏。是故喜卓詭則狡吏銧筩者顯矣，美儇捷則奏成手中者先矣，事筐篋則禮義化俗者弗尚矣，於郡縣何裨焉？今覈將非不密也，然黠將恒買名以邀功，上或采名而任將。是故快談辯則能讀父書者售矣，憑級報則性喜殺戮者競矣，竒征戰則坐困羌夷者見絀矣，於疆場奚賴焉？此名實之覈不可不嚴也。覈之維何？三年無囚，不以無異見遺，而戸口僞增必斥也；四壁堅守，不以無功聽讒，而馬邑生事必誅也。凡此，覈之嚴矣。然後視中材之患，懸其法整齊之：有爵賞以誘乎其前，而不然者則奉三尺隨其後。彼既有慕於爵賞，而又悚乎其黜罰，則日兢兢焉惟
translation_en: …cannot be avoided; these are the failings to which generals of middling talent are prone. With their talents being such as that, and their failings being such as this, how then can we rouse them? In the past, when Emperor Xuan of Han 漢宣帝 devoted his utmost energy to governance, whenever reputation and reality did not correspond, he made sure to know the reason why; therefore his rule was praised as flourishing. Today, the evaluation of civil officials is not lacking in detail. Yet artful officials often flaunt their reputation to achieve the top rating in assessments, and superiors sometimes go by reputation when assessing officials. Consequently, if superiors delight in the extraordinary and eccentric, then狡猾 officials who use secret举报 receptacles [銧筩] become prominent; if superiors admire nimble quickness, then those who fabricate ready-made reports right out of their hands take precedence; if superiors busy themselves with document boxes and registers, then those who transform customs through ritual and righteousness are not esteemed. What benefit is this to the commanderies and counties? Today, the evaluation of generals is not lacking in thoroughness. Yet cunning generals constantly buy reputation to seek merit, and superiors sometimes adopt reputations when appointing generals. Consequently, if superiors take pleasure in eloquent debate, then those who can merely read their fathers' books [like Zhao Kuo 趙括] find favor; if superiors rely on reports of severed heads, then those whose nature delights in slaughter compete for advancement; if superiors prize aggressive campaigns, then those who sit firm to wear down the Qiang and Yi [like Zhao Chongguo 趙充國] are sidelined. What reliance does this offer on the frontiers? Thus, the verification of reputation and reality cannot but be strict. How should they be verified? When an official goes three years without a single prisoner, he is not passed over for lacking extraordinary feats, whereas one who falsely inflates household registration figures is surely dismissed; when a general firmly defends his four walls, slander against him is not heeded on account of his lacking offensive merit, whereas one who provokes trouble as at Mayi 馬邑 is surely executed. In all these ways, verification is made strict. Only then, looking at the failings of those of middling talent, does one hold up the law to regulate them: there are ranks and rewards in front to entice them, and if they do otherwise, the three-foot law follows right behind them. Since they both yearn for ranks and rewards and stand in dread of demotion and punishment, day by day they will be cautious and trembling, only…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
上之所奔走明敏者不以苛刻伐平和溫
良者不以優柔敗果斷湛靜者不以玩愒
誤事機即中材文武吏其奮而至豪傑不
難也語曰尺有所短寸有所長飭其短全
其長而各適其用寧非法之善哉雖然此
待中材之法也非所以論於法之外也若
夫豪傑之士無法而勸者也教養未厚於
烝庶而簷部或抱幽憂戎馬猶生於郊圻
而谿峪時肆兇焰皆其所恫瘝而深愧者
===
奚俟人責之而後爲彼不事吾法而吾以
常法拘之視中材等是使不羈之士與牛
驥同皁此鮑焦所以忿於世也謂宜於文
法外稍寬繩束以大展其所注厝是故吏
而豪傑也則憫窮而輒赦不爲矯賑饑而
擅發不爲專由潁川徵至公卿不爲驟誠
優之也將而豪傑也則按轡徐行不爲屈
與數十萬金勿問不爲疑去中官都統不
爲恣誠假之也夫十圍之木置諸廟堂則
punctuated: 上之所奔走。明敏者不以苛刻伐平和，溫良者不以優柔敗果斷，湛靜者不以玩愒誤事機。即中材文武吏，其奮而至豪傑不難也。語曰：「尺有所短，寸有所長。」飭其短，全其長，而各適其用，寧非法之善哉？雖然，此待中材之法也，非所以論於法之外也。若夫豪傑之士，無法而勸者也。教養未厚於烝庶，而簷部或抱幽憂；戎馬猶生於郊圻，而谿峪時肆兇焰，皆其所恫瘝而深愧者，奚俟人責之而後爲？彼不事吾法，而吾以常法拘之，視中材等，是使不羈之士與牛驥同皁，此鮑焦所以忿於世也。謂宜於文法外，稍寬繩束，以大展其所注厝。是故吏而豪傑也，則憫窮而輒赦不爲矯，賑饑而擅發不爲專，由潁川徵至公卿不爲驟，誠優之也。將而豪傑也，則按轡徐行不爲屈，與數十萬金勿問不爲疑，去中官都統不爲恣，誠假之也。夫十圍之木，置諸廟堂則
translation_en: …rush to serve where the sovereign directs. Those who are bright and agile will not let harshness undermine harmony; those who are gentle and kind will not let indecisiveness ruin resolution; and those who are calm and composed will not let negligence miss critical opportunities. Even civil and military officials of average talent will find it not difficult to rouse themselves and become extraordinary heroes. As the saying goes, "A foot has its shortcomings, and an inch has its strengths." To correct their shortcomings, preserve their strengths, and suit each to his proper use—is this not the excellence of the law? Even so, this is the method for treating men of average talent, not something to be discussed regarding what lies beyond the law. As for extraordinary heroes, they are spurred to action without the need for laws. When instruction and nourishment have not yet generously reached the common people, and humble cottages still harbor hidden sorrows; when warhorses still arise on the frontiers, and mountain valleys at times unleash fierce flames of violence—all these are what cause them acute pain in their own persons and deep shame. Why would they wait for others to demand it of them before taking action? They do not rely on our laws, yet if we bind them with ordinary laws and view them as equal to men of average talent, this is to make untrammeled men share a stable with oxen and thoroughbreds alike—which is why Bao Jiao 鮑焦 resented the world. I would say that outside the written regulations, we should slightly relax the restraints so as to allow them to grandly unfold their measures and arrangements. Therefore, if a civil official is an extraordinary hero, then taking pity on the desperate and promptly granting pardons is not considered falsifying orders; relieving famine by opening granaries on his own authority is not considered usurpation; and being summoned from Yingchuan 潁川 straight to the rank of Ducal Minister is not considered overly abrupt—this is truly to treat him with generous favor. If a general is an extraordinary hero, then holding the reins and marching slowly is not considered insubordination; granting him hundreds of thousands in gold without asking for an accounting is not considered grounds for suspicion; and removing a eunuch Army Supervisor (dutong 都統) is not considered unbridled license—this is truly to grant him wide latitude. Now, a tree ten spans in circumference, when placed in the ancestral temple or court hall,…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
稱良材斵之小而棄焉反拱把弗若矣連
城之璧世所傳以爲至寶混之璞與瓦礫
同則狂夫易之矣故善待豪傑者必於法
之外也噫法內法也法之外而能奔走豪
傑不用法者之法也尤所以爲善用其法
也以法內待天下之中材而人益勉以法
外待天下之豪傑而人益勸天下士更相
勸勉爲良吏爲名將則何昔人不可追而
國家其有不登諸理乎
===
第四問
胡天霞
同考試官訓導徐批鹽筴錢法爲粵西急務而
平官鹽之價開廣南之路尤行鹽鑄錢所必資者子
能發明詳盡豈直可以經生目之耶
考試官教諭陳批講粵西鹽筴錢法鑿鑿可
行且筆力高古讀之悚然起敬
考試官教諭尹批讀子之文知子通達世務
且淹貫古典矣錄之
punctuated:
稱良材；斵之小而棄焉，反拱把弗若矣。連城之璧，世所傳以爲至寶；混之璞，與瓦礫同，則狂夫易之矣。故善待豪傑者，必於法之外也。噫！法內，法也；法之外而能奔走豪傑，不用法者之法也，尤所以爲善用其法也。以法內待天下之中材，而人益勉；以法外待天下之豪傑，而人益勸。天下士更相勸勉，爲良吏，爲名將，則何昔人不可追，而國家其有不登諸理乎？

第四問
胡天霞
同考試官訓導徐批：鹽筴、錢法爲粵西急務，而平官鹽之價、開廣南之路，尤行鹽、鑄錢所必資者。子能發明詳盡，豈直可以經生目之耶？
考試官教諭陳批：講粵西鹽筴、錢法，鑿鑿可行，且筆力高古，讀之悚然起敬。
考試官教諭尹批：讀子之文，知子通達世務，且淹貫古典矣。錄之。
translation_en:
…is acclaimed as fine timber; if one chops it small and discards it, it turns out to be worse than a sapling a hand's span thick. A jade disk worth a string of cities is passed down in the world as a supreme treasure; if one mixes it among unworked stones as if it were the same as broken tiles and pebbles, even a madman would treat it lightly. Therefore, he who knows well how to treat extraordinary talents must do so outside the bounds of the law. Alas! What lies within the law is the law; what lies outside the law and yet can command the service of extraordinary talents is the law of one who does not rely on the law—and it is all the more the way to make good use of one's law! When one treats those of middling talent in the realm within the bounds of the law, men exert themselves all the more; when one treats the extraordinary talents of the realm outside the bounds of the law, men are encouraged all the more. When the gentlemen of the realm mutually encourage and exert one another to become good officials and renowned generals, then what men of antiquity cannot be equaled, and how could the state fail to ascend to great order?

Question Four
Hu Tianxia 胡天霞
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Xu 徐: Salt administration and monetary policy are urgent affairs for Guangxi, while stabilizing the price of official salt and opening the route through Guangnan 廣南 are especially essential prerequisites for circulating salt and casting coins. You have been able to elucidate this thoroughly and in full detail—how could one regard you merely as a student of the classics?
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳: Your discussion of Guangxi's salt administration and monetary policy is concrete and practicable; moreover, the vigor of your brush is lofty and antique, inspiring awe and respect as one reads it.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yin 尹: Reading your essay, I know that you thoroughly understand the affairs of the world and are steeped in the ancient classics as well. Selected for inclusion.

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
君子之理財也豈能求之財之外哉求之
財之外者是謂蠹國是謂瘠民吾無取焉
吾惟順其財之所自生而講求其故劑量
于輕重變通于緩急因其賦之必不可加
稍有以充其賦因其用之必不可不足稍
有以足其用不病乎其私而有濟于其公
夫亦何所不可苟不察其所以而惟泥於
故常乃吾當縮乏之地處兵荒之交所需
四出莫知所應其於國計民瘼無裨萬分
===
一則何以善其後執事因粤西之縮於財
以近日所行之鹽筴錢法講求其無病于
公私可行于經久甚盛心也承學未與經
國之事則何所知然不可不有以復明問
今海內稱瘠土當多事者則孰過粤西哉
巖壑交錯水脉不生無可耕之地也谷箐
孤險雞犬不聞無可耕之民也爲郡者九
不足當東南一二大郡也爲邑者七十有
七不足當東南一二大邑也爲土州爲土
punctuated:
君子之理財也，豈能求之財之外哉？求之財之外者，是謂蠹國，是謂瘠民，吾無取焉。吾惟順其財之所自生，而講求其故，劑量于輕重，變通于緩急。因其賦之必不可加，稍有以充其賦；因其用之必不可不足，稍有以足其用。不病乎其私，而有濟于其公，夫亦何所不可？苟不察其所以，而惟泥於故常，乃吾當縮乏之地，處兵荒之交，所需四出，莫知所應，其於國計民瘼無裨萬分一，則何以善其後？執事因粤西之縮於財，以近日所行之鹽筴、錢法，講求其無病于公私、可行于經久，甚盛心也。承學未與經國之事，則何所知？然不可不有以復明問。

今海內稱瘠土、當多事者，則孰過粤西哉？巖壑交錯，水脉不生，無可耕之地也；谷箐孤險，雞犬不聞，無可耕之民也。爲郡者九，不足當東南一二大郡也；爲邑者七十有七，不足當東南一二大邑也。爲土州、爲土
translation_en:
When a gentleman manages fiscal affairs, how could he seek resources outside of wealth itself? To seek them outside of wealth is what is called acting as a parasite upon the state and impoverishing the people; I take no part in such things. I simply follow the natural sources from which wealth is generated and investigate their underlying principles, balancing what is light and heavy and adapting to what is urgent and routine. Because the regular land tax absolutely cannot be increased, one finds modest ways to supplement the revenue; because state expenditures absolutely cannot fall short, one finds modest ways to meet those needs. Without harming private interests while yet benefitting the public good—what could be wrong with that? If, however, one fails to examine the underlying causes and merely clings to established routines, then when we find ourselves in a region of scarcity and exhaustion, caught at the juncture of warfare and famine, with demands arising from all sides and no way to meet them, it will not benefit the state finances or the people's livelihood by even a ten-thousandth part—how then could we manage the aftermath? Because Guangxi is strained for revenue, Your Excellency has inquired into the recently implemented salt monopoly and monetary policies, seeking ways by which they may neither harm public nor private interests and may be practiced enduringly; this is a most magnanimous intention. As a junior student who has not participated in affairs of statecraft, what could I know? Yet I cannot fail to offer a reply to your enlightened question.

Today, among the regions within the seas known for barren soil and facing frequent troubles, which surpasses Guangxi? Its crags and ravines interlock and water veins do not spring forth, so there is no arable land; its valleys and bamboo thickets are isolated and perilous, where the sounds of chickens and dogs are not heard, so there are no people to till the soil. Its nine prefectures are not equivalent to one or two great prefectures of the southeast; its seventy-seven counties are not equivalent to one or two great counties of the southeast. Those that are native-run subprefectures, native-run…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
縣爲土司者環四面以居公租不入法令
不行一有事且嗷嗷望我以濟也是執事
之所謂賦之必不可加者也萬山盤錯道
路孤遠三江夾出舟楫艱難今日報劫路
則道路塞明日報劫江則舟楫阻某處議
鵬剿某處議夾剿日所需於軍餉者紛如
也某州告饑且云將盡出爲盜某縣告饑
且云將坐以待斃搜之民間無可貸搜之
倉庫無可發日所請於公帑者繹如也此
===
執事之所謂用之必不可不足者也賦必
不可加而又不可不加用必不可不足而
又不能足爲粵西籌者自古難之矣自近
日鹽筴行司庫稍有所貯乃公私輒又告
病蓋民生所不可一日缺者莫如鹽東南
煮于海西北產于池生于井永康崖鹽出
于木石決源釃流脉寫膏浸神液陰漉甘
鹵密起自管子謹正鹽筴計口食鹽始立
禁以佐兵賦而倚頓郭縱羅裒皆擅鹽之
punctuated:
縣、爲土司者，環四面以居，公租不入，法令不行，一有事，且嗷嗷望我以濟也。是執事之所謂「賦之必不可加」者也。萬山盤錯，道路孤遠，三江夾出，舟楫艱難。今日報劫路，則道路塞；明日報劫江，則舟楫阻。某處議鵬剿，某處議夾剿，日所需於軍餉者紛如也。某州告饑，且云將盡出爲盜；某縣告饑，且云將坐以待斃。搜之民間，無可貸；搜之倉庫，無可發，日所請於公帑者繹如也。此執事之所謂「用之必不可不足」者也。賦必不可加，而又不可不加；用必不可不足，而又不能足，爲粵西籌者，自古難之矣。

自近日鹽筴行，司庫稍有所貯，乃公私輒又告病。蓋民生所不可一日缺者莫如鹽：東南煮于海，西北產于池，生于井，永康崖鹽出于木石，決源釃流，脉寫膏浸，神液陰漉，甘鹵密起。自管子謹正鹽筴，計口食鹽，始立禁以佐兵賦，而猗頓、郭縱、羅裒皆擅鹽之
translation_en:
… aboriginal counties, and aboriginal chieftaincies surround us on all four sides; public revenues do not enter from them and government laws do not reach them, yet as soon as trouble arises, they clamor in expectation of our relief. This is what Your Excellency refers to when saying that "taxes certainly cannot be increased." Myriad mountains twist and interlock, making the roads isolated and remote; the three rivers wind between cliffs, making boat navigation arduous. Today a road robbery is reported, and the land routes are blocked; tomorrow a river piracy is reported, and boat traffic is halted. In one place they deliberate on a sweeping campaign of suppression (pengjiao), and in another on a pincer campaign (jiajiao), so that the daily demands for military provisions pour in from all sides. A certain subprefecture reports famine and says its people are all about to go out as bandits; a certain county reports famine and says its people are about to sit waiting for death. If we search among the populace, there is nothing to borrow; if we search the granaries and treasuries, there is nothing to disburse, so that the daily requests upon the public funds follow one after another in an unbroken stream. This is what Your Excellency refers to when saying that "expenditures certainly must not fall short." That taxes certainly cannot be increased, and yet must be increased; that expenditures certainly must not fall short, and yet cannot be made sufficient—for those who plan for Guangxi (Yuexi), this has been difficult since antiquity.

Since the recent implementation of the salt fiscal policy, the provincial treasury has accumulated some reserves, yet both the public administration and private citizens have promptly reported distress once again. Indeed, among the things that the people's livelihood cannot lack for a single day, nothing compares to salt. In the southeast it is boiled from the sea; in the northwest it is produced from salt lakes or drawn from wells; and the cliff salt of Yongkang emerges from trees and rocks—tapping springs and channeling streams, seeping through veins and soaking like rich oil, its marvelous essence filtering darkly and its sweet brine rising thick. Ever since Guanzi carefully regulated the salt administration, calculating salt consumption by head of population and first establishing a monopoly to assist military levies, figures such as Yi Dun, Guo Zong, and Luo Pou all monopolized the [profits] of salt …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
利見于貨殖傳者可考也粤西非産鹽之
地鹽之由南海出湖湘也其路必由粤西
當事之臣因粤西公賦之縮得請于
朝出公帑之積轉鬻南海達于桂林召商上
納每二年可足三運每四運可得十萬本
息相半用助兵荒之需名曰官鹽商人出
私本由别路運其一由清遠縣至連州其
一由封川江至寧遠原額食熟鹽後乃改
造生鹽越界變賣紊亂成規遂不可制名
===
曰私鹽官鹽轉輸頗難而其價亦稍高私
鹽乘便往返爲易而其價亦稍下以故私
鹽盛行官鹽阻滯今鹽場積至六百萬有
竒此公之所以病也官鹽滯不得不禁私
鹽邏兵譏察無所得縱私鹽之行非復往
昔之便湖湘之民籍鹽于粤西者不得不
告困此私之所以病也夫病之生也必有
所以爲病之原不究其原而欲救其病其
道無由也故欲通官鹽之滯不得不平官
punctuated: 利，見于《貨殖傳》者可考也。粤西非産鹽之地，鹽之由南海出湖湘也，其路必由粤西。當事之臣因粤西公賦之縮，得請于朝，出公帑之積，轉鬻南海，達于桂林，召商上納。每二年可足三運，每四運可得十萬，本息相半，用助兵荒之需，名曰官鹽。商人出私本，由别路運，其一由清遠縣至連州，其一由封川江至寧遠。原額食熟鹽，後乃改造生鹽，越界變賣，紊亂成規，遂不可制，名曰私鹽。官鹽轉輸頗難，而其價亦稍高；私鹽乘便往返爲易，而其價亦稍下。以故私鹽盛行，官鹽阻滯，今鹽場積至六百萬有竒，此公之所以病也。官鹽滯，不得不禁私鹽。邏兵譏察，無所得縱，私鹽之行，非復往昔之便。湖湘之民籍鹽于粤西者，不得不告困，此私之所以病也。夫病之生也，必有所以爲病之原；不究其原而欲救其病，其道無由也。故欲通官鹽之滯，不得不平官
translation_en: … profits, as can be verified from what appears in the "Biographies of Usurers and Merchants" (Huozhi zhuan). Guangxi (Yuexi) is not a salt-producing region; yet when salt goes from the Southern Sea (Nanhai, i.e., Guangdong) out to Hunan and Hubei (Huxiang), its route must pass through Guangxi.
