Because public revenues in Guangxi had shrunk, the officials in charge obtained permission from the Court to draw upon accumulated public treasury funds to purchase salt in Nanhai and transport it to Guilin, summoning merchants to pay for and distribute it. Every two years suffices for three shipments, and every four shipments yields a hundred thousand [taels], half principal and half profit, used to aid the needs of military campaigns and famine relief; this is called "official salt" (guanyan). Meanwhile, merchants put up private capital and transport salt by other routes—one from Qingyuan County to Lianzhou, and one by the Fengchuan River to Ningyuan. Originally the quota was for boiled salt (shuyan), but later they switched to producing raw salt (shengyan), crossing boundaries to sell it off, disrupting established regulations until it could no longer be controlled; this is called "private salt" (siyan). Official salt is quite difficult to transport, and its price is also somewhat higher; private salt takes advantage of convenient routes for easy round trips, and its price is also somewhat lower. For this reason, private salt flourishes while official salt is bogged down; today the salt depots have accumulated over six million [catties/packs], which is why the public sector suffers. Because official salt is bogged down, one cannot but prohibit private salt. Patrol soldiers inspect and intercept it, leaving no room for indulgence, so the circulation of private salt no longer enjoys its former convenience. The people of Huxiang who depend on Guangxi for salt cannot help crying out in distress, which is why the private sector suffers. Now, when an ailment arises, there must be a root cause that produces the ailment; if one does not investigate its root cause and yet wishes to cure the ailment, there is no way to do so. Therefore, if one wishes to clear the stagnation of official salt, one cannot but level the [price of] official…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
鹽之價使其價不甚遠於私則人何苦不
樂趨於官欲嚴私鹽之禁不得不重私鹽
之稅使其稅不甚遠於官則人何苦冒犯
于私通利于國而不病于民公利于商而
不病于國審如是而鹽有不行者乎此鹽
筴之不可不講者也自近日錢法行兵荒
稍有所需乃銅料又苦不繼蓋民生所利
用者莫如錢若布帛尺拆之則裂金銀細
分之則耗惟錢之爲用寶於金利於刀流
===
於泉自太公立九府圜法而周則母子相
權秦則上下相等漢爲八銖筴錢赤仄五
分理道夷陵有鵝眼綖環之别風飄水浮
之異大較錢重則病國錢輕則病民唯我
朝錢法輕重相等粵西僻在邊徼民便於錢
頃
皇上從廷臣之請令天下分省得各自鑄錢以
便行使粵西舊苦乏錢新錢一出鼓舞稱
便今所患者不在錢之不行而在錢之不
punctuated:
鹽之價，使其價不甚遠於私，則人何苦不樂趨於官？欲嚴私鹽之禁，不得不重私鹽之稅，使其稅不甚遠於官，則人何苦冒犯于私？通利于國而不病于民，公利于商而不病于國，審如是而鹽有不行者乎？此鹽筴之不可不講者也。
自近日錢法行，兵荒稍有所需，乃銅料又苦不繼。蓋民生所利用者莫如錢：若布帛尺拆之則裂，金銀細分之則耗，惟錢之爲用，寶於金、利於刀、流於泉。自太公立九府圜法，而周則母子相權，秦則上下相等，漢爲八銖、筴錢、赤仄、五分，理道夷陵，有鵝眼、綖環之别，風飄、水浮之異。大較錢重則病國，錢輕則病民，唯我朝錢法輕重相等。粵西僻在邊徼，民便於錢。頃皇上從廷臣之請，令天下分省得各自鑄錢，以便行使。粵西舊苦乏錢，新錢一出，鼓舞稱便。今所患者，不在錢之不行，而在錢之不
translation_en:
… the price of government salt. If its price is not far from that of private salt, why would people go to the trouble of not gladly turning to the government? If one wishes to strictly enforce the prohibition on private salt, one must increase the tax on private salt; if that tax is not far from the rate on government salt, why would people go to the trouble of risking the law for private salt? When circulation benefits the state without harming the people, and public administration benefits the merchants without harming the state—if things are truly managed in this way, could salt ever fail to circulate? This is why salt policy must be carefully examined.

Recently, since the coinage regulations were put into effect, they have somewhat met the needs arising from military campaigns and famine, yet we suffer from an unsustainable supply of copper material. Now, nothing is more useful to the people's livelihood than copper cash: if cloth and silk are torn apart by the foot, they ruin; if gold and silver are divided into tiny fractions, they suffer loss through wastage. Only coin, in its utility, is as precious as metal, as sharp in function as a knife, and flows like a spring. Since Taigong (太公) established the round-currency system of the Nine Treasuries (九府), the Zhou dynasty balanced heavy "mother" and light "child" coins against each other; the Qin dynasty made the upper and lower currencies equal in value; and the Han dynasty minted eight-zhu (八銖) coins, pod-cash (筴錢), red-rimmed coins (赤仄), and five-fen (五分) coins. When principles of governance declined, there arose distinctions such as "goose-eye" (鵝眼) and "thread-ring" (綖環) coins, and anomalies so thin they would drift on the wind or float on water. Broadly speaking, when coins are too heavy, it harms the state; when coins are too light, it harms the people. Only the coinage system of our dynasty balances weight and lightness equally. Guangxi (粵西) lies isolated on the remote frontier, and the people find it convenient to use copper cash. Recently His Majesty followed the request of court officials and ordered the various provinces of the empire each to cast their own coins for convenient circulation. Guangxi had long suffered from a shortage of cash, so as soon as the new coins came out, the people rejoiced and praised their convenience. What gives cause for concern today is not that the coins do not circulate, but that the coins are not…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣不在錢之不廣而在銅之不繼開局之
初卽工作之具銅料之需俱取足粤東乃
粤東之銅亦取辦他省開局旣多用銅日
廣銅價高貴貿易爲難且在在有鬻銅出
省之禁此東路之銅有所不足恃也新錢
旣行舊錢遂閣原議以新易舊聽民自至
局兩平相易至者如流今則舊錢漸少不
及夙昔十之一二此舊錢之易有所不足
恃也不得已則以官吏齎銅價易於貴之
===
鎭遠乃道路孤遠時日曠乆不足以應急
需則將奈何夫利之興也必有所以爲利
之原不得其原而欲興其利其道無由也
銅產於滇滇之由楚至粤也其路爲獨僻
商賈不至故得銅爲獨難今滇之廣南與
粤之田州其地爲接壤由廣南至田州江
從舟楫行也止半月程其路爲甚便滇人
議開官路置驛舍辨車馬惟以粤西應置
五驛費無所辦論大事者不計小費誠兩
punctuated: 廣；不在錢之不廣，而在銅之不繼。開局之初，卽工作之具、銅料之需，俱取足粤東。乃粤東之銅，亦取辦他省。開局旣多，用銅日廣，銅價高貴，貿易爲難；且在在有鬻銅出省之禁，此東路之銅有所不足恃也。新錢旣行，舊錢遂閣。原議以新易舊，聽民自至局兩平相易，至者如流；今則舊錢漸少，不及夙昔十之一二，此舊錢之易有所不足恃也。不得已，則以官吏齎銅價易於貴之鎭遠，乃道路孤遠，時日曠乆，不足以應急需，則將奈何？夫利之興也，必有所以爲利之原；不得其原而欲興其利，其道無由也。銅產於滇，滇之由楚至粤也，其路爲獨僻，商賈不至，故得銅爲獨難。今滇之廣南與粤之田州，其地爲接壤，由廣南至田州江，從舟楫行也，止半月程，其路爲甚便。滇人議開官路，置驛舍，辨車馬，惟以粤西應置五驛，費無所辦。論大事者不計小費，誠兩
translation_en: … widespread; and not in their not being widespread, but in the supply of copper not being sustained. When the mints were first opened, both the tools for the work and the required copper materials were obtained entirely from Guangdong. Yet the copper of Guangdong is also procured from other provinces. Since many mints have been opened, the use of copper has grown daily, the price of copper has become high, and trade has become difficult; moreover, everywhere there are prohibitions against selling copper out of the province. Thus the copper from the eastern route cannot be relied upon. Once the new coins came into circulation, the old coins were shelved. Originally it was proposed to exchange the new for the old, allowing the people to come to the mints themselves to trade on equal terms, and those who came flowed like water; now, however, the old coins have gradually dwindled to less than one- or two-tenths of what they were in the past. Thus the exchange of old coins cannot be relied upon. Having no alternative, officials and clerks are sent carrying the funds for copper to purchase it in Zhenyuan 鎭遠 in Guizhou, yet the road is isolated and distant, and the time required is long and drawn out, so it is insufficient to meet urgent needs—what then is to be done? Now, in the promotion of any benefit, there must be a source from which the benefit arises; if one does not obtain its source and yet wishes to promote the benefit, there is no way to do so. Copper is produced in Yunnan. In going from Yunnan through Huguang to Guangxi, the route is exceptionally out of the way, and merchants do not come, which is why obtaining copper is uniquely difficult. Now, Guangnan 廣南 in Yunnan and Tianzhou 田州 in Guangxi border upon each other; going from Guangnan to the river at Tianzhou and traveling by boat is a journey of only half a month, making the route very convenient. The people of Yunnan have proposed opening an official road, establishing postal stations, and preparing carriages and horses, except that for the five postal stations that ought to be established in Guangxi, there is no way to provide the funds. Those who deliberate on great affairs do not reckon small expenses; if truly both…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
省公議協通此道則銅至如流矣從而立
稅課廣錢局其利豈止於今日之費耶此
錢法之不可不講也雖然鹽價旣平公私
俱利故必大出公帑爲鹽本乃可以充公
家之用則轉運之法不可不行也由大舟
轉至梧州立場以頓由小舟運至桂林立
廠以發自梧州而上多立博淺之船自昭
平而上廣布哨守之卒則官鹽無滯轉運
不難其所積於司庫者豈止於今日之所
===
餘已哉南路旣通銅料日廣故必多開爐
以鑄錢乃可以備兵荒之需則私鑄之禁
不可不嚴也城中則
宗室私鑄以撓公家之權曠遠則土官私鑄
以擅公家之利請一切繩以法可行者禁
之以官不可行者請之於
上則官錢無滯流行日廣其所以備兵荒之需
者豈止於今日之所餘已哉嗚呼廣行鹽
之利是轉粵東之所生以充粵西之所積
punctuated: 省公議，協通此道，則銅至如流矣。從而立稅課、廣錢局，其利豈止於今日之費耶？此錢法之不可不講也。雖然，鹽價旣平，公私俱利，故必大出公帑爲鹽本，乃可以充公家之用，則轉運之法不可不行也。由大舟轉至梧州，立場以頓；由小舟運至桂林，立廠以發。自梧州而上，多立博淺之船；自昭平而上，廣布哨守之卒。則官鹽無滯，轉運不難，其所積於司庫者，豈止於今日之所餘已哉？南路旣通，銅料日廣，故必多開爐以鑄錢，乃可以備兵荒之需，則私鑄之禁不可不嚴也。城中則宗室私鑄以撓公家之權，曠遠則土官私鑄以擅公家之利。請一切繩以法，可行者禁之以官，不可行者請之於上。則官錢無滯，流行日廣，其所以備兵荒之需者，豈止於今日之所餘已哉？嗚呼！廣行鹽之利，是轉粵東之所生以充粵西之所積；
translation_en:
… provinces deliberate together in the public interest and cooperate to open this route, then copper will arrive like a flowing stream. If we thereupon establish tax levies and expand the minting bureaus, how could the profit merely match today's expenditure? This is why monetary policy must be carefully examined.

Even so, once the price of salt is stabilized, both the state and private individuals benefit. Therefore, public funds must be generously disbursed as salt capital so that the needs of the state can be met; thus, a system of transport and distribution must be put into practice. Transport it by large vessels to Wuzhou 梧州 and establish depots to store it; ship it by small boats to Guilin 桂林 and establish yards to distribute it. Upstream from Wuzhou, set up numerous shallow-draft lighters [? 博淺之船]; upstream from Zhaoping 昭平, widely deploy patrolling and guarding soldiers. Then government salt will suffer no bottlenecks, transport will not be difficult, and how could what is accumulated in the provincial treasury merely match today's surplus?

Once the southern route is opened and copper supplies grow daily more abundant, more furnaces must be opened to cast coins so as to prepare for the needs of military emergencies and famine; thus, the prohibition against illicit minting must be strictly enforced. Within the city, imperial clansmen mint illicitly, thereby disrupting the authority of the state; in distant borderlands, native officials (tuguan 土官) mint illicitly, thereby usurping the profits of the state. I beg that all of them be restrained by law: where local action is feasible, have the officials prohibit it; where it is not feasible, petition the Throne above. Then government coins will suffer no bottlenecks, their circulation will grow daily wider, and how could the reserves prepared for military emergencies and famine merely match today's surplus?

Alas! To expand the profits of the salt trade is to transfer what is produced in eastern Yue (Guangdong 廣東) to replenish what is stored in western Yue (Guangxi 廣西); …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
開運銅之路是轉滇南之所有以濟粤西
之所無往來日眾財賦日生行之十年而
後之粤西非今之粤西比矣此百世之利
也不知執事者可採而見之施行否也
第五問
李時盛
同考試官訓導吳批粤西猺獞撫勦事宜具見
此篇讀至功級俘獲處令人惻然真仁人之言哉反
覆慨歎可深長思錄之非徒以文辭之古雅也
===
考試官敎諭陳批兵家事以不樂言不諱言
立柱而議論疊出區畫詳明籌粤西者尚有出此哉
考試官敎諭尹批事情洞悉敷敘詳明予其
有感時事而慨于衷者宜錄以傳
君子未始樂言乎兵而亦未始諱言乎兵
樂言之則有用於其所不當用而何以全
吾之仁諱言之則有不用於其所不可不
用而何以行吾之義用於其所不可用是
疲民也其勢必至於弗戢不用於其所不
punctuated:
開運銅之路，是轉滇南之所有，以濟粤西之所無。往來日眾，財賦日生，行之十年，而後之粤西非今之粤西比矣。此百世之利也，不知執事者可採而見之施行否也？

第五問
李時盛
同考試官訓導吳批：粤西猺獞撫勦事宜，具見此篇。讀至功級俘獲處，令人惻然，真仁人之言哉！反覆慨歎，可深長思。錄之，非徒以文辭之古雅也。
考試官敎諭陳批：兵家事以不樂言、不諱言立柱，而議論疊出，區畫詳明。籌粤西者，尚有出此哉？
考試官敎諭尹批：事情洞悉，敷敘詳明，予其有感時事而慨于衷者，宜錄以傳。

君子未始樂言乎兵，而亦未始諱言乎兵。樂言之，則有用於其所不當用，而何以全吾之仁？諱言之，則有不用於其所不可不用，而何以行吾之義？用於其所不可用，是疲民也，其勢必至於弗戢；不用於其所不
translation_en:
… Opening the route for transporting copper is to transfer what southern Yunnan possesses in order to supply what Guangxi lacks. With traffic growing more numerous by the day and revenues generated daily, if this is practiced for ten years, the Guangxi of the future will bear no comparison to the Guangxi of today. This is a benefit for a hundred generations; I do not know whether the examiners might adopt it and see it put into practice?

Fifth Question
Li Shisheng 李時盛
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Wu 吳: The appropriate measures for pacifying and suppressing the Yao and Zhuang peoples of Guangxi are fully presented in this essay. Reading to the passage on merit-grades for heads taken and captives seized makes one feel deep compassion—truly the words of a benevolent man! Its repeated sighs of lamentation invite deep and lasting reflection. We record it not merely for the classical elegance of its diction.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Chen 陳: In military affairs, he sets up the twin pillars of "not taking pleasure in speaking of war" and "not shunning speaking of war," from which arguments emerge layer upon layer and plans are laid out in clear detail. Among those who devise strategies for Guangxi, could anyone surpass this?
Comment by Examiner Instructor Yin 尹: He thoroughly understands the realities of the situation and sets them forth with clear detail. Approving how he is moved by current affairs and laments them from the heart, it is fitting to record this for transmission.

The superior man has never taken pleasure in speaking of war, yet neither has he ever shunned speaking of war. If one takes pleasure in speaking of it, then weapons will be used where they ought not to be used—and how then can one preserve one's benevolence intact? If one shuns speaking of it, then weapons will not be used where they cannot but be used—and how then can one carry out one's righteousness? To use them where they ought not to be used is to exhaust the people, and the situation will inevitably lead to weapons never being laid down; not to use them where they cannot…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
可不用是玩寇也其勢必至於棄民君子
爲之審輕重之辨酌先後之宜必有所用
以成其不用也必有所不用以全其用也
執事者有感於粵西之猺獞歲歲征剿弗
息也下策愚生愚生粵西人也請言粵西
猺獞之大略而後及所以處之者西粵猺
獞居萬山之中當三江之險深箐絕壑人
跡有所不通也古木懸崖日月有所不照
也層岡疊阜莫知其涯際也荒村遠落莫
===
窮其終始也種類莫可識別巢穴莫可蹤
尋其所以爲室廬者則巖巔也其所以相
往來者則狼虎也其所以代耒耜者則鋒
鏑也殆天驕之若犬羊豺狼然莫可以人
理化也粵之西則有曰大藤曰八寨曰連
城曰六十三山曰七山等巢諸若此類莫
可枚舉也粵之東則有曰羅旁曰王母曰
雲稍曰母雞等巢諸若此類莫可枚舉也
濱于江者擾及舟楫濱于路者擾及行旅
punctuated: 可不用，是玩寇也，其勢必至於棄民。君子爲之審輕重之辨，酌先後之宜，必有所用以成其不用也，必有所不用以全其用也。執事者有感於粵西之猺獞，歲歲征剿弗息也，下策愚生。愚生，粵西人也，請言粵西猺獞之大略，而後及所以處之者。西粵猺獞居萬山之中，當三江之險。深箐絕壑，人跡有所不通也；古木懸崖，日月有所不照也；層岡疊阜，莫知其涯際也；荒村遠落，莫窮其終始也。種類莫可識別，巢穴莫可蹤尋。其所以爲室廬者，則巖巔也；其所以相往來者，則狼虎也；其所以代耒耜者，則鋒鏑也。殆天驕之若犬羊豺狼然，莫可以人理化也。粵之西，則有曰大藤、曰八寨、曰連城、曰六十三山、曰七山等巢，諸若此類，莫可枚舉也；粵之東，則有曰羅旁、曰王母、曰雲稍、曰母雞等巢，諸若此類，莫可枚舉也。濱于江者，擾及舟楫；濱于路者，擾及行旅。
translation_en:
… must be used, this is trifling with bandits, and the situation will inevitably lead to abandoning the people. Therefore, the superior man carefully weighs the distinction between what is of greater or lesser importance and deliberates on the appropriateness of what comes first or last; there must be occasions where force is used in order to achieve its non-use, and there must be occasions where force is not used in order to preserve its efficacy when used.

The examiners, moved by the fact that campaigns of suppression against the Yao and Zhuang of western粵 (Guangxi) continue year after year without cease, have posed this policy question to this humble student. I, this humble student, am a native of Guangxi; allow me to speak first of the general situation of the Yao and Zhuang in Guangxi, and then proceed to how they should be dealt with.

The Yao and Zhuang of Guangxi dwell amid ten thousand mountains and occupy the strategic passes of the Three Rivers. In their dense bamboo groves and sheer ravines, human footsteps cannot penetrate; beneath their ancient trees and overhanging cliffs, the sun and moon do not shine; across their tiered ridges and stacked hills, no one knows their boundaries; and in their wild villages and distant settlements, no one can trace their beginning or end. Their tribes and clans cannot be distinguished, and their lairs cannot be tracked down. What they take for houses and huts are the peaks of crags; those with whom they associate are wolves and tigers; what they use in place of plows and shares are blades and arrowheads. Indeed, Heaven has indulged them to be like dogs, sheep, jackals, and wolves—impossible to transform through human moral principles.

In the west of the region, there are lairs called Dateng 大藤, Bazhai 八寨, Liancheng 連城, the Sixty-three Mountains 六十三山, and the Seven Mountains 七山; others of this sort are too numerous to enumerate. In the east of the region, there are lairs called Luopang 羅旁, Wangmu 王母, Yunshao 雲稍, and Muji 母雞; others of this sort are likewise too numerous to enumerate. Those along the rivers harass boats and oars; those along the roads harass travelers…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
民財被劫虜且及公賦村落被剽略且及
城邑如是而猶曰兵不祥器也而吾諱言
之是居者無以為居將棄編氓也行者無
以為行將棄商賈也公賦無以為公賦將
棄公賦也城邑無以為城邑將棄城邑也
此必不可者也其動大衆者不得不動也
其興大役者不得不役也調兵數十萬不
得計其擾也費糧數十萬不得計其費也
何者誠計其大也誠不得不為士民請命
===
也大兵一動風聲輒露其濱江濱路探知
內地消息者寧無有潛避遠匿脫然於鋒
鏑之外者耶其深山絕澗耕山而食結茅
而居不識內地言語不通者寧無有莫知
禍端駢首於鋒鏑之下者耶其所報功級
者果皆慣盜劇惡耶其所報俘獻者果皆
寇賊種類耶同生天地同稟血屬使其蠢
然無知莫知所謂而受俘獲罹刀鋸也此
又仁人之所隱而天地日月之恩有所不
punctuated: 民財被劫虜，且及公賦；村落被剽略，且及城邑。如是而猶曰：「兵，不祥器也」，而吾諱言之，是居者無以為居，將棄編氓也；行者無以為行，將棄商賈也；公賦無以為公賦，將棄公賦也；城邑無以為城邑，將棄城邑也。此必不可者也。其動大衆者，不得不動也；其興大役者，不得不役也。調兵數十萬，不得計其擾也；費糧數十萬，不得計其費也。何者？誠計其大也，誠不得不為士民請命也。大兵一動，風聲輒露。其濱江濱路、探知內地消息者，寧無有潛避遠匿、脫然於鋒鏑之外者耶？其深山絕澗、耕山而食、結茅而居、不識內地、言語不通者，寧無有莫知禍端、駢首於鋒鏑之下者耶？其所報功級者，果皆慣盜劇惡耶？其所報俘獻者，果皆寇賊種類耶？同生天地，同稟血屬，使其蠢然無知、莫知所謂，而受俘獲、罹刀鋸也，此又仁人之所隱，而天地日月之恩有所不
translation_en:
…Private property is seized and plundered, and it even reaches public tax revenues; villages are raided and pillaged, and it even reaches walled cities and towns. When things have come to such a pass, if one still says, "Weapons are instruments of ill omen," and we shrink from speaking of them, then those who dwell at home will have no way to dwell, which is to abandon the registered populace; travelers will have no way to travel, which is to abandon the merchants and traders; public tax revenues will have no way to serve as public tax revenues, which is to abandon public taxation; and walled cities and towns will have no way to serve as walled cities and towns, which is to abandon the cities and towns. This is utterly impermissible. Those who mobilize great multitudes do so because they have no choice; those who launch great campaigns do so because they have no choice. In deploying hundreds of thousands of troops, one cannot reckon the disruption; in expending hundreds of thousands in grain, one cannot reckon the expense. Why is this? Truly because one is reckoning the greater good, and truly because one has no choice but to plead for the lives of the gentry and commoners.

Yet once a great army is mobilized, word of it inevitably leaks out. Among those along the rivers and roads who spy out news from the interior, could there not be some who secretly flee and hide far away, escaping unscathed beyond the reach of blades and arrows? And among those in deep mountains and cut-off ravines who till the hills for food and thatch huts for shelter, who are unfamiliar with the interior and do not understand our language, could there not be some who, knowing nothing of the cause of the calamity, perish side by side beneath the blades and arrows? Are the severed heads reported for merit truly all hardened bandits and heinous villains? Are the captives presented in triumph truly all of rebel and bandit stock? Born together between Heaven and Earth, endowed alike with flesh and blood, that they should in their ignorant simplicity know nothing of what is happening and yet suffer capture and fall victim to the blade and saw—this, in turn, is what pains a benevolent person, and where the grace of Heaven, Earth, Sun, and Moon fails to…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
及也然則兵者將諱言之耶將樂言之耶
往歲督府重臣因粵東羅旁諸巢爲地方
害且數十年動衆二十萬一舉殲之兵威
所震山谷爲空計所得功級俘獻即萬萬
勿計也乃西之六十三山等處逼近羅旁
畏威悔罪乞憐求生編里輸差盡從撫處
一時東西兩山竝稱寧靖說者謂當時收
兵太早經略事宜尚未萬全逃匿餘黨尚
未搜捕乃不踰年舊日餘孽呼攜潜出盤
===
據舊巢劫掠水陸攻擾所城謂其藏匿者
在六十三山等巢然無實跡可考也謂其
糾合者爲六十三山等獞亦無實跡可據
也即日將東西夾剿滅此朝食而西之糧
餉稱乏八寨濱近之民又數數請兵將從
撫耶將從剿耶較之八寨將孰先耶將孰
後耶此執事者之所以私憂而過計之也
竊以爲撫剿有定議而恩信不可失也兵
糧有定處而騷擾所當禁也行師有紀律
punctuated:
及也。然則兵者，將諱言之耶？將樂言之耶？往歲督府重臣因粵東羅旁諸巢爲地方害且數十年，動衆二十萬，一舉殲之。兵威所震，山谷爲空，計所得功級俘獻，即萬萬勿計也。乃西之六十三山等處逼近羅旁，畏威悔罪，乞憐求生，編里輸差，盡從撫處，一時東西兩山竝稱寧靖。說者謂當時收兵太早，經略事宜尚未萬全，逃匿餘黨尚未搜捕。乃不踰年，舊日餘孽呼攜潜出，盤據舊巢，劫掠水陸，攻擾所城。謂其藏匿者在六十三山等巢，然無實跡可考也；謂其糾合者爲六十三山等獞，亦無實跡可據也。即日將東西夾剿，滅此朝食，而西之糧餉稱乏，八寨濱近之民又數數請兵。將從撫耶？將從剿耶？較之八寨，將孰先耶？將孰後耶？此執事者之所以私憂而過計之也。
竊以爲撫剿有定議，而恩信不可失也；兵糧有定處，而騷擾所當禁也；行師有紀律，
translation_en:
… fail to reach. If so, then as for military action, should one avoid speaking of it, or should one delight in speaking of it? In recent years, the senior official at the Supreme Commander's headquarters, because the various lairs of Luopang 羅旁 in eastern粵 (Guangdong) had plagued the region for several decades, mobilized a force of two hundred thousand and annihilated them in a single stroke. Shaken by our military might, the mountains and valleys were emptied; as for tallying the severed heads taken for merit and the captives presented, they were truly beyond all counting. Thereupon, the Sixty-three Mountains and other places to the west, being in close proximity to Luopang, feared our majesty and repented their crimes, begging for pity and pleading for their lives. They were organized into administrative villages (li) to pay taxes and render labor service, all being handled through pacification. For a time, the mountains of both east and west were alike proclaimed peaceful and tranquil. Yet commentators said that at the time the troops were withdrawn too early, that the arrangements for strategic regulation were not yet completely secure, and that the fleeing and hidden remnant bands had not yet been hunted down and captured. Indeed, before a year had passed, the surviving miscreants of old called to one another and stealthily emerged, reoccupying their former lairs, plundering by water and land, and attacking and harassing the battalion cities. Some say that those hiding them are in the lairs of the Sixty-three Mountains and elsewhere, yet there is no concrete evidence to verify this; some say that those banding together with them are the Zhuang 獞 of the Sixty-three Mountains and elsewhere, yet there is no concrete evidence to substantiate this either. Now, on short notice, we are about to launch a pincer campaign of extermination from both east and west, vowing to destroy them before breakfast; yet in the west, military provisions and funds are reported to be lacking, while the people living near the Eight Stockades (Bazhai 八寨) are also repeatedly requesting troops. Should we pursue pacification, or should we pursue extermination? Compared with the Eight Stockades, which should come first, and which should come later? This is why the examiners privately worry and take such anxious thought over the matter.

I venture to consider that pacification and extermination have a settled course of deliberation, and grace and good faith must not be lost; troops and provisions have fixed arrangements, and disturbance and harassment ought to be prohibited; the conduct of an army has discipline, …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而玉石所當辨也善後有長策而犬羊不
可無統也地方有緩急而機宜不可失也
此今日爲粵西籌者誠無以過之也夫曰
撫勦有定論而恩信不可失者何也蓋六
十三山連城等山與羅旁相去不遠其所
藏匿其所糾合誠不知其有無夾勦之師
欲杜禍根收全功誠不可已也然昔之受
招安當編差者尚未有叛逆顯迹也一旦
使之一槩受鋒鏑何以示往日之恩信開
===
後日之悔悟也大兵一出願察其素受招
處者許立旗挿牌以保其生其怙惡不悛
素未招撫者必誅無赦則畏威感恩忠信
行于蠻貊矣此以勦行撫之道也夫曰兵
糧有定處而騷擾所當禁者何也蓋粵西
司庫所入不支所出興師十萬支糧三月
欲取辦粵西難矣兩廣用兵調粵西之兵
食粵東之糧舊有定額無議也但近日右
江一帶饑歉特甚狼兵一調勢必騷動窮
punctuated:
而玉石所當辨也；善後有長策，而犬羊不可無統也；地方有緩急，而機宜不可失也。此今日爲粵西籌者，誠無以過之也。
夫曰撫勦有定論，而恩信不可失者，何也？蓋六十三山、連城等山與羅旁相去不遠，其所藏匿、其所糾合，誠不知其有無。夾勦之師，欲杜禍根、收全功，誠不可已也。然昔之受招安、當編差者，尚未有叛逆顯迹也。一旦使之一槩受鋒鏑，何以示往日之恩信，開後日之悔悟也？大兵一出，願察其素受招處者，許立旗挿牌以保其生；其怙惡不悛、素未招撫者，必誅無赦。則畏威感恩，忠信行于蠻貊矣。此以勦行撫之道也。
夫曰兵糧有定處，而騷擾所當禁者，何也？蓋粵西司庫所入不支所出，興師十萬，支糧三月，欲取辦粵西，難矣。兩廣用兵，調粵西之兵，食粵東之糧，舊有定額，無議也。但近日右江一帶饑歉特甚，狼兵一調，勢必騷動，窮
translation_en:
…while jade and stone must be distinguished; post-campaign rehabilitation requires a long-term strategy, while these dog- and sheep-like tribes cannot be left without governance; and local conditions vary in urgency, while the opportune moment must not be missed. For anyone planning for Guangxi today, there is truly nothing that surpasses these principles.

Why do I say that pacification and suppression have a settled conclusion, while grace and good faith must not be lost? Because the Sixty-Three Mountains, Liancheng, and other mountains are not far from Luopang; whether they are harboring fugitives or banding together with them is truly impossible to know for certain. A joint pincer campaign, aimed at eradicating the root of the trouble and achieving complete success, truly cannot be dispensed with. Yet those who previously accepted amnesty and submitted to registration for corvée labor have not yet shown any overt signs of rebellion. If, all of a sudden, we subject them indiscriminately to the blades and arrows of war, how can we demonstrate the grace and good faith of the past, or open the way for repentance and awakening in the future? Once the grand army marches out, I would wish that we investigate those who have consistently accepted pacification and settlement, permitting them to erect flags and plant placards to preserve their lives; whereas those who persist in evil without remorse and have never accepted pacification must be executed without pardon. Then they will fear our majesty and feel gratitude for our grace, and loyalty and good faith will prevail even among the southern and northern tribes. This is the way to carry out pacification by means of suppression.

Why do I say that military provisions have a fixed source of supply, while disturbances and exactions must be prohibited? Because the revenues entering the provincial treasury of Guangxi do not cover its expenditures; if we mobilize an army of a hundred thousand and supply them with rations for three months, trying to procure it all from Guangxi will be difficult indeed. In military campaigns across the Two Guangs, mobilizing the troops of Guangxi and feeding them with the grain of Guangdong has long had an established quota, which is beyond dispute. However, recently the region along the You River has suffered from particularly severe famine and crop failure. Once the native “wolf troops” (langbing) are mobilized, it will inevitably cause agitation and disturbance; in impoverished…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
山空谷乘時將起而爲盜請出公帑之積
預買糧食分布大兵所過州縣以備行糧
饑荒處所大加賑恤以安反側兵一出境
一切糧食取濟粵東則閭里寧輯民得安
生糧餉有藉不至告乏此動衆安民之道
也夫曰行師有紀律而玉石所當辨者何
也蓋東西猺獞其相濱大江州邑浪人糾
合出沒焚燒劫殺無歲無之誠不可不誅
乃其在遠地與華人絕不相聞一槩取而
===
殺戮俘獲之以爲功無乃傷天地之和虧
好生之德也今之用兵誠不以殺戮爲功
而以安集爲功不以俘獲爲功而以制馭
爲功使兇惡醜類無所逃於
天罰而無辜羣生得保全於
太和之世豈不恩威並著哉此則神武不殺之
道也夫曰善後有長策而犬羊不可無統
者何也蓋夷性獷悍難馴惟自服其酋長
今宇內疆土與夷爲界者不知幾千萬里
punctuated: 山空谷，乘時將起而爲盜。請出公帑之積，預買糧食，分布大兵所過州縣，以備行糧；饑荒處所，大加賑恤，以安反側。兵一出境，一切糧食取濟粵東，則閭里寧輯，民得安生，糧餉有藉，不至告乏。此動衆安民之道也。夫曰「行師有紀律，而玉石所當辨」者，何也？蓋東西猺獞，其相濱大江州邑，浪人糾合出沒，焚燒劫殺，無歲無之，誠不可不誅；乃其在遠地，與華人絕不相聞，一槩取而殺戮俘獲之以爲功，無乃傷天地之和、虧好生之德也？今之用兵，誠不以殺戮爲功而以安集爲功，不以俘獲爲功而以制馭爲功，使兇惡醜類無所逃於天罰，而無辜羣生得保全於太和之世，豈不恩威並著哉！此則神武不殺之道也。夫曰「善後有長策，而犬羊不可無統」者，何也？蓋夷性獷悍難馴，惟自服其酋長。今宇內疆土，與夷爲界者，不知幾千萬里
translation_en:
… mountains and empty valleys will seize the moment to rise up and become bandits. I beg that accumulated public funds be disbursed to purchase grain in advance and distribute it among the subprefectures and counties through which the grand army will pass, so as to prepare marching rations; and that in famine-stricken areas, generous relief be given to pacify those wavering in allegiance. Once the troops cross the border, if all grain and provisions are supplied by Guangdong (Yuedong), then the villages will be peaceful and orderly, the people will be able to live in security, and military supplies will have a reliable source without running short. This is the way to mobilize the multitude while keeping the people at peace.

Now, why do I say that "in marching an army there is discipline, and jade and stone must be distinguished"? It is because among the Yao and Zhuang of the east and west, those who border the subprefectures and counties along the great rivers join up with roving vagrants to appear and disappear unpredictably, burning, plundering, and killing—not a year goes by without this, and they truly must be executed. Yet as for those in remote places who have no contact whatsoever with the Chinese people, if we indiscriminately seize, slaughter, and capture them to claim merit, would this not injure the harmony of Heaven and Earth and impair the virtue of loving life? In employing troops today, if we truly count merit not by slaughter but by pacification and settlement, and count merit not by taking captives but by control and management—so that the fierce and wicked cliques have nowhere to escape Heaven's punishment, while innocent living beings are preserved intact in an era of Great Harmony—would not grace and majesty both be made manifest! This is the way of divine martiality that does not resort to killing.

Now, why do I say that "for post-war reconstruction there is a long-term strategy, and dogs and sheep cannot be without governance"? It is because the nature of the non-Chinese tribes is fierce, unruly, and hard to tame; they submit only to their own chieftains. Today, the territory within the empire that borders on non-Chinese tribes extends for one knows not how many tens of thousands of li…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也獨有土官者制服爲易而其莫相君長
自相種類者則剽掠出沒莫可制也大功
旣成請以猺獞所居之山川畫地分區擇
其衆所推服者令其招出遺黨分地以居
官給以名色不徵其租稅行之三年地方
無事立爲土司等官令其約束地方聽調
徵發仍增置哨堡廣添兵卒則地方永永
無虞也此以夷治夷之道也夫曰地方有
緩急而機宜不可失者何也蓋六十三山
===
等山當粵西之一隅乃八寨患在腹心土
民數數請兵緩急之辨亦旣較然矣顧一
省所急者在八寨兩省所急者在夾勦欲
獨舉之則不可欲兼舉之則不能願且置
八寨於不論兵威一振八寨諸獞果能悔
罪輸誠分土立官自同齊民豈不能略其
旣往許其將來如其怙罪不悛爲害地方
則乘此餘威以殲滅之特摧朽也此則酌
量緩急之道也嗚呼兵者豈得已哉將樂
punctuated:
也。獨有土官者制服爲易，而其莫相君長、自相種類者，則剽掠出沒，莫可制也。大功旣成，請以猺獞所居之山川，畫地分區，擇其衆所推服者，令其招出遺黨，分地以居。官給以名色，不徵其租稅。行之三年，地方無事，立爲土司等官，令其約束地方，聽調徵發；仍增置哨堡，廣添兵卒，則地方永永無虞也。此以夷治夷之道也。
夫曰地方有緩急，而機宜不可失者，何也？蓋六十三山等山當粵西之一隅，乃八寨患在腹心，土民數數請兵，緩急之辨亦旣較然矣。顧一省所急者在八寨，兩省所急者在夾勦，欲獨舉之則不可，欲兼舉之則不能。願且置八寨於不論，兵威一振，八寨諸獞果能悔罪輸誠，分土立官，自同齊民，豈不能略其旣往，許其將來？如其怙罪不悛，爲害地方，則乘此餘威以殲滅之，特摧朽也。此則酌量緩急之道也。
嗚呼！兵者豈得已哉？將樂
translation_en:
…Only those who have native officials (tuguan) are easy to bring under control, whereas those who have no rulers over one another and merely group together by their own kind raid and vanish unpredictably, and cannot be controlled. Once the great campaign is accomplished, I beg that the mountains and streams inhabited by the Yao and Zhuang be demarcated into districts, and that those whom the multitude respects and submits to be selected and ordered to summon forth the remaining bands and divide the land for them to dwell in. The authorities should grant them nominal titles and not levy land taxes upon them. After practicing this for three years, if the region remains peaceful, they should be established as native officials (tusi) and similar officers, ordered to restrain and govern their localities and obey calls for troop mobilization. If we also increase the number of sentry forts and widely add soldiers, then the region will eternally be free from worry. This is the way of using barbarians to rule barbarians.

As for saying that regions have differing degrees of urgency and that opportune moments must not be lost, what does this mean? The Sixty-three Mountains (Liushisan Shan) and other mountains lie in one corner of western Guangdong and Guangxi (Yuexi), whereas the trouble of the Eight Stockades (Bazhai) lies in the vital heartland. The local people have repeatedly requested troops, so the distinction between what is urgent and what is not is already quite clear. Yet what is urgent for a single province lies in the Eight Stockades, while what is urgent for the two provinces together lies in a joint pincer campaign of suppression. To launch a campaign alone is unfeasible, and to launch both simultaneously is beyond our capacity. I would ask that we temporarily set the Eight Stockades aside without discussion. Once our military might is demonstrated, if the various Zhuang of the Eight Stockades are indeed able to repent their crimes and pledge their sincerity, dividing the land, establishing officials, and making themselves like registered commoners, how could we not overlook their past deeds and grant them a future? If they persist in their crimes without repentance and harm the region, then riding on the remaining momentum of our military prestige to annihilate them will be just like crushing dry rot. This is the way of weighing relative urgency.

Alas! How could weapons be used unless unavoidable? Should we delight in…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
言之耶將諱言之耶樂言之而所謂寡人
妻孤人子獨人父母見聞所不及者獨不
足念耶諱言之而近日古田之復城邑府
江之通往來可以無兵得之耶酌量於緩
急之間識察於輕重之勢以撫爲勦則其
不用也猶用也爲雨露爲日星而莫非天
地之仁也以勦爲撫則其用也猶不用也
爲雷霆爲霜雪而莫非天地之義也仁義
竝行恩威兼著此兵家之善道也愚生書
===
生也何所知因明問而陳其一得者如此
惟執事者進教之
punctuated: 言之耶？將諱言之耶？樂言之，而所謂寡人妻、孤人子、獨人父母，見聞所不及者，獨不足念耶？諱言之，而近日古田之復城邑、府江之通往來，可以無兵得之耶？酌量於緩急之間，識察於輕重之勢，以撫爲勦，則其不用也猶用也，爲雨露，爲日星，而莫非天地之仁也；以勦爲撫，則其用也猶不用也，爲雷霆，爲霜雪，而莫非天地之義也。仁義竝行，恩威兼著，此兵家之善道也。愚生書生也，何所知？因明問而陳其一得者如此，惟執事者進教之。
translation_en: … to speak of it? Or shall one shrink from speaking of it? If one delights in speaking of it, are not those of whom it is said that men's wives are widowed, their children orphaned, and their parents left childless—even those beyond the reach of sight and hearing—worthy of compassionate thought? Yet if one shrinks from speaking of it, could the recent recovery of the walled town of Gutian 古田 and the reopening of traffic along the Fu River 府江 have been achieved without troops? By weighing what is urgent against what can wait, and discerning the relative gravity of circumstances, when one uses pacification as a means of suppression, then not employing force is itself a way of employing it—like rain and dew, or the sun and stars, all of which are nothing other than the benevolence of Heaven and Earth. When one uses suppression as a means of pacification, then employing force is as though not employing it—like thunderbolts, or frost and snow, all of which are nothing other than the righteousness of Heaven and Earth. For benevolence and righteousness to proceed together, and grace and awe to be manifested alike—this is the supreme way of military strategy. I, an ignorant student, am a mere scholar; what do I know? In response to your enlightened question, I have set forth my humble understanding thus; I pray only that the examiners will summon me forward and instruct me.

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
萬曆巳卯秋巡按廣西御史
顧鈴奉
皇帝典制賓士于澤宮闋歌謂志
頤曰士且駕矣若亦何言志
頤伏內忖泳游
恩澤如海未知所報而告所愧以
===
訓人越鷄伏鵠難矣雖然使
誨規矩者必班倕離朱然後
可匠將微乎告諸士曰有司
之求士甚于士之求有司也
比者玄黃以志頤而來以爲
權衡以爲律量揣銖黍度毫
末瞠乎其視芒也手其編中
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序
萬曆巳卯秋，巡按廣西御史顧鈴奉皇帝典制，賓士于澤宮。闋歌，謂志頤曰：「士且駕矣，若亦何言？」志頤伏內忖：泳游恩澤如海，未知所報，而告所愧以訓人，越鷄伏鵠，難矣！雖然，使誨規矩者必班、倕、離朱然後可，匠將微乎？告諸士曰：「有司之求士，甚于士之求有司也。比者玄黃以志頤而來，以爲權衡，以爲律量，揣銖黍，度毫末，瞠乎其視芒也！手其編，中…
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the jimao year of the Wanli era [1579], the Regional Inspector of Guangxi, Censor Gu Ling 顧鈴, upholding the statutory institutions of the Emperor, feasted the scholars as guests at the Hall of Marshland [the examination compound]. When the singing concluded, he said to me, Zhiyi 志頤: "The scholars are about to set off in their carriages; what words do you have for them?" I humbly reflected within myself: swimming in imperial grace and bounty as vast as the sea, I do not yet know how to repay it; to speak of that wherein I feel ashamed in order to instruct others is like a small fowl of Yue trying to hatch a swan's egg—hard indeed! Even so, if those who teach the use of the compass and square had to be like Gongshu Ban 公輸班, Artisan Chui 倕, or Li Zhu 離朱 before they were permitted to do so, would not craftsmen become vanishingly few? I therefore say to the scholars: "The authorities seek scholars even more eagerly than scholars seek the authorities. Recently, with gifts of black and yellow silk they came to summon me, Zhiyi, taking me as the balance and scale, taking me as the pitch-pipe and measure. Weighing down to the finest grains and measuring down to the tips of hairs, I stared wide-eyed until my vision grew dim! Holding a scroll in hand, if the beginning hit…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
程變矣竟蒐之而殊患其愉
也此何愛而不忍哉曰人才
實難脫一不終安得以瑕瑜
不掩爲解而汙賢能書蓋其
慎也士由此進于
天子矣譬則貢焉明金紣羽英犀
澤象雖遐裔之林不數數產
===
也日月而獲之意駭色動置
驛而上而不知都市之駢闐
天府之委擲直奇贏已耳士無自
謂英英奇矣而妄驅馳脫一
不終猶汙今日賢能書也其
慎自愛哉且夫取士以藝法
之窮也豈無他科自周漢以
punctuated: 程變矣，竟蒐之而殊患其愉也。此何愛而不忍哉？曰：人才實難。脫一不終，安得以瑕瑜不掩爲解，而汙賢能書？蓋其慎也。士由此進于天子矣。譬則貢焉：明金、紣羽、英犀、澤象，雖遐裔之林，不數數產也；日月而獲之，意駭色動，置驛而上，而不知都市之駢闐，天府之委擲，直奇贏已耳。士無自謂英英奇矣，而妄驅馳；脫一不終，猶汙今日賢能書也，其慎自愛哉！且夫取士以藝，法之窮也。豈無他科？自周、漢以
translation_en:
… standard, their expression transformed; yet in the end we still searched through them all, deeply worried lest any be frivolous [?]. Why do we cherish them so and yet cannot bear to be lenient? Because genuine talent is truly hard to find. Should even one man fail to maintain his integrity to the end, how could we excuse ourselves with the saying that "flaws and merits do not conceal each other," and thereby sully the register of the worthy and able? Such is our caution.

From here, scholars will advance to the Son of Heaven. Compare this to presenting tribute: bright gold,bundled kingfisher feathers, fine rhinoceros horn, and lustrous ivory—even in the forests of the distant frontiers, such things are not produced in abundance. When one acquires them after days and months of effort, one's mind is amazed and one's countenance stirred, and one sends them up by post relay—not realizing that in the thronging markets of the metropolis and the heaped-up stores of the Imperial Treasury, they are treated merely as surplus curiosities. Let the scholars not consider themselves brilliantly extraordinary and recklessly gallop ahead. Should anyone fail to see his virtue through to the end, he would still stain today's register of the worthy and able. Let them carefully cherish their own integrity!

Moreover, selecting scholars by means of literary art is the last resort of institutional method. Were there no other categories of selection? From the Zhou and Han dynasties…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
來置罷罷置凡以十數
明興要氏六經之言以爲卒亡
以喻而已昔孔子觀於上古
患其言不皆爾雅削觚裁方
所存者廑廑止此爲萬世程
授學者習之雖才不達猶堪
自植訓詁之興棼如絲毛至
===
朱子乃有條貫六經之旨復
章章著明我
聖朝統一道真塞岐旁示周行令
學者尊尚師說不悖亦足以
脩行先王之道矣由此言之
雖有超觀冥覽秪嘵嘵亂羣
無益今所不取而況俗化彫
punctuated: 來，置罷罷置，凡以十數。明興，要氏六經之言，以爲卒亡以喻而已。昔孔子觀於上古，患其言不皆爾雅，削觚裁方，所存者廑廑止此，爲萬世程。授學者習之，雖才不達，猶堪自植。訓詁之興，棼如絲毛，至朱子乃有條貫，六經之旨復章章著明。我聖朝統一道真，塞岐旁，示周行，令學者尊尚師說不悖，亦足以脩行先王之道矣。由此言之，雖有超觀冥覽，秪嘵嘵亂羣無益，今所不取，而況俗化彫
translation_en: … [since the Zhou and Han dynasties,] they have been established and abolished, abolished and established, by the dozens in all. With the rise of the Ming, the method ultimately came to rest upon [氏 for 氐?] the words of the Six Classics, in the belief that in the end nothing could surpass them. In antiquity, when Confucius surveyed the remote past, he was troubled that its words were not all refined and orthodox; he pared away the corners and trimmed them square, so that what remained was merely this much, serving as a standard for ten thousand generations. Handed down for scholars to practice, even those whose talents do not reach far are still able to establish themselves. When exegetical commentaries arose, they were as tangled as silk fibers and hairs; only when it came to Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] was there a coherent thread, and the purport of the Six Classics once again became brightly manifest. Our Sacred Dynasty has unified the true Way, blocked off diverging side-paths, and pointed out the grand highway, commanding scholars to revere the teachings of the masters without transgression—which is indeed sufficient for cultivating and practicing the Way of the Former Kings. From this perspective, even if someone possesses transcendent insights and abstruse readings, they merely clamor and confuse the multitude to no avail and are not selected today; how much less so when vulgar customs carve and…

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
文樂難攻之書而弋獨用之
言以飾其瑣譎謬悠之論讀
之如太上靈檢絕域重譯非
同文之化而罔施于用文章
道喪瀰瀰下矣此世之所謂
千金而有司方敝帚棄者也
士無寧詆有司眊哉士第以
===
===
故業往卽經緯
國華康賛
聖功無匱用已毋更謁師不信有
司將謂聖賢掌不然之辯以
迷世而有司張無目之羅以
招不制之羽也必非指矣劉
邵有言人之質量中和最貴
punctuated: 文，樂難攻之書，而弋獨用之言，以飾其瑣譎謬悠之論。讀之如太上靈檢、絕域重譯，非同文之化而罔施于用，文章道喪，瀰瀰下矣。此世之所謂千金，而有司方敝帚棄者也。士無寧詆有司眊哉？士第以故業往，卽經緯國華、康賛聖功，無匱用已。毋更謁師、不信有司，將謂聖賢掌不然之辯以迷世，而有司張無目之羅以招不制之羽也，必非指矣。劉邵有言：「人之質量，中和最貴。
translation_en: … carving and embellishing prose, delighting in books that are difficult to master, and fishing for idiosyncratic words in order to dress up their petty, deceitful, and absurd arguments. Reading them is like reading the esoteric talismanic scriptures of the Most High or texts from remote lands requiring multiple translations; they do not belong to a culture of unified writing and are of no practical use. The Way of literature is lost, and standards have steadily declined. What the world values as a thousand pieces of gold, the authorities are right now casting aside like a worn-out broom. Would scholars not rather slander the authorities as dim-sighted? If scholars simply go forth with their established studies, then in weaving the splendor of the state and peacefully assisting the sacred achievements, they will never lack for practical utility. Do not seek out other teachers or distrust the authorities—otherwise it would be as if to say that the sages and worthies wielded specious arguments to delude the world, and that the authorities spread a meshless net to summon untamable birds, which is surely not the true aim. Liu Shao 劉邵 once said: "Among the qualities and capacities of men, equilibrium and harmony are the most precious. …

title: 萬曆七年廣西鄉試錄
text:
中和之職必平淡無味故能
調成五材變化應節是以觀
人察質必先其平淡而後求
其聰明吾願諸士以平淡赴
公家羽髦齒角之珍不能過也
志頤今所以誨者輗軏不具
又無竒理雖然亦猶行古之
===
道也猶冠者持里父之醮言
只得持吾所以受里父之醮
言安有持父之醮言而不免
者哉
江西吉安府廬陵縣儒學敎
諭陳志頤謹序
punctuated:
中和之職，必平淡無味，故能調成五材，變化應節。是以觀人察質，必先其平淡，而後求其聰明。吾願諸士以平淡赴公家，羽髦齒角之珍，不能過也。志頤今所以誨者，輗軏不具，又無竒理。雖然，亦猶行古之道也。猶冠者持里父之醮言，只得持吾所以受里父之醮言，安有持父之醮言而不免者哉？
江西吉安府廬陵縣儒學敎諭陳志頤謹序。
translation_en:
… the office of equilibrium and harmony is necessarily plain and flavorless, and therefore it is able to blend and perfect the five endowments and adapt in response to due measure. Thus, in observing men and examining their natural qualities, one must first look for their plainness and only afterward seek their cleverness and brilliance. I wish that all you scholars would go forth to serve the public realm with such plainness; even the treasures of feathers, pelts, ivory, and horns cannot surpass it. What I, Zhiyi, offer as instruction today lacks crossbar and yoke-pin, nor does it possess any marvelous principles. Even so, it is still a way of practicing the之道 of antiquity. It is like a newly capped youth holding fast to the ceremonial admonition given at the wine-blessing by a village elder—I can only offer the ceremonial admonition that I myself once received from the village elders. How could anyone hold fast to a fatherly ceremonial admonition and yet fail to avoid fault?”

Respectfully prefaced by Chen Zhiyi 陳志頤, Instructor of the Confucian School of Luling County in Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi.
